context.topic: Mac shell intended workload and current read-only allowlist
context.text:
run_shell takes an arbitrary command string and runs it with a 120s default timeout via computerControl.runShell.
actionRisk.isStatusShellCommand auto-approves only: no shell metacharacters, under 240 chars, no sudo/doas, no curl/wget/nc/ssh/python/node/ruby/perl/bash -c/zsh -c/osascript, and matching STATUS_SHELL_PATTERNS.
BUT executor.js:21 branches on FULL_CONTROL_MODE and calls executeComputerAction directly, bypassing classifyAction entirely. FULL_CONTROL_MODE is ON. So in practice nothing is gated and any command runs unattended. This is intentional for now — the owner wants maximum capability. Judge the surface on that basis.

context.topic: approved Mac shell use cases and trust boundary
context.text:
run_shell as built (computerControl.js:404).
Arbitrary command string. cwd is optional and passed through resolveUserPath; otherwise inherited. Timeout is action.params.timeout or DEFAULT_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000 (line 38). The environment is NOT restricted, there is no network restriction, and no separate audit log beyond the job record.
actionRisk.isStatusShellCommand would allow only: no shell metacharacters, under 240 chars, no sudo/doas, no curl/wget/nc/ssh/python/node/ruby/perl/bash -c/zsh -c/osascript, matching STATUS_SHELL_PATTERNS — but executor.js:21 bypasses it entirely while FULL_CONTROL_MODE is on, which it is.
Real commands already run through this path: pmset -g batt, scutil --nwi, system_profiler SPAirPortDataType, osascript -e set volume output volume 30.

context.topic: Mac shell safety policy and migration scope
context.text:
Owner policy, stated explicitly: give agents as much access as possible, no restrictions. The models are trusted to judge what they should and should not do.
FULL_CONTROL_MODE stays ON. actionRisk.classifyAction stays bypassed. There is no confirmation step and none is wanted for reversible work.
Do NOT propose adding approval gates or shrinking the shell surface — that has been considered and rejected. Propose things that make the agent MORE capable: better observability of what ran, faster/cheaper paths to the same result, and recovery when a command fails.
undo.js reverses only some actions (set_volume and a few others); everything else is permanent. Knowing which is which is worth more here than gating.

Shell authorization: none. FULL_CONTROL_MODE bypasses actionRisk entirely (executor.js:21). Arbitrary commands run unattended with a 120s default timeout, unrestricted env, unrestricted network. This is the owner deliberate choice and will not change — do not propose gates.

context.topic: execution grant and replacement shell policy
context.text:
Do not design a replacement shell policy. The owner has considered and rejected narrowing the surface: maximum capability is the requirement, and the models are trusted to judge.
What IS wanted: observability of what ran, cheaper/faster paths to the same answer, and recovery when a command fails. undo.js reverses only a few action types (set_volume among them); everything else is permanent, so knowing which is which beats gating.

Commands already proven on this Mac through run_shell: pmset -g batt, scutil --nwi, system_profiler SPAirPortDataType, df -h, osascript -e set volume output volume N, git branch lookups.
One real failure worth knowing: finding the owner project took five attempts because nothing tells you where it lives. It is /Users/evanliu/agentic-gadget, branch main. Home is /Users/evanliu, hostname MacBook-Air-6.local, arm64 darwin, macOS 26.5.2.

tools.name: safe_mac_command
tools.why: Current run_shell executes arbitrary shell unattended because FULL_CONTROL_MODE bypasses actionRisk. Useful Mac work needs narrowly scoped read-only diagnostics and explicitly confirmed mutations without shell injection or unrestricted filesystem/network access.

input_schema.operation: string enum: [system_info, process_list, disk_usage, file_stat, read_text, list_directory, git_status]
input_schema.path: optional string, must be under approved roots for file operations
input_schema.args: optional object with operation-specific typed fields; no raw command string

tools.name: mac_readonly_diagnostics
tools.why: The granted safe_mac_command has no implementation, while my only job is environment reconnaissance. I need a narrowly scoped read-only diagnostic capability rather than arbitrary shell execution.

command.description: One command selected from a fixed read-only diagnostic allowlist; reject shell metacharacters, pipes, redirects, command substitution, interpreters, network clients, privilege escalation, and writes.

tools.name: mac_readonly_diagnostics
tools.why: The granted safe_mac_command has no implementation, while arbitrary shell is unsafe. We need useful Mac status discovery without arbitrary command execution.

tools.name: mac_read_diagnostics
tools.why: The granted safe_mac_command has no implementation, while reconnaissance and future routing need bounded host facts without arbitrary shell execution.

tools.name: mac_execute_typed_actions
tools.why: Replace arbitrary run_shell exposure with a narrow executor for the Mac planner's foreseeable tasks while preserving confirmation and auditability.

tools.name: mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl
tools.why: The granted safe_mac_command and mac_readonly_diagnostics interfaces are present but return 'no implementation yet', so I cannot verify cwd inheritance, timeout behavior, host OS, storage, battery, or network state needed to assess argv migration compatibility. I need a read-only diagnostic path only; no mutation or arbitrary shell.

permissions.scope: read-only access to authenticated Mac-agent observability endpoints (/jobs, /logs, /journal, /routing) via the existing local-agent auth context
permissions.askedFor: read-only access to authenticated Mac-agent observability endpoints (/jobs, /logs, /journal, /routing) via the existing local-agent auth context

proposals.user_asks: “Run an audio check.” The pendant should play a short private test phrase, measure the microphone-to-relay-to-Mac-to-headphones path, and tell me exactly whether the problem is capture, LTE transport, speech generation, or headphone playback—then switch to the best compatible audio profile for the next call.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can hear degraded, delayed, or silent audio but cannot identify which node is responsible. This turns an opaque multi-device failure into a one-sentence diagnosis and an automatic recovery choice, without sending the owner's test recording into long-term storage.
proposals.model_tier: Background/diagnostic work should use a cheap deterministic protocol and DSP checks; use the realtime model only to phrase the final spoken result if needed. No expensive model call is needed to detect sample-rate mismatch, packet loss, clipping, underruns, or latency.
proposals.latency_budget: The owner should get the diagnosis in under 5 seconds. A normal conversation must not pause unless the owner explicitly asks for the check.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost: one small marked test burst and compact telemetry. The dominant cost is engineering the shared test protocol and implementing bounded DSP counters on the pendant and bridge.
proposals.security_concerns: Use a synthetic tone or locally generated phrase rather than uploading live microphone content. Persist only aggregate measurements and an expiring correlation ID. Switching profiles must be limited to known-safe audio settings; do not change Bluetooth pairing or transmit recordings without confirmation.
missing: A versioned diagnostic protocol understood by the nRF9160, Cloudflare relay, Mac bridge, and ESP32 or replacement audio bridge
Firmware counters for I²S overruns/underruns, Opus loss, clock drift, and playback completion
A relay job that correlates capture, upload, TTS generation, download, and playback timestamps
A small dashboard or spoken-result formatter that maps measurements to actionable diagnoses and records the selected fallback profile
A production audio bridge capable of reporting its actual A2DP sample rate instead of exposing only the current 31.25-to-44.1 kHz prototype path

proposals.user_asks: “Use the best audio quality available for these headphones.” The pendant should negotiate and remember a per-headphone profile, preserving the network's 24 kHz speech quality until the final Bluetooth boundary, selecting 44.1 or 48 kHz only when required, and fall back safely when the headphones reconnect or change.
proposals.why_useful: The owner should not have to understand that LTE speech, I²S clocks, and A2DP have different sample-rate contracts. Today the prototype silently resamples through a fixed 31.25-to-44.1 kHz path and gives no indication whether a connected headset can do better. This would make every headset sound as good and as reliably as it can.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic capability negotiation and DSP configuration, not an LLM. The realtime model is unnecessary; a cheap background planner may explain an incompatibility only when one occurs.
proposals.latency_budget: Profile selection should complete within 1 second of headphone connection and add no more than 10 ms to normal playback. Reconnection should automatically reuse the last known-good profile.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero per-use API cost. Engineering cost is concentrated in Bluetooth capability discovery, clock configuration, and profile persistence; hardware redesign may dominate if the current ESP32 A2DP source cannot expose the required controls.
proposals.security_concerns: Store only a non-secret headphone identifier, supported codec/rate profile, and health counters. Pairing keys remain on the bridge. Never upload Bluetooth identifiers or audio samples to the relay unless the owner enables diagnostics.
missing: Bluetooth source capability discovery and per-device profile storage
A bridge implementation with selectable 44.1/48 kHz output and observable actual clock rate
A canonical distinction between 24 kHz relay PCM and the final Bluetooth output rate
A pendant/bridge reconnect handshake that rejects stale profiles and reports fallback reasons
Hardware or firmware replacement for the current HUZZAH32 precompiled 44.1 kHz-only path if it cannot support negotiated output

proposals.user_asks: “Make the computer ready for this, then do it.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a voice request can fail because the browser extension is offline, Safari has no attached tab, accessibility is unavailable, or the Mac agent is stale. This lets the owner state the goal once; the pendant reports the blocker, the Mac repairs only the local connection state it can repair, the browser reattaches the right private session, and the relay resumes the original job with a sourced completion receipt instead of asking the owner to repeat everything.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short spoken blocker/status exchange. Use the cheaper background planner for readiness diagnosis and the actual browser/Mac job; use deterministic health checks and typed reconnect actions before any model call.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgement under 1 second; readiness checks 1–3 seconds; reconnect/reopen usually under 15 seconds. If a human login or permission is genuinely required, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen to visit, then resume when the heartbeat returns.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per invocation when deterministic checks suffice; model cost dominates only ambiguous diagnosis and task planning. Heartbeats and receipts are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: The repair path may open apps or URLs but must not bypass authentication, change permissions, or move private page content to the relay. Keep session/tab identifiers and evidence local; relay only receives health state, blocker reason, and final redacted receipt. Require confirmation only for the owner's already-defined destructive actions (sending, deleting, buying), not for reversible readiness actions.
missing: A readiness contract exposing local-agent, browser-extension, Safari-session, accessibility, and network health as typed dependencies
Safe idempotent reconnect/open/focus actions and a browser tab/session reattachment operation
The cross-surface execution lease and handoff journal proposed above
A pendant status-event protocol for blocker/recovered/completed states

proposals.user_asks: “Use the pendant as the key for this task, and revoke it when I say stop.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner could delegate one concrete goal to the Mac and authenticated browser without granting an invisible, indefinite trust relationship. A physical press or spoken confirmation on the worn pendant would bind the request to the owner, let the relay authorize only the named task and selected private session, and let the owner revoke it from anywhere—even if the Mac is unattended. This is not available today: the pendant starts conversations, but it is not an authenticated, task-scoped authority for the other nodes.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic cryptographic checks and typed capability evaluation for authorization; use the realtime model only to explain the request and status. No expensive model call is needed to mint, validate, expire, or revoke a token.
proposals.latency_budget: A local pendant confirmation and relay-issued grant should complete in under 2 seconds. Revocation should reach the Mac and browser within one heartbeat interval (target under 5 seconds), with the Mac refusing new work immediately when its lease expires.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost after implementation: small D1/token-state writes and heartbeat traffic dominate; model cost is limited to the spoken explanation. Hardware can use the existing button/LED initially; a production pendant should add a secure element or protected key storage, roughly $1–$3 BOM and negligible active power.
proposals.security_concerns: Use asymmetric device identity, nonce-bound grants, audience (relay/Mac/browser), task hash, permitted operations, private-session identifier, expiry, and revocation epoch. Never transmit the owner's long-lived secret to the Mac or browser. Keep authenticated page data local; the relay carries opaque grants and receipts. A lost pendant requires server-side revocation; a compromised Mac must not mint grants. The grant authorizes execution of the specified task, not unrestricted shell access, while preserving the owner's deliberate maximum-capability policy inside that grant.
missing: A hardware-backed pendant identity and signed button-confirmation protocol
Relay token minting, revocation, expiry, and replay protection stored durably in D1
Mac-agent and browser-bridge verification middleware that fences jobs on grant validity
A dashboard view showing active grants, scope, expiry, and immediate revoke, plus a pendant LED/error signal for revoked or expired authority

proposals.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” while wearing the pendant, capture what I am looking at in Safari, the short reason I gave, and the relevant local Mac context as one private, searchable research card; keep a compact version available on the pendant when the Mac is offline, and let me later ask “why did I save this?”
proposals.why_useful: Today a spoken thought, a browser page, and local context live in separate places, so the owner must manually copy URLs, explain the purpose again, and hope the page remains available. This would preserve the meaning and provenance of an idea at the moment it occurs, then make it retrievable from either the pendant or Mac without replaying the original browsing session.
surfaces: pendant captures the utterance and gives immediate confirmation
browser extension reads the active tab URL/title/selected or main text under the paired private-browser session
Mac planner gathers only explicitly relevant local context and stores the searchable card
relay assigns the card identity, synchronizes it when the Mac is unavailable, and serves the compact offline pendant copy
dashboard provides provenance, expiration, redaction, and deletion controls
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic extraction and hashing for URL/title/timestamps and a background-tier model to write a short reason and keywords. Escalate to the planner tier only when the page is ambiguous or the owner asks a semantic question; realtime is only for the spoken confirmation and retrieval conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the save on the pendant in under 1 second with a local placeholder. Capture browser metadata within 3 seconds; text summarization can finish in the background. Offline mode should preserve the utterance and URL locally, then synchronize on reconnection.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.001–$0.01 per saved card depending on page-text length and whether semantic summarization is needed. Storage and browser extraction dominate operational cost; most saves should avoid the expensive planner tier.
proposals.security_concerns: The active tab may contain credentials, health, financial, or work information. Require explicit pairing and a clear spoken/visual indication when page content is being captured; default to URL/title/selection rather than the whole DOM, redact secrets and form values, encrypt relay and Mac storage, apply per-card TTLs, and provide pendant commands to delete the last card or all cards. Never send captured page text to the relay unless the owner’s capture policy permits it.
missing: A cross-surface private-card schema with provenance (tab/session, URL, timestamp, selection hash), sensitivity labels, TTL, and deletion propagation
A browser-extension command to return the active tab’s bounded selection or readable region without form values
A small encrypted offline card cache and sync protocol shared by pendant and relay
A Mac-local search/index and a retrieval response that can cite the original browser source
User-configurable capture policy distinguishing URL-only, selection, and page-summary modes

proposals.user_asks: If a task spans my Mac and logged-in browser, keep it alive through disconnects: retry when the right device returns, never duplicate a completed step, and tell me exactly what finished and what still needs me.
proposals.why_useful: Today the live agent can leave browser commands pending while the bridge is offline, and Mac readiness can be false when Accessibility or Screen Recording is missing. The owner should not have to remember which steps ran or restart a workflow—especially for a long task started from the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: background for workflow bookkeeping, retries, reconciliation, and spoken summaries; realtime only for the initial request and urgent status questions
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant in under 2 seconds; resume within 30 seconds of a heartbeat returning; status summary within 5 seconds of each retry outcome.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per workflow: deterministic state transitions and receipt reconciliation dominate; background model only for ambiguous recovery or the final concise summary.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, page extracts, and local command receipts remain on the Mac/relay according to existing retention. Never resend a browser form submission or shell mutation solely because a network response was lost; require an explicit owner confirmation for an actually irreversible step, while preserving the owner's no-gate policy for ordinary Mac execution.
missing: A durable cross-node workflow/DAG state store shared by relay and Mac, with step idempotency keys and dependency leases
A reconciliation probe that distinguishes 'not started', 'completed but reply lost', and 'unknown side effect' for browser and shell actions
Heartbeat-triggered retry policy with exponential backoff, quiet hours, and a pendant/dashboard explanation of degraded state
A single completion receipt that links Mac job receipts, browser command receipts, and relay delivery attempts

proposals.user_asks: Before I rely on you, tell me whether you actually checked everything relevant across my Mac, logged-in browser, and relay-held tasks—and if you say nothing needs me, show me what was checked, what was unreachable, and how fresh each result is.
proposals.why_useful: An ordinary briefing can sound complete even when the browser bridge is offline or a permission is missing. The owner needs an honest, coverage-aware absence claim rather than false reassurance, especially when delegating work while away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: deterministic coverage computation and freshness checks first; background model only to compress the evidence into a short spoken explanation; realtime only for follow-up questions
proposals.latency_budget: Return a coverage verdict in under 3 seconds from cached observations; refresh reachable surfaces within 20 seconds; explicitly label any surface that could not be checked.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.005 per check set: endpoint reads and cached fingerprints dominate, with minimal background summarization only when many sources are present.
proposals.security_concerns: The coverage report itself reveals which private accounts, tabs, files, or jobs exist. Keep it owner-scoped, speak only names and statuses by default, and require an explicit request to reveal snippets or URLs. Never claim a negative result for an unobserved surface.
missing: A typed inventory of checkable sources and their authority/coverage scope across Mac, browser sessions, relay jobs, and pendant queues
Freshness leases and explicit unreachable/stale/error states rather than treating empty results as success
A deterministic completeness verdict with per-source evidence IDs and a dashboard drill-down
A spoken response format that distinguishes 'checked and clear' from 'not checked' and 'checked with low confidence'

proposals.user_asks: If I ask you to do something across my Mac and logged-in browser, just start it; if one part is unavailable, tell me exactly what is blocked, keep the rest moving, and resume automatically when that part comes back.
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser task can sit in a queue while the extension is offline, and the Mac reports missing Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions only as a generic not-ready state. The owner should get a useful spoken explanation instead of a 45-second failed attempt, while independent Mac/relay work continues and the browser step resumes without repeating completed work.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic capability preflight and job dependency scheduling first; use background gpt-4.1-mini only to summarize the blocked reason and next step, and realtime only for the owner's live spoken interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight and dependency split under 300 ms; pendant hears a blocked/continuing status within 1 s. Browser heartbeat retry every 5–10 s with exponential backoff; no model call on retries.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for health checks/retries; roughly one background gpt-4.1-mini call (about 2k input tokens today) only when the user-facing explanation materially changes. Storage is a small durable job/dependency record and event log.
proposals.security_concerns: Health data stays in the relay/Mac job metadata; do not transmit page contents or credentials in readiness events. Never replay a browser mutation automatically unless its idempotency key and prior receipt prove it did not complete; resume only at the first unacknowledged step.
missing: A shared capability snapshot API consumed by relay and Mac planner, with explicit states for browser online/offline, permission missing, queue depth, and retry-after
A DAG-style job runner that splits Mac/browser/relay steps, persists completed receipt IDs, and reattaches a waiting browser step to the same authenticated session/tab
A browser reconnect handshake that drains or reconciles the 2 currently pending commands instead of allowing stale commands to execute blindly
Pendant event types for blocked, partial-progress, resumed, and permanently-failed jobs, plus a dashboard view of dependency and retry state

proposals.user_asks: When I’m in a meeting or focused, keep the pendant silent and collect only genuinely urgent things; when I’m free, give me one short, prioritized catch-up, including anything the Mac or my logged-in browser discovered.
proposals.why_useful: The owner should not have to manually switch modes or receive fragmented alerts from separate agents. The pendant’s physical presence, Mac focus state/calendar, browser activity, and always-on relay can jointly infer an interruption budget and turn scattered events into one timely catch-up without losing urgent items.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event correlation and urgency rules first; use a cheap background model to cluster and rank accumulated events; use realtime only when the owner explicitly asks for the catch-up or an urgent alert must be spoken immediately.
proposals.latency_budget: Mode changes reflected within 1–2 seconds; urgent alerts under 5 seconds; normal catch-up generated in under 10 seconds after the owner becomes available. No model call for ordinary mode transitions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low relay storage and event traffic; one small background ranking call per catch-up, typically far cheaper than a realtime turn. Retain event summaries and source links, not full page contents or audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar titles, browser page metadata, and focus state are sensitive and must remain in the owner’s encrypted account scope. Do not infer or announce sensitive meeting details aloud; announce only urgency and a neutral source label. The owner needs a physical pendant override to force quiet or urgent mode.
missing: A shared interruption-state protocol with states such as available, focused, meeting, quiet, and emergency, including source confidence and expiry
A Mac focus/calendar signal adapter and browser event publisher that emit normalized, privacy-minimized events to the relay
Pendant-local quiet/urgent override and a durable on-device unread counter that works across a dropped link
Relay-side event deduplication, urgency policy, and release queue with explicit source links and dismissal state
A dashboard timeline showing why an item was held, surfaced, or suppressed, with per-source quiet rules

proposals.user_asks: “Do this and keep going even if my Mac, Safari, or connection drops; tell me when it is truly finished.”
proposals.why_useful: This is the missing everyday promise: the pendant can capture intent immediately, the relay can keep the work alive, the Mac can act with the owner's local authority, and the browser can use private sessions when available. The owner gets one concise completion or an honest parked/unknown state rather than a false success or a dead request.
surfaces: Pendant captures the goal and speaks immediate acknowledgement
Relay creates a durable parent job, decomposes it into checkpointed steps, and wakes on health transitions
Mac local-agent executes shell/typed actions and emits receipts, stderr, exit status, and undoability
Browser extension executes authenticated-tab steps when online and returns tab/session provenance
Relay reconciles all receipts, retries only idempotent transient failures, and sends final audio plus a Mac review artifact
proposals.model_tier: Background model for decomposition, retry classification, and final summary; deterministic routing and state transitions first. Realtime only for the initial spoken acknowledgement and urgent completion alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge from pendant in under 1 second; dispatch when a capable surface is online; no fixed completion deadline. Retry/backoff should be invisible unless it exceeds a user-configured quiet-period, then speak one status update.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per multi-step invocation depending on decomposition and final summary; most health checks, checkpointing, and receipts are deterministic. Browser screenshots or long page extraction dominate exceptional cases.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay stores intent and minimal step metadata, never shell secrets or page contents by default. Authenticated browser actions remain on the Mac bridge. Non-idempotent actions must be marked unknown after disconnect and held for owner review rather than replayed. Final audio should reveal only the minimum needed.
missing: Cross-surface parent/child job and checkpoint protocol
Stable local-agent health lease and reconnect event
Durable relay queue with idempotency and unknown-outcome handling
Browser bridge online/offline wakeup integration
Pendant completion-status notification and quiet-hours policy

proposals.user_asks: “Make sure this actually happened, not just that you clicked the button.” For example: send the prepared message, update the appointment, or change the setting, then independently verify the resulting state and tell me if reality disagrees with the intended outcome.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can report that a local action or browser command returned success, but that is not proof that the external world accepted or retained the change. The owner needs outcome-level confidence for consequential everyday tasks: confirmation that the recipient/server/state reflects the requested result, with an immediate warning when it does not.
surfaces: Pendant states the intended outcome in the owner's words and speaks a concise verified/unverified result
Relay stores the intent, expected postcondition, evidence requirements, and a short-lived verification deadline
Mac agent performs local actions and reads back local state, logs, notifications, or application results
Browser bridge performs authenticated read-back in the same session, while a separate safe read path checks the resulting page/API-visible state when available
Relay compares independent evidence against the expected postcondition and sends the owner either proof, a discrepancy explanation, or a request to inspect manually
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic postcondition evaluation and evidence matching first; background model only translates natural-language intent into a typed expected state and explains discrepancies. Realtime is used only for the spoken result.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate action acknowledgement, then verification within 5–30 seconds for local/browser changes. Long-running external confirmations may remain pending and notify the owner once, rather than holding the conversation open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per invocation. Most verification is deterministic; cost is dominated by a background interpretation call and occasional authenticated page extraction or screenshot.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must not expose message bodies, account data, or credentials to the relay unnecessarily. Evidence should be hashed or reduced to the relevant fields, with sensitive read-back remaining on the Mac. Never label an action verified from the same untrusted acknowledgement that triggered it; distinguish accepted, observed, and independently confirmed states. Non-idempotent retries remain prohibited.
missing: A typed expected-postcondition schema covering local apps, browser pages, and external acknowledgements
An evidence-capture API that returns minimal field-level proof with source, timestamp, and session identity
A verifier that can use a distinct read-back route and represent accepted/observed/confirmed/contradicted/unknown states
Cross-surface correlation between the original action receipt and later read-back
Pendant and relay UX for pending verification, discrepancy alerts, and manual inspection

proposals.user_asks: “If something I asked you to do fails while I’m away, keep going where it’s safe, tell me exactly what stopped, and give me one command to resume it.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a long Mac/browser job can leave partial side effects with a receipt but no coherent explanation or continuation. This would turn failures into recoverable work: the owner wakes to a concise spoken status, a sourced report on the Mac, and a resumable plan rather than repeating commands or guessing what already happened.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model (GPT-5.6-luna or equivalent) to classify failures, summarize receipts, and construct a resume plan; use realtime only to answer the owner's live follow-up through the pendant. Use the Mac vision model only for a failed GUI step that needs visual diagnosis.
proposals.latency_budget: Start/resume acknowledgement under 2 seconds from the relay; background recovery and report within 30 seconds for shell/API work and up to 2 minutes for browser/GUI work. Spoken report should be under 30 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per delegated job depending on output volume; most cost is the background recovery model and any mac-vision retry, not receipt storage or relay delivery.
proposals.security_concerns: The Mac shell remains unrestricted by owner policy. Preserve exact command, cwd, exit code, stderr, touched paths/apps/URLs, and redaction metadata in the private ledger; do not send raw stdout, page contents, cookies, or secrets to the relay unless needed for the owner's request. Never silently repeat a non-idempotent browser submission or destructive shell command; mark it stopped/uncertain and report the last confirmed side effect. No new approval gate is introduced; existing action semantics remain unchanged.
missing: A durable cross-surface job runner (the current backend still lacks one) with dependency-aware checkpoints and idempotency keys spanning Mac shell and authenticated browser actions.
A shared failure taxonomy and typed step state: succeeded, retryable, blocked-on-device/session, failed-before-effect, effect-uncertain, and irreversible.
A resume endpoint/tool that accepts a job ID, skips confirmed action IDs, revalidates sessions/tabs/files, and emits a new receipt chain linked to the original.
Relay-to-pendant delivery of compact failure/resume notifications and a dashboard view showing the step graph, evidence, and exact stopping point.

proposals.user_asks: “Pack up what I’m doing so I can leave this Mac, and let me pick it up later from the pendant or another device exactly where I stopped.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently loses the relationship between open Mac work, authenticated browser tabs, terminal state, unsent drafts, and the reason a task was paused. This would create a private, resumable handoff rather than a pile of tabs and vague notes: the pendant can explain the active threads while the Mac or browser later restores only the relevant state.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to summarize and index the work session; use realtime only when the owner asks the pendant for a spoken handoff. Use mac-vision only to capture/restore GUI state that accessibility APIs cannot represent.
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken 'pack this up' acknowledgement in under 2 seconds; produce the handoff within 15 seconds for ordinary tabs/files and under 60 seconds when screenshots or GUI reconstruction are required. Resume should show a concise state within 5 seconds, then restore asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per pack/resume, dominated by summarization and occasional screenshots; storage and local state fingerprints are negligible. Repeated spoken queries should use cached summaries rather than re-running the model.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep cookies, tokens, private page bodies, clipboard contents, and raw terminal output on the Mac/browser boundary; relay and pendant receive minimized summaries and opaque references. Encrypt the handoff bundle, bind browser restoration to the existing authenticated session, expire sensitive captures, and clearly label drafts as unsent. The feature should not submit forms, send messages, or mutate files merely by restoring a session.
missing: A session-bundle schema that links Mac windows/apps, terminal jobs, browser tab/session IDs, selected files, drafts, and task intent while storing provenance and sensitivity per item.

A local Mac snapshot/restore adapter for accessibility-visible windows, terminal cwd/job IDs, editor locations, and browser tab reattachment; browser bridge support for redacted page anchors rather than copying private page contents.
Relay storage and retrieval for encrypted, expiring handoff manifests plus a pendant-friendly spoken-summary endpoint.
A cross-device resume protocol that can rehydrate on the Mac, or provide an actionable spoken queue when the Mac is unavailable, without pretending that GUI state was restored.

proposals.user_asks: “Check that logged-in page for me. If my Mac or browser is unavailable, wait safely and finish when it comes back—tell me whether it is waiting, completed, or failed, and never repeat a step that already ran.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a pendant request can encounter an offline browser extension, spend roughly 45 seconds timing out, and leave the owner unsure whether the site, Mac, or command failed. This gives the owner dependable cross-device continuity: the relay stays awake, the Mac owns execution, Safari contributes the private session, and the pendant reports truthful progress and completion without duplicate navigation or submissions.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic health checks, job state transitions, idempotency, and receipts for most of the flow; use the background tier only to summarize a completed result or explain an unusual failure. Reserve realtime for the owner's spoken status/questions.
proposals.latency_budget: Healthy requests should begin within 1–2 seconds. An unavailable browser should be reported in under 1 second rather than waiting for a 45-second action timeout. Reconnection resumes on the next authenticated heartbeat; spoken completion follows within a few seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental model cost: heartbeat checks, queueing, and resume are deterministic. A short background summary costs one inexpensive model call only when a completed result needs narration; storage is a few KB per pending job and receipt.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents and cookies remain in Safari on the paired Mac. The relay stores only encrypted job state, action IDs, status, and minimal result metadata. Reconnection must not authorize an irreversible action by itself: resume only actions proven unstarted/idempotent, expire stale leases, and report any ambiguous step for owner review.
missing: A paired-browser heartbeat/capability lease visible to the Mac bridge and relay
A durable waiting-for-device job state with bounded retry and dead-letter expiry
Cross-surface resume keyed by stable action IDs and existing receipts
Pendant and dashboard status events that distinguish waiting, completed, failed, and ambiguous outcomes
A browser preflight that fails fast when the extension is offline instead of waiting for the action timeout

proposals.user_asks: “Why didn’t that work?”—give me the actual evidence from the pendant request, relay, Mac command, and browser session, explain the failure in plain language, and tell me the safest next step without rerunning anything.
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed cross-device task is fragmented: the pendant knows the request, the relay knows delivery, the Mac knows the job, and Safari knows whether a session was alive. The owner cannot ask one place for a causal answer and may accidentally retry a command or browser transaction that already partly ran. A cross-surface failure explanation turns raw receipts and health state into a trustworthy diagnosis before any retry.
proposals.model_tier: Collect and correlate evidence deterministically from job receipts, shell envelopes, relay delivery events, and browser heartbeat/session state. Use the background tier to produce the concise explanation; use realtime only to speak it interactively. Never invoke the planner merely to collect evidence.
proposals.latency_budget: Evidence collection under 500 ms when devices are online; under 2 seconds if the relay must fetch recent records. A spoken explanation within 3 seconds, with a follow-up link to the detailed dashboard evidence.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for correlation and classification; one short background summarization call when wording is needed. Local evidence retention is bounded and cheaper than a blind low-latency retry.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not send shell stdout, URLs, page text, cookies, or environment values to the relay by default. Relay receives opaque IDs and redacted failure classes; detailed evidence stays on the Mac and is shown only through the paired dashboard or on explicit owner request. The capability is strictly read-only and must not trigger retry or undo.
missing: A shared operation ID linking pendant intent, relay delivery, Mac job/receipt, and browser command/session
A normalized event schema with timestamps and causal links across relay, Mac, and browser
Shell execution envelopes containing bounded, redacted failure evidence
Browser heartbeat/session evidence that distinguishes offline bridge, closed tab, navigation failure, and page-level error
A read-only cross-surface diagnosis endpoint and concise pendant response formatter

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving my Mac—save what I’m looking at and what I was trying to do, keep working on it, and give me the result on my pendant when it’s ready.”
proposals.why_useful: Today work is split between a live browser tab, Mac state, and relay jobs; walking away loses the exact page, evidence, and intent. A physical pendant handoff makes an interrupted task resumable and returns a concise result without reopening the computer.
surfaces: pendant button/voice: capture a handoff request and later announce a result
Mac agent: snapshot focused app, open tabs, selected text, downloads, and current job context into a checkpoint
browser extension: capture authenticated tab/session IDs plus page URL/title and a redacted evidence excerpt; resume the same tab later
relay: persist the checkpoint, run background research or Mac/browser steps while offline/asleep, and route completion to the pendant
dashboard: show checkpoint, evidence, progress, and a one-tap resume/stop control
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize the checkpoint and poll/reconcile progress; use realtime only for the spoken handoff and completion summary. Escalate to the expensive tier only when the owner asks an ambiguous follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the button/voice handoff in under 2 seconds; checkpoint in under 10 seconds; background work may take minutes. Completion notification should be under 5 seconds after the relay records success.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per handoff, dominated by extracting/summarizing page context; polling and typed state transitions are negligible. Avoid resending page text by storing a content hash plus short excerpt and fetching only on resume.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page URLs, tab IDs, and excerpts leave the Mac for the relay; redact secrets/form values and store only the minimum evidence with a short TTL. Never submit/send browser mutations as part of automatic resume; require the existing owner confirmation at the final irreversible step. A lost pendant should not expose page contents through notifications.
missing: A Mac/browser checkpoint API that atomically captures focused UI plus authenticated tab/session binding
A durable relay handoff job with lease, retry, expiry, and pendant push notification
A browser resume protocol that validates the original tab/session and reports when it has changed
A pendant-side offline queue/notification state (single button, LED/audio)
Dashboard UI for evidence, progress, and final approval

proposals.user_asks: “What am I looking at right now—and what’s the one thing I should notice?”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can ask while away from the keyboard and get a grounded answer about the exact private page or Mac window in front of them, without explaining which tab, copying text, or uploading the whole screen. The system should identify the active context, extract only the relevant region, and speak a concise answer with a way to inspect its evidence.
surfaces: pendant: capture the spoken question and play the answer; a double-press can request the source snippet
Mac agent: identify the focused window and coordinate a one-shot capture, OCR/accessibility extraction, or focused-app metadata
browser extension: attest the active authenticated tab, extract only the visible/relevant DOM region, and return URL/title plus a short evidence hash
relay: route the request to the correct local surface, enforce an ephemeral context token, and discard the payload after answer delivery
dashboard: show the exact source region and confidence after the answer, without retaining the full screen
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles the short spoken answer and ambiguity resolution; a cheaper vision/text model performs OCR and relevance extraction locally or in the relay. Use the expensive tier only for genuinely ambiguous visual interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Identify and answer in 3–6 seconds, with a spoken progress cue by 1 second. Evidence view may arrive within 10 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per question, dominated by one small image or DOM-region inference; local accessibility extraction should avoid sending pixels whenever possible.
proposals.security_concerns: The active window may contain passwords, messages, or other people’s data. Require an ephemeral per-question token, region minimization, local redaction of password fields and secrets, no raw screenshot retention, and an explicit indicator when capture is active. If the active context cannot be attested, say so rather than inspect an arbitrary tab.
missing: A focused-window/context-attestation API shared by the Mac agent and browser extension
A one-shot, region-limited extraction endpoint with local secret redaction and evidence hashes
Relay support for ephemeral context tokens and guaranteed payload expiry
Pendant UX for capture-active indication and source/evidence replay

proposals.user_asks: “Run a health check on the Mac and pendant, fix anything safe, and tell me what still needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner cannot get one truthful answer about the whole system: the Mac agent reports relay reachability, browser offline with two queued commands, missing Accessibility/Screen Recording, and full-control readiness in one snapshot, while pendant audio and relay health live elsewhere. A spoken diagnostic should correlate those states, perform only reversible repairs (reconnect bridge, retry stale queue, refresh machine context, restart a failed job), and leave permission or destructive issues as explicit owner tasks.
proposals.model_tier: background for collection and deterministic correlation; realtime only to ask a follow-up or speak the short result
proposals.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for deterministic status; up to 30 seconds for one repair-and-recheck cycle
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per invocation; most calls are deterministic, with a small background summary only when several failures need prioritizing
proposals.security_concerns: The Mac snapshot contains local paths, app inventory, permission state, and job metadata; relay must return redacted typed health facts rather than raw logs. Repairs must be allowlisted as reversible and idempotent; never alter files, send mail, or change permissions without an owner request.
missing: A relay endpoint that aggregates pendant telemetry, Mac /ops/snapshot, and bridge heartbeat into one signed health report
Typed repair operations with idempotency keys and before/after receipts (reconnect, retry, refresh, cancel stale browser command)
A pendant button/voice intent and concise spoken rendering of severity plus owner-required steps
A clear readiness model: distinguish 'agent process up' from 'permissions ready' and 'browser online'

proposals.user_asks: “Show me exactly how that request moved through the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, and point to the first thing that went wrong.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner gets isolated job results and logs, not a single causal explanation spanning the spoken request, model routing, relay delivery, Mac execution, browser state, and spoken response. When something silently fails or produces the wrong result, they cannot tell whether the fault was recognition, planning, transport, stale browser state, a Mac permission, or synthesis. A voice-triggered causal replay would make the hive debuggable by the person wearing it, without requiring them to inspect developer logs.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event correlation first; use a cheaper background model only to turn the correlated timeline into a short explanation. Realtime is unnecessary except for the owner's spoken query.
proposals.latency_budget: Return a first fault location in 2 seconds from indexed events; generate a detailed replay in under 15 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01, dominated by a small background summarization call; correlation and redaction are local/deterministic.
proposals.security_concerns: A replay may contain private speech transcripts, authenticated URLs, page text, file paths, and action parameters. Store event payloads encrypted with short retention, expose hashes and redacted excerpts by default, and require an explicit owner request to reveal sensitive fields. Never replay credentials or full page contents into speech.
missing: A shared causality envelope propagated from pendant utterance through relay, model calls, Mac jobs, browser commands, and TTS, with parent/child IDs and monotonic timestamps
An append-only, encrypted event index on the relay and Mac that records outcomes, retries, routing decisions, and permission failures without raw secrets
A cross-surface redaction and evidence API that can return the first divergent event plus bounded excerpts
A dashboard and concise pendant rendering for timeline, confidence, and 'show more' drill-down

proposals.user_asks: “If something I asked you to do gets stuck or fails, figure out what went wrong, try the safe alternative, and ask me on the pendant only if you truly need me.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a Mac/browser job can be queued and eventually reported, but a failure is mostly an endpoint rather than a recoverable conversation. This would turn unattended work into a resilient handoff: the Mac classifies the failure, the browser facet can refresh or reattach a session when appropriate, the relay keeps the job alive across sleep, and the pendant receives one concise question only when recovery needs owner input.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna for failure diagnosis and recovery planning; gpt-4.1-mini only for deterministic browser/UI retries; relay-realtime speaks the short interruption, while background diagnosis uses the cheaper planner tier where possible.
proposals.latency_budget: Normal recovery under 10 seconds after a failure; never hold the live voice turn open. Queue diagnosis immediately, try at most two bounded alternatives, and notify the pendant within 30 seconds if blocked.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per failed job depending on whether a planner retry needs screenshots/page text; most successes add negligible cost because the executor emits structured failure data without another model call.
proposals.security_concerns: Command output, URLs, and browser excerpts may leave the Mac for diagnosis, so redact secrets and send only the failing step plus bounded evidence. Automatic recovery must be limited to idempotent/reversible retries; anything that could submit, send, purchase, delete, or duplicate must stop and ask. Keep an audit trail of every attempted alternative and its result.
missing: A typed failure envelope from run_shell and browser actions (exit code, timeout/signal, stderr classification, step id, idempotency/reversibility, and redacted evidence).
A recovery state machine with retry budgets, compensating actions, and session reattachment for sleeping/restarted Macs.
A relay endpoint for owner questions that binds the reply to the paused job, plus pendant-friendly “resume/cancel” controls.
Dashboard UI showing the failed step, attempted alternatives, and exact next action before escalation.

proposals.user_asks: “Don’t just do it—make sure it actually happened, check the result from the right source, and tell me if anything disagrees.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can report that a Mac or browser action completed, but completion of a command is not proof that the owner's intended real-world state changed. This capability would verify the postcondition independently—for example, confirm a calendar event in the logged-in web account after creating it, confirm a downloaded file exists and opens on the Mac, or confirm a setting is reflected in the app—then reconcile conflicting observations instead of claiming success from an exit code alone.
proposals.model_tier: Use gpt-5.6-luna for selecting the postcondition and reconciling evidence; use deterministic Mac/browser reads for collection; use relay-realtime only to speak the concise result. Background verification can run on a cheaper planner tier.
proposals.latency_budget: For local checks, 2–5 seconds; for browser/account checks, up to 20 seconds asynchronously. The pendant should immediately say that verification is in progress, then deliver verified, contradicted, or inconclusive status.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually $0.005–$0.04 per verification for structured reads; $0.05–$0.15 when reconciliation needs screenshots, page extraction, or a second model pass. The dominant cost is authenticated page context, not the Mac reads.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may access more private state than the initiating action. Each check should use the minimum source needed, redact values in relay speech and dashboard previews, and preserve source URL/app, timestamp, and evidence hashes. Never silently “repair” a contradiction; any corrective mutation remains a separate owner-directed action.
missing: A first-class postcondition specification in each action/job, including acceptable evidence sources and freshness window.
Cross-surface verification adapters that can query Mac state, browser state, and relay receipts under one correlation ID.
An evidence reconciler that distinguishes command success, observed state change, stale cache, and contradictory sources.
A pendant/dashboard result format with confidence, evidence links, and a clear “verified / not verified / needs you” outcome.

proposals.user_asks: When I tell you to take care of something, verify that it actually stuck everywhere, and tell me exactly what is still unfinished.
proposals.why_useful: Today an agent can report that a Mac command, browser edit, or relay job completed even when the application rejected it, a page reverted it, sync was delayed, or the Mac went offline. This gives the owner a closed-loop result about the real outcome rather than a claim that steps were attempted. It is especially valuable for cross-surface tasks where Safari, a local app, the relay, and the pendant can each show different state.
surfaces: pendant: capture the goal and speak a concise final status or an exception
relay: own the goal, schedule delayed verification, correlate all attempts, and notify when the outcome changes
mac-bridge: inspect application/file/system postconditions and re-check after sync delays
browser: inspect authenticated page state and compare the resulting semantic fields with the intended change
dashboard-ux: show an evidence timeline of intended state, observed state, pending checks, and unresolved discrepancies
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the initial conversation and short spoken explanation. Use a cheaper background model for postcondition planning, evidence reconciliation, delayed rechecks, and discrepancy summaries; use deterministic typed checks before invoking a model.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement in under 2 seconds; first result after the action completes; delayed verification should run at configurable intervals (for example 10 seconds, 2 minutes, and 15 minutes) without keeping the voice session open. The pendant should interrupt only for a meaningful failure or eventual success after an earlier uncertain result.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually well below one realtime turn: deterministic Mac/browser checks dominate latency but not API cost, with one small background reconciliation call only when observations disagree. Roughly $0.005–$0.05 per task depending on the number of delayed checks and page evidence size; authenticated browser screenshots or large DOM captures dominate transfer and processing cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may read private browser pages, local files, and application state, so evidence must inherit the originating job's permissions, remain local-first where possible, and redact secrets from dashboard and spoken output. The system must distinguish 'verified', 'not yet observable', and 'failed' rather than claiming success. It should never submit an additional irreversible action merely to verify; verification is read-only unless the owner separately requested a repair.
missing: A durable goal/postcondition schema that expresses what success means independently of the action sequence
Mac and browser adapters for typed, read-only postcondition checks with freshness timestamps
Relay scheduling and deduplication for delayed verification attempts
Evidence reconciliation that can represent conflicting observations without collapsing them into success
Dashboard and pendant status vocabulary for verified, pending, uncertain, and failed outcomes

proposals.user_asks: If a task I handed you on my Mac fails or the connection drops, diagnose it, resume from the last completed step when safe, and tell me exactly what recovered and what still needs me.
proposals.why_useful: Today an unattended shell command can run with maximum access, but a timeout, sleep, network blip, or partial multi-step result leaves the owner unsure whether rerunning would duplicate work. This makes long Mac work dependable without adding approval gates: the pendant/relay can report progress, while the Mac can inspect and recover locally.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for heartbeat interpretation, failure classification, and retry planning; use realtime only for the owner's spoken status or an explicit follow-up question. Deterministic Mac-side code should own checkpoints and idempotency; the model should not invent completion.
proposals.latency_budget: Start/acknowledgement under 2 seconds; progress events every 10–30 seconds; recovery decision under 10 seconds after failure. Long commands continue detached from the voice session.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per long job for a few small background classifications; dominant cost is occasional model calls on failure, not heartbeats or receipts.
proposals.security_concerns: The existing FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted environment remain unchanged; this adds observability and recovery, not blocking. Persist command metadata, exit code, bounded stdout/stderr tails, cwd, and checkpoint hashes, with secret-pattern redaction before relay/dashboard storage. Never auto-retry a command classified as non-idempotent or whose checkpoint is ambiguous; report it for owner review. Browser actions must retain tab/session affinity and before/after evidence.
missing: A Mac-local supervisor that detaches shell processes, emits heartbeats, captures bounded/redacted output, and records checkpoint boundaries
A shared job state machine with attempt IDs, resumable checkpoints, and explicit states (running, link-lost, failed, recovered, needs-owner)
Failure classifiers and command-specific recovery recipes (sleep/network unavailable, missing path, transient browser tab loss, nonzero exit)
Relay push/status subscription to the pendant and a dashboard timeline that distinguishes completed steps from merely attempted steps

proposals.user_asks: Do it on my Mac, then prove to me that the intended result actually exists—not just that the command finished—and tell me if anything differs from what I asked for.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can report that an action or shell command ran, but completion is not the same as the desired real-world state: a file may be written to the wrong folder, an upload may be rejected after a click, or a setting may be changed by another process. The owner should receive an independent outcome check with concrete evidence and a clear mismatch report.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic validators first (file hashes/metadata, process and preference reads, browser DOM/state checks). Use a cheap background model to choose or synthesize a validator from the goal, and mac-vision only when visual confirmation is genuinely required. Realtime is reserved for the concise spoken result.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate action acknowledgement under 2 seconds; verification within 5 seconds for local state and under 20 seconds for browser/server propagation. If propagation is asynchronous, keep a background watch and notify only on confirmed success or a bounded timeout.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per invocation when typed validators suffice; $0.02–$0.08 when a model must construct a validator or vision is needed. Storage and network transfer of small evidence artifacts dominate only for screenshots or large file checks.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may inspect private files and authenticated browser pages. Keep raw evidence on the Mac where possible; relay only hashes, selected fields, redacted snippets, and a user-readable explanation. Never claim proof from an identical action receipt. For destructive or externally visible actions, verification reports state but does not silently repair; any repair must be separately planned and visible.
missing: A goal-to-postcondition schema that records what success means independently of the action used
A typed validator registry spanning filesystem, app preferences/processes, browser DOM/network-visible state, and mac-vision screenshots
An evidence bundle format linking each postcondition to source, timestamp, validator, and before/after values
Relay and pendant UI for a concise proof/mismatch/timeout result, with dashboard drill-down to the evidence
A policy for eventually consistent sites that polls for confirmation without duplicating the original action

proposals.user_asks: "If something I ask needs Safari, just do it—or tell me immediately what is offline and use another route when possible."
proposals.why_useful: The live Mac agent currently spends roughly 45 seconds attempting browser actions even when the extension is known offline, and repeats the same failed job. A fleet-aware preflight would make the system feel dependable: detect extension reachability first, route public pages to the relay/browser backend, and give a concise spoken recovery instruction for private pages instead of burning a long job.
proposals.model_tier: background for preflight classification and fallback planning; realtime only to tell the owner the short result or request that they open Safari
proposals.latency_budget: Health check under 500 ms; public-page fallback under 2–5 s to begin; authenticated-page offline response under 1 s. Do not spend 45 s on an impossible browser action.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually deterministic health checks and routing: near-zero model cost. One background call only when intent/fallback is ambiguous (roughly a few thousand input tokens, dominated by context); no realtime call unless speaking to the owner.
proposals.security_concerns: Never send authenticated URLs, cookies, page text, or session identifiers to the public fallback. Classify origin and session binding before routing; private pages must remain on the Safari bridge. Record which backend was selected and why, but redact URLs/query strings in the spoken receipt unless the owner asked for them. Fallback should remain read-only unless the original action explicitly permits mutation.
missing: A single fleet preflight endpoint/contract exposing browser online state, last heartbeat age, pending-command count, and whether a requested URL is public or session-bound
A relay public-browser execution adapter and a planner rule that refuses to use it for authenticated sessions
A fast-fail/idempotent browser job state so an offline attempt is not duplicated or left pending
Pendant-friendly error/result event carrying a one-sentence recovery instruction

proposals.user_asks: “What am I looking at, and what should I do next?”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must manually explain which document, browser task, meeting, and deadline they mean. This capability would turn the pendant into a genuinely ambient second set of eyes: it combines the Mac’s active application/window and selected text, the browser’s authenticated tab context, the next calendar commitment, and the owner’s current spoken goal into one cited, privacy-aware answer—without requiring them to touch the laptop or recite context.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic local collection and filtering first; use a background reasoning model to reconcile the compact evidence and propose next steps. Use realtime only to speak the short answer and handle a follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: Button-to-first spoken acknowledgement under 300 ms; evidence collection under 2 s; answer under 5 s. If screen/browser evidence is unavailable, say exactly which source is missing rather than hallucinating.
proposals.cost_estimate: One background call per explicit request, with a compact evidence packet (roughly 1–3k input tokens and a short completion); deterministic Mac/browser reads dominate neither API cost nor latency. No periodic model polling.
proposals.security_concerns: Selected text, window titles, calendar details, and authenticated page content can be highly sensitive. Collection must be explicit per request, local-first, with source-level opt-outs and redaction of passwords, payment data, and hidden tabs. Never transmit raw screenshots or page text to the relay unless the owner has enabled visual context; attach source URL/window and timestamp to every claim. Speaking aloud must omit sensitive details when headphones are not connected, and the owner must be able to say “forget that snapshot.”
missing: A cross-surface 'situational snapshot' contract with typed fields, timestamps, confidence, and sensitivity labels for active Mac UI, selected text, browser tab/session, calendar horizon, and recent pendant utterance
A Mac bridge read path for active window/selection and a browser bridge read path for the foreground authenticated tab, both returning bounded provenance rather than raw unrestricted dumps
A local privacy filter and per-source consent state, including an audio-output safety mode for spoken answers
A relay request that correlates the pendant press, snapshot ID, reasoning trace, and cited answer, plus a dashboard card showing exactly what evidence was used
A pendant interaction for explicit capture, cancellation, and deletion of the snapshot

proposals.user_asks: “Keep working, but only interrupt me if it truly matters; otherwise collect everything and tell me at a good time.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently express one interruption policy that follows work across the pendant, relay, Mac jobs, and authenticated browser sessions. This would let background work continue without turning every completion or failure into noise, while still surfacing a genuinely urgent deadline, failed irreversible step, or required owner decision at the right moment.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event aggregation and deadline/severity rules first; use a background model only to resolve ambiguous urgency or cluster related results. Realtime is reserved for a genuinely urgent spoken interruption.
proposals.latency_budget: Events classified locally in under 200 ms; non-urgent items batched into the next digest. Urgent delivery under 2 s after a qualifying event, subject to quiet hours and availability.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for typed job/browser events and fixed urgency rules; occasional background clustering call (short context, dominated by event metadata) and no call per routine completion.
proposals.security_concerns: Notification content can reveal private mail, browser pages, or work details aloud. Store policy and urgency decisions locally/relay-authenticated, redact summaries by default, and require an explicit owner setting for audible interruptions. Never let an urgency classifier authorize a mutation; it can only notify or defer. Preserve source links and event IDs for review.
missing: A shared interruption-policy object with quiet hours, channels, severity thresholds, deadline windows, and per-source sensitivity rules
Normalized event envelopes from Mac jobs, browser watches, relay jobs, calendar deadlines, and pendant connectivity, with deduplication and causal links
A durable notification queue supporting defer, snooze, bundle, acknowledge, and escalation, synchronized between relay, pendant, and Mac dashboard
A deterministic urgency evaluator with an auditable reason code and a safe fallback of 'defer, do not interrupt' when evidence is incomplete
Pendant controls for 'quiet now', 'tell me at [time]', and 'why did you interrupt me?'

proposals.user_asks: “If the computer or browser is unavailable, figure out another safe way to finish this, or keep trying until it is available, and tell me exactly what remains.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a task can fail because one dependency is offline, leaving the owner to diagnose the Mac, reopen Safari, and repeat the request. The owner should get one resilient outcome: the system distinguishes an unavailable surface from a failed step, chooses a viable alternate surface when one exists, parks the rest when it does not, and resumes without duplicating completed work.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic readiness checks, dependency planning, receipt/idempotency handling, and retry scheduling for most of the workflow; use a cheap background model to explain a failure or select among known fallback plans; reserve realtime only for the owner's brief spoken update and any clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Readiness and fallback selection under 500 ms; speak the blocker immediately instead of waiting for a timeout. Recovery may take minutes or hours, but the owner need not stay present; notify on completion or when human input is genuinely required.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost for preflight, state transitions, and retries. Occasional background explanation/planning call, roughly $0.001–$0.02 depending on context; the dominant cost is repeated browser/vision execution, which should be avoided through typed receipts and step-level idempotency.
proposals.security_concerns: Fallbacks must not export authenticated page contents to the relay or substitute a weaker surface for a sensitive action without an explicit policy match. Keep credentials and private DOM on the Mac/browser, send only task state and redacted receipts upstream, and require confirmation only for genuinely irreversible external effects—not for retries or reversible local work.
missing: A cross-surface dependency graph describing which steps require browser, GUI permissions, shell, relay, or pendant presence
A durable state machine with parked, waiting-for-device, resumed, partially-complete, and terminal-failure states
Step-level idempotency keys and receipts shared by Mac, browser, relay, and faculty-action so recovery cannot repeat mutations
A readiness heartbeat and wake/resume signal from the browser bridge and Mac agent to the relay
A fallback planner that is constrained to approved equivalent routes and can explain why no equivalent exists
A single owner-facing completion/blocker protocol delivered both as a pendant utterance and a cited Mac dashboard record

proposals.user_asks: “Don’t just tell me you did it—verify from the actual destination that it took effect, and tell me what you checked.”
proposals.why_useful: Current completion receipts describe what the Mac agent attempted, but an attempted click, sent request, or local mutation is not proof that the destination accepted it. Independent postcondition checks would catch stale tabs, dropped network requests, UI false positives, and actions that partially applied before the owner relies on them.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic postcondition probes and source comparison first; use a cheap background model only to reconcile conflicting evidence or summarize the verification. Realtime is only needed to speak the short result.
proposals.latency_budget: Verification should begin immediately after each mutating step and complete within 2–5 seconds for local/browser state; allow a bounded wait for remote systems, then report pending verification rather than claiming success.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal model cost when selectors, file hashes, process state, or API responses are deterministic. Occasional background reconciliation, roughly $0.001–$0.02; browser/vision calls dominate when a destination has no structured observable state.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may read sensitive destination state, so keep authenticated content on the originating Mac/browser and send only a redacted assertion plus evidence hash to the relay. Never treat an optimistic UI toast or local receipt as verified; for high-impact external actions, surface the exact evidence and distinguish accepted, observed, and unknown.
missing: A typed postcondition schema for shell, GUI, browser, and relay actions, including acceptable evidence sources and freshness limits
Independent verification recipes that are separate from the action command and can reattach to the correct tab/session
A cross-surface evidence bundle linking before-state, action receipt, after-state, timestamp, and source locator/hash
Conflict handling when the Mac says success but the browser or remote destination still shows the old state
Owner-facing language and dashboard fields that clearly separate attempted, accepted, observed, and unverifiable outcomes

proposals.user_asks: “Make sure that happened.” After any computer task, independently verify the visible result, tell me whether it really took effect, and if the Mac could not receive input, fix or retry only the uncertain part.
proposals.why_useful: Today the Mac can return a successful-looking UI receipt even when macOS rejects synthesized input from the running agent. The owner needs a dependable distinction between attempted and accomplished work, especially when they are away from the screen and relying on the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only to interpret the spoken request and report the result; use a cheaper background planner for verification/retry planning, with mac-vision only when visual confirmation is necessary.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial reachability/result check within 1 second after the action; visual verification within 5–10 seconds. Do not delay ordinary non-UI shell/API jobs unnecessarily.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental model cost for structured postcondition checks; roughly $0.01–$0.05 when a vision verification frame and background reasoning are required. The dominant cost is image analysis, not telemetry.
proposals.security_concerns: Screen images may contain private data and should remain on the Mac unless the owner has already enabled vision upload. Spoken results must say 'unverified' rather than claim success. Retrying should be limited to explicitly uncertain steps and preserve the original receipt; mutations still follow the owner's existing maximum-access policy.
missing: A typed postcondition contract for each UI action (expected app/window/text/state), rather than checking only that dispatch returned.
Mac executor fields for input reachability and permission state at action start/end.
A verification adapter that can use accessibility state, app/API queries, or local screenshots without falsely treating dispatch success as completion.
A retry operation addressing only unverified action IDs, with stable idempotency keys.
Relay/pendant wording and dashboard rendering for verified, unverified, and failed outcomes.

proposals.user_asks: “Do that, and don’t tell me it worked unless you can verify the result.”
proposals.why_useful: Today /observe shows a critical false-success condition: Accessibility is not trusted for the running agent, so UI clicks and typing can report success while doing nothing. This capability turns the pendant into a trustworthy completion channel: it preflights the Mac, chooses the reachable surface, verifies a concrete postcondition independently, and reports failure or recovery rather than a misleading success.
proposals.model_tier: background for planning and verification recipes; deterministic checks and Mac observation for most jobs; realtime only to acknowledge the spoken request and deliver the short result
proposals.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds for preflight plus deterministic verification; up to 30 seconds for a fallback or retry, with the pendant giving an immediate 'working' acknowledgement
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one background planner call (roughly 2k input tokens, small output; about $0.01 or less depending on model pricing); deterministic observe/receipt calls dominate neither cost nor latency. Vision fallback is the expensive path and should be opt-in per job.
proposals.security_concerns: The command still runs under the owner's deliberate FULL_CONTROL_MODE with no gates. Verification must not expose private page contents to the relay unnecessarily: return typed predicates and hashes, keeping evidence local on the Mac. Browser mutations remain draft/approval semantics where applicable. A failed verification, timeout, or ambiguous state must be reported plainly and never converted into success.
missing: A typed postcondition/verification schema shared by mac-planner, browser bridge, and relay (for example file hash, app state, URL/title, process state, or reversible setting)
A preflight health contract that marks UI automation unavailable when Accessibility/input reachability is false and permits shell/browser fallback
Receipt fields for attempted, verified, unverified, fallback, and recovered outcomes, plus durable retry/repair jobs
A relay-to-pendant result event that can speak a concise receipt and expose detailed evidence in the dashboard

proposals.user_asks: “I’m stopping here—save exactly where I am and let me resume this later from the pendant.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can leave a job record or a browser tab behind, but cannot preserve a coherent, cross-device stopping point: the exact open tab and evidence, Mac working files and app state, the last confirmed step, unresolved decisions, and the next safe action. This gives them a reliable pause/resume boundary instead of reconstructing their train of thought.
