proposals.latency_budget: A cached summary should start within 2 seconds and finish within 5 seconds; if raw evidence must be fetched from the Mac or browser, announce that and complete within 15 seconds. Never claim an effect without a receipt or explicit device evidence.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: event normalization and deterministic correlation dominate; one small background-model call for causal compression. No vision or realtime generation is needed unless the owner asks for a live explanation.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep page text, shell commands, and private app contents on the Mac/browser. Send the relay only redacted event types, timestamps, target surface, outcome class, and receipt references. The owner must be able to request local evidence, and the system must label inferred causality separately from observed facts.
missing: A shared event schema spanning local jobs, relay pipeline events, browser commands, and pendant notifications
A durable correlation ID that survives retries, handoffs, and reconnects
A local evidence index that can answer completed/no-op/unknown without exposing raw command or page contents
A causal summarizer with strict observed-versus-inferred wording and a pendant-sized output mode

proposals.user_asks: When you do something on my Mac, tell me whether it actually worked; if it fails, diagnose and retry safely, and if the Mac disconnects, resume when it returns without repeating completed steps.
proposals.why_useful: Today shell jobs can run unattended and receipts record outcomes, but a failed or disconnected multi-step task still leaves the owner to interpret partial state. This makes Mac automation dependable while preserving the owner's deliberate maximum-access/no-gate policy: it adds verification and recovery, not blocking.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for job decomposition, polling, and retry classification; use realtime only to explain a live failure or ask the owner a genuinely ambiguous question. mac-vision is invoked only when a GUI postcondition needs visual confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; normal shell verification within 2-5 seconds. Disconnect recovery is background polling (for example every 15 seconds, with exponential backoff) and should not consume realtime turns.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per task when typed/shell postconditions are used; the dominant cost is occasional vision or realtime escalation, not polling. Persisting receipts and hashes is negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Commands remain unrestricted as the owner requires. Store command text, exit status, stdout/stderr digest, touched paths/apps, and verification evidence in the existing job record; redact environment secrets and avoid copying raw stdout to the pendant. Never silently repeat non-idempotent actions: resume by stable action IDs, and mark an action unknown when the connection drops during execution. Require owner confirmation only for an explicit question about an ambiguous outcome, never as a general gate.
missing: A durable Mac job runner that survives local-agent restarts and reconnects, with stable action IDs and leases/heartbeats
A postcondition schema for shell, app, browser, and vision steps (exit code alone is insufficient)
A reconnect protocol from pendant/relay to Mac that returns partial receipts and resumes only unresolved actions
Idempotency metadata and an unknown-outcome state for commands interrupted after dispatch
A compact owner-facing failure summary delivered through the pendant, with full evidence retained in the dashboard

proposals.user_asks: After I ask you to do something, let me say “show me everything that changed” and get one trustworthy timeline across my Mac, browser sessions, pendant, and relay—with the exact evidence for each side effect and a way to undo only the changes I choose.
proposals.why_useful: Today effects are split across Mac job receipts, browser commands, relay jobs, and pendant interactions. The owner cannot answer the practical question “what did that request actually change?” across substrates, nor selectively reverse a subset. A causally linked, owner-readable change ledger would make this hive usable without requiring trust in invisible automation.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize and causally group structured events; use realtime only to answer a live spoken follow-up. The ledger itself should be deterministic, not model-generated, and the dashboard can render the detailed evidence.
proposals.latency_budget: Start speaking a compact summary within 2 seconds for recent jobs; full cross-node correlation may complete in under 10 seconds. Selective undo should report each target's status independently rather than blocking on the whole batch.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost, typically <$0.01 for normalization and summarization; most work is local indexing and receipt transport. Realtime cost is reserved for the owner's conversational query.
proposals.security_concerns: The ledger is highly sensitive because it reveals files, URLs, account activity, and device events. Keep raw evidence on the originating device, send the relay only signed metadata and redacted excerpts, encrypt links in transit and at rest, enforce per-owner retention/deletion, and never include secrets or full page text in the pendant response. Undo must use existing reversibility declarations and explicitly report irreversible effects; it must never pretend a browser send or external side effect was reversed.
missing: A shared event envelope and correlation ID propagated from pendant request through relay, Mac, browser, and returned audio
Durable cross-node append-only indexing with signatures, timestamps, source, and evidence pointers
Browser receipts that describe navigation, form mutation, and submission outcomes, not merely command completion
Relay/pendant receipts for queued jobs and delivered audio or notifications
A cross-surface selective-undo coordinator with honest per-effect reversibility and partial-failure reporting
Owner-facing timeline query and compact spoken renderer

proposals.user_asks: “Do it, and make sure it actually worked.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an unattended Mac shell command can return exit 0 while producing the wrong state, and a browser or authenticated service may be the only place the real outcome is visible. This gives the owner a closed loop: the pendant captures the goal and can announce completion, the relay keeps the job alive, the Mac performs local work, and the browser verifies the externally visible result. If verification fails, the system explains the failure and retries with a different strategy rather than claiming success.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for planning and postcondition checking; reserve realtime only for the brief spoken acknowledgment and final exception. Use deterministic checks (exit status, file hash, accessibility/UI state, page text) before spending model tokens on semantic comparison.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgment under 1 second; local verification 1–3 seconds; browser verification normally under 10 seconds. Long retries continue as a durable job and notify the pendant only on verified completion or an actionable exception.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per invocation when deterministic checks suffice; roughly $0.02–$0.10 when semantic reconciliation across Mac and authenticated browser evidence is needed. Browser/session latency and model context, not shell execution, dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may include private files, URLs, or authenticated page text and must stay in the existing owner-scoped job/session context, with sensitive stdout and page excerpts redacted in receipts. Never claim success from a command exit code alone. Actions remain under the owner's deliberate unrestricted shell policy; verification is not an approval gate. Require explicit confirmation only for any newly proposed irreversible follow-up, if policy ever changes.
missing: A typed goal/postcondition schema shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser (including evidence source, freshness, and tolerance).
A verifier that can combine shell receipts with browser/page evidence and distinguish transport failure, command failure, and wrong-result success.
Durable retry/reroute state with idempotency and a terminal 'needs owner' outcome.
A dashboard and pendant protocol for concise verified-success versus uncertain/failure notifications.

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving my desk—make sure I’m not leaving anything exposed, and tell me if you couldn’t.”
proposals.why_useful: A spoken or button-triggered departure check would coordinate the pendant’s physical presence, the Mac’s actual lock/power/network state, the browser’s authenticated tabs, and the relay’s independent record. It could lock the Mac, stop sensitive screen sharing, identify authenticated tabs or unsaved work that cannot safely be closed, and leave an exact exception list. This is not a generic reminder or a Mac-only command: it gives the owner a trustworthy privacy handoff when they physically walk away and can still report failure if the Mac is asleep, disconnected, or unreachable.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic local checks and typed actions for lock, sharing, power, and tab state; use a cheap background model only to rank exceptions and explain them. Realtime is needed only for the brief spoken result.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the button or phrase immediately; complete local checks in 2–5 seconds and browser/session inspection in up to 10 seconds. If a device is unreachable, report that explicitly rather than waiting indefinitely; relay can finish and notify when it reconnects.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 because most checks are deterministic; occasional semantic exception grouping may cost $0.01–$0.04. Latency is dominated by browser tab/session access and Mac wake/connect behavior.
proposals.security_concerns: The check necessarily touches authenticated-tab metadata and potentially sensitive window titles, so keep evidence owner-scoped, retain only hashes and minimal exception text, and redact page contents by default. Locking and stopping sharing are reversible; closing tabs, discarding edits, or signing out must never happen implicitly. The owner should choose a policy preset, but the system must report every skipped action and why.
missing: A pendant departure trigger (button gesture, explicit voice intent, or proximity transition) routed to a multi-surface job.
Typed Mac privacy-state observers/actions for lock state, active screen sharing/remote-control sessions, unsaved documents, and wake/connect status.
Browser APIs that enumerate authenticated tabs and detect unsaved or sensitive state without reading full page contents.
A relay-held privacy-check job with a short-lived, encrypted evidence record and reconnect completion semantics.
A policy engine for owner-selected safe actions versus report-only exceptions, plus a concise pendant result protocol and dashboard audit view.

proposals.user_asks: When something you did on my Mac fails, tell me what happened and give me the safest concrete way to finish it.
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed unattended shell or browser step leaves the owner to reconstruct context. This creates a spoken, evidence-backed incident packet: exact task chain, failure point, relevant Mac/browser state, and a proposed next step, while preserving the owner's maximum-access policy and avoiding an opaque retry.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model to assemble and classify the transcript; use realtime only when the owner asks from the pendant and needs a concise explanation. Escalate to the stronger model only for ambiguous multi-surface diagnosis.
proposals.latency_budget: Background incident packet within 5 seconds of terminal failure; pendant answer under 2 seconds when the transcript is already indexed. A fresh browser/Mac verification may take up to 15 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per incident depending on transcript size and whether a browser verification is needed; storage/indexing and browser re-check dominate, not the short explanation.
proposals.security_concerns: Receipts can expose private command output, paths, authenticated URLs, and account data. Keep raw evidence on the Mac, send redacted excerpts and hashes to relay, require explicit owner request before fetching full output, and never execute a suggested retry automatically. Expire incident packets.
missing: Shell execution transcript with bounded stdout/stderr, exit classification, and correlation IDs
Cross-node incident packet API and relay retrieval
A Mac-side verification step that can check postconditions without changing state
Dashboard/pedant rendering for evidence, proposed next step, and explicit retry

proposals.user_asks: Do this when the right moment arrives: wait until my Mac is idle, I'm not in a meeting, the right logged-in page is open, and I'm on trusted Wi‑Fi; then carry out the reversible steps and tell me what happened.
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently express a multi-surface condition and have the system safely wait for it. This would prevent actions at disruptive or stale moments—for example, preparing a form only when its authenticated tab is present and the owner is not presenting—while allowing the relay to keep watching after the Mac temporarily disconnects.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to compile the request into typed predicates and a step plan. Use realtime only for the initial spoken request and completion alert; use the stronger model only when a predicate is ambiguous or the page changed materially.
proposals.latency_budget: Predicate evaluation every 15–60 seconds, with event-driven wakeups from browser heartbeat and Mac state changes. After all conditions hold, begin within 2 seconds and provide a completion or refusal notice within 10 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per armed task; most cost is one-time plan compilation and occasional semantic page re-checks. State monitoring should be local/event-driven rather than model-polled.
proposals.security_concerns: The system observes meeting state, network identity, active windows, and authenticated page metadata. Keep raw state on the Mac/browser, expose only predicate results to the relay, encrypt the durable plan, expire it automatically, and never treat a changed page or untrusted network as satisfying the original predicate. The action plan must remain reversible and produce a receipt.
missing: A durable conditional-trigger engine distinct from clock-based routines
Typed Mac predicates for idle/lock/presentation/audio/network state
Browser predicates based on authenticated tab identity and semantic page fingerprint
Relay-side lease, reconnect, deduplication, and expiry handling
Pendant notification and dashboard controls to pause, inspect, or cancel an armed task

proposals.user_asks: “Just do it wherever you can, and if one part of the Mac or browser is unavailable, keep going with the parts that are possible and tell me exactly what is left.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system reports a browser that is offline with four pending commands and a Mac agent that is not ready because Accessibility and Screen Recording are missing, yet a planner can still attempt a multi-step request. This capability would make partial completion honest and useful: the pendant hears what finished, the relay keeps the remainder alive, and the owner is not told a task succeeded when only a subset ran.
proposals.model_tier: Use faculty-perception plus deterministic health/permission checks for the preflight; use background gpt-4.1-mini only to summarize partial completion. Escalate to the expensive planner only when choosing among materially different fallback plans.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight under 300 ms from cached heartbeats, with a fresh probe only for stale surfaces. Start reachable work immediately; partial-result speech under 2 seconds after the first completed step. Offline remainder can continue as a durable relay job.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually zero model calls for health checks and routing; about $0.001–$0.01 equivalent for an occasional background partial-completion summary. Dominant cost is context transfer if a long multi-step plan is re-sent; use step IDs and compact state deltas.
proposals.security_concerns: The health snapshot must expose permission state and browser session identifiers only to the authenticated owner path. Never copy private page contents into the relay merely to decide availability. Do not attempt to repair macOS permissions or submit browser transactions automatically; report the missing capability and preserve the exact pending step for later.
missing: A typed, timestamped fleet-health contract covering Mac readiness, Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions, browser heartbeat/session reachability, relay reachability, and pendant link state
Planner support for dependency graphs with independently executable steps and explicit partial-success states
A durable pending-step queue that can resume when the browser extension reconnects without replaying completed mutations
Dashboard and pendant status language for completed / running / blocked / uncertain, with source timestamps
A routing policy that treats unavailable surfaces as plan inputs rather than generic action failures

proposals.user_asks: “Watch me do this once, then let me ask you to repeat the whole workflow for me later.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner could teach a genuinely personal workflow by performing it once—such as gathering information from several private browser tabs, transforming it on the Mac, and leaving a result somewhere—then invoke it from the pendant without rebuilding the instructions every time. Today the system can execute individual actions, but it cannot capture the owner's intent, variable fields, cross-surface dependencies, and stopping points as a reusable, reviewable routine.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic event capture and replay for known actions; use a background model to name steps, identify variables, and summarize changes. Use the expensive planner only when a replay encounters a changed UI or ambiguous intent.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture must be invisible during the demonstration apart from a pendant start/stop signal. A routine invocation should begin within 1 second; deterministic steps run at device speed, with model escalation only on drift. A changed step may take a few seconds to resolve.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero cost for capture, storage, and deterministic replay. Typical replays use no model calls; an ambiguous UI recovery costs one background call, with planner escalation rarely. Storage is compact event metadata plus optional redacted screenshots or DOM anchors.
proposals.security_concerns: Recording must be explicit and visibly bounded; never capture microphone audio, passwords, tokens, or unrelated windows. Private browser content stays on the Mac unless the owner explicitly includes it. Before saving, show the owner the workflow steps, data fields, destinations, and which actions are mutations. Replays need variable redaction, per-step provenance, and a hard stop when the observed page or target differs materially.
missing: An explicit pendant-controlled capture mode that records cross-surface action events without microphone access
A normalized workflow format with steps, variables, preconditions, outputs, checkpoints, idempotency, and sensitivity labels
Browser and Mac harness instrumentation that emits semantic events rather than only raw commands or screenshots
A local workflow compiler that turns a demonstration into an editable recipe and detects secrets before persistence
Durable versioning, dry-run/diff preview, pause/resume, and drift recovery for replayed workflows
A dashboard and pendant interaction for naming, editing, testing, and disabling learned routines

proposals.user_asks: “Do it, and if one of your connections or permissions is down, recover or use another part of the hive instead of leaving me with a dead end.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the Mac agent reports browser offline, Accessibility untrusted, and Screen Recording missing while still advertising broad capabilities; a request can therefore fail late or silently queue behind five stale browser commands. This capability would preflight the exact path, select a viable pendant/relay/Mac/browser route, retry transient failures as a durable job, and give one concise explanation plus a recovery option. It is materially more useful than merely exposing status because the owner does not need to diagnose which node is broken.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic health/precondition classifier and durable job runner first; background model for summarizing the failure and alternatives; realtime only to speak the short result over the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for local health checks and route selection; up to 2 s for one retry decision; long-running work becomes a durable job with pendant notification, so the owner is not held on the voice turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost when deterministic checks and typed actions suffice; roughly 1–3k background tokens only when explaining alternatives. Dominant cost is existing Mac/browser execution, not realtime inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Health data can reveal logged-in tabs, app names, permissions, and network state; keep raw diagnostics local and send the relay only typed capability state and redacted error summaries. Never silently substitute a public page for an authenticated one, and preserve the existing owner policy of no confirmation gates for ordinary actions; explicitly surface when a requested authenticated action cannot be completed.
missing: A single typed precondition schema shared by Mac, browser, relay, and pendant (online, permission, session, freshness, retryability).
A route planner that distinguishes transient transport failure from missing permission and chooses a safe fallback without claiming completion.
A durable retry/dead-letter worker tied to job receipts, with stale browser-command reconciliation and an owner-visible reason code.
Implementation of the granted read-only diagnostics tool; its current interface returns “no implementation yet,” so the health preflight cannot cheaply verify host facts.

proposals.user_asks: “When you say you did it, prove it—and if you can’t verify the result, tell me that instead of guessing.”
proposals.why_useful: Today Mac, browser, relay, and pendant actions can each produce local receipts, but the owner cannot reliably distinguish “command accepted” from “the world now matches what I asked.” This capability would define a completion test for each request, collect independent postconditions where possible, and speak a short evidence-backed result. For example, after changing a setting it would re-read the setting; after editing a browser form it would verify the DOM value and session state; after a cross-surface handoff it would verify the downstream receipt. It is a new trust guarantee, not merely another log or undo button.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic postcondition checks and receipt correlation do the core work; a cheaper background model normalizes evidence into a concise explanation; realtime only handles the immediate spoken response.
proposals.latency_budget: Add 100–500 ms for local verification on short actions. For browser or multi-step work, verification runs asynchronously and the pendant says it is checking, then delivers a durable result.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for typed postconditions and existing receipts; typically under 1k background tokens when evidence must be summarized. The dominant cost is any extra Mac/browser read, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private URLs, window titles, form values, or file paths. Keep raw evidence on the Mac/browser bridge, transmit only redacted claims and hashes to relay, and expose the source surface and timestamp in the dashboard. Never treat an executor acknowledgement as proof of a real-world mutation.
missing: A common completion-contract format with preconditions, postconditions, evidence source, freshness, and confidence.
Typed verification probes for Mac actions and browser actions, including safe readback after mutations.
A receipt state that distinguishes accepted, executed, verified, contradicted, and unverifiable, with contradiction recovery rather than silent success.
Pendant/dashboard rendering for a concise claim plus “why I believe this” evidence trail.

proposals.user_asks: “If my Mac is asleep or disconnected, remember exactly what I asked from the pendant and finish it when the Mac comes back—without making me repeat myself.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface continuously with the owner, while the Mac and browser are intermittent. Today a spoken request can end at a transient bridge or browser failure, and the owner has no durable, user-visible intent envelope preserving the exact request, constraints, and intended verification. This capability would capture the request locally/at the relay, acknowledge it immediately, bind it to the returning Mac/browser session, and resume only when the required surface is available. It preserves uncertainty and asks a focused follow-up if the request becomes stale instead of improvising.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime extracts a compact intent envelope during the voice turn; deterministic relay storage, wake/reconnect matching, and execution handle the rest; a cheaper background model resolves stale or ambiguous intents. No realtime model is needed while waiting.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 500 ms when offline; reconnect matching under 2 s; execution time is asynchronous and reported through the pendant/dashboard.
proposals.cost_estimate: Small durable relay storage and reconnect polling cost; usually no additional model call. Background resolution of stale intents is roughly 1–3k tokens only when needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Queued intents may contain private account or file details. Encrypt the envelope at rest, bind it to the paired pendant and Mac identity, expire it by owner-selected TTL, and avoid replaying authenticated browser mutations after session or page context changes. The owner must be told when execution is deferred and when context changed.
missing: A pendant/relay intent-envelope protocol with encrypted storage, TTL, constraints, and required-surface declarations.
A reconnect matcher that binds an intent to the correct Mac/browser session and rejects stale or changed authenticated contexts.
An offline-safe pendant acknowledgement and later completion notification path.
Dashboard controls to inspect, edit, cancel, or expire queued intents before reconnect execution.

proposals.user_asks: “Before you start, verify that the Mac and the browser session are actually reachable right now—and if one is stale, use the part that is available and tell me exactly what you could not verify.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can be told that the browser is online even while commands are timing out and five requests are pending. They cannot obtain a trustworthy, active end-to-end readiness answer before delegating work. This capability prevents wasted 45-second waits, makes failures intelligible, and lets the pendant distinguish a live Mac, a live browser poller, and merely cached status.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic health probes and signed challenge correlation do the normal work; use the background model only to turn the typed result into a concise explanation or choose an alternate route. Realtime is needed only when the owner asks verbally.
proposals.latency_budget: Active Mac challenge plus browser poll acknowledgment should complete in 2–5 seconds; if the browser does not answer within the lease window, return a definitive stale/unreachable result rather than waiting 45 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model/API cost for the probe. Dominant cost is engineering and a small amount of durable heartbeat/lease metadata; no browser-minute budget should be spent merely checking readiness.
proposals.security_concerns: Challenge tokens must be single-use, short-lived, and bound to the paired Mac/browser session; never include page contents, cookies, URLs, or command output. A stale result must be marked unknown, not healthy. The probe must be read-only and must not open tabs or alter the owner's session.
missing: A single end-to-end readiness protocol spanning relay, Mac agent, and browser extension
Active challenge/ack messages with monotonic timestamps and lease generations
Separate freshness fields for Mac process health, browser heartbeat, browser poll, and pending command age
A typed readiness result consumed by the planner before dispatch
Pendant/relay rendering for verified, degraded, and unknown states

proposals.user_asks: “Keep working on this across my Mac and logged-in browser even if I walk away or one device disconnects; resume from the last safe checkpoint and tell me exactly what finished, what failed, and what I should do next.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a pendant request can span relay, Mac shell, and private browser tabs, but a disconnect or partial failure leaves the owner reconstructing state. A durable cross-surface run would checkpoint each completed step with evidence, retry only idempotent work, reattach to the right browser session, and deliver a concise spoken completion/failure report when the pendant reconnects. This is more than a Mac job runner: it coordinates the wearable's conversational intent, the always-awake relay, the Mac's unrestricted execution, and browser-only authenticated reach.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the goal and speak the final status. Run planning, checkpoint reconciliation, extraction, and retry classification on a cheaper background model; use the expensive tier only when evidence conflicts or the recovery plan is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds, then execute asynchronously. Reconnect status should be available within 1–2 seconds; ordinary step retries should add under 5 seconds, with no need to keep the voice session open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per short run on a background model; dominant costs are authenticated browser calls and any generated audio, not Mac command execution. Realtime usage is limited to the initial and final utterances.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page text and Mac command output may leave the device through the relay; retain only bounded evidence snippets and hashes, redact secrets, and bind checkpoints to the owner/session. Never silently repeat non-idempotent browser submissions or destructive shell commands; mark them manual-stop even though the owner's current policy intentionally permits unrestricted execution.
missing: A single durable run/checkpoint schema spanning Mac jobs, browser command IDs, relay pipeline IDs, and pendant delivery receipts
Idempotency and retry classification for shell and browser steps, with explicit non-repeatable/manual-stop states
Reconnect delivery that summarizes evidence rather than replaying the whole transcript
A coordinator that can reattach an authenticated browser session after extension heartbeat recovery

proposals.user_asks: “Pause what I’m doing here and give me this exact work state back later, wherever I am.” The pendant should snapshot my active Mac window, browser tabs and selections, unsaved text, relevant terminal state, and the spoken reason; later I can say “resume the paused thread” and have the Mac and authenticated browser restore the right state before the pendant reminds me where I left off.
proposals.why_useful: This is not a scheduled briefing or a background job: it preserves the owner's partially completed, human-in-the-loop work when they have to leave suddenly. Today the system can observe apps and run individual actions, but it cannot create a coherent, resumable cognitive checkpoint across a GUI, terminal, private browser session, and the pendant's conversation. The owner would stop losing half-finished investigations and drafts.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to capture the pause/resume utterance and speak the short orientation. Use a cheaper background model to normalize window/tab metadata, summarize visible text and unsaved drafts, and rank which checkpoint is the requested thread. Use the vision model only for GUI state that accessibility metadata cannot represent.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 2 seconds; checkpoint creation in under 10 seconds for a typical 5–10 window session. Resume should restore the selected Mac/browser state within 5 seconds and speak a 15-second orientation, with deeper summarization deferred.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.02 per checkpoint, dominated by one or two screenshots/vision calls and summarization; metadata capture and local state hashing are effectively free. No audio generation is needed beyond the short spoken orientation.
proposals.security_concerns: The checkpoint may contain private browser URLs, authenticated page snippets, draft text, and terminal paths. Store encrypted, redact tokens/password fields, keep screenshots opt-in and short-lived, bind records to the owner's device identity, and provide deletion. Never submit a draft or alter a page while restoring; restore focus and scroll/selection only, and clearly say when exact restoration was impossible.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint object with title, owner-provided reason, app/window identities, browser session/tab IDs, selection/scroll anchors, terminal cwd and recent command metadata, evidence snippets, sensitivity labels, and expiry
Mac APIs to capture and restore window geometry, focus, selection, and unsaved text without relying solely on screenshots
Browser-extension commands for tab-group snapshot and restoration with authenticated session affinity
Pendant/relay commands to list, expire, and resume named checkpoints with a compact spoken orientation
A local-first encrypted store and conflict handling when the Mac or browser is offline

proposals.user_asks: “While I’m concentrating, decide which things are worth interrupting me for across my Mac and logged-in browser, and hold everything else until I’m free.” The pendant should let me change the mode with one button press or a short phrase, announce only genuinely urgent items, and give me a compact deferred queue when I switch modes.
proposals.why_useful: The current system can generate briefings and execute tasks, but it does not arbitrate attention in real time across local Mac notifications, browser events, relay jobs, and the owner's pendant state. The owner would get fewer disruptive alerts without missing a time-sensitive private-site change, failed long-running job, or direct human message. This requires the wearable's immediate presence, the Mac's foreground/app signals, the browser's authenticated reach, and the relay's always-on queue—not any one node alone.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic local rules for mode, quiet hours, deadlines, and known contacts; use a cheap background model to classify ambiguous events and deduplicate the deferred queue. Reserve realtime for the actual interruption and the owner's mode-change conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Event classification under 500 ms for local/browser events; urgent pendant notification under 2 seconds. Deferred digest can be generated asynchronously in under a minute when requested.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-matched events; roughly <$0.005 for an ambiguous batch classification. The main cost is not tokens but durable event retention and browser polling.
proposals.security_concerns: Notification titles and private-page snippets are sensitive. Classify locally where possible, send only minimal redacted event capsules to the relay, encrypt the queue, and let the owner define VIPs, deadline thresholds, and sites that may never be spoken aloud. Never infer urgency from message content without recording the source and confidence.
missing: A shared event envelope for Mac notifications, browser page-watch changes, relay job failures, and pendant state, with source, urgency, deadline, confidence, and sensitivity
A durable attention policy and deferred queue with deduplication, quiet modes, escalation, expiry, and spoken/non-spoken channel preferences
Mac notification observation and controlled notification-mode integration
Browser event forwarding from authenticated sessions without exposing full page contents
Pendant firmware support for a local mode toggle and queued-alert indicator that works during a dropped relay link

proposals.user_asks: “If something can’t run on my Mac, tell me exactly why, fix what can be fixed, and give me the best fallback instead of just failing.”
proposals.why_useful: The Mac currently reports ready:false (Accessibility and Screen Recording missing) and the browser bridge is offline with five pending commands. Today an action can spend ~45 seconds failing with only “extension offline.” A cross-node readiness-and-recovery turn would let the pendant ask in plain speech, the relay retain the request while the Mac is unavailable, the Mac run cheap health checks, open the exact System Settings pane or restart/re-poll the bridge when appropriate, then either retry idempotently or hand the work to shell/relay/public-web fallback. The owner gets a useful answer and a completion receipt rather than a dead end.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic checks and retry policy first; gpt-4.1-mini only to explain a multi-fault diagnosis or choose among safe fallbacks; reserve realtime for the spoken interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: Health check under 1 second; bridge re-poll/retry up to 10 seconds; permission repair is user-paced. Speak the diagnosis immediately, then deliver a later pendant receipt when queued work completes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually $0 model cost for /ops/status and typed checks; roughly $0.001–$0.01 only when a compact multi-fault explanation needs gpt-4.1-mini. Dominant cost is not tokens but waiting for the bridge or a queued Mac job.
proposals.security_concerns: Diagnostics may reveal app names, host state, and permission status; keep them local and send only a terse fault code to relay. Opening System Settings is reversible, but changing permissions remains the owner's action. Retry only actions marked idempotent and preserve the existing job receipts; never duplicate a submit/send step after an ambiguous timeout.
missing: A readiness contract that returns machine-readable blockers, capability-specific fallbacks, and an idempotency/retry classification
A bridge watchdog that converts offline/heartbeat state into a bounded re-poll or reconnect attempt
A durable cross-node retry envelope linking pendant request, relay job, Mac job, browser command, and final receipt
A dashboard panel showing blocker, attempted repair, fallback, and whether work is queued or abandoned

proposals.user_asks: “Put what I just said into the thing I’m looking at.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the pendant can hear an instruction and the Mac can type, while the browser can access authenticated tabs, but there is no trustworthy handoff of the immediately preceding spoken content to the currently focused Mac or browser field. This capability would make the pendant a hands-free keyboard: capture the utterance, resolve the active destination on the Mac, preview the exact text and target, then insert it into the focused app or authenticated tab and return a spoken receipt. It is especially useful for long addresses, notes, ticket updates, and form fields while the owner’s hands are occupied.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic active-window/tab and field metadata where possible; use gpt-4.1-mini only to normalize dictated text or resolve ambiguity. Realtime handles only the short capture and spoken confirmation; no planner-tier call for straightforward dictation.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 300 ms; destination lookup under 1 second; show/announce a preview before insertion; insertion and receipt under 2 seconds when the Mac/browser bridge is online. If disconnected, relay retains the utterance and resumes on heartbeat.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for transport, focus lookup, and typed insertion; about $0.0005–$0.003 for optional compact normalization. The dominant cost is speech transport/TTS, not reasoning.
proposals.security_concerns: The utterance may contain passwords, health data, or private work content. Encrypt the relay envelope, retain it only until delivery or explicit save, and never log raw text in general activity logs. Require an unmistakable preview/confirmation for sensitive-looking values or destinations such as payment, password, or message-send fields; insertion itself must never submit or send. Include app, tab URL, field label, and text hash in the local receipt, not the full secret.
missing: A focus-intent protocol that reports the active Mac app/window and, for browser tabs, the focused field label/DOM locator without exposing full page contents
A short-lived encrypted voice-to-text envelope linking one pendant utterance to one Mac/browser insertion, with replay protection and delivery acknowledgment
A typed insert_text_at_focus action implemented by the Mac agent and browser extension, distinct from submit/send
A privacy-preserving preview channel that lets the pendant speak the target and text summary before insertion
A lease/timeout policy so a queued utterance cannot be inserted after the owner has changed focus

proposals.user_asks: “Do that on my Mac, and if anything fails or the Mac disconnects, keep the work safe, resume from the last confirmed step, and tell me exactly what ran and what remains.”
proposals.why_useful: Today Mac shell is deliberately unrestricted and trusted, but its receipts are mostly per-job and undo covers only a few action types. A pendant request that crosses relay → Mac → authenticated browser needs one owner-readable proof packet: intended steps, exact commands/actions, stdout/stderr or typed results, timestamps, which steps are reversible, the last durable checkpoint, and a concrete recovery plan. This turns silent partial completion into a dependable handoff rather than making the owner repeat work or guess what happened.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short spoken status and decisions; use a cheaper background model on the relay to normalize receipts, detect a failed/ambiguous step, and draft a retry plan. The Mac planner/vision loop performs execution; the browser extension contributes tab-scoped evidence when a step touches logged-in pages.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 s from the relay. Each execution step remains bounded by its existing Mac timeout; reconnect reconciliation should complete within 5–10 s after the Mac heartbeat returns. No extra model call is needed for successful typed actions; background summarization can take 1–3 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per job in incremental model cost: most work is structured receipt aggregation and hashing; ~$0.01–$0.05 only when a failure needs background diagnosis. Storage is small JSON proof packets plus optional bounded stdout/stderr, with redaction before relay persistence.
proposals.security_concerns: Unrestricted shell remains the owner's deliberate policy; this does not add a gate or reduce capability. Proof packets must redact environment secrets, tokens, cookies, and likely personal data before leaving the Mac. Browser evidence must be tab/session scoped and never include raw credentials. Require explicit owner confirmation only where existing product policy already requires it; never claim a step succeeded without a typed result or captured exit status.
missing: A shared step/checkpoint schema spanning mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, mac_delegate, and relay jobs
Mac-side capture of exit code, stdout/stderr truncation, working directory, timeout, and action reversibility in every receipt
Idempotency and resume markers that distinguish completed, started-but-unknown, and not-started steps
Relay reconciliation on Mac reconnect plus a dashboard proof-packet view and concise pendant status messages
Secret/PII redaction and bounded retention for shell/browser evidence

proposals.user_asks: “Whenever you tell me something important, let me ask ‘show me why’ and take me straight to the exact source on my Mac or in the browser—without making me repeat the question.”
proposals.why_useful: Today evidence is fragmented: browser work can have tab context, Mac jobs have receipts, and spoken relay answers are not consistently linked back to either. The owner cannot reliably distinguish a remembered fact, a shell observation, a browser extraction, and a model inference—or jump from a pendant answer to the exact file, tab, command output, or timestamp that supports it. This would make the system trustworthy for consequential everyday decisions while preserving the fast spoken interface.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to answer the short follow-up and select an existing evidence reference. Build evidence links and source classification asynchronously with a cheaper background model or deterministic adapters; no expensive call is needed when the source is already typed.
proposals.latency_budget: Normal answers remain unchanged. “Show me why” should acknowledge in under 1 second, return a source summary within 2 seconds, and open the selected Mac file/window or browser tab within 3–5 seconds when the relevant surface is online.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low incremental model cost, generally under $0.01 per evidence lookup. Main costs are bounded local metadata indexing and small relay records, not inference. Store hashes/snippets and pointers rather than duplicating files or pages.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may expose private files, authenticated pages, commands, or personal data. Keep raw content on the Mac/browser where possible; send only a redacted excerpt, source type, timestamp, and opaque reference to the relay. Opening a private source should require the same existing owner control as the underlying Mac/browser action. Never expose shell environment values, cookies, access tokens, or full page contents merely because an answer cites them.
missing: A typed evidence-reference envelope emitted by every Mac, browser, memory, and relay answer
A provenance graph linking spoken claims to source spans, command/job IDs, tab IDs, timestamps, and confidence/inference status
Mac actions that can focus the exact source window/file and browser actions that can reattach to the cited tab
Pendant protocol support for a short source summary plus a follow-up reference token
Dashboard rendering that clearly separates observed evidence from model inference and stale memory

proposals.user_asks: “Before you start, tell me whether the Mac, browser, relay, and pendant can actually do this—and if one is unavailable, keep going with the best safe route and tell me exactly what I need to fix.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser read can sit for ~45 seconds and then fail because the extension is offline, while /ops/status already knew the browser was offline and Mac readiness was false. The owner should get immediate, actionable reachability rather than a mysterious timeout, and long work should be able to continue on another body when privacy and task requirements permit.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic local preflight for health, permissions, and route selection; background gpt-4.1-mini only to turn a typed failure into a concise spoken explanation; realtime only for the live interruption/answer.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 250ms to report readiness and choose a route; asynchronous repair hints and durable-job updates can arrive later. No planner-tier call for health checks.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for normal requests (local GETs and typed rules). A few cents or less only for unusual natural-language recovery explanations; the dominant saving is avoiding planner retries and 45-second doomed browser waits.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated tabs must never fall back to public browsing or relay fetches unless the task is explicitly public. Surface permission state and failure reasons without sending page contents. Opening System Settings is okay as a hint, but permission changes remain the owner's action under the existing maximum-access policy.
missing: A shared prerequisite/route registry mapping action types to /ops/status and /browser/status facts
Fast-fail dispatch before browser commands and retry-on-heartbeat-change
Pendant/relay notification for typed reachability failures and repair hints
The granted mac_read_diagnostics tool needs an implementation; current invocation returns 'no implementation yet'
The owner must bring home-chrome online and grant Accessibility/Screen Recording if GUI vision is desired

proposals.user_asks: “Show me exactly what happened across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser when my request went wrong—and tell me the one thing I should do next.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can see isolated job receipts and typed failures, but cannot reconstruct one causal timeline across the spoken request, relay delivery, model routing, Mac dispatch, browser heartbeat, and final outcome. When something fails or partially succeeds, they are left to infer whether the problem was the pendant, network, relay, Mac permissions, browser session, or the action itself. A single evidence-backed incident replay would make the system trustworthy and recoverable rather than merely capable.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event correlation and causal classification first; use background gpt-4.1-mini only to summarize the correlated incident in owner language. Reserve realtime for answering a spoken follow-up while the replay is already available.
proposals.latency_budget: Maintain an append-only event timeline during execution with sub-100ms local writes. Produce a normal replay in under 2 seconds; large incidents may be assembled asynchronously while the pendant gives a short preliminary status.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: correlation is local/relay work and does not require an LLM. A short background summary costs only a small fraction of planner-tier work; the main cost is bounded event storage and dashboard rendering.
proposals.security_concerns: Events must contain references, hashes, and redacted metadata rather than raw authenticated page contents, shell output, audio, or secrets. The owner should be able to delete an incident and its linked artifacts. Cross-device correlation IDs must not become a way for unrelated users or sessions to join histories.
missing: A single end-to-end correlation ID propagated from pendant speech through relay, routing, Mac jobs, browser commands, and receipts
Durable, ordered event envelopes with monotonic timestamps, source surface, parent event, redaction class, and retention policy
A causal correlator that distinguishes unavailable surface, transport loss, planner failure, executor failure, partial completion, and confirmed completion
Cross-surface incident replay in the dashboard and a compact spoken explanation/next-step response
A recovery link from each failure node to the exact retry, undo, or owner-side repair action that is valid for that state

proposals.user_asks: “If I tell you something while the network or Mac is unavailable, remember it on the pendant, acknowledge that it is safely queued, and carry it out or ask me about it when the connection returns—without losing or duplicating it.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner wears the pendant precisely when the rest of the system may be unreachable. Today a dropped relay, sleeping Mac, or offline browser can turn a spoken request into uncertainty: there is no durable local acknowledgment that the intent was captured, nor a guaranteed once-only handoff when connectivity returns. An offline intent mailbox would make the pendant dependable in the moments the owner relies on it most.
proposals.model_tier: Pendant stores and acknowledges a compact intent envelope without invoking a model. Relay performs deduplication and dispatch on reconnection; background gpt-4.1-mini interprets queued text only when needed. Realtime is used only for the initial spoken acknowledgment if the link is available.
proposals.latency_budget: Local capture and audible/LED acknowledgment under 300ms when disconnected. Reconciliation begins within one heartbeat after reconnect; the owner receives a queued, dispatched, or needs-review state rather than waiting synchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low: bounded flash writes and relay D1 metadata dominate; no LLM cost for simple captured utterances. Background interpretation is charged only for ambiguous queued intents.
proposals.security_concerns: The pendant must not retain raw audio longer than necessary; store encrypted text or a short content hash plus encrypted payload, with a visible retention limit and physical/button deletion. High-impact or privacy-sensitive actions remain pending for review rather than executing solely because connectivity returned. Sequence numbers and idempotency keys prevent duplicate reminders, messages, or browser submissions.
missing: A pendant-side encrypted intent queue that survives link loss and power cycling within available flash/RAM limits
A local acknowledgment state and retry/backoff protocol over the pendant link
Relay ingestion with device sequence numbers, idempotency keys, ordering, and explicit queued/dispatched/expired states
A reconnect reconciler that hands work to the Mac or authenticated browser only after current reachability is verified
A pendant/dashboard view for queued intents, expiration, deletion, and conflicts when the owner later gives a revised instruction

proposals.user_asks: “Keep an eye on my Mac and browser bridge. If a job is stuck or the bridge goes offline, tell me on the pendant, retry safe work when it comes back, and give me one concise recovery report.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the Mac reports browser offline with five pending commands, computer-use disabled, and missing Accessibility/Screen Recording while jobs continue to accumulate failures; the owner otherwise discovers this only after asking. An always-awake relay can detect the outage, preserve intent, retry only idempotent/read jobs, and deliver a short spoken explanation instead of silently losing work.
proposals.model_tier: background for periodic health classification and retry decisions; deterministic rules for heartbeat, idempotency, backoff, and receipt aggregation; realtime only to announce an urgent outage or answer a status question
proposals.latency_budget: Health checks every 1–5 minutes; outage detection under one interval, pendant alert under 2 seconds once detected; recovery report within 10 seconds of bridge heartbeat. No planner call for ordinary healthy checks.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero when healthy (HTTP checks and D1 state). Occasional gpt-4.1-mini call, roughly 2–4k input tokens, only to compress several failures into a spoken report; dominant cost is the rare recovery summary, not monitoring.
proposals.security_concerns: Health metadata, job labels, and failure text leave the Mac for relay state; command payloads and page contents must not. Retry allowlist must be idempotent/read-only (status, list tabs, snapshot, read page); never retry typing, sending, deleting, purchasing, or shell mutations. Preserve the owner's existing maximum-access/no-gate policy, but make the retry classification auditable and expose exact receipts.
missing: A durable bridge-health monitor and lease/heartbeat state in the relay
A retry queue that understands idempotency keys, exponential backoff, tab/session affinity, and safe-vs-never-auto-retry action types
A pendant notification/audio event for bridge outage and recovery (not just a response to a spoken request)
A compact cross-surface recovery receipt correlating relay alert, Mac job, browser command, and final result
A way to distinguish temporary missing permissions/offline extension from a permanently unsupported action and suppress repeated alerts

proposals.user_asks: “When I’m away from my Mac, let me tap the pendant to queue a task with a short voice note; when I get back, have the relay and Mac resume it from the right project and tell me exactly what completed, without making me repeat myself.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac/browser connection turns an in-progress request into a conversational dead end: the owner must remember what they asked, repeat it, and reconstruct context. A wearable tap plus relay persistence can capture intent at the moment it matters, while the Mac later supplies files, apps, and authenticated sessions. This is a true handoff between the body, always-on service, and private machine rather than a Mac-only task runner.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief voice note and immediate acknowledgement; deterministic relay storage, deduplication, and delivery; background gpt-4.1-mini to normalize the note and select the active project when the Mac reconnects; planner tier only if the resumed task is genuinely ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 500 ms using a local canned response; relay persistence under 1 second; resume within 15 seconds of Mac reconnection; completion spoken or queued for playback within 5 seconds after the Mac returns a receipt.
proposals.cost_estimate: Tiny for short notes: roughly 300–800 input tokens to normalize only when needed, plus a few hundred tokens for a completion summary. Most handoffs use deterministic storage and existing Mac execution, so the dominant cost is ambiguity escalation.
proposals.security_concerns: Voice notes and task metadata are stored in relay D1 and may contain private intent; encrypt or minimize them and expire unclaimed handoffs. Never transmit authenticated page contents, arbitrary shell output, or secrets to the relay. Bind delivery to the paired pendant and Mac identity, preserve project/session provenance, and require the existing owner policy before any destructive or external side effect.
missing: A pendant-side offline capture and acknowledgement mode that survives a dropped relay link
A durable relay handoff record containing audio/text note, capture time, pairing identity, intended surface, project hint, and lifecycle state
A reconnect protocol that lets the Mac claim handoffs exactly once and report progress/receipt updates
A context reattachment operation that resolves the handoff to the Mac's active project, session, and relevant recent thread without resending the entire conversation
A pendant playback queue for completion receipts when the owner is no longer in a live voice session

proposals.user_asks: “Read this private log or folder and tell me what matters, but do not send the raw contents off my Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a terminal agent can read local material, but the owner cannot reliably ask for a useful cross-device answer while guaranteeing that raw secrets, source code, credentials, or personal documents stay local. This would make the Mac a privacy boundary: the owner gets a concise answer and evidence without exporting the underlying data to the relay or model.
proposals.model_tier: Use a small local deterministic redaction/classification pass first; use a local Mac model for summarization when available, and only send a typed, lossy finding or approved snippets to the slower background model/relay. Realtime is only needed to speak the final short answer through the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: 2–10 seconds for ordinary logs, with immediate progress on the pendant; large folders may run as a background job and notify when the local digest is ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero relay/model cost when local summarization succeeds; otherwise a small request containing only the redacted digest. Dominant cost is local CPU and optional local-model memory, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: The local pass must detect and suppress credentials, tokens, private keys, health/financial identifiers, and configured path classes before any network call. Keep raw input and intermediate parses on disk only under short retention, show the owner exactly what categories and snippets would leave the Mac, and make network export opt-in per request. A failed classifier must fail closed for export, while still allowing a fully local answer.
missing: A local privacy-boundary pipeline that can parse files/logs and produce typed findings without sending raw content
A local summarizer or constrained on-device model on the Mac
Redaction scanners for secrets and owner-configured sensitive paths
A typed relay payload that accepts only findings/citations rather than arbitrary terminal output
A pendant response that states “kept local” and identifies the local evidence used

proposals.user_asks: “If one of my devices is unavailable, keep the request alive and finish it through the best available path—and tell me plainly what is waiting, what already happened, and what could not be done.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the relay is reachable but the Mac reports ready=false (Accessibility and Screen Recording missing), the computer-use loop is disabled, and the browser extension is offline with five queued commands. A pendant request can therefore look accepted while silently having no executor. This capability turns outages and permission loss into an explicit, recoverable handoff: the relay records a goal and an execution lease, the Mac/browser advertise health, and the system either reroutes a safe read to another surface or resumes exactly once when the missing surface returns. The owner gets a short spoken/LED status rather than a false success, and a final receipt that separates completed, skipped, and pending steps.
surfaces: pendant: button starts/ends the request and plays a terse state update; LED distinguishes queued, executing, waiting-for-Mac, and failed
relay-realtime: persists the intent, leases steps, applies expiry and idempotency, and emits a spoken update without keeping the expensive realtime model busy
mac-planner: publishes /ops/status readiness and executes Mac-native fallback steps when permissions and app access are available
browser-extension: heartbeats and claims only commands for its bound tab/session; reconnect replays pending work without duplicating a completed step
relay/background worker: wakes on heartbeat/job timeout and performs retry/reroute bookkeeping; dashboard/iOS shows the same state and receipts
proposals.model_tier: Use realtime only for the initial conversational acknowledgment and urgent spoken status. Use a cheaper background model for step decomposition, capability-health matching, fallback selection, and final reconciliation; deterministic code handles leases, idempotency, retries, and receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge from the pendant in under 1 second. Health/routing decision in under 2 seconds when a node is online. A disconnected node may wait until its next heartbeat; surface a 30-second stale warning and an owner-configurable expiry rather than polling expensively.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.01 per request beyond the normal voice turn, dominated by one small background planning/reconciliation call; heartbeat, lease, retry, and receipt work is database/Worker compute. Avoid sending full page or Mac context on every status update.
proposals.security_concerns: Health metadata must not include page contents, credentials, or shell output. Bind browser work to an extension/session/tab identity and Mac work to the paired host. Persist only the goal, step hashes, surface, timestamps, and typed result summaries. Never retry a non-idempotent browser submission or shell mutation automatically; preserve the existing before/after receipt and checkpoint semantics. Tell the owner when a fallback changes what was actually done.
missing: A shared capability-health schema with freshness and surface-specific failure reasons
A durable step lease/idempotency record spanning relay, Mac bridge, and browser bridge
Heartbeat-triggered resume and timeout worker; current browser has pending commands but no demonstrated end-to-end claim/resume contract
Pendant status vocabulary for queued/waiting/rerouted/completed states
A compact cross-surface receipt that can be rendered as speech, LED patterns, and dashboard history

proposals.user_asks: “Remember this exactly where I found it, and let me ask about it later from the pendant even if that tab or my Mac is closed.”
proposals.why_useful: A useful fact often exists only in a private Safari tab or a local Mac file, then disappears when the tab closes. This would create a small, provenance-preserving capsule rather than dumping an entire page into long-term memory: the browser supplies the authenticated URL/tab and selected text or DOM citation, the Mac supplies local-file provenance when relevant, the relay stores an encrypted, expiring snapshot plus a compact semantic index, and the pendant can retrieve it by voice. Later answers can quote the captured evidence and say when it was captured, instead of pretending that a stale memory is current.
surfaces: pendant: voice command “remember this” and later spoken retrieval; button controls capture timing so no microphone is left open
browser-extension: captures only the user-selected text/region, URL, title, tab/session identity, and a DOM locator/source hash; does not scrape unrelated tabs
mac-planner/mac-terminal: captures a selected local artifact or command result with path, modification time, content hash, and a redacted excerpt when the source is on the Mac
relay: encrypts and stores the capsule with owner-defined TTL, sensitivity label, and source provenance; retrieves only matching capsules for a later question
dashboard/iOS: shows capsule list, source link, expiry, evidence excerpt, and delete/export controls
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short capture acknowledgment or spoken lookup. A cheaper background model generates a compact title, entities, and retrieval keywords; deterministic code preserves the exact excerpt/hash and enforces TTL. Use no model for a direct exact-quote lookup.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 1 second; persist the capsule in under 3 seconds. Exact retrieval under 1 second; semantic retrieval under 3 seconds. Never block the owner on summarizing a large source—store first and summarize asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per capture for optional compacting, plus small D1/R2 storage; exact lookup costs no model call. The dominant cost is embedding/semantic indexing if enabled, so cap excerpt size and index only owner-selected content.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and local files are highly sensitive. Require an explicit user gesture/phrase for capture, never capture whole tabs by default, encrypt at rest, keep raw content local when the owner chooses, redact credentials/financial identifiers before indexing, and give every capsule a visible source, TTL, and delete action. A later answer must distinguish captured evidence from current web state and offer a fresh browser check rather than silently using stale text.
missing: A first-class capsule schema (source surface, citation, exact excerpt/hash, sensitivity, TTL, and capture consent)
A browser command for selected-region capture and a Mac command for selected-file/command-result capture
Relay encryption/key handling and retrieval endpoint separate from general context graph memory
Pendant capture/retrieval intent and a compact spoken provenance format
Dashboard/iOS capsule management and retention controls

proposals.user_asks: “Only show private Mac and logged-in-browser results when I’m actually wearing the pendant; if I take it off, pause the sensitive work and continue when I put it back on.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the Mac, browser, and relay can continue acting while the owner is away, but none of them has reliable proof that the intended person is physically present. This would let the owner walk away from a shared room without leaving private notifications, authenticated-page excerpts, or draft contents exposed, while preserving useful continuity: non-sensitive background work may finish, sensitive results remain sealed, and the pendant announces the exact point at which work resumes.
surfaces: pendant: periodic authenticated presence beacon, local wear/presence sensor, and a short button gesture to re-authorize; LED indicates present, paused-sensitive, or expired authorization
mac-planner: receives the signed presence state, suppresses private onscreen/audio presentation when absent, and checkpoints work without discarding results
browser-extension: keeps authenticated tabs bound to the paired presence epoch and withholds page text, screenshots, and form previews after the epoch expires
relay: stores encrypted pending results, rotates short-lived presence leases, and sends only coarse state transitions to the pendant; it may continue explicitly non-sensitive background jobs
dashboard/iOS: shows the last presence epoch, paused jobs, and a deliberate resume control without exposing the sealed payload on an untrusted surface
proposals.model_tier: No realtime model is needed for presence enforcement. Deterministic firmware/relay cryptography handles leases and state; a cheap background model classifies a job's output sensitivity at planning time, with owner-configurable overrides. Realtime is used only if the owner asks for a spoken explanation while present.
proposals.latency_budget: Presence loss recognized within 2–5 seconds, with no model round trip. Re-authorization and release of sealed results under 1 second after a valid button gesture. Background jobs continue without waiting for model responses.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per-event API cost; cryptographic lease checks and D1 writes dominate. Optional sensitivity classification costs roughly $0.001–$0.01 per job, cached for the job lifetime.
proposals.security_concerns: Presence must be cryptographically bound to the paired pendant, not inferred from an easily spoofed MAC-visible Bluetooth name. Do not transmit raw audio, page content, or credentials in the beacon. Use short-lived rotating tokens, replay protection, and a fail-closed policy for sensitive presentation. The owner must be able to revoke a lost pendant from the dashboard. Clearly distinguish ‘paused because absent’ from ‘failed’; never delete sealed results automatically without the configured retention policy.
missing: A real pendant presence/wear signal or secure proximity channel; the current single-button/LED prototype has no presence sensor
Firmware support for rotating signed presence leases and replay counters within the device's constrained RAM/flash budget
A relay-side encrypted sealed-result store and presence-epoch API
A Mac/browser presentation broker that classifies and withholds sensitive output without terminating resumable work
An owner-facing sensitivity policy and lost-pendant revocation flow

proposals.user_asks: “For that request I made earlier, show me the complete chain of what happened, what is still queued, what failed, which device did each step, and roughly how much model time it cost.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner gets separate Mac jobs, routing receipts, and browser queue state, but no single trustworthy, human-readable explanation joining them. This would make cross-device behavior understandable after delays, dropped connections, partial completion, or duplicate attempts—without requiring the owner to inspect technical logs.
proposals.model_tier: background for assembling and summarizing existing structured records; deterministic joins and totals first, with a small model only for concise spoken wording. Realtime is unnecessary unless the owner asks during a live conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a recent request from retained records; under 5 seconds if browser reconnect reconciliation is needed. The pendant can say 'I am checking the Mac and browser trace' while the background job assembles it.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost when records are structured; roughly 1–3k input tokens and a short completion only when summarization is needed. Dominant cost is not inference but retaining and joining bounded trace metadata.
proposals.security_concerns: The report may reveal private URLs, shell commands, file paths, account names, and model prompts. Store raw spans locally with short retention, redact secrets and sensitive arguments, expose opaque IDs and summaries by default, and require owner-authenticated access for detailed views. Never include bearer tokens or full private page contents in relay speech.
missing: A shared request-lineage ID propagated from relay routing into Mac jobs, shell actions, and browser commands
A bounded redacted trace store that survives the current 120-job eviction window through aggregate summaries
Browser reconnect reconciliation that records whether pending commands eventually completed, failed, or remain indeterminate
A join endpoint or dashboard view combining routing, journal, job receipts, and browser queue state

proposals.user_asks: “After anything gets interrupted, tell me what is definitely complete, what is only partly done, and what cannot be verified—and offer the next safest way to reconcile it without blindly repeating the action.”
proposals.why_useful: A dropped Mac connection, browser disconnect, timeout, or process crash currently leaves the owner to guess whether a command ran before the failure. This capability distinguishes completed, failed, and indeterminate effects, then proposes inspection or continuation rather than silently replaying potentially permanent work.
proposals.model_tier: Background/deterministic for effect-state calculation from receipts, exit codes, checkpoints, browser acknowledgements, and reconnect state; use the planner tier only to explain ambiguous cases or formulate a recovery plan. Realtime is only needed to read the short result aloud.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial interruption classification under 2 seconds from local records; reconciliation under 10 seconds when it needs a live Mac or browser check. The owner should get an immediate compact uncertainty report, followed by an update if a device reconnects.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic classification; roughly 1–3k model input tokens only for an ambiguous multi-step recovery explanation. Most cost is local state tracking, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Recovery inspection can expose private files, authenticated pages, and command arguments. Keep evidence local by default, redact secrets, require explicit owner choice before any compensating mutation, and make the spoken summary disclose uncertainty rather than claiming success.
missing: Per-step effect checkpoints with an explicit unknown/indeterminate state rather than only job success or failure
Command- and browser-operation effect probes that can verify postconditions without replaying the original action
A recovery-plan record that separates read-only reconciliation from compensating mutations and records the chosen outcome
Cross-device acknowledgement and reconnect handling so a late browser result or Mac receipt can close an uncertain step

proposals.user_asks: If something I asked you to do fails while I'm away, figure out why, try the safest equivalent route on the Mac or in my logged-in browser, and tell me only what worked and what still needs me.
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed shell/browser step becomes a vague failed job: /ops/snapshot shows 14 failed actions and 112 actions without tier attribution, while five browser commands remain pending and the extension is offline. A wearable request should survive transient bridge/browser outages and executor-specific failures rather than making the owner repeat the whole task. This is genuinely hive-only: the relay retains the job, the Mac has local alternatives, the browser owns authenticated sessions, and the pendant delivers a concise outcome.
proposals.model_tier: background for failure classification and recovery planning; deterministic rules first, planner-tier escalation only when the error or fallback is ambiguous; realtime only to acknowledge receipt on the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; classify within 2 seconds; retry deterministic/transient failures within 10 seconds; background recovery can run for minutes while the owner is away; never block a later independent job.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually zero model calls for exit-code/timeout/bridge-offline signatures. Roughly 2k–5k input tokens to gpt-4.1-mini for an ambiguous failure, with planner escalation only for multi-surface recovery; dominant cost is retained error/output context, not transport.
proposals.security_concerns: Shell remains unrestricted per owner policy and no new gate is proposed. Store only bounded, redacted stderr/stdout and typed error metadata; never send environment variables, cookies, page bodies, or secrets to the relay/model. Browser retries must preserve tab/session affinity and stop before irreversible submission. Show the exact fallback and changed inputs in the receipt; require owner confirmation only where the existing action semantics already require it.
missing: A durable cross-surface recovery state machine with attempt lineage, failure taxonomy, bounded redacted diagnostics, and retry budgets
A capability map describing equivalent Mac, browser, and relay executors plus idempotency/undo semantics
A background worker that can wake when the Mac bridge or browser extension reconnects and resume pending attempts
A single receipt schema joining pendant request, relay job, Mac job/action receipt, browser command, and final evidence
A small dashboard/pendant summary for recovered, waiting, and permanently failed work

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me which parts of my AI assistant were slow or unreliable today, what they cost, and automatically improve the routing for tomorrow without changing what actions it is allowed to take.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can see individual job receipts, but cannot get a trustworthy cross-surface reliability/cost diagnosis. The live data already shows a serious blind spot—112 of 120 jobs lack tier attribution—and repeated browser failures consume about 45 seconds each. A daily report would turn invisible waste into concrete improvements while preserving the owner's maximum-access policy.
proposals.model_tier: background for aggregation and anomaly explanation; deterministic code for latency, failure, tier-attribution, and retry statistics; planner only if the owner asks for a natural-language investigation
proposals.latency_budget: Daily report under 10 seconds from cached journal data; interactive drill-down under 3 seconds. No low-latency voice model needed unless the owner asks verbally.
