proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for the normal report because metrics and thresholds are deterministic; approximately 2k–4k input tokens to background model only when generating a concise explanation. Dominant cost is local aggregation, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep command text, URLs, tab titles, and receipt evidence on the Mac by default; send the relay only aggregate counts, durations, failure classes, and model-token totals. Require explicit owner confirmation before applying any routing-policy change, and retain the previous policy for rollback.
missing: A durable normalized event schema joining job receipts, journal entries, routing receipts, and browser heartbeat periods by request/job/action ID
A cost attribution fallback for jobs currently marked unattributed, with an explicit unknown bucket rather than fabricated prices
A deterministic policy simulator that can compare routing changes against the last 7 days before activation
A dashboard/pendant report and rollbackable routing-policy store

proposals.user_asks: “When something fails, tell me in one sentence what stopped it, show me the evidence if I ask, and tell me the fastest safe way to continue—without making me repeat the whole request.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently gets surface-specific errors such as “browser extension offline,” but not a causal explanation spanning relay, planner, Mac permissions, queue state, and browser heartbeat, nor a resumable continuation. This would convert a failed request into an actionable handoff instead of a dead end.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic causal-chain assembly and recovery classification first; background model for a short spoken explanation; planner only for genuinely ambiguous fallback choices.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for the first spoken diagnosis using existing receipts and status caches; evidence drill-down under 5 seconds. Resume should reuse the existing job/request ID rather than re-plan from scratch.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually no model call for diagnosis; under 1k background-model tokens for phrasing. Main cost is a durable causal event index and status sampling.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private URLs, text, or application names. Keep detailed capsules on the Mac and expose redacted summaries to the relay/pendant by default. Never infer that a failed write had no effect unless its receipt proves that; distinguish unknown outcome from confirmed no-op.
missing: A durable causal chain linking request, routing decision, job, action receipt, browser heartbeat, permission snapshot, and terminal outcome
A resumable checkpoint format that records completed actions and explicitly excludes uncertain writes
A fallback registry describing alternatives by required surface and privacy boundary
A redaction layer for spoken relay summaries and owner-requested evidence

proposals.user_asks: “Did that actually happen?” — give me one trustworthy answer about a multi-step task, including what the Mac did, what Safari changed, whether the relay delivered it, and what remains uncertain after an interruption.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can get separate job receipts, browser results, and relay status, but cannot obtain a single causal account when a task crosses surfaces or the connection drops. This would prevent duplicate actions and false confidence: the pendant could say “the form was filled but not submitted,” “the Mac command exited successfully but the browser confirmation never arrived,” or “the result is unknown; here is the exact safe point to inspect.” It is an evidence-and-uncertainty capability, not another action history.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event correlation first; use the cheaper background model to summarize conflicting evidence, escalating to the planner only when evidence is incomplete or contradictory. Realtime is used only to answer the owner's spoken question.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a status assembled from existing receipts; under 10 seconds when reconciling several event streams or generating an uncertainty explanation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost for correlation; roughly one background call for ambiguous cases, with planner escalation uncommon. Storage is a compact event graph and hashes rather than full duplicated payloads.
proposals.security_concerns: The graph may link sensitive browser URLs, shell commands, and form values. Keep raw values local to the owning surface, send relay only redacted event claims and stable IDs, encrypt the cross-surface graph, and clearly label unknown versus verified facts. Never infer successful submission from a mere click or network dispatch.
missing: A shared cross-surface task/run identifier propagated through Mac jobs, browser commands, relay delivery, and pendant acknowledgement
An append-only event envelope with timestamps, causal parent IDs, idempotency keys, outcome confidence, and redacted evidence references
A reconciler that detects contradictory or missing terminal events and produces explicit unknown states
A pendant/dashboard presentation for a causal timeline and a recommended inspection or resume point

proposals.user_asks: “That failed—figure out what went wrong, pick up from the last successful step, and finish it.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed Mac/browser job leaves the owner to reconstruct the error and repeat earlier work. This would turn a failure into a recoverable conversation: the pendant gives a concise diagnosis, the relay assembles evidence, and the system resumes only the unfinished portion while preserving the owner’s authenticated browser state.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/exit-code analysis first and a cheaper background model for diagnosis and continuation planning; use realtime only to explain the result or answer the owner’s follow-up. Escalate to the expensive model only when the failure is ambiguous or the next step has meaningful semantic alternatives.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken failure summary in under 2 seconds from stored receipts; continuation planning in 5–15 seconds; execution proceeds asynchronously with a pendant notification when complete. Do not block on an expensive model for obvious timeout, missing-path, or stale-tab failures.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental API cost because exit metadata, receipts, browser command results, and workspace facts are already structured. Ambiguous recovery costs one background planning call, roughly a few cents or less; storage is bounded failure artifacts and checkpoints.
proposals.security_concerns: Recovery evidence may contain private shell output, local paths, or authenticated page text. Keep raw artifacts local/encrypted with short retention, redact tokens and cookies, and send the relay only structured error summaries by default. Never silently substitute a different recipient, destination, payment, or submitted browser form; semantic changes must be surfaced as a new plan for owner review. Exact retries of the original trusted action remain available under the owner’s maximum-access policy.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint graph that relates Mac action IDs, browser command IDs, and their dependency edges rather than only a flat job list
A bounded local artifact store with redaction and TTL, plus a relay endpoint that can fetch selected evidence on demand
A recovery planner contract that distinguishes exact retry, deterministic repair, and semantically different alternatives
A continuation executor that resumes from the last successful node and reports any changed preconditions without replaying completed work

proposals.user_asks: “Pack up what you’re doing so I can close the lid, then continue it later exactly where you left off.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a task’s state is scattered across Mac processes, browser tabs, shell cwd, temporary files, and relay job records. The owner cannot intentionally pause a real workflow and later resume it as a coherent unit. A portable task capsule would preserve the useful state and make interruption—sleep, reboot, lost network, or switching machines—ordinary rather than destructive.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic serializer and integrity checker for the capsule. Use a slower background model only to summarize human intent and identify which external state must be revalidated; realtime is only for the spoken pause/resume interaction.
proposals.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement and capsule manifest in under 2 seconds; capture local/browser state asynchronously in under 30 seconds for ordinary jobs. Resume should validate dependencies first and then start within 5 seconds, with the owner notified if anything drifted.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal API cost for manifests and hashes; occasional background summarization is a few cents or less. Storage depends on selected artifacts, with a default small manifest and explicit opt-in for large files or screenshots.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules can contain private paths, shell output, authenticated-tab identifiers, and pending form data. Encrypt them, bind browser references to the owner’s device/session, expire abandoned capsules, and never export cookies or credentials. On resume, revalidate external state; do not assume a saved form or page is unchanged. Any irreversible action remains a newly presented step, not a replayed side effect.
missing: A versioned capsule format spanning Mac action receipts, shell cwd/environment fingerprints, browser tab/session affinity, pending checkpoints, and relay job IDs
A local encrypted capsule store with resumable upload and conflict handling after reboot or device change
A pause protocol that drains in-flight actions and records a consistent cut between completed and pending steps
A resume validator that checks repository hashes, app availability, browser tab identity, network assumptions, and expiry before continuation
Pendant and dashboard controls for naming, listing, expiring, and resuming capsules

proposals.user_asks: “The thing I asked you to do on my Mac failed—figure out why, try the safest repair, and tell me exactly what you changed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed shell or browser job leaves the owner to diagnose it manually, and the model often repeats the same discovery. This gives the pendant a useful failure-recovery loop: identify the exact failed step, use evidence from the Mac receipt, retry with a cheaper known alternative, and report whether anything changed. It is explicitly more than Mac-only because the pendant is the low-friction trigger, relay preserves the job after the owner walks away, browser sessions can be the failing dependency, and the Mac is the only node able to inspect or repair local state.
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model for receipt parsing, error categorization, and selecting a previously successful repair recipe; realtime only for the short spoken acknowledgement and final concise explanation. Escalate to the expensive tier only when evidence is contradictory or the repair plan is novel.
proposals.latency_budget: A receipt-based diagnosis in under 2 seconds after the owner asks; one unattended retry/repair within 30 seconds; long repairs become a durable relay job with progress and a final pendant notification. Never loop indefinitely: max 2 attempts per step and stop on unchanged error.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.003–$0.02 per ordinary incident, dominated by model calls only when the local error classifier cannot match a cached recipe; shell/browser execution is local. A successful cached diagnosis should require no expensive model call.
proposals.security_concerns: The Mac remains maximum-access and unattended per owner policy; this is not a new gate. Repair recipes must record exact commands/actions, exit code, cwd, timestamps, and before/after observations, while redacting tokens, environment secrets, and page contents. Do not silently retry irreversible commands; mark them non-retriable and explain why. Browser repairs must preserve authenticated-session boundaries and never send a form as part of diagnosis.
missing: A durable failure record linking each failed step to its parent job and surface
A local error taxonomy plus a small, signed recipe cache of known reversible repairs and pre/post checks
An executor mode that can run a bounded repair plan, capture structured stdout/stderr/exit code/duration, and emit a final receipt
Relay notification/event handling for completion after the pendant disconnects
Cross-surface correlation between browser command failures and the Mac job that depended on them

proposals.user_asks: “While you’re working on my Mac, let me know from the pendant—without opening a conversation—when it finishes, gets stuck, or needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: A durable Mac job is invisible once the owner walks away. The owner should be able to keep cooking, commuting, or working and recognize completion or a blocked step from a private LED/haptic pattern, then press once to hear a concise result. This is not another spoken briefing or job-status query: it is a low-attention, physical interrupt that only exists because the Mac executor, always-awake relay, and worn pendant are coordinated.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive realtime inference for routine state changes. Mac emits typed progress events; relay applies a deterministic state-to-signal map. Use a cheap background model only to turn the final receipt or blocker into a one-sentence spoken summary when the owner presses the button.
proposals.latency_budget: Signal completion or blocker within 1 second of the Mac event reaching the relay. Button press should produce the spoken summary within 2 seconds; stale/offline events are queued and coalesced rather than replaying every intermediate step.
proposals.cost_estimate: Essentially $0 model cost for progress and LED/haptic signals; approximately $0.001–$0.005 for an optional final summary, dominated by text generation. Negligible relay storage for the latest state and one compact receipt pointer per job.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not encode sensitive task names, page titles, command text, or account data in LED/haptic patterns; signals should reveal only state class (working, done, blocked, failed). Relay notifications must be authenticated and bound to the owner’s pendant. Quiet hours and a local mute button are needed, and a blocked browser task must not expose private page content until the owner requests audio.
missing: A pendant firmware notification primitive supporting a small set of distinct LED/haptic patterns, queue/coalescing, mute, and acknowledgement
A relay event subscription from Mac/browser jobs with authenticated owner-device binding and latest-state persistence
A normalized job lifecycle event schema with working, waiting, completed, failed, and needs-owner states
A button-triggered lookup that retrieves the associated redacted receipt and speaks a short explanation
Dashboard controls for signal preferences, quiet hours, and per-job notification policy

proposals.user_asks: “Keep this terminal task alive while I leave, and when I come back let me continue it from exactly where it stopped—without starting over.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a long shell task is tied to a request/HTTP lifetime and can disappear behind a timeout or bridge disconnect. The owner cannot reliably leave a build, export, backup, or research command running, return later through the pendant, inspect only the unseen output, and resume after a Mac or agent restart. This would make the pendant a dependable remote terminal companion rather than a one-shot command launcher.
proposals.model_tier: background for status, deterministic for cursor/lease bookkeeping, planner only when the owner asks to interpret a failure or choose a continuation command; realtime is used only to speak the concise status through the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge launch or reconnect in under 500 ms; status and unseen-output retrieval in under 2 seconds. Interpretation or continuation planning may take 2–5 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for launch/status/reconnect because these are deterministic. Occasional background/planner call costs roughly one short request only when interpreting output or constructing a continuation; local spool and relay metadata dominate storage, not API spend.
proposals.security_concerns: A detached process can continue using CPU, files, credentials, or network after the owner leaves. Require explicit long-running intent, a maximum lifetime and disk quota, visible lease status, and pendant cancellation; do not auto-retry. Keep raw output on the Mac with TTL deletion and send only redacted tails/summaries to relay. Restrict status access to the paired owner.
missing: A Mac process supervisor that owns process groups independently of HTTP requests
Durable lease, output-cursor, and bounded spool records surviving bridge/agent restart
Reconnect/unseen-output and explicit process-group-cancel operations
Pendant/relay protocol for long-running job status and cancellation
Dashboard UI for active leases, age, resource use, and last output cursor
built_from: existing action receipts exposed through GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts

proposals.user_asks: When something I asked takes multiple steps, show me one trustworthy timeline of what the pendant heard, what the relay decided, what the Mac or browser actually did, and what remains undone — with a one-tap way to retry only the failed step.
proposals.why_useful: Today job receipts exist on the Mac, but the owner must reconstruct a multi-surface action from separate job records, browser command IDs, and audio/voice events. A cited timeline would make unattended work understandable and safely recoverable without repeating successful or irreversible steps.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to acknowledge the pendant request and speak a short status; use a cheaper background model (or deterministic reducer) to merge event records, classify the next retry, and generate the dashboard timeline.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 second; append each event within 2 seconds; background reconciliation under 10 seconds after a job completes. Retry should be explicit and only dispatch a selected failed action.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per job with deterministic event reduction; <$0.03 when a background model must summarize ambiguous failures. Storage is small JSON events plus existing receipts; dominant cost is any model-generated explanation, not transport.
proposals.security_concerns: The timeline may contain private URLs, shell commands, file paths, and authenticated-page snippets. Keep raw evidence on the Mac/relay, send the pendant only a redacted status, encrypt and TTL event bundles, and require confirmation before replaying any action marked irreversible. Never infer success from a model summary when a receipt or browser result is absent.
missing: A shared event envelope with correlationId, parent step, source surface, monotonic timestamp, redacted payload, and receipt/command/job references.
Relay-side append-only event journal and reducer that joins POST /pipeline/events, Mac job receipts, and browser results.
A retry endpoint that accepts a specific failed step and idempotency key, rather than rerunning the whole plan.
Dashboard timeline and pendant status summaries with explicit unknown/stale states.

proposals.user_asks: While I’m focused, quietly decide whether a new Mac or browser notification is worth interrupting me: use what app or page it came from, my current calendar context, and urgency; tell me immediately on the pendant only when it truly matters, and leave everything else in a review queue.
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has to notice and triage interruptions themselves. A Mac-only notifier cannot know the owner’s wearable availability or relay context, while the pendant cannot see desktop notifications or authenticated browser state. Combining all surfaces provides attention protection rather than another generic briefing.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic rules for meeting/focus state, sender/domain, and notification metadata. Use the cheaper background tier to rank ambiguous items; reserve realtime for the short pendant alert after a high-confidence urgent result.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture and classify within 2 seconds of a notification; pendant alert within 3 seconds for urgent items. Queue low-confidence items without interrupting. Dashboard review can update within 30 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for common rule matches; roughly $0.005–$0.02 per ambiguous notification using a small background call. Main costs are a Mac notification observer and compact encrypted event storage.
proposals.security_concerns: Notification text and authenticated page titles may contain private work or health information. Keep raw payloads on the Mac, transmit only a minimized classification and short redacted explanation to the relay/pendant, encrypt the queue, support per-app exclusions and quiet hours, and expire raw evidence quickly. Never open a browser page or send a response as a side effect.
missing: A Mac notification observer that emits normalized events without stealing keyboard focus or recording screen/audio.
A shared focus/availability state combining calendar, active app/window, pendant connection, and explicit do-not-disturb commands.
A privacy-preserving urgency classifier with per-source policies, deduplication, and feedback (“important”/“not important”).
A relay push route to the pendant plus a durable review queue and dashboard controls for exclusions, retention, and correction.
A browser-extension event bridge for meaningful authenticated-site alerts that do not appear as native Mac notifications.

proposals.user_asks: “Continue the thing that failed when my browser was offline.”
proposals.why_useful: Today relay_job_status can report a failure but cannot turn a transient offline-browser failure into a resumed task. This lets the owner recover hands-free after reopening the browser, without repeating the whole instruction or guessing which step is safe to retry.
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model for job classification and resume planning; realtime only for the short spoken acknowledgement and final result.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; health check under 2 seconds; execution continues asynchronously and speaks only on completion or a non-recoverable diagnosis.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap classification call plus local/relay calls; no vision or realtime model unless the failed step specifically needs computer-use.
proposals.security_concerns: Resume only the failed idempotent action using its stored idempotency key and prior receipt; never replay completed writes. Keep page text and shell arguments out of the spoken acknowledgement unless needed.
missing: A resumable-job endpoint that accepts a job id or natural-language reference and starts from the failed action boundary
Preflight/failure classification and bounded retry described in the proposed Mac harness change
Browser heartbeat/online transition wake-up that releases queued resumptions

proposals.user_asks: “Why did that take so long, and what exactly happened on my Mac?”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently get a trustworthy end-to-end explanation of a task: model planning, relay transit, Mac execution, and browser availability are recorded in separate places, and most actions have no model-tier attribution. This gives a concise spoken postmortem with a linked, inspectable timeline rather than another generic failure message.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic aggregation first; use a cheap background model only to turn the structured timeline into a short explanation. Realtime is reserved for the spoken follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for the structured status and under 5 seconds for the optional spoken summary; no re-execution of the task.
proposals.cost_estimate: Normally no model call; otherwise one small background completion over redacted events. Storage is a few KB per job for correlation metadata.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep shell arguments, tokens, page contents, and prompt text out of the owner-facing summary by default. Show app/domain names and failure classes, with a dashboard drill-down requiring local authentication. Preserve unknown attribution instead of guessing.
missing: A single immutable correlation ID propagated from pendant request through relay, planner, Mac job, browser command, and action receipts
A read-only timeline joiner that combines /routing, /journal/:jobId, job receipts, and browser heartbeat state
A redaction-and-explanation formatter exposed to the pendant and dashboard
Backfill or explicit unknown markers for the 112 currently unattributed actions

proposals.user_asks: “Make the Mac ready so you can use my browser and see the screen.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner receives opaque failures when Accessibility, Screen Recording, or the browser bridge is unavailable. They cannot ask the pendant to diagnose the complete readiness chain, open the right Mac settings, wake the bridge, verify each prerequisite, and tell them exactly what remains.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic health checks and typed Mac actions; background model only for interpreting an unfamiliar permission dialog. No realtime planning is needed beyond the spoken acknowledgement.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial diagnosis under 2 seconds; opening settings and bridge recovery within 10 seconds; wait for owner-granted permissions and recheck automatically when they return.
proposals.cost_estimate: Mostly local checks and typed actions, with negligible model cost. A small persistent readiness record avoids repeating checks on every request.
proposals.security_concerns: The system may open settings but must not claim permissions were granted until the OS and extension report them. Never transmit screen pixels merely to diagnose readiness. Require explicit local OS consent where macOS requires it.
missing: A readiness state machine spanning Accessibility, Screen Recording, browser-extension heartbeat, and vision-loop availability
Typed deep links/open-and-verify actions for the relevant macOS Privacy & Security panes
A browser-extension wake/reconnect handshake and owner-facing pending-permission state
Pendant notification when readiness changes from blocked to usable

proposals.user_asks: When I ask you to do something in Safari, start immediately; if the browser bridge is offline, tell me right away and continue automatically when it reconnects, then give me one completion or failure report instead of making me ask again.
proposals.why_useful: Today an offline bridge can waste roughly 45 seconds per browser action and leave several duplicate pending commands. This turns a transient laptop/browser state into a transparent background job: the owner gets an immediate explanation, no duplicate retries, and a single spoken result when Safari returns.
proposals.model_tier: background for queue monitoring, deterministic health/receipt handling, planner only for interpreting the original goal and final summary
proposals.latency_budget: Return an offline status within 1–2 seconds by reading bridge health; resume within one heartbeat (target 5–10 seconds) after reconnect; final summary under 3 seconds after actions complete.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for health checks, queueing, and receipts; one background-model call only for a final natural-language summary when needed. Avoids repeated planner calls from timeout/retry loops.
proposals.security_concerns: The queued browser goal and tab/session identifiers remain in the local job store; authenticated page contents stay in the browser bridge and should not be copied into relay notifications. Spoken offline notices must contain only status, not private page data. Preserve existing action receipts and irreversible-action behavior; reconnect must not duplicate an action ID.
missing: A browser-command state machine with offline_pending and resume-on-heartbeat states, keyed by idempotency/action IDs
A fast local browser-health preflight that returns the existing offline reason instead of waiting for command timeout
A reconnect worker that re-polls pending commands and resumes only incomplete actions
Relay/pendant event projection for immediate offline and final completion notices, with deduplication by job ID

proposals.user_asks: When you run something on my Mac and it fails, diagnose it locally, try a safe alternative way to accomplish the same goal, and tell me exactly what worked, what did not, and what changed—without making me repeat the request.
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed shell, AppleScript, app, or browser handoff is usually just a dead-end receipt. The owner has to understand Mac-specific errors and restate the task. A local recovery loop would turn transient app state, wrong working directories, missing utilities, and stale browser connectivity into completed work or a precise explanation.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic classification and local diagnostics first; use the background tier for ordinary error interpretation and retry selection; escalate to the planner only when the goal has multiple viable recovery paths. Realtime is used only to tell the owner the concise outcome.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture failure context in under 1 second; choose a deterministic retry in under 3 seconds; allow up to 2 alternative attempts for ordinary tasks, with progress returned to the pendant. Do not silently loop.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually no extra model call for known exit codes, missing paths, offline bridge, or permission errors. One background call for an unfamiliar failure; planner cost only for ambiguous multi-step recovery. Local diagnostic output is the dominant storage cost, not API cost.
proposals.security_concerns: The recovery executor retains the owner's deliberate unrestricted shell policy and adds no approval gate. Diagnostic bundles must redact environment secrets, authorization headers, cookies, and full file contents; cap stdout/stderr and never send raw shell output to relay by default. Retries must preserve the original job/action identity and label every mutation, especially when an alternative command could have different side effects. Ask for confirmation only if the original task itself required it; recovery must not invent a broader goal.
missing: A typed failure taxonomy spanning shell exit/timeout, app automation errors, browser bridge state, and Mac permission state
A bounded recovery planner that maps each failure class to alternate commands or surfaces and records why each was attempted
A local diagnostic bundle attached to the job receipt (argv/command fingerprint, cwd, exit code, duration, relevant status probes, redacted stderr)
A retry ledger with attempt IDs, effect summaries, and a final owner-readable explanation surfaced through relay_job_status and pendant events

proposals.user_asks: Take the file I mention on my Mac, verify that it is the right version, upload it to the matching form in my logged-in browser, and show me the exact file, destination, and fields before anything is submitted.
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently bridge a local artifact and an authenticated web workflow as one coherent task: finding the correct file, validating it, selecting the right private tab, and presenting a trustworthy pre-submit preview are split across surfaces. This removes a tedious, error-prone handoff while still stopping before the irreversible submit.
proposals.model_tier: Background tier for file inventory, metadata/hash comparison, and deterministic tab/form matching; planner only when the requested file or destination is ambiguous; realtime only for concise status and the review prompt.
proposals.latency_budget: Find and validate a candidate within 3 seconds for a named path; identify the matching logged-in tab within 5 seconds; produce a review package within 10 seconds. No upload or submit should happen after the review package until the owner explicitly approves.
proposals.cost_estimate: No model call for exact paths, hashes, MIME/size, and typed browser metadata. One background call for semantic matching of filenames to fields; planner only for ambiguity. Browser screenshot/DOM extraction and local hashing dominate latency, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Local files can contain sensitive data, and authenticated pages can contain private account information. Keep the file on the Mac until the browser upload is approved; send only metadata and a redacted field preview to relay. Bind the review to file hash, tab/session ID, URL, and form-field locators so a changed file or navigated tab invalidates it. Never submit automatically.
missing: A local artifact manifest/read-and-hash operation exposed to the planner without returning file contents by default
A browser upload action that accepts a local artifact handle, reports selected filename/hash and target field, and supports a staged-not-submitted state
A cross-surface review capsule joining file hash, destination URL/tab, field values, and screenshot/DOM evidence
An approval-bound commit that revalidates the file and tab immediately before upload/submit

proposals.user_asks: “If something can’t run right now, don’t leave me waiting—tell me what is unavailable, use the best safe fallback, and keep the original task ready to resume when the device comes back.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can spend 45 seconds waiting on an offline browser bridge, while the Mac snapshot simultaneously reports missing Accessibility/Screen Recording and a disabled vision loop. The owner should receive an immediate, truthful answer instead of a timeout, and public work should continue through the relay/web tools while private work is held for the authenticated browser. This only works across the pendant, always-on relay, Mac observability, and browser session lease—not on one node alone.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic health/preflight and fallback routing first; background model only to summarize a degraded result or explain a recovery plan; realtime model only for the spoken interruption.
proposals.latency_budget: Health check and route decision under 500 ms; fail-fast private-browser requests in under 2 s rather than the current ~45 s poll timeout. Resume automatically on the next heartbeat, without replaying non-idempotent steps.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually zero model calls for health, classification, quarantine, and retry. At most one small background summarization call for a fallback result; realtime speech cost is only the brief status sentence.
proposals.security_concerns: Private authenticated content must never fall back to public web search or leave the Mac. Each task must declare public/private data class, permitted surfaces, and idempotency. Keep existing owner policy of no approval gates; instead attach receipts showing why a fallback or defer occurred and require explicit confirmation only where an existing action already requires it.
missing: A shared capability preflight contract reporting online state, permissions, lease age, queue depth, and supported fallbacks per surface
A durable degraded-task record with original intent, completed steps, quarantined steps, retry policy, and idempotency key
A relay-to-Mac/browser health event stream and resume trigger; current polling only discovers failure after a long wait
A router rule that maps public reads to web_search/read_web_page while preserving authenticated tasks for browser reattachment
A single owner-facing status/receipt view and spoken status event for degraded, deferred, resumed, and permanently failed work

proposals.user_asks: “If I lose connection while you’re doing something, pick up the same conversation where we left off—without making me repeat myself or doing an action twice.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable conversation can drop while the Mac or browser is still working, leaving the owner unsure whether an instruction was heard, completed, or partially applied. Today durable jobs and receipts exist, but they are not a conversational resume protocol: a reconnecting pendant cannot reliably recover the exact turn, pending question, spoken response, and action frontier as one coherent interaction.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic session checkpointing, action idempotency, and receipt reconciliation; use the realtime model only to continue a live spoken turn, and a cheaper background model to summarize completed work after a long disconnect.
proposals.latency_budget: On reconnect, restore the last checkpoint and status in under 1 second; do not replay an action until its prior execution is reconciled. If reconciliation is unavailable, speak a concise “still checking” response and continue in the background.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for checkpoints, hashes, and receipt reconciliation. One short background summary only when the disconnected task completed or needs clarification. Storage is a small append-only record per active conversation.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only encrypted task state and references, not raw microphone audio or secret page contents. Bind checkpoints to the paired pendant and Mac/relay session. Use exactly-once/idempotency keys for mutations, and expose an audit trail when a step is resumed, skipped, or reconciled.
missing: A durable conversation checkpoint schema containing turn id, spoken-response state, task graph frontier, pending clarification, and last acknowledged receipt
A shared exactly-once action ledger spanning relay, Mac jobs, and browser commands
A reconnect handshake that exchanges checkpoint versions and reconciles divergent outcomes before continuing speech
Pendant-side playback/acknowledgement markers so the owner does not hear a response twice
A user-facing recovery state for ambiguous outcomes such as Mac completed but relay never received the receipt

proposals.user_asks: "Keep my browser tasks reliable: if Safari disconnects, stop retrying blindly, tell me once what is waiting, resume when it reconnects, and never alert me about the same page change twice."
proposals.why_useful: The live Mac snapshot shows the browser bridge offline with 5 pending commands; the journal contains repeated identical Order 42 change reports, and /ops data shows browser_list_tabs ran 37 times with 7 failures. Today the owner can receive duplicate alerts or wait through doomed retries without knowing the real state. A cross-surface liveness lease, durable queue, and semantic notification dedupe turns a flaky bridge into dependable background work.
proposals.model_tier: background for liveness classification, retry scheduling, and semantic fingerprint comparison; deterministic for queue state, lease expiry, and exact duplicate suppression; realtime only to speak one concise outage/resumption notice on the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Bridge heartbeat evaluation under 2 seconds; reconnect drain begins within 5 seconds of a healthy heartbeat. One outage notice immediately and one recovery summary after reconnect; no per-retry model call.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero when healthy (deterministic heartbeats and hashes). Roughly 1 cheap background call per genuinely changed watch batch, not per poll; realtime cost only if the owner is actively listening for the spoken notice.
proposals.security_concerns: Queue metadata must retain only session/tab identifiers and encrypted private results, never expose page contents in relay logs. Reconnect must revalidate the browser session binding before replaying any action. Reads may resume automatically; queued writes need the existing action receipt/undo semantics and should remain explicitly marked in the spoken/dashboard summary. No URL or excerpt should be spoken unless the owner asks.
missing: A durable per-session browser connection lease with monotonic heartbeat and explicit offline/online transitions
A queue state machine that coalesces superseded reads, applies bounded exponential backoff, and resumes idempotently after reconnect
A semantic watch fingerprint store keyed by watch id and source revision, so identical changes produce one report and later retries reference the original report
A notification acknowledgement/recovery record shared by relay and dashboard
A health-triggered command-drain worker; current /browser/poll and /browser/result/:commandId are transport endpoints, not a durable scheduler

proposals.user_asks: "When you change something for me, don't just say the command ran—check that the intended result is actually true, keep watching it briefly, and tell me if it failed or was undone."
proposals.why_useful: Today a Mac receipt can report that an action completed, but completion is not the same as the owner's desired state: a setting may be overwritten by another process, a file may be rejected by a sync service, or a browser form may display a stale success page. The owner needs outcome verification rather than execution theater, especially when they are away from the Mac and only have the pendant to hear the result.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic checks first (exit status, file hash, app state, browser DOM value, receipt evidence). Use the cheaper background model to select or interpret a verification probe when the request is ambiguous. Use realtime only for a concise success/failure report while the owner is engaged; do not spend the realtime tier on polling.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial verification within 2 seconds of a local action when possible; delayed checks at 10 seconds and 2 minutes for state likely to converge. Report provisional completion immediately only when labeled provisional, then replace it with a verified result.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal for typed checks and hashes. One background-model call only when deriving a probe from a natural-language goal. Browser and Mac polling add small local/relay traffic but no recurring planner calls.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must not broaden access beyond the original task: do not inspect unrelated files, tabs, or account data. Store hashes and typed state where possible rather than raw private content. A failed verification must never silently trigger a compensating mutation; the owner should be told what was observed and what, if anything, is proposed next.
missing: A goal-level contract separating intended outcome from the action steps that attempt it
A typed postcondition probe registry for Mac files/settings/apps, browser DOM values, and relay/persistent state
Delayed verification timers tied to the original job with cancellation and expiry
Evidence linking that records observed-after state and confidence, not merely action receipts
A unified result vocabulary such as verified, provisionally-complete, contradicted, or unverifiable across pendant speech and dashboard

proposals.user_asks: When the pendant notices a crash or I say “file this bug,” collect the relevant UART/device log, reproduce context, and leave a ready-to-review issue draft on my Mac with a short spoken summary—never submit it automatically.
proposals.why_useful: The owner's stated idea is a pendant that files its own bug reports. The pendant is the only node that can capture the immediate button/audio/device context; the Mac is the only node that can inspect the local repo and logs; the relay can preserve the report if the Mac disconnects; and the browser can optionally populate the authenticated issue tracker without sending. This turns an intermittent wearable failure into an actionable, sourced report instead of a vague memory.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic parsers and a cheap background model for log clustering and reproduction-summary prose; use realtime only for the immediate spoken acknowledgement. Escalate to the planner only when stack traces, repo state, and user narrative conflict.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 300 ms and local ring-buffer snapshot immediately; relay receipt under 2 s; Mac collection and draft in 10–30 s. If the browser is offline, leave the draft locally and resume tracker population later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per report: most work is local parsing and background summarization; planner escalation and optional issue-tracker extraction dominate. Storage is a small compressed log bundle plus metadata per incident.
proposals.security_concerns: UART logs may include tokens, Wi-Fi identifiers, transcripts, or private paths. Redact secrets and audio by default, hash/label sensitive fields, and show the exact bundle and issue body before any browser submission. Browser login/session data stays in the extension; the relay stores encrypted metadata and expires raw logs. Automatic filing should be limited to local draft creation, never send/publish.
missing: A firmware ring buffer and crash marker that survives a dropped link and exports a bounded incident bundle
A relay incident-ingest endpoint with encrypted, expiring attachments and deduplication by device/firmware/time
A Mac log collector that correlates UART, local-agent job receipts, /journal/:jobId, git branch/commit, and machine health into one evidence capsule
A redaction and stack-trace clustering worker plus a draft writer that targets Markdown and optionally a browser issue form
Browser-side preview/fill integration that can populate but not submit an issue, with resume after extension heartbeat
built_from: POST /capture and GET /capture for a local incident pointer
POST /pipeline/events and POST /pipeline/audio for the pendant's event/audio context
POST /jobs and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for action evidence
GET /journal/:jobId and GET /routing for execution trace and model attribution
GET /machine-context and GET /ops/snapshot for host/permission/relay state
POST /browser/sessions and POST /browser/result/:commandId for optional authenticated tracker drafting
Existing dashboard/job receipts and /jobs/:jobId/cancel for review and control

proposals.user_asks: When I double-press the pendant while I’m listening, bookmark the exact moment and later give me a searchable note with the surrounding transcript, audio clip, and any related Mac or browser context.
proposals.why_useful: People often hear an idea, instruction, or important detail while away from the keyboard and lose it before they can write it down. The pendant can mark the moment with no microphone session needing to stay open, the relay can preserve the audio event through a dropped Mac connection, and the Mac/browser can add nearby document, tab, or task context when available. The result is a precise, replayable memory rather than a vague dictated note.
proposals.model_tier: Use firmware and deterministic event capture for the bookmark; use a cheap background model for transcription, timestamp alignment, and context matching. Reserve realtime for an optional immediate acknowledgement, not processing.
proposals.latency_budget: Local bookmark acknowledgement under 200 ms; durable relay receipt under 2 s; searchable transcript and context enrichment within 30 s. If the Mac or browser is unavailable, preserve the clip and enrich it later.
proposals.cost_estimate: A few cents or less per bookmark, dominated by transcription; deterministic capture and metadata are negligible. Storage is a bounded clip plus transcript and context pointers, with configurable expiration.
proposals.security_concerns: The clip may contain private speech or third-party voices. Make capture explicit through the double-press, show an LED/haptic confirmation, encrypt in transit and at rest, redact likely secrets before indexing, and provide per-bookmark delete/export. Browser context must remain metadata-only unless the owner has an authenticated session; never silently capture continuous audio.
missing: A firmware bookmark event with a precise monotonic timestamp and a bounded pre/post audio ring-buffer export
Relay storage and APIs for encrypted clip fragments, transcript alignment, retention, and later enrichment
Mac-side correlation of bookmark time with active application/document/window and local job history
Browser-side read-only context snapshot tied to the bookmark without requiring a new navigation
A dashboard/search view that joins audio, transcript, source context, and deletion controls
built_from: POST /pipeline/events and POST /pipeline/audio for timestamped pendant events and audio
POST /capture and GET /capture for durable bookmark metadata
GET /ops/snapshot for device and relay availability
GET /jobs and GET /journal for nearby Mac activity
Existing browser session/status and result routes for optional authenticated context
Existing dashboard and durable audio capabilities for review and playback

proposals.user_asks: When I ask you to do something involving my browser, just proceed: use the fastest available route, automatically fall back for public pages when Safari is offline, queue private-page work until the bridge returns, and tell me on the pendant exactly what ran, what was deferred, and why.
proposals.why_useful: Today a dead extension can burn 45 seconds per navigation and produce repeated opaque failures. This would make the hive resilient: public work still completes through the relay, private work is preserved rather than retried blindly, and the owner gets a concise spoken status instead of discovering failure later.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic health/preflight and routing first; background model for summarizing deferred/completed work; realtime only for the immediate spoken acknowledgement.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second for health classification and pendant acknowledgement; public fallback should begin within 3 seconds; private work waits for a heartbeat or configurable deadline without repeated 45-second attempts.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible for health checks and routing; roughly 1 background-model call per multi-step task (about 2k–4k prompt tokens) only when a human summary is needed. Avoids the current repeated planner calls and browser timeout waste.
proposals.security_concerns: Never send authenticated/private URLs, DOM, or cookies to the public fallback. Classify a task before routing; private sessions remain on the local bridge. Persist only task metadata and failure reason. Any eventual browser mutation keeps the existing owner policy and receipts; this proposal adds no blocking gate.
missing: A single availability classifier with freshness TTL for Mac bridge, browser extension, and relay browser backends
A resumable task state machine that distinguishes public fallback-safe steps from private steps and records the exact deferred checkpoint
A circuit breaker/backoff keyed by extension/session so an offline bridge cannot consume repeated 45-second attempts
A pendant/relay notification path for completion, deferral, and recovery events

proposals.user_asks: When several background tasks finish or fail while I am away, give me one interruption at the right moment that bundles only the decisions I need, lets me ask for any receipt, and otherwise leaves everything quietly queued.
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface can create its own job, failure, audio, or browser update, but there is no shared attention budget. The owner should not receive five separate pendant alerts for one stalled workflow, nor miss a meaningful failure because it was buried in Mac logs.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event aggregation, deduplication, urgency scoring, and quiet-hours handling; background model only to compress a multi-job digest; realtime only when the owner opens the interruption.
proposals.latency_budget: Aggregate events within 1 second; deliver immediately only for configured urgent failures, otherwise wait for the next attention window or explicit pendant request. Digest generation under 3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for aggregation; approximately one background call per digest, typically 1k–3k prompt tokens. No planner call for ordinary receipts.
proposals.security_concerns: Digest content must inherit each artifact's residency label and avoid putting private page text into relay notifications or durable audio unless permitted. Never infer urgency from sensitive content without a local policy decision. The owner can inspect the underlying receipt before any follow-up action.
missing: A shared attention ledger with deduplication keys, urgency, quiet hours, and delivery state
Cross-surface event emission from Mac jobs, browser commands, relay jobs, and audio completion
A pendant acknowledgement/query protocol that marks a digest read without losing individual receipts
Owner-configurable urgency rules and escalation limits
built_from: durable audio and pendant notification capabilities

proposals.user_asks: “Keep my browser work reliable: if Safari or the bridge drops, preserve my queued requests, tell me what is stuck, and when it comes back reconcile each request and continue only the safe ones.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can receive repeated 45-second browser failures and stale commands can remain processing with empty parameters and eight attempts, while seven requests remain pending. No single Mac, browser, pendant, or relay node can both preserve authenticated browser intent, detect bridge recovery, explain what happened on the wearable, and safely resume across the outage. This gives the owner continuity rather than silent loss or blind replay.
proposals.model_tier: background for heartbeat classification, queue reconciliation, and recovery summaries; deterministic state transitions and idempotency checks do the normal work; realtime only speaks an immediate short alert when the owner is actively waiting.
proposals.latency_budget: Heartbeat detection within 15–30 seconds; immediate outage notice within one polling interval; recovery reconciliation under 2 seconds per queued item before producing a concise pendant summary. Do not wait 45 seconds for each known-offline request.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost because health checks, leases, retries, and idempotency are deterministic; occasional gpt-4.1-mini summary at roughly 1–3k prompt tokens per outage, plus a few D1 writes. This saves repeated planner/browser timeout calls.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated URLs, tab/session IDs, and action payloads must remain on the Mac or encrypted relay store; pendant notifications contain only sanitized status and request labels. Never replay non-idempotent browser actions solely because a heartbeat returns: reattach and verify tab/session state, require an existing idempotency key, and classify unsafe or ambiguous items as skipped with an explanation. This is recovery and observability, not a new approval gate or restriction on the owner's unrestricted Mac shell.
missing: Relay durable queue-health state machine with lease expiry, dead-letter records, and recovery events
Mac read adapter exposing normalized browser queue item age, attempts, status, idempotency key, and session affinity
Browser extension handshake that acknowledges command completion or explicit cancellation and reports tab identity/version
Cross-surface notification event from relay to pendant with a compact recovery receipt

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving my Mac. Package up exactly where I am across my open tabs and apps, and when I’m back, bring me back to the right place and remind me what I was doing.”
proposals.why_useful: Today work is fragmented across Safari/Chrome tabs, Mac applications, and the pendant conversation. The owner should be able to leave without manually reconstructing their state: the system would preserve the active work thread, distinguish intentional context from unrelated tabs, and restore it later with a short spoken orientation. This depends on the pendant’s physical presence, the Mac’s application state, the browser’s private sessions, and the relay’s durable memory together.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic local capture and matching for app/tab titles, URLs, window geometry, selected project, and job checkpoints. Use the background tier to produce a compact orientation and only escalate to the realtime tier when the owner asks for spoken clarification during return. No planner call is needed for ordinary capture/restore.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture in under 2 seconds when the owner presses the pendant button; restore the Mac workspace in under 5 seconds after return. Spoken orientation should begin within 1 second of the pendant reconnecting.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per handoff: mostly local metadata and relay storage. One background summarization call only when the workspace contains enough changed material to require a narrative; raw page contents remain local unless explicitly requested.
proposals.security_concerns: Browser URLs, window titles, and app state can reveal sensitive work. Encrypt the handoff capsule, bind it to the paired pendant and Mac, allow per-app exclusions, and default to storing metadata rather than page contents. Never transmit cookies, form values, or screenshots to the relay without explicit request. Restoration must not submit forms or send messages.
missing: A durable cross-surface handoff capsule schema with app/tab/job provenance and owner-selected sensitivity rules
Mac APIs to capture and restore window/application state without losing existing sessions
Browser extension support for tab-group capture and reattachment to the same authenticated session
Pendant reconnect/button event delivered to the relay with a stable handoff identifier
A return-flow UI and spoken summary that can resolve stale or missing tabs instead of silently opening substitutes
built_from: Existing browser command queue and session-affinity work
Existing relay persistent agent state and pendant pipeline telemetry

proposals.user_asks: “Give me a focused 25-minute block. Keep my Mac and browser quiet, but let through anything genuinely urgent, and tell me when the block is over.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has separate distraction tools and browser sessions, but no single intent spanning Mac notifications, authenticated browser tabs, relay routines, and the physical pendant. A pendant-triggered focus block would turn a spoken or button request into a coordinated, reversible state: suppress noise everywhere, continue monitoring only narrowly defined urgent signals, and provide a physical end-of-block cue without requiring the owner to keep checking the screen.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic state machine for start, timer, suppression, restore, and end notification. Background model classifies candidate events against the owner's configured urgency rules. Realtime is used only if the owner asks a follow-up while the block is active.
proposals.latency_budget: Start suppression within 2 seconds of the button or spoken command. Restore within 2 seconds of expiry or cancellation. Urgent-event classification should be asynchronous and should not delay the focus state.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for the timer and local notification controls. Background classification is occasional and can be batched; no planner call for ordinary start/stop. Relay storage is one small focus-session record.
proposals.security_concerns: Notification contents and private browser activity are sensitive. Keep raw content on the Mac/browser; send the relay only urgency category, timestamp, and session ID. Require explicit per-source configuration, never auto-read arbitrary pages, and make restoration idempotent so a dropped connection cannot leave notifications suppressed indefinitely. The owner must always be able to cancel with a pendant press.
missing: A cross-surface focus-session protocol with expiry, cancellation, lease renewal, and crash-safe restoration
Mac notification and Do Not Disturb integration exposed as reversible typed actions
Browser extension hooks to pause non-urgent page watches and queue low-priority commands
A local urgency classifier with owner-editable source and keyword rules
Pendant firmware support for distinct start/cancel/expired haptic or LED patterns
Relay watchdog that restores or expires sessions when the Mac or pendant disconnects

Existing relay persistent agent state and pendant pipeline telemetry

proposals.user_asks: When something I asked you to do on my Mac or in Safari fails, recover it automatically when it is safe, switch to the other available surface when possible, and tell me exactly what happened without making me repeat the request.
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser extension outage or blocked Safari dialog can consume repeated 45-second attempts, while the owner has to diagnose the failure and restate the task. This would make the pendant, relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge behave like one resilient system: preserve the goal, avoid duplicate side effects, and return either a completed result or a precise recovery step.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic/background routing for health checks, failure classification, receipt lookup, and safe retries; invoke the planner only for ambiguous recovery or cross-surface replanning. Realtime is used only to report progress or ask a necessary clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Health checks and known-failure diagnosis under 1 second; avoid repeating a known 45-second timeout. Permit one bounded retry for explicitly idempotent actions, then report the result promptly.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low incremental API cost: most recovery turns are deterministic and reuse existing receipts. Occasional planner escalation costs roughly one normal planner request; storage and health polling are the dominant non-model costs.
proposals.security_concerns: Retries must be limited to actions whose receipts prove no effect or that are explicitly idempotent; never blindly repeat a mutation. Keep browser URLs and shell diagnostics authenticated, redact cookies, environment variables, command secrets, and page contents from recovery summaries, and preserve an auditable link between original and retried jobs.
missing: A shared failure fingerprint schema covering offline surfaces, blocked dialogs, timeouts, invalid targets, and transport errors
A live cross-surface health registry that the executor can consult without planner involvement
Recovery receipts linking original job, health snapshot, retry decision, alternate surface, and final outcome
An idempotency/retry-safety declaration on every action type
A goal-preserving recovery coordinator that can choose Mac, browser bridge, or relay fallback without duplicating writes

proposals.user_asks: If my Mac or Safari is unavailable when I ask, remember the exact task on the pendant, tell me it is queued, and resume it automatically when the right surface comes back—without me asking again.
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac link or offline browser bridge turns an otherwise valid request into a failed interaction and loses momentum. The owner should be able to speak once while walking away, receive a truthful queued receipt, and later get the completed result or a precise question only if the task cannot safely resume.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background/deterministic worker to persist, health-check, and resume a structured task. Use the planner only when the resumed environment differs materially or the original goal is ambiguous. Use realtime only for the immediate queued acknowledgement and completion announcement.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement within 2 seconds, with no need for the Mac to be online. Health checks can be minutes apart or event-driven; resume within one polling interval after the required surface returns.
proposals.cost_estimate: Small durable-queue and health-check cost; normally no additional model call. One background planner call may be needed to rehydrate a stale or changed task. Audio completion delivery is the main bandwidth cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only the minimum structured intent and references, not page contents or shell secrets. Bind queued work to the owner's authenticated device and surface session, expire tasks with sensitive data, and never replay a mutation unless its original action is marked retry-safe and its preconditions still match. Tell the owner when a task expired or needs clarification.
missing: An offline-capable pendant task envelope with durable sequence numbers and bounded local storage
A relay durable queue with leases, retry backoff, expiry, and exactly-once intent delivery
Surface-return events or health subscriptions for the Mac agent and browser bridge
Task rehydration that binds the original goal to current session/tab context and revalidates preconditions
A completion/expiry notification path back to the pendant

proposals.user_asks: Just do it, but first figure out which parts of my Mac, browser, pendant, and relay are actually available; use safe fallbacks when one is unavailable, and tell me what you could not do without making me ask again.
proposals.why_useful: Today the planner can know a route exists while the real surface is unusable: this Mac reports computer-use disabled, missing Accessibility and Screen Recording, and an offline browser extension with seven queued commands. A cross-surface preflight would prevent 45-second browser timeouts and impossible GUI plans, hand public reads to relay/browser-run, hand Mac reads to shell, queue private browser work until the extension returns, and give the pendant one concise capability/fallback explanation. It is materially different from generic goal routing because it uses live permission, heartbeat, queue, and model-consent facts before each step and rechecks them after failures.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic preflight and routing policy first; use a background/standard model only to map a failed capability to a fallback. Reserve realtime for the owner's spoken explanation or a genuinely ambiguous decision.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for local /ops/status plus cached relay health; under 1 s for a cross-surface matrix. Do not spend 45 s waiting on a browser command when its heartbeat/queue already says unavailable. Recheck only the affected surface after a failure.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for local health and typed policy; roughly one small standard-model call only when fallback mapping is ambiguous. Dominant cost is the optional spoken summary, not preflight.
proposals.security_concerns: Health facts must not include page contents, cookies, or tokens. Private-page work stays on the authenticated browser bridge; public fallback must be explicitly classified as non-private. Persist only capability state, timestamps, reason codes, and job IDs. No mutation is blocked by policy—the owner chose maximum access—but an unavailable or stale surface must not be represented as successful.
missing: A versioned capability matrix contract combining Mac permissions/readiness, computer-use consent, browser heartbeat/queued-command state, relay reachability, and pendant link state
Preflight hooks in POST /plan and POST /execute, with per-step required capabilities and fallback candidates
A bounded health-aware retry/recovery state machine that consumes existing receipts and records why a fallback was selected
Pendant/relay notification payload for unavailable, deferred, and completed-with-fallback outcomes
A durable queue policy for private browser work that distinguishes stale queued commands from safe replayable commands

proposals.user_asks: After you do something across my Mac and logged-in browser, tell me whether it actually took effect—not merely whether the commands succeeded—and show me the short before/after proof if I ask.
proposals.why_useful: Today a successful receipt means an executor reported success, not that the external world changed. A browser submit can be accepted but fail validation, a Mac app can ignore input, or a page can update another tab. The owner needs one trustworthy answer that correlates the Mac observation, authenticated browser evidence, and relay-delivered pendant response, with uncertainty made explicit.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/evidence correlation and host/browser re-reads first. Use a cheaper standard model to compare before/after semantic state; reserve realtime only for the owner's spoken explanation when the verdict is ready.
proposals.latency_budget: For reversible Mac-only work, verify within 2 seconds. For browser workflows, allow up to 10 seconds for a fresh authenticated read. If verification cannot complete, return 'executed but unverified' rather than claiming success.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually no additional model call when typed fields or hashes match; one small standard-model comparison for semantic page changes. Main cost is one additional browser or Mac read, not realtime inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Proof may contain private page text, so keep raw snapshots on the Mac/browser bridge and send the relay only a redacted verdict, field names, hashes, and minimal snippets on explicit request. Bind evidence to job ID, tab/session ID, URL, and timestamps to prevent stale-tab confusion. Never treat a public fallback as proof of a private mutation.
missing: A cross-surface verification record linking action receipts to postcondition checks
Typed postconditions for Mac actions and browser mutations (field value, URL/state, app status, or semantic predicate)
A browser read-after-write primitive that guarantees the same tab/session and returns provenance-bound evidence
A Mac observe-after-action primitive for foreground app state, document values, and synthesized-input reachability
A redaction layer and pendant-friendly proof summary format
A verdict state machine distinguishing succeeded-and-verified, succeeded-but-unverified, failed-before-change, and changed-but-postcondition-failed

proposals.user_asks: “If my Mac or browser connection is unhealthy, keep my request moving where it can, tell me what could not run, and retry the missing Mac steps when it recovers.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the relay is reachable while the Mac reports not-ready (Accessibility and Screen Recording are missing), the browser extension is offline with 7 queued commands, and recent browser navigations spent about 45 seconds timing out. The owner should get useful public/reasoning work immediately instead of a silent failure, plus a precise recovery rather than manually repeating the whole request.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic health/circuit-breaker and retry planner first; gpt-4.1-mini in background for summarizing partial results and deciding safe retry ordering; realtime only to narrate a short status when the owner is waiting.
proposals.latency_budget: Health preflight under 300 ms from cached heartbeats; immediate partial result in 2–5 s; recovery retries are background and should not block the pendant conversation. Browser commands must expire or be revalidated before replay, not blindly drain the stale queue.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero for preflight, queue, and routing; roughly 2k–4k input tokens per failed multi-step request when a background model summarizes partial completion. Realtime cost occurs only for the spoken interruption/status.
proposals.security_concerns: Health telemetry stays local/relay metadata; private browser page contents never go to the public fallback. A retry must bind to the original tab/session, verify URL and a fresh page fingerprint, and omit irreversible actions unless the owner explicitly asks again. The owner permits unrestricted Mac execution, so this is observability/recovery rather than a new gate.
missing: A single preflight contract combining relay heartbeat, Mac readiness/permission state, browser online state, and pending-command age
Circuit-breaker states and per-step capability requirements (Mac shell, GUI, authenticated browser, public web)
Stale-command quarantine with idempotency-aware replay and page/session revalidation
A durable partial-result/retry plan linking relay job IDs to local job receipts and pendant notifications

proposals.user_asks: “When something failed, tell me whether it is safe to retry, what already happened, and retry only the missing pieces.”
proposals.why_useful: The current receipts can say an action failed and whether it is undoable, but they do not provide a durable, owner-facing retry decision for a partially completed multi-surface goal. This matters because the job store shows 77 write actions, 16 failures, and zero undoable actions; blindly repeating a request could duplicate work.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic receipt/effect analysis for known action types; background gpt-4.1-mini only to summarize an ambiguous partial state; realtime only when the owner asks aloud.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 s for known receipt chains; under 5 s for an ambiguous cross-surface summary. Retry execution remains asynchronous and reports progress through the pendant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for typed receipt analysis; 1k–3k background input tokens only when effects cannot be reconciled deterministically.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not infer success from a timeout. Require fresh before-state evidence for browser and filesystem operations, preserve private page data on the local path, and present a concise list of potentially duplicated effects before any replay. This adds explanation and recovery, not an approval gate.
missing: Effect-aware retry planner that understands completed, failed, timed-out, and unknown actions
Cross-surface receipt graph joining relay request, local job, browser command, and evidence capsule IDs
Owner-readable duplicate-risk and retry-scope response, with a dry-run replay preview
Persistent retention of the minimal receipts needed after the 120-job rolling store evicts old jobs

proposals.user_asks: “Save what I’m looking at right now for me, with enough evidence that I can trust it later, and let me pick it back up from the pendant without reopening the page.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the browser can inspect or capture a page and the Mac can run jobs, but there is no owner-facing handoff object that preserves the exact authenticated tab state, a compact local evidence bundle, the owner’s spoken note, and a resumable follow-up across devices. This would turn an ephemeral browsing moment into a reliable personal queue without sending private page contents through the relay.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic capture and provenance first; background gpt-4.1-mini optionally labels and compresses the evidence; realtime only reads a short queued item or records the owner’s note.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 2 seconds; evidence packaging under 10 seconds; pendant playback starts from a compact summary while the full bundle remains local.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for tab metadata, DOM excerpt hashing, local encrypted storage, and queueing; about 1k–3k background input tokens only when the owner asks for a generated summary.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page text, screenshots, cookies, and URLs stay on the Mac/browser side; the relay carries only an opaque item ID, short owner note, status, and optionally a redacted summary. Bind the bundle to tab/session identity, show source URL and capture time, and expire or delete it on request.
missing: A first-class cross-device handoff object linking browser tab/session, local evidence files, spoken note, and resumable follow-up state
Local encrypted evidence bundles with content hashes and DOM/screenshot provenance, separate from the rolling job store
Relay APIs for opaque handoff IDs, pendant queue/playback, and later resume requests
A browser command that freezes a coherent page snapshot (metadata, selected content, screenshot, and page fingerprint) atomically

proposals.user_asks: "Keep trying that browser task, and tell me on the pendant when it actually succeeds."
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser command can sit for 45 seconds, fail while the extension is stale, and leave seven pending commands. This lets the owner delegate the waiting: the Mac observes extension recovery, retries only the safe/idempotent step, and the relay delivers one concise success or an actionable failure to the pendant without another conversation turn.
proposals.model_tier: Background model for retry classification and a final short status; deterministic local logic for heartbeat, queue reconciliation, and idempotent retry. Use realtime only to speak the result when the owner is actively listening.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; heartbeat checks every 5–15 seconds while a task is pending; speak within 2 seconds of a confirmed result. Stop after a bounded deadline set by the owner.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero when healthy (local status checks). One small background-model call only for ambiguous failure classification or final wording, roughly 2k–4k prompt tokens; realtime/TTS cost only if spoken immediately.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated browser session contents stay on the Mac/browser bridge and are not sent to the relay. Relay receives job id, health state, typed outcome, and a redacted summary. Never retry clicks, submits, purchases, or other non-idempotent writes automatically; expose receipts and require the owner's existing conversational authorization for a new write.
missing: Durable retry/watch state that survives local-agent restart and relay reconnect
Browser command acknowledgement with command age and idempotency classification
A scheduler/heartbeat worker that can wake on browser reconnection
Relay event routing from job completion to the pendant pipeline
A compact owner-facing policy for retry deadline and safe action types

proposals.user_asks: "Make this Mac ready for you to control, and tell me exactly what I still need to click."
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently cannot tell why the agent is not ready: live status reports Accessibility and Screen Recording missing even though most automation grants are present. A pendant-initiated readiness check would turn a mysterious failure into a guided, verified setup, then confirm when visual and control capabilities are genuinely available.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic checks and routing for known permission states; background model only to turn the state into a short spoken checklist. Realtime is used only for the live pendant response.
proposals.latency_budget: Return the first diagnosis in under 3 seconds; launch the relevant System Settings pane immediately; re-check after the owner returns, with no polling longer than 30 seconds unless explicitly requested.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually zero model calls because /ops/status already provides structured permission state. One short background response when the state is ambiguous; dominant cost is local verification and the owner's manual click, not API usage.
proposals.security_concerns: The agent must not claim permissions were fixed until a fresh local check verifies them. Opening Settings is reversible, but changing privacy permissions remains an explicit owner action inside macOS. Send only boolean permission states and remediation URLs to the relay; never transmit screen contents or permission databases.
