changes.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$6 added BOM for a contact/proximity sensor, glue/enclosure changes, and a few milliwatts only while sensing; negligible API cost beyond one small fleet event and receipts per transition.
changes.latency_impact: Local sensor-to-relay event target under 1 second when connected; on LTE loss, the pendant can immediately stop its own playback and mark the Mac state unknown. Restoration waits for authenticated presence and a heartbeat, typically a few seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by making absence a signed, fleet-wide signal. Do not send microphone audio or page contents with the event. Use a hardware-backed device key and monotonic event counter so an intercepted old 'present' event cannot undo privacy mode.
depends_on: A hardware-backed pendant identity and signed event channel
A relay-wide privacy-state protocol understood by Mac and browser nodes
Typed Mac/browser privacy actions with truthful receipts
A production enclosure with a reliable skin/contact or proximity sensor

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface execution trace and continuation ledger. The pendant/relay assigns a traceId and intentId at utterance time; every relay dispatch, Mac job, shell command, browser command, retry, and result receipt carries that ID. Persist a compact append-only event record on the Mac and relay (with payload redaction and a 30-day TTL), reconcile duplicate/out-of-order events by idempotency key, and expose one GET /continuations/:traceId plus a relay push topic. When the pendant reconnects, it receives a concise status (running, waiting for Mac/browser, completed, failed with next retry time) rather than losing the task. Add a background reconciler that marks stale leases, retries only retry-safe operations, and emits a human-readable completion/failure receipt. This is deliberately observability and recovery only: it does not gate or refuse any FULL_CONTROL action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the owner says “do this” and walks away or the pendant link drops, they can later ask “what happened?” and get one trustworthy answer spanning shell, Safari, Mac, and relay—not a partial job list. Failures become actionable (“browser was offline; resumed at 9:14”) instead of silent or duplicated work, and repeated retries stop rerunning completed steps.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared trace schema and propagation in relay, executor, browserBridge, and jobTracker; small durable event store and reconciler; dashboard/pendant status view; integration tests for disconnect, restart, duplicate, and out-of-order delivery.
changes.risk: Trace records could leak URLs, shell commands, or private snippets; redact arguments and store hashes/metadata by default, encrypt relay records, and make detailed evidence opt-in. Reconciliation bugs could duplicate mutations, so only actions already declared idempotent/retry-safe are auto-retried; all others are reported as needing continuation, never replayed automatically. Recover by disabling the reconciler while retaining raw receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic ID/event handling and a cheaper background reconciler; roughly 1–3 KB of metadata per action before retention, with relay storage and dashboard reads dominating rather than model tokens.
changes.latency_impact: No added latency on the first action beyond generating an ID and one local append (<10 ms target). Reconnect status is immediate from persisted state; background reconciliation may add seconds only after failures.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding authority. Use scoped trace tokens, redact command text/DOM content and credentials, encrypt relay-at-rest data, and enforce owner-device pairing for continuation queries. Never expose raw shell/environment values in pendant speech.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 (implemented per-action receipts)
relay durable state and paired-device identity
chg-14accc01's resumable browser queue or equivalent lease API
a stable Mac job lifecycle event hook

changes.change: Add a cross-node execution ledger and recovery coordinator above the existing Mac job store and browser command queue. Each workflow is a versioned DAG whose steps carry an idempotency key, device/session affinity, precondition fingerprint, receipt links, retry budget, and an explicit outcome enum (succeeded, failed-before-effect, failed-after-effect, or unknown). The relay owns the durable ledger and leases; Mac and browser agents atomically claim steps, report heartbeats, and expose a read-only reconciliation operation. On reconnect, reconcile unknown steps from local receipts/page state before retrying. Render one compact pendant/dashboard timeline rather than separate Mac and browser histories.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A lost connection will no longer force the owner to guess whether an order lookup, file operation, or draft was already done. Long tasks can resume safely across sleep, browser restarts, and relay reconnects without duplicate side effects.
changes.effort: Medium-high: new relay D1 schema and coordinator, adapters in jobTracker/browser bridge, reconciliation handlers, and dashboard timeline; staged rollout can start with read-only workflows and simulated disconnect tests.
changes.risk: A faulty reconciliation rule could classify an effect incorrectly or retry a non-idempotent action. Default unknown to paused, preserve all raw receipts, and provide operator replay/repair tooling; do not delete existing job history.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible steady-state storage and request overhead; roughly one small D1 write per transition/heartbeat. Background model cost only for ambiguous human-readable recovery summaries.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds to normal step dispatch; reconnect recovery is bounded by heartbeat plus one reconciliation round, typically under 30 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Ledger contains sensitive URLs, snippets, and local paths, so encrypt sensitive fields, scope records to the paired owner, and apply existing audio/job retention. It must not become a new channel for raw page contents.
depends_on: Existing Mac action receipts and browser command IDs must be exposed as stable references
Relay↔Mac authentication and pairing already present
A typed, read-only reconciliation endpoint on both Mac and browser surfaces
Dashboard and pendant status rendering for paused/unknown steps

changes.change: Add a local execution preflight and result normalizer that runs before arbitrary shell actions without blocking them: resolve the project/workspace from known roots and recent successful cwd values, snapshot PATH/tool availability and relevant app permissions, classify the command's expected output shape, and attach exit code, signal, duration, cwd, redacted environment/tool versions, stdout/stderr byte counts plus bounded tail, and an undoability hint to the existing receipt. For failures, automatically suggest one deterministic retry (for example corrected cwd, missing executable path, or expired GUI session) and record whether the retry was attempted.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent will stop wasting turns hunting for the project or asking the same status question, and spoken results will say whether a command failed before doing anything, ran successfully with noisy output, or needs a Mac permission/session repair.
changes.effort: Medium: a preflight module, receipt schema extension, workspace index, and tests against the already-proven pmset/scutil/df/git/osascript commands.
changes.risk: Capturing environment or output tails could leak secrets; redact known token/password patterns, never persist full environment, cap output, and let the owner disable command-output retention. A bad automatic retry could repeat a mutation, so only retry commands classified as read-only or explicitly idempotent.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; one local process and small receipt metadata per action. Saves planner tokens and repeated failed commands.
changes.latency_impact: Usually 10–100 ms for cached facts; skip expensive scans when a matching cwd/tool fingerprint is fresh.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding gates or narrowing FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Store receipts locally, send only summaries to relay, and preserve existing unrestricted execution policy.
depends_on: Stable action receipts and journal endpoints (now present)
A local workspace/cwd index with bounded retention
Output redaction and receipt-size limits

changes.change: Create an owner-visible causal provenance graph for every multi-surface request. At planning time, record the request version, selected surfaces, facts actually used (with freshness and confidence), routing decisions, model tier, generated action arguments, device/session identity, data sent off-device, and each resulting receipt. At completion, materialize a signed, compact explanation with links between cause and effect, including discarded alternatives and the exact uncertainty that caused a pause or fallback. Expose it as a pendant-sized spoken answer and an expandable Mac dashboard view; allow the owner to correct a fact or revoke a provenance edge without deleting the underlying execution receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the pendant says something was done—or failed—the owner can ask “why did you use Safari instead of the Mac, what did you rely on, and what left my computer?” and receive a trustworthy answer grounded in the actual run, not a reconstructed model story. This makes a multi-device personal agent understandable enough to delegate consequential work to it.
changes.effort: High: define a versioned provenance schema, instrument planner/routing/relay/Mac/browser boundaries, sign and retain append-only edges, build redaction and sensitivity handling, and add spoken plus dashboard renderers.
changes.risk: Provenance can expose private page text, file paths, or credentials and can become misleading if agents write free-form explanations. Store references and hashes by default, redact sensitive values, separate observed facts from inferences, and generate explanations only from recorded edges. Preserve raw receipts if the owner edits or revokes a displayed edge.
changes.cost_impact: Small local/relay storage and serialization overhead per step; no extra model call for the graph. A cheap background model may summarize a large graph, while realtime only reads a precomputed short explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible dispatch overhead (structured edge writes); explanation retrieval should be sub-second for normal jobs and under a few seconds for long workflows.
changes.security_impact: Adds an auditable record of data movement, but increases the sensitivity of retained metadata. Encrypt the graph, scope it to the paired owner, apply field-level TTLs, and never include raw secrets in relay payloads or speech.
depends_on: Stable cross-surface request and step IDs across relay, Mac, and browser
Existing Mac job/action receipts and browser command receipts
A durable owner-scoped store with append-only integrity checks
A dashboard/pendant renderer that distinguishes observed evidence from inferred explanation

changes.change: Add a fail-fast preflight and reconciliation layer before browser actions are dispatched. The Mac bridge publishes a signed capability heartbeat (extension online, session/tab identity, queue depth, last-seen age); the relay planner converts an offline or stale heartbeat into a waiting dependency instead of sending the action. On reconnect, reconcile each queued command by requestId/idempotencyKey against browser receipts, mark completed commands, and execute only unacknowledged steps. Emit blocked/resumed/expired events to the pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request will no longer burn 45 seconds and end in a generic browser-offline failure. The owner hears that the Mac portion is continuing, gets a precise recovery instruction, and the browser portion resumes safely after Safari is available without duplicate clicks or submissions.
changes.effort: Medium-high: bridge heartbeat and reconciliation protocol, relay durable dependency state, planner integration, pendant event plumbing, and tests for disconnects during navigation and submit.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could cause either unnecessary waiting or duplicate execution. Use short leases, monotonic command sequence numbers, idempotency keys, and receipt reconciliation; expire commands with an explicit explanation rather than guessing. Roll back by treating the runner as fail-fast as it is now.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/relay storage and heartbeat traffic; no additional model calls for retries. One background summarization call only when status needs natural-language explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms preflight when healthy; avoids the current ~45 s timeout when offline. Reconnect latency is heartbeat interval plus one reconciliation round.
changes.security_impact: Heartbeat carries capability/session metadata, never page text or credentials. Bind commands to authenticated extension ID plus tab/session lease; reject commands whose lease or idempotency scope has changed.
depends_on: Shared typed capability snapshot between Mac bridge and relay
Durable job dependency/receipt schema
Browser command request IDs and tab/session affinity (the still-open browser reliability change)

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution health and recovery coordinator. Before dispatch, relay polls a compact Mac-agent capability lease (agent reachable, browser bridge online, accessibility/screen-recording state, pending-job count, supported action families) and chooses Mac shell, typed Mac action, browser bridge, or durable queue accordingly. Every dispatched step carries a jobId, idempotency key, checkpoint, and deadline; failures are normalized into transient (retry/backoff), unavailable (park until a health transition), or permanent (surface-specific explanation). On reconnect, resume only from the last acknowledged checkpoint and publish one signed result receipt containing attempted route, exact failure, retry history, and final state. This is observability/recovery, not an approval gate; FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say one thing and leave. Instead of silently spending 45 seconds on a browser action while the extension is offline, the system immediately says what is unavailable, parks the work, resumes when Safari or the Mac returns, and avoids duplicate shell/browser mutations after a dropped link.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a small health lease endpoint and typed state schema in local-agent, relay-side coordinator and durable queue, idempotent checkpoint persistence, and unified spoken/result formatting. Existing /ops/snapshot, /browser/status, /jobs, receipts, and journal provide most inputs.
changes.risk: A stale lease could select the wrong route or retry a non-idempotent action. Leases need short TTLs, action idempotency classes, and an explicit 'unknown outcome' state that never retries automatically. Recovery is replayed from receipts and can be manually abandoned; no existing execution path is removed.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic health checks and retry logic; only final explanation needs background/planner inference. Small D1/R2 or local job-store growth for checkpoints and receipts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for cached health; avoids long doomed attempts (currently an offline browser navigate took about 45 seconds). Reconnect work is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Health leases must omit page content and secrets, authenticate Mac↔relay, bind results to jobId/idempotency key, and redact command env/stderr before relay storage. Existing unrestricted shell authority is preserved.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface job identity/idempotency schema
Local-agent read-only health snapshot with stable machine-readable fields
Relay-to-Mac authenticated callback or polling for parked-job wakeups

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution ledger and recovery coordinator. Every delegated plan gets a durable job/step DAG with stable step IDs, parent/child dependencies, attempt records, start/end timestamps, command or browser action fingerprints, exit/HTTP/UI outcomes, touched-resource summaries, and a monotonic receipt chain. The Mac shell adapter records argv-equivalent parsing when possible but preserves the original command string, cwd, environment-difference hash, stdout/stderr size plus redacted excerpts, signal/timeout, and resource probes. A classifier labels failures as retryable, session/device unavailable, failed-before-effect, effect-uncertain, or irreversible. Recovery policies are declarative: retry only steps marked idempotent or proven to have failed before effect; otherwise stop downstream dependents, preserve the evidence, and create a resume token. Browser steps use tab/session affinity and page fingerprints; Mac steps use receipt snapshots and existing undo metadata. A relay worker polls/pushes state, and the pendant receives only a compact status plus job ID. Dashboard exposes 'resume from step', 'retry failed step', and 'show evidence', while retaining the owner's no-gate maximum-access policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A failed overnight task will no longer force the owner to rerun a whole workflow or wonder whether an email/form/file change already happened. They get an honest stopping point, automatic safe continuation, and a single resume action that avoids duplicate side effects.
changes.effort: Medium-high: new durable schema/worker, adapters in executor.js and browser bridge, failure classifier, relay notification, dashboard state view, and integration tests for timeout, disconnect, duplicate delivery, and uncertain side effects.
changes.risk: A classifier could wrongly call a step retryable and duplicate an external effect, or a stale browser session could produce misleading evidence. Default uncertain states to stop (not block owner actions), require explicit idempotency declarations for automatic retries, and preserve raw receipts for forensic review. If the coordinator dies, the existing executor and receipts continue operating; recovery can be manual.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2/storage and polling cost; approximately $0.001–$0.01 per job for ledger writes and background classification, plus occasional vision/model retries. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible overhead per action (one local ledger write, generally <50 ms); recovery reports arrive asynchronously. Durable writes may add modest latency before acknowledging a multi-step job.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without reducing capability: raw shell commands and private browser data stay on the Mac/local-agent boundary, while relay/dashboard receive typed summaries and redacted evidence. Encrypt ledger at rest, limit job visibility to the owner's identity, and expire raw stdout/page excerpts separately from durable step metadata.
depends_on: The existing actionReceipts.js result/undo integration and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts.
The browser request-ID/session-affinity work already present in browserBridge.js/browserSessions.js.
A durable backend job runner and authenticated relay-to-Mac job status channel, which are still absent.

changes.change: Add a first-class encrypted Work Handoff Bundle protocol. At pack time, Mac-planner asks local Mac and browser adapters for typed state records (window/app identity, file path plus content hash, terminal cwd and job ID, browser tab/session ID plus URL/title and redacted anchor hashes, draft identifiers, and the current goal). A local model compiles these into an ordered task graph with 'safe to restore', 'needs revalidation', and 'reference only' classifications; private bodies remain local and the relay stores only encrypted manifests and short-lived opaque pointers. The pendant receives a compact spoken index. On resume, the target Mac requests each record, revalidates hashes/session ownership, restores tabs/windows/focus where possible, and reports omissions instead of fabricating continuity; from the pendant, the owner can ask for any thread and get its next concrete step. Add expiry, per-record deletion, and a provenance trail for every restored item.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave a complicated task without losing their place or leaving a vulnerable Mac session open. Returning later—or asking from the pendant—restores the actual working context and tells them honestly what changed while they were away.
changes.effort: Medium-high: local state collectors and restore adapters, encrypted manifest storage, redaction/sensitivity rules, browser and terminal identity hooks, and end-to-end interruption/resume tests.
changes.risk: Some applications cannot restore state safely, browser pages can change, and stale file hashes may make a restoration misleading. Treat each item independently, require revalidation before opening or editing changed resources, preserve the original snapshot for comparison, and degrade to a spoken summary rather than claiming success. If bundle storage fails, leave the live Mac session untouched.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring storage and encryption overhead; roughly $0.002–$0.02 per bundle plus occasional model summarization. No pendant hardware change required.
changes.latency_impact: Packing adds local collection time (typically seconds); restoration is asynchronous after the initial acknowledgement and should not block the pendant conversation.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy over sending whole desktop/browser snapshots to the relay by keeping sensitive payloads local and expiring encrypted manifests. Requires strict owner identity binding, no cookie/token export, and audit/delete controls for every bundle.
depends_on: A durable relay job/storage facility with authenticated owner binding.
Browser tab/session affinity and typed results from the existing browser bridge.
Mac action receipts and local-agent observability for terminal jobs and app state.
A pendant/relay protocol for retrieving compact handoff summaries.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface browser availability supervisor. The relay/mac agent records extension heartbeats and a short-lived capability lease; before dispatching any browser action, the Mac performs a cheap local health read. If the lease is stale, fail the action immediately (not after the current ~45-second browser timeout), classify it as 'device unavailable' rather than action failure, retain the idempotent job in a dead-letter/waiting state, and notify the pendant. When a fresh Safari bridge heartbeat arrives, resume only unstarted action IDs and send one completion/failure receipt. Include outage start, last heartbeat, retry count, and the exact reattachment instruction in the spoken status.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request made from the pendant will no longer burn nearly a minute per browser step or look like the account/site is broken when Safari is simply closed or the extension is offline. The owner gets a truthful spoken 'waiting for Safari' status and automatic continuation when the Mac/browser comes back, without duplicate form submissions or repeated navigation.
changes.effort: Medium: add lease/heartbeat state to the Mac bridge, a preflight in browser dispatch, a waiting/dead-letter job state with idempotent resume, relay event propagation, and pendant notification copy; test crash/reconnect and stale command cleanup.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could delay a healthy but briefly reconnecting bridge; use a short preflight timeout and explicit manual retry. A reconnect during a step could create ambiguity, so resume only after receipt says the step never started or the action ID is safely idempotent. Keep pending commands bounded and expire them with a visible reason.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost: deterministic health checks and event forwarding; one small D1/SQLite state record per lease/job. Saves expensive planner retries and 45-second local timeouts.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy browser actions gain only a few milliseconds for the local preflight; offline actions return in under a second instead of ~45 seconds and reconnect jobs resume on the next heartbeat.
changes.security_impact: No page contents or cookies leave the Mac. Heartbeats carry extension ID, capability state, and timestamps only; bind leases to the paired device and never treat a heartbeat as authorization to submit a pending irreversible action.
depends_on: A browser bridge heartbeat endpoint that reports online/offline and pending-command ownership
Durable action IDs/receipts already implemented in the Mac harness
Relay-to-pendant job status events and a waiting/resume state in the job tracker

changes.change: Add a shell execution envelope and recovery record around every run_shell invocation without changing the owner's unrestricted FULL_CONTROL policy. Persist command text plus SHA-256, resolved cwd, start/end monotonic times, timeout, exit code/signal, stdout/stderr byte counts and bounded tails, environment fingerprint (names and hashes only), and whether the process spawned children. For failures, deterministically classify timeout, missing executable, permission, nonzero exit, and transport crash; attach a suggested retry strategy and allow the planner to retry only transient classes with a fresh job/action ID while linking attempts under one parent operation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails, the agent can say what actually happened—wrong directory, missing tool, timeout, or a command error—and recover from transient failures instead of blindly repeating or asking the owner to diagnose. The owner can audit exactly what ran without dumping secrets such as tokens or full environment variables.
changes.effort: Medium: wrap computerControl.runShell's child-process result, redact/size-limit output, add parent/attempt links to existing receipts and journal, implement deterministic failure taxonomy and bounded retry policy, and expose a concise dashboard/pendant completion receipt.
changes.risk: Output can contain secrets; redact known token/key/password patterns and store only bounded tails with configurable retention. Retrying arbitrary shell is not always safe, so default automatic retry only for process launch/transport/timeouts when the command is marked retry-safe; otherwise report a one-click/manual retry. Child-process accounting is platform-specific and may be unavailable for some commands.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model cost; a few KB of local journal storage per attempt with retention cleanup. Avoids planner calls for straightforward diagnosis and transient recovery.
changes.latency_impact: A few milliseconds of wrapper overhead; transient retry adds bounded delay only when needed. Failure reporting becomes immediate and structured rather than requiring another low-latency model turn.
changes.security_impact: Preserves unrestricted execution and no approval gates. Store command/output locally with permissions, hash the command for correlation, redact environment values, and send only the summary/error class to relay unless the owner explicitly requests diagnostic details.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and /journal observability
A bounded local retention policy for shell transcripts
A planner/executor contract that marks an action retry-safe without blocking other actions

changes.change: Add a shell execution flight recorder and failure-recovery loop without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: record command hash, exact argv/string, cwd, selected environment names (not values), start/end timestamps, exit/signal, stdout/stderr byte counts plus capped tails, and host resource snapshot; on timeout/nonzero exit, automatically run a small fixed diagnostic bundle (cwd, disk, network, process, permissions), classify the failure, and retry only when the planner marks the command idempotent. Store a content-addressed compressed transcript linked to the existing receipt and expose a single job timeline in /jobs/:id and the dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a task fails, the agent can explain whether it was a bad path, missing permission, timeout, or unavailable network and recover instead of asking the owner to repeat it. The owner gets a trustworthy answer about what ran, while retaining the deliberately unrestricted capability.
changes.effort: Medium: executor instrumentation, bounded transcript storage/redaction, typed failure schema, retry metadata, and dashboard timeline; no shell-policy change.
changes.risk: Command output can contain secrets and large logs; redact common credential patterns, cap output, encrypt or short-retain transcripts, and allow deletion. Automatic retries could duplicate side effects, so retries are opt-in per command and disabled after ambiguous termination. Recovery is to fall back to the current one-shot executor.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and CPU overhead per job; roughly cents per GB-month for retained compressed logs. Diagnostic commands add negligible local cost and avoid repeated expensive model turns.
changes.latency_impact: Successful commands gain only milliseconds; failed commands take a few seconds for diagnostics and optional retry, while the owner receives an immediate queued/running status.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without gates. Do not persist full environment values, stdin, or unrestricted page contents; hash/redact sensitive fields and make transcript access follow existing Mac-agent auth.
depends_on: Existing job receipts and /jobs/:jobId lifecycle
A bounded local transcript store and authenticated observability endpoint
Planner support for explicit idempotent=true retry intent

changes.change: Create an ephemeral 'active-context capsule' protocol shared by Mac agent and browser extension. On request, the Mac issues a single-use token bound to the focused window and browser tab; the extension or accessibility adapter returns only a selected visible/semantic region, source metadata, redacted text or low-resolution crop, and a content hash. The relay expires the capsule after one answer or 60 seconds and links the evidence hash to the job receipt without storing raw pixels.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask about exactly what is in front of them and trust that the answer came from the current page, not an old tab or an invented context, while reducing the chance that private screen contents leak or linger.
changes.effort: Medium-high: cross-process focus attestation, browser/Mac adapters, secret-field redaction, token expiry, typed evidence schema, and a small dashboard evidence viewer.
changes.risk: Focus can change during capture or accessibility APIs can fail; return an explicit stale/unknown result and never silently substitute another tab. Redaction can miss novel secrets, so default to minimal regions and short-lived transport. Recovery is a fresh capsule request.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring cost; mostly local metadata/OCR, with a small model call only when visual interpretation is needed. Short-lived capsule storage is bounded and automatically deleted.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under a second for token negotiation and extraction; avoids sending full screenshots and usually reduces model latency and token cost.
changes.security_impact: Strengthens least-retention and provenance without adding an approval gate. It needs authenticated local IPC, per-request nonce binding, encrypted relay transport, and deletion verification.
depends_on: Mac focused-window API
Browser extension active-tab attestation
Relay ephemeral payload store and expiry sweeper
Pendant capture indicator and evidence replay control

changes.change: Add an end-to-end 24 kHz audio negotiation and validation protocol: the relay advertises codec/rate/frame parameters, the pendant acknowledges them, and every stream begins with a short loopback/test-vector exchange carrying sequence numbers, CRC, encode/decode timing, underrun counters, and resampler mode. Persist only the last health counters and negotiated profile; automatically fall back to the existing 16 kHz uplink/24 kHz downlink profile when the 24 kHz path misses its latency budget.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely consistent wideband playback instead of silently hearing a degraded or glitchy stream. When it fails, the pendant can say whether the cause was network loss, relay transcoding, decoder CPU saturation, or the Mac TTS path, rather than making the owner debug three machines.
changes.effort: Medium: shared protocol fields in relay and Mac bridge, a small fixed-point test vector in firmware, and telemetry/receipt display in the dashboard; validate on the current nRF9160 DK before selecting product silicon.
changes.risk: A negotiation bug could leave the pendant silent or produce incompatible frames. Keep the current profile as a versioned fallback, require a timeout before switching, and make the test-vector path run before user audio only.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 2–4 KB flash and under 2 KB RAM for counters/test buffers on the pendant. Test packets add a few hundred bytes per session.
changes.latency_impact: Adds approximately 100–250 ms once per session for validation; steady-state target remains 60 ms frames, with fallback if decode plus encode exceeds the observed ~87% single-core combined load.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry should contain counters and negotiated formats only, not audio content. Authenticate the profile exchange with the existing paired relay/session identity.
depends_on: A relay telemetry schema and dashboard view for negotiated audio profiles
A Mac bridge receipt path that records TTS sample rate and resampling decisions
The owner's requested 24 kHz superwideband path being enabled in the production audio pipeline

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface causality ledger with a signed trace envelope. Every pendant utterance, relay decision, model call, Mac job, browser command/result, retry, and TTS segment receives a trace ID, parent span ID, sequence number, monotonic duration, wall-clock estimate, actor, sensitivity label, and outcome. Mac and pendant buffer events while disconnected and reconcile them on reconnect; the relay detects duplicate or missing spans rather than presenting an apparently complete but false timeline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the system acts incorrectly or appears to ignore them, the owner can get a trustworthy answer about where it diverged instead of hearing a generic failure. It also makes cross-device handoff and recovery intelligible: the owner can see whether the Mac never received the request, the browser acted on stale state, or the response was generated but never played.
changes.effort: High: a shared envelope library, durable append-only storage and reconciliation, instrumentation in relay/Mac/browser/pendant paths, redaction, and dashboard queries. Start with one trace through voice → relay → Mac job → TTS.
changes.risk: Tracing can leak more personal data and create a second failure path. Keep payloads separate from metadata, encrypt sensitive attachments, bound per-trace size, degrade to metadata-only when storage is unavailable, and make correlation IDs opaque. Clock skew could misorder events, so use per-device monotonic clocks and mark wall-clock ordering as estimated.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and bandwidth overhead per event; no meaningful model cost for correlation. A background summarizer is optional and only invoked when the owner asks for a human explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond local event creation and a few milliseconds per relay write when online; disconnected buffering avoids adding network latency to voice execution.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but expands the sensitive metadata surface. Encrypt at rest and in transit, apply short retention, redact transcripts/URLs/paths by default, and enforce owner-scoped trace access.
depends_on: A common trace-envelope schema adopted by pendant firmware, Cloudflare relay, Mac bridge, and browser extension
Durable encrypted event storage and reconnect reconciliation
A redaction-aware trace query API and dashboard/pendant presentation

changes.change: Add a failure-aware execution envelope and recovery journal around every Mac and browser action without narrowing FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Before execution, record a generated step ID, intent, idempotency/reversibility class, timeout, and retry budget. Afterward persist exit code or browser error class, duration, redacted stdout/stderr tail, affected app/tab/session, and a compact evidence hash. A classifier maps failures into transient transport/session, missing dependency, permission, semantic mismatch, or irreversible-uncertainty. The job runner may automatically retry only declared-idempotent steps, reattach a browser tab or relaunch an app when the class permits, and produce a compensation suggestion for everything else. Expose a single timeline to relay_job_status and the dashboard, with machine-readable pause/resume/cancel tokens.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When they leave a job running, they get an honest explanation and a useful next attempt instead of “failed.” They can resume after a Mac sleep or browser restart without repeating completed work, and can see exactly which alternative was tried. This preserves the owner's maximum-access policy while making failure recovery and trust substantially better.
changes.effort: Medium-high: executor/job schema, redaction and journal persistence, retry state machine, browser reattachment hooks, relay status projection, and dashboard timeline; roughly 1–2 weeks for a robust first version.
changes.risk: Retries could duplicate side effects if an action is misclassified, and captured output could contain secrets. Default unknown actions to no automatic retry, use idempotency keys where possible, redact credential-like patterns, and keep compensation advisory rather than silently mutating. Recovery is straightforward by replaying the journal and marking a job paused.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and compute overhead per step; roughly 1–5 KB of metadata plus bounded output per action. Fewer planner calls on transient failures should reduce API cost; diagnosis costs an extra small planner call only on failure.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible for normal actions if journaling is append-only/local; a few milliseconds per step. Recovery adds seconds only after failure, with retries bounded and asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding approval gates or reducing access. Sensitive command output and URLs must be redacted before relay/dashboard projection; retain full evidence locally under existing Mac trust boundary and expire it by job retention policy.
depends_on: The existing receipt/undo records need a common step identifier and reversible/irreversible metadata.
Durable relay job records and browser session/tab affinity must expose pause/resume semantics.
A small, shared redaction library must run before evidence leaves the Mac.

changes.change: Add a failure-aware execution journal and recovery loop around run_shell and typed Mac actions. For every invocation, persist a compact, redacted execution capsule (request/job ID, argv or action type, cwd, selected environment fingerprint, start/end/duration, exit/signal, stdout/stderr hashes plus bounded tails, and filesystem/network/process diagnostics collected only on failure). When a command fails, classify likely causes (missing executable, wrong cwd, permission, transient network, lock/contention, timeout), automatically retry only when the planner marks the action idempotent, and otherwise generate a concrete recovery plan. Link the capsule to the relay job receipt and expose a one-click 'retry with suggested fix / open artifact' view in the shared dashboard; send the pendant only a terse failure and next step, never raw logs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A failed 'handle this' request would stop being a dead end or require the owner to reproduce an invisible terminal error. The agent can find the project, repair a stale path or transient connection, resume safely after a timeout, and tell the owner exactly what happened when it cannot. Cross-surface linkage means the spoken pendant answer, Mac evidence, and durable relay history agree.
changes.effort: Medium: local-agent journal schema and bounded collectors, planner failure classifier/retry policy, relay receipt fields and dashboard detail view, plus pendant notification formatting and tests for redaction/idempotency.
changes.risk: Diagnostic data can contain secrets or personal paths; redact environment values and cap/TTL raw tails, hash by default, and keep capsules local unless the job is explicitly relay-visible. Automatic retries can duplicate side effects, so require an explicit idempotency annotation from the planner and never retry unknown commands. Recovery is straightforward: disable the retry worker and retain the original receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and CPU cost on the Mac; relay adds a few D1 rows and occasional short R2 artifacts. No extra model call for ordinary success; a cheap classifier or the existing planner is invoked only on failures.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful success-path delay beyond journal write; failure diagnosis adds roughly 1–5 seconds locally, with relay/dashboard synchronization asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding an approval gate (preserves the owner's maximum-access policy). Must implement secret redaction, local-first retention, per-job access control, and explicit deletion of capsules alongside existing audio/job retention.
depends_on: Existing action receipts (chg-5fc73ce3)
Durable job/result linkage and relay receipt APIs
A typed/idempotency annotation in the Mac planner
Dashboard job detail UI

changes.change: Add a Mac-local execution supervisor around run_shell and browser actions. Each job gets a durable execution manifest with attemptId, parent job ID, command/action fingerprint, cwd, start/heartbeat/exit timestamps, bounded stdout/stderr tails, and explicit checkpoint markers. Run long work in a detached process group so voice-session loss does not kill it; on restart, reconcile live process groups and manifests. Classify failures into retryable, resumable-from-checkpoint, ambiguous-partial, and terminal. Emit signed progress events to relay and store redacted evidence; permit automatic retry only for an allowlisted idempotent step or a deterministic checkpoint recipe, never by shrinking FULL_CONTROL_MODE.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A Mac job will finish—or clearly explain why it cannot—rather than silently dying when the pendant disconnects or leaving the owner guessing whether a second attempt will duplicate changes. They get useful progress and a trustworthy completion boundary for long tasks.
changes.effort: Medium-high: local supervisor/manifest store, process-group lifecycle, checkpoint adapters for shell/browser steps, event transport, crash-reconciliation tests, and dashboard/pendant status rendering.
changes.risk: A process can outlive the original intent, and a mistaken idempotency classification can duplicate work. Recover by defaulting ambiguous jobs to needs-owner, recording every attempt, exposing a stop/kill action, and retaining raw local evidence while relaying only redacted tails. Existing receipts remain the final user-visible outcome.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing compute/storage; a few KB of manifest and bounded logs per attempt. Occasional background-model failure classification costs cents per long job. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible for short actions; detached launch adds under 200 ms. Heartbeats are asynchronous. Recovery adds seconds only after failure.
changes.security_impact: No new execution authority and no approval gate. It does introduce durable command metadata, so encrypt local manifests, redact likely secrets (tokens, cookies, API keys), and enforce retention/deletion controls. Signed event envelopes prevent stale relay updates from being mistaken for current completion.
depends_on: A durable relay job record and event stream with attempt IDs
Mac-local persistence outside the voice process (SQLite or append-only journal)
An explicit checkpoint/idempotency contract for multi-step Mac and browser plans
Existing action receipts/undo integration so recovered jobs produce the same evidence

changes.change: Add a structured shell execution ledger alongside the existing job receipt without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: record argv/tokenized command form, resolved cwd, start/end timestamps, timeout, exit code, signal, stdout/stderr byte counts plus bounded redacted tails, environment/network classification, and a stable command fingerprint. Emit lifecycle events at start, timeout, completion, and failure; link each shell record to the originating pendant request, planner trace, jobId, and undo status. Add a deterministic retry recommendation (never automatic retry for unknown side effects) and expose a compact GET job detail for the dashboard and spoken receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When an unattended Mac command fails or changes something permanent, the owner can currently learn that a job failed but not reliably what ran, where it ran, how long it waited, or whether retrying is safe. This gives a trustworthy answer to “what happened?” and prevents blind duplicate commands, while preserving the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: typed ledger schema, executor instrumentation, redaction/fingerprint utility, job-detail endpoint, dashboard rendering, and tests for timeout/nonzero/signal paths.
changes.risk: Command text may contain secrets; redact common token/key/password patterns and cap tails, with an opt-out only for explicit owner debugging. Ledger writes must be append-only/idempotent so a crash cannot falsely report completion. Do not infer reversibility from the fingerprint; retain the existing action receipt as authority. Recovery is to fall back to the current job record if ledger writing fails.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local JSON/SQLite append and a few KB per command. Add retention/rotation to prevent the ledger growing without bound.
changes.latency_impact: Usually under 5 ms per command for event writes; dashboard reads become cheaper than scanning full logs. No extra model latency.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding a gate or reducing shell capability. Store only redacted output and hash/fingerprint of sensitive command material; protect the ledger with the same local-agent auth as jobs.
depends_on: Existing job IDs, trace IDs, and receipt linkage
A bounded local retention/rotation policy
Dashboard support for a shell-specific execution timeline

changes.change: Create a deterministic 'receipt compiler' for completed/failed Mac jobs: consume typed job/receipt fields and render concise spoken and dashboard variants (success, partial, timeout, offline dependency, retry-safe/unsafe), with model escalation only when the owner asks a follow-up that requires interpretation. Add a token-budget guard that strips full traces and large output from the planner context, retaining IDs, effect, evidence, and next action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A simple request such as “prepare a concise completion receipt” currently consumed a background model call with about 2,163 input tokens for 34 output tokens. The owner gets faster, cheaper, more consistent answers for routine Mac work, while nuanced questions can still escalate to the model.
changes.effort: Small to medium: define receipt templates and status taxonomy, implement compiler in relay/local agent, add routing metric, and test partial/failed/undo cases.
changes.risk: Templates could omit an important caveat or misstate a partial result. Require explicit unknown fields and say “I could not verify” rather than guessing; retain a one-tap/voice path to request full job evidence. Existing raw receipt remains available.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model cost for routine receipts; saves repeated background calls and context tokens. Small local CPU/storage overhead.
changes.latency_impact: Typically sub-100 ms locally instead of ~1.3 s model round trip.
changes.security_impact: Less sensitive command/output text is sent to models. Keep raw evidence behind authenticated local-agent access and redact it from spoken output by default.
depends_on: Typed shell execution ledger and existing action receipts
Stable job status/effect vocabulary
A routing hook that can identify receipt-only requests

changes.change: Add a dependency-aware preflight and parked-job coordinator before execution. Each job declares required surfaces (shell, browser bridge, accessibility, screen recording, relay); the Mac agent snapshots readiness, immediately returns a typed blocked/parked receipt when a dependency is offline or permission-missing, and subscribes to bridge heartbeats to resume idempotently when readiness returns. Surface the exact blocker, age, retry count, and next action in /jobs and relay status, rather than spending tens of seconds timing out.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request involving Safari or screen control would no longer silently burn 45 seconds and fail; the pendant could say “Safari bridge is offline—open Safari and enable the extension; I’ll continue automatically,” then finish the work when the Mac becomes ready.
changes.effort: Medium: capability requirement metadata, readiness snapshot, parked state machine, heartbeat-triggered resume, idempotency linkage, and receipt/dashboard fields.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could resume work unexpectedly or duplicate a mutation. Mitigate with idempotency keys, per-step receipts, lease expiry, and resume only from the last confirmed step; preserve the existing no-gate maximum-access policy.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; avoids wasted planner retries and long failed computer-use calls. Small local state growth for parked jobs and readiness history.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds preflight; removes 30–120 second dead-end waits and enables immediate completion after bridge recovery.
changes.security_impact: No new authority; readiness metadata may reveal local permissions/device state, so expose only to paired relay and redact paths/details from spoken summaries.
depends_on: durable job lifecycle with explicit parked/resume states
browser heartbeat/command queue
typed action receipts and idempotency keys

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution-confidence envelope to every Mac action and relay receipt. At dispatch, snapshot /observe permission and reachability state; tag UI-mediated actions (click/menu/type/keys and vision loop steps) as verified, unverified, or not-applicable. If Accessibility/input reachability is false, preserve FULL_CONTROL_MODE and still execute, but mark the result unverified with the exact cause, affected steps, and a recovery hint; never emit a plain successful receipt for an action that could not reach the screen. Propagate the envelope through GET /jobs, /jobs/:id/receipts, /ops/snapshot, and the pendant completion message. When reachability later recovers, offer an explicit retry of only unverified action IDs, while stable IDs and existing receipts prevent replaying verified steps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing 'done' when nothing happened on screen. They get an honest spoken/dashboard result such as 'I attempted it, but macOS rejected input from AI Pendant Agent; nothing is verified,' plus a one-tap or spoken retry after permissions are fixed. This adds truth without taking away the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: centralize pre/post reachability sampling in executor.js, extend actionReceipts schema and relay serialization, add unverified-step retry endpoint, and cover permission-failure tests. No approval gate or command restriction is introduced.
changes.risk: A transient permission probe failure could over-label a genuinely completed UI action as unverified; retain raw result, timestamps, and before/after observations, and allow retry only for explicitly unverified IDs. Non-UI shell/API actions remain unaffected. Existing jobs need a backward-compatible 'confidence: unknown' default.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a small local probe per action and a few receipt fields. Storage increases minimally per receipt.
changes.latency_impact: Tens of milliseconds for pre/post observation; no extra model round trip. Retry remains user-initiated or planner-selected after state recovery.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability and prevents false claims; it does not narrow FULL_CONTROL_MODE, add confirmations, or expose new secrets. Permission details should be summarized rather than leaking paths/fingerprints to the relay.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo implementation
/observe permission and inputReachability telemetry
relay job and pendant completion serializers

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution assurance layer around every Mac job: snapshot /observe before execution; classify input reachability, Accessibility, screen recording, browser bridge presence, and shell availability; attach an explicit postcondition recipe to the plan; execute unchanged under FULL_CONTROL_MODE; then re-observe and evaluate the predicate. If UI reachability is false, mark UI steps unavailable and automatically select a shell or browser strategy when equivalent; if no predicate can be checked, return unverified rather than success. Persist before/after evidence, fallback attempts, and recovery hints in the job journal.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets honest answers. A request will no longer sound completed when the agent's UI events were accepted by the harness but never reached the screen, and common failures can recover through another machine or surface without making the owner repeat themselves.
changes.effort: Medium: typed predicate model, pre/post hooks in executor, strategy fallback rules, journal schema, dashboard rendering, and relay receipt mapping. No change to the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.risk: Some actions have no observable postcondition and will become 'unverified', which may feel less convenient; predicates can be stale or too weak. Recover by retaining raw evidence and allowing a follow-up verification command. Do not claim verification from the action receipt alone.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for deterministic checks; one background planner call only when a predicate must be synthesized. Small local journal growth; add retention/compaction.
changes.latency_impact: Typically <1 second for /observe and deterministic checks; fallback or vision adds seconds and should be visible in the receipt.
changes.security_impact: No new restriction or approval gate. Keep page text and command output local where possible; relay receives typed status, hashes, and minimal evidence rather than full private content.
depends_on: A shared typed postcondition schema across Mac, browser, and relay
Existing /observe, /journal, and receipt plumbing
A durable retry/fallback job record

changes.change: Create a local-first cross-surface checkpoint store and protocol. On a pendant save command, ask Mac and browser agents for typed snapshots (active job and receipt, selected tabs and DOM/evidence hashes, focused project/files, pending decisions), have the relay assign a checkpoint ID and encrypt only the minimal index, and expose a revalidation endpoint that marks each fact fresh, changed, inaccessible, or deleted before resume. Resume returns a proposed next step, never an unverified continuation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can stop work on the Mac, walk away with only the pendant, and later continue from the real point they reached instead of hunting through tabs, files, and conversation history.
changes.effort: Medium-high: protocol and schema, local encrypted storage, browser/Mac collectors, relay index, pendant utterances, and dashboard controls.
changes.risk: A snapshot may include more context than intended or become stale. Mitigate with explicit selection, short TTLs, redaction, per-field provenance, local deletion, and a visible stale-state review before resuming.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring model cost; storage is modest. Encryption and local indexing add implementation complexity but no meaningful runtime expense.
changes.latency_impact: Save is parallel and should complete in a few seconds; resume revalidation adds roughly 1–5 seconds before showing the owner the continuation plan.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy versus sending full context to the cloud by keeping content local and syncing only encrypted metadata/hashes; still requires careful key management and deletion semantics.
depends_on: Typed cross-surface snapshot schema
Authenticated Mac and browser collectors
Relay durable state with encryption and TTL
Pendant command/result events
Dashboard support for provenance and stale-state review

changes.change: Add a capability-aware preflight and fast-fail layer shared by relay, mac-planner, browser-extension, and mac-terminal. Before dispatch, query a compact readiness contract (Mac agent health/permissions, browser extension heartbeat and pending-command age, active session/tab binding, relay reachability, and pendant link). Classify each planned step as ready, degraded, or unavailable; route ready steps normally, substitute another surface when safe, and return a typed failure immediately when unavailable instead of letting browser commands sit for ~45 seconds. Persist the preflight snapshot and include it in the existing job receipt, with suggested recovery (e.g. open Safari/enable bridge, grant Screen Recording) but no approval gate or capability restriction.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Requests finish quickly and explain themselves. The owner stops waiting through repeated browser timeouts and gets an actionable answer about which device or permission is actually missing; multi-surface jobs can still use the parts that are online.
changes.effort: Medium: define readiness schema, adapters for existing /ops/status and browser heartbeat/session state, planner dispatch hook, receipt/dashboard rendering, and tests for stale heartbeats and partial failures.
changes.risk: A stale or overly strict health signal could incorrectly skip a workable action, or leak permission/device details into receipts. Mitigate with short TTLs, an explicit degraded/unknown state, fallback dispatch for unknown, and local redaction. No mutation is performed by preflight.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few deterministic JSON reads per job. Saves model and wall-clock cost by preventing doomed retries/timeouts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms for local checks; avoids 45–120 s failed browser attempts and allows partial execution.
changes.security_impact: Read-only readiness metadata only; do not include URLs, page text, tokens, or environment secrets in relay-visible snapshots. Keep detailed permission diagnostics local and send only typed reasons.
depends_on: A stable local readiness endpoint aggregating existing /ops/status, /browser/status, and job/session state
Browser heartbeat freshness and command queue timestamps
Receipt schema support for preflight evidence

changes.change: Add a shell execution manifest and event journal around the existing unrestricted runShell path, without changing authorization. Before launch record a command fingerprint, explicit/inherited cwd, timeout, start time, and redacted environment names; during execution emit heartbeat, byte counts, and bounded stdout/stderr tails; on completion record exit code, signal, duration, termination reason, output hashes, and a best-effort touched-process/file summary. Persist the manifest locally and attach its jobId/receiptId to relay events. Add a typed failure taxonomy (spawn, timeout, nonzero exit, signal, transport loss) and a resumable cursor so a disconnected client can retrieve the exact final result. Keep raw output local by default and expose a redacted excerpt only when requested.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can trust what the Mac actually did and recover from a dropped pendant or relay connection, instead of guessing from a generic failed job. It also makes expensive diagnosis target the real failure and makes repeated commands auditable without reducing the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: wrapper and journal in local-agent, relay event fields, retention/redaction tests, and dashboard detail view.
changes.risk: Manifest overhead and output truncation could hide an important line; preserve a local full log path and hashes, and mark excerpts as incomplete. Process/file summaries are heuristic and must be labeled as such. A crash between spawn and journal flush needs startup reconciliation of child PIDs and orphaned jobs.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; small local JSON/D1 storage per job, bounded by retention. CPU overhead is low except optional process/file sampling.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond launch bookkeeping; heartbeat sampling can be 1–5 seconds. No meaningful delay for short commands.
changes.security_impact: Improves observability while preserving unrestricted execution. Redact values matching token/key/password patterns, never persist full env or stdin by default, and keep raw stdout/stderr on-device unless the owner asks to share it.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and job IDs
A relay subscription/status endpoint for shell jobs
A real local-agent observability reader (the currently granted diagnostics interfaces have no implementation)

changes.change: Implement the already-granted bounded Mac diagnostics interface as a real local-agent endpoint/tool, backed by fixed native queries rather than shell strings. Return a stable typed snapshot with timestamp, freshness, permission state, battery, network, audio/displays, disk, process summary, and local-agent health. Add capability/version negotiation so mac-planner can use it for routine status questions and fall back to unrestricted runShell only for unsupported requests. Include a snapshot ID that can be cited in relay answers and correlated with shell-job manifests.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Routine questions like 'is my Mac online?', 'why did that fail?', or 'is the agent ready?' become fast, cheap, and reliable instead of spending a model turn constructing shell commands. The owner gets accurate explanations of missing Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions and offline browser state.
changes.effort: Small to medium: implement the fixed-query adapter, schema validation, freshness/error handling, and planner integration tests.
changes.risk: A stale snapshot could be mistaken for current truth; every field needs capturedAt and maxAge, and failures must be explicit. Process summaries can expose sensitive names, so default to counts/status and require an intentional detail level.
changes.cost_impact: Usually zero model cost and minimal local CPU; reduces shell and model usage for status requests. Small local/relay storage for recent snapshots.
changes.latency_impact: Typically under 200 ms locally; avoids the current shell round trip and 120-second timeout ceiling.
changes.security_impact: Narrow read-only diagnostics reduce accidental secret exposure for routine reads without narrowing or gating arbitrary shell. Keep detailed process/network data local by default and redact identifiers in relay summaries.
depends_on: Implement the granted mac_read_diagnostics tool (currently no implementation)
A typed snapshot schema shared with mac-planner and relay
Permission-aware local-agent health endpoint

changes.change: Add an execution-capsule layer around every run_shell and typed Mac action. Persist a bounded, redacted record containing normalized command/argv, cwd, timeout, environment key fingerprint (never values or secrets), start/end timestamps, exit code or signal, stdout/stderr byte counts plus tail/digest, host/app identity, and files/URLs/settings named by the action. Classify failures as transient (timeout/agent disconnect), dependency (missing binary/permission), semantic (nonzero result), or likely destructive/unknown. For transient failures, automatically retry only commands explicitly marked idempotent or read-only; otherwise return a diagnosis and a copyable rerun recipe. Link capsule IDs to existing action receipts, jobs, journal, and relay status, with retention/redaction controls.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a voice request fails after the owner walks away, the system can explain what actually happened instead of saying only “failed,” retry harmless status work, and provide an exact rerun or recovery path. This makes unattended Mac work dependable without reducing the owner's deliberately unrestricted access.
changes.effort: Medium: executor wrapper and schema, redaction/digest utility, bounded artifact storage, failure classifier, retry worker, and dashboard/relay rendering; add integration tests for timeout, nonzero exit, disconnect, and secret-containing environments.
changes.risk: Command output can contain private data, and even bounded tails may expose secrets; redact common token patterns and make retention configurable, with an explicit raw-output opt-in. Misclassifying a command as idempotent could duplicate an external effect, so retry eligibility must be opt-in metadata rather than inferred from text. Capsule persistence itself can consume disk; enforce byte/age quotas and degrade to metadata-only.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost. Small local disk writes per action (typically 2–20 KB metadata/tails); no extra cloud call unless the relay requests diagnosis. A cheap background classifier can handle known failure classes; use the expensive model only when diagnosis is ambiguous.
changes.latency_impact: ~1–5 ms local bookkeeping on success; retries add latency only for explicitly idempotent transient failures. Relay response can stream the initial failure immediately while diagnosis/retry continues.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates a new sensitive artifact. Store locally, encrypt/permission it like job history, redact env/output, hash rather than retain full files, and never transmit raw stdout to the relay by default.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and job/journal IDs (implemented)
A bounded local capsule store and redaction utility
Explicit idempotency metadata on action plans
Relay/dashboard support for capsule summaries

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution telemetry and recovery journal around every FULL_CONTROL shell/action dispatch. Record start/heartbeat/finish, argv or shell text hash plus redacted command label, cwd, exit code, signal, timeout, stdout/stderr byte counts and tail, CPU/memory/disk pressure, and whether the process is still alive. Persist large output as a content-addressed local artifact and expose a compact live event stream plus a resume recipe to the relay. On timeout or Mac disconnect, classify the failure (transient transport, process timeout, missing permission, missing binary, nonzero exit), retain the exact receipt, and let the planner retry only when its recipe says that retry is safe; never gate execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a long task fails or the laptop sleeps, the owner gets an honest answer—what ran, how far it got, and whether it can continue—instead of a generic failure or duplicated side effects. The pendant can announce a one-line status while the dashboard opens the full output and undo evidence.
changes.effort: Medium: local-agent journal/artifact store and SSE or polling endpoint, relay ingestion and planner retry schema, dashboard status view, and tests for crash/reconnect/timeout. Reuse existing action receipts and jobs rather than adding approval logic.
changes.risk: Command output may contain secrets; redact known tokens and restrict relay upload to requested artifacts, with local-only default. A bad retry classification could duplicate an irreversible shell command, so retry is advisory and only for explicitly idempotent recipes; recovery is manual otherwise. If journaling fails, execution still proceeds and the receipt marks telemetry incomplete.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost; mostly local disk and a small D1 event record per action. Large stdout stays on the Mac unless explicitly requested.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible dispatch overhead for metadata; live updates add no model call. Failure diagnosis may save repeated planner turns.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without reducing the owner's deliberate unrestricted access. Requires careful redaction, artifact TTL, and authenticated relay-to-Mac event transport.
depends_on: existing actionReceipts.js and /jobs receipts
authenticated Mac-agent observability transport
a durable relay job/result stream

changes.change: Make the granted Mac diagnostic/action interfaces real adapters instead of schema-only tools. Implement mac_read_diagnostics as a fixed-query adapter backed by the local agent's authenticated status routes, mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl as an exact-command compatibility adapter for the already-proven read-only commands, and mac_execute_typed_actions as a typed-to-existing-action translator that preserves FULL_CONTROL_MODE and emits the same action receipts. Return an explicit capability-unavailable error only when the local agent is offline; do not pretend a tool ran.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The hive can currently be granted a tool that always returns 'no implementation yet', so the pendant and relay cannot reliably inspect battery/network/agent health or perform simple Mac controls. Real adapters make routing truthful and let the system choose a fast status path instead of spending a planner turn on a shell command.
changes.effort: Small to medium: wire schemas to existing local-agent routes, map typed actions to mac_run_actions, add contract tests and a capability-health field. Keep arbitrary shell available as the owner requires.
changes.risk: A bad adapter mapping could report stale status or mislabel an action. Include source timestamp, route, and raw error class; fall back visibly to the existing action path rather than silently dropping work.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; fewer planner/model turns for routine checks. Small local implementation and test cost.
changes.latency_impact: Faster routine checks (one typed call rather than planning a shell command); no impact on unrestricted shell execution.
changes.security_impact: No new privilege beyond the existing Mac agent token and FULL_CONTROL policy. Typed calls should inherit the same authenticated transport and receipt/audit trail.
depends_on: local-agent authenticated route contract
existing get_mac_status and mac_run_actions tool implementations
action receipt wrapper

changes.change: Add a non-blocking shell execution envelope around every run_shell call (without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE): record exact command, resolved cwd, start/end timestamps, timeout, exit code/signal, stdout/stderr byte counts plus redacted preview and content hashes, environment fingerprint (keys only), action-risk label, and an automatic retry classification. Persist it in the existing job receipt/journal and expose a 'resume failed job' endpoint that retries only the failed step with the same idempotency key and prior evidence attached.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a command fails or the Mac link drops, the pendant can say exactly what happened instead of guessing, and can resume a long task rather than making the owner repeat it. The owner keeps unrestricted capability; this only makes shell behavior explainable and recoverable.
changes.effort: Medium: executor wrapper, receipt schema, journal projection, retry endpoint, and relay-safe summary formatter.
changes.risk: Command text and output can contain secrets; store full output only locally with short retention, send hashes and redacted previews to relay, and support deletion. Retrying arbitrary commands can duplicate side effects, so default resume is only for a step marked failed before confirmed completion; preserve the current no-gate policy.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and one cheap background classification call only when a failure occurs; no additional realtime calls.
changes.latency_impact: ~5-20 ms local bookkeeping; retries add only the command's own runtime.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without narrowing access. Requires secret scrubbing and strict local receipt permissions.
depends_on: existing actionReceipts/jobTracker/journal integration
relay job status and idempotency plumbing
a durable step/checkpoint representation for multi-action jobs

changes.change: Add an offline-queue reconciliation state machine to browserBridge/browserSessions: every queued command gets createdAt, TTL, originating request, tab fingerprint, and intended effect class; while the extension is offline the queue is visibly 'held' rather than silently pending. On reconnect, revalidate the tab/session fingerprint, collapse idempotent duplicates, expire stale commands with a receipt, and publish a compact reconciliation event to the relay/pendant. Do not auto-replay a command whose target tab changed or whose TTL elapsed; preserve it for explicit re-planning.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent currently reports the browser offline with three pending commands, so the owner cannot tell whether reconnecting will safely continue old work or unexpectedly act on a changed page. This prevents surprise replay and turns abandoned browser work into a clear, recoverable answer.
changes.effort: Medium: queue schema migration, reconnect reconciliation, tab fingerprinting, receipts, and a small dashboard/pendant status surface; test extension restarts and Mac sleep/wake.
changes.risk: A legitimate long-running task could expire or be held. Recovery is to retain the original request and re-plan it against the current tab; never delete without a tombstone. Fingerprints must avoid storing page secrets.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local storage/D1 receipts are small. One cheap classification pass per reconnect batch, not per command.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds on extension reconnect; avoids costly and confusing failed replays.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by preventing stale authenticated actions against a different tab. Store only hashed tab identity/URL origin and redacted command metadata, not DOM or credentials.
depends_on: Shared readiness schema from the proposed preflight capability
Existing browser request IDs/idempotency and action receipts
Relay event delivery to the pendant/dashboard

changes.change: Create a durable cross-device capture ledger with append-only capture IDs, encrypted payloads, delivery acknowledgements, semantic deduplication fingerprints, and merge outcomes. The relay accepts a pendant capture once, the Mac consumes it idempotently after reconnect, and every attempted project/file/reminder/browser association records source, confidence, target, and conflict status. Unresolved items remain in an inbox rather than being silently discarded or misfiled.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A thought spoken while away from the Mac would survive dead batteries, Wi-Fi gaps, sleep, and reconnects, and the owner could trust that it was either filed exactly once or visibly awaiting review.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: protocol and schema design, encrypted relay persistence, pendant retry state, Mac ingestion adapters, conflict UI, and fault-injection tests for crashes between acknowledgement and write.
changes.risk: Duplicate delivery, incorrect project inference, or partial writes could create confusing records. Idempotency keys, immutable originals, atomic local writes where possible, and an explicit unresolved inbox provide recovery.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable-storage cost; one background transcription/classification call per capture. Raw-audio retention can be capped to control cost.
changes.latency_impact: Acknowledgement is immediate; final filing is asynchronous and may wait for Mac/browser availability.
changes.security_impact: Captures may contain private speech and authenticated-work context. Encrypt in transit and at rest, minimize raw-audio retention, keep credentials local to Mac/browser, and expose provenance without exposing secrets.
depends_on: Pendant capture trigger and retry state
Relay durable encrypted storage
Mac project/file/reminder ingestion API
Browser context lookup with redacted evidence

changes.change: Add a synchronous browser preflight and circuit breaker in the Mac/browser bridge: before enqueueing any browser_* action, consult the latest heartbeat/status, return a typed OFFLINE result immediately when no extension has polled recently, and mark queued commands as blocked_until_online rather than letting them time out after ~45 seconds. On the next heartbeat, retry each command with its original session/request id and emit one receipt linking the preflight failure, retry, and final result. Expose a compact readiness object (extension age, pending count, required Mac permissions) for relay and pendant status queries.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Browser requests fail honestly in seconds instead of leaving the owner waiting nearly a minute, and a spoken Mac-status answer can say exactly whether the issue is Safari/extension, Accessibility, or Screen Recording. When the owner reopens the bridge, work resumes instead of being lost or duplicated.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: bridge heartbeat freshness/circuit-breaker, queue state transition and receipt linkage, plus one status projection consumed by relay/mac-planner.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could be misclassified as offline; use a conservative freshness window and retain manual retry. Retrying a write could duplicate effects, so only auto-retry commands carrying an idempotency key; otherwise require planner reissue. Existing pending commands need a migration state.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; saves repeated planner calls and long failed execution attempts. Local implementation only.
changes.latency_impact: Offline response under 100 ms instead of ~45 s; online path adds one local status check, typically <50 ms.
changes.security_impact: No new data access. Status exposes only extension/permission health, not page contents; preserve existing auth and session affinity.
depends_on: A browser heartbeat/status endpoint with timestamp and pending-command visibility
Stable idempotency keys and receipt linkage across browser retries
Relay/mac-planner status projection

changes.change: Add a machine-readable Mac capability health contract and reconciliation loop. /ops/status should emit per-capability states (available, degraded, blocked, stale), blocker codes, observedAt, remediation kind, and a monotonic health revision. The relay/mac-planner should heartbeat browser state, reconcile pending command IDs, and only then derive an overall readiness summary; dashboard and pendant consume the same typed result.
