changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer about what the Mac can do right now instead of a generic failure after a long task. Stale browser work is surfaced and recoverable, while missing Accessibility or Screen Recording is explained before GUI automation begins.
changes.effort: Medium: route/schema changes, browser queue reconciliation, one shared reducer, dashboard card, and pendant intent wiring; likely 2–4 engineering days plus failure-mode tests.
changes.risk: A bad reducer could report the Mac ready when it is not, or repeatedly retry stale browser commands. Recover with revisioned snapshots, bounded retries, expiry, and preserving raw status receipts for diagnosis. No action should be silently discarded.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; fewer failed planner calls and retries should reduce spend. Small local JSON/D1 storage for health snapshots and command reconciliation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local status aggregation and usually one browser heartbeat; target under 500 ms and no LLM call on the happy path.
changes.security_impact: Expose only capability state, blocker codes, and timestamps to relay/dashboard; keep filesystem paths, browser URLs, and auth details local. Health receipts should be redacted and access-controlled.
depends_on: mac-agent /ops/status remains available
browser command queue exposes request IDs and expiry/ack state
shared typed context projection so readiness facts are not copied into per-surface prompts

changes.change: Add a cross-surface outcome-verification stage after execution. For eligible tasks, the Mac executor and browser bridge each publish independent typed observations tied to the same action ID; a deterministic verifier compares the expected postcondition against both observations (for example, browser confirmation plus local notification/history). If observations disagree or one surface is unavailable, mark outcome-unknown and present the evidence instead of reporting success. Store compact hashes and source locators, not duplicated page contents.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a trustworthy answer that something actually happened, rather than a confident report that a click or command was sent. This is especially valuable when a browser submission, Mac automation, or network timeout leaves the real-world outcome uncertain.
changes.effort: Medium to high: define postcondition contracts for common actions, add observation adapters to Mac and browser surfaces, implement a deterministic verifier, and expose disagreement receipts in the dashboard and pendant.
changes.risk: Some legitimate actions have no observable confirmation or produce delayed state, causing false 'unknown' results. Recover with action-specific verification windows, explicit eventual-state polling, and a manual 'check again' path; never convert uncertainty into success.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and polling cost; deterministic verification avoids extra model calls. Optional background summarization is inexpensive and only used for complex evidence.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–5 seconds depending on confirmation polling; immediate voice acknowledgment can say 'sent, verifying' while the background verifier runs.
changes.security_impact: Keep authenticated evidence local where possible; send only typed outcomes, redacted snippets, hashes, and source metadata to the relay. Do not expose private page content merely to achieve a second opinion.
depends_on: Cross-surface task envelope with shared action IDs and checkpoints
Typed observation adapters for Mac and browser
Action-specific postcondition definitions
Durable receipts and dashboard presentation for outcome-unknown states

changes.change: Add a shell execution bundle and replay/failure-recovery layer without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE or adding gates. For every run_shell action, persist a redacted command record plus cwd, timeout, host identity, start/end, exit code/signal, stdout/stderr artifact references, and a before/after manifest of touched files and git worktree state. Classify failures (not-found, permission, timeout, nonzero, transport) and expose `rerun`, `retry-with-diagnosis`, and `revert-if-supported` operations keyed by the existing job/action IDs. Secret-looking env values and tokens are hashed/redacted, while the original command remains available locally for trusted replay.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails or changes the wrong project, the owner can see exactly what ran, where, and what it changed, then recover or rerun it instead of asking the agent to guess. Repeated diagnostics become reproducible, and the agent can automatically explain a timeout or missing-directory failure.
changes.effort: Medium: shell wrapper and artifact store, git/file manifest collection, failure classifier, replay endpoints, dashboard/relay receipt fields, and tests for timeout plus partial-write recovery.
changes.risk: Capturing manifests can add latency and may miss changes outside observed roots; redaction can hide useful values; replaying a command can repeat irreversible effects. Preserve the current no-gate policy, mark replay as potentially irreversible, cap artifact sizes, and never claim a revert unless verification succeeds.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and CPU cost per shell job; no model/API cost. Dominant cost is stdout/stderr and manifest retention, bounded with size caps and retention cleanup.
changes.latency_impact: Approximately 50–300 ms for metadata and git/file manifests on normal projects; no extra model round trip. Large trees should use declared/learned roots and sampling.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability while retaining unrestricted execution. Redaction and local-only raw command storage reduce accidental secret propagation to relay/dashboard; network access remains unrestricted by owner policy.
depends_on: implemented action receipts (chg-5fc73ce3)
durable job IDs and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
a bounded local artifact/retention store

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface outcome ledger with immutable intent IDs and typed postconditions. The planner records the requested goal and expected predicates before dispatch; Mac, browser, relay, and pendant append signed observations tied to that ID. A verifier re-reads authoritative state after each mutation, evaluates predicates, and emits completed, partially_applied, reverted, or unverifiable with evidence pointers. This is an outcome ledger, not another action log: a successful process exit or click is insufficient evidence.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust “done” only when the real result is visible, and gets an honest explanation when the system cannot prove it. It prevents silent half-completion across a sleeping Mac, stale browser tab, dropped relay link, or interrupted voice session.
changes.effort: High: shared event schema and ID propagation, local signed append-only storage, browser readback, Mac predicate evaluators, relay reconciliation, and dashboard/pendant rendering.
changes.risk: External systems can change between checks, some outcomes are inherently unverifiable, and extra reads can expose sensitive data. Use freshness windows, source provenance, redacted evidence, and never collapse unknown into success.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and deterministic compute; occasional browser reloads and one cheap summarization call for ambiguous evidence. No recurring realtime-model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a readback phase, typically milliseconds locally and seconds for authenticated browser verification; expose pending state immediately.
changes.security_impact: Improves integrity through signed, provenance-linked observations, but creates a sensitive cross-device event trail. Encrypt local records, minimize relay projection, and apply retention by sensitivity.
depends_on: A typed goal-to-postcondition schema
Cross-surface correlation IDs in Mac and browser jobs
Authenticated browser readback and Mac predicate evaluators
Relay/pendant support for outcome states

changes.change: Add a cross-surface capability preflight and circuit breaker before dispatching Mac/browser jobs. The Mac agent should publish a compact, cached readiness vector (bridge heartbeat age, browser online/tab binding, Accessibility and Screen Recording status, app automation grants, disk/battery/network, queue depth) with a short TTL. The relay/planner consults it before dispatch: fail browser work immediately when the extension is offline instead of waiting ~45 seconds, purge or mark stale pending browser commands with an explicit expiry, and select a declared fallback (Mac shell/public web/pendant-only explanation) when one exists. On recovery heartbeat, retry only idempotent read steps with the original request/idempotency key; never replay mutations automatically. Include the preflight snapshot and decision in the job receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an immediate, truthful answer instead of a minute-long 'failed' job when Safari or permissions are unavailable. When the bridge comes back, safe reads can resume without repeating a form submission, and every failure explains whether the problem was browser, permission, network, or queue health.
changes.effort: Moderate: readiness endpoint/schema in local-agent, heartbeat and stale-command sweeper in browser bridge, planner dispatch hook, and receipt/dashboard rendering. Add integration tests for offline->online and mutation retry suppression.
changes.risk: A stale readiness cache could incorrectly choose a fallback or miss a newly recovered bridge; use a short TTL and recheck on dispatch. Incorrect idempotency classification could duplicate a mutation, so default unknown actions to non-retryable. Sweeping commands must preserve active leases and audit every expiration.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; reduces wasted planner/realtime calls and 45-second local job waits. Small local CPU/storage cost for heartbeat snapshots and queue metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a local sub-100ms preflight when healthy; cuts known-offline browser failures from ~45s to near-instant. Recovery retries remain background.
changes.security_impact: Readiness exposes permission and device-health metadata only to the authenticated local agent/relay; do not include URLs, page text, tokens, or command payloads. Receipts should redact sensitive paths and browser data.
depends_on: A typed readiness schema shared by local-agent, browser bridge, relay, and planner
Stable request/idempotency keys and action mutability classification in job receipts
A stale-command lease/expiry field in the browser command queue

changes.change: Add an execution-truth layer around every Mac UI action: before dispatch, attach the latest /observe reachability and permission state; after dispatch, run a bounded postcondition probe (foreground app, window title, file/reminder existence, or typed action result). Store an explicit outcome enum—completed, failed, or unverified/no-op—with the exact blocker (for this Mac, Accessibility is granted to a different binary and Screen Recording is missing). Emit a machine-readable remediation event that the relay and pendant can speak, and let faculty-action retry through a non-UI path when one exists. This is observability and recovery, not a gate: FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unrestricted.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will stop saying an action succeeded when the Mac demonstrably did nothing, and can tell the owner the one concrete fix or use a reliable fallback instead of making them debug silent failures.
changes.effort: Medium: add pre/post probes to the executor and receipt schema, classify a small set of common postconditions, persist remediation events, and wire relay speech plus retry selection.
changes.risk: Postcondition probes may be inconclusive or add latency; label those as unverified rather than failure, cap probe time, and preserve the raw action receipt for recovery. No action is blocked.
changes.cost_impact: Small additional local CPU and storage; one short background-model call only when the result is ambiguous, otherwise no API cost.
changes.latency_impact: ~100–500 ms for local probes; retries may add normal command latency.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without narrowing authority. Permission details and paths stay on the Mac unless a remediation summary is explicitly sent to the relay.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo records
GET /observe reachability probe
GET /ops/status readiness state

changes.change: Add a structured execution envelope around every run_shell dispatch without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE or blocking anything. Persist cwd (resolved path), argv/command hash, start/end timestamps, exit code/signal, timeout classification, stdout/stderr separately with bounded tails plus byte counts, environment fingerprint (names and hashes only, never values), and a small post-failure probe (cwd existence, executable lookup, disk space, network reachability only when the command itself attempted network). Attach this envelope to the existing action receipt and expose it through /jobs/:id/receipts, /journal, and the relay-facing job completion event. Add a retry hint classifier for not-found, permission, timeout, and transient network failures; hints are advisory and never auto-retry or refuse execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails—or succeeds in the wrong place—the owner gets an honest explanation instead of 'command failed'. The agent can recover from wrong-directory and missing-tool mistakes quickly, and the pendant can report exactly what ran while the owner was away. This directly prevents the repeated project-location dead ends without reducing the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: executor wrapper, receipt schema migration, bounded output storage, four failure probes, dashboard/journal serialization, and tests for timeout/nonzero/oversized output.
changes.risk: Command output can contain secrets; redact known credential patterns and keep only bounded tails, with configurable retention. A probe must never alter the command result. Large output and malformed encodings need defensive handling. Existing receipts remain backward-compatible when the envelope is absent.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; modest local disk/D1 growth bounded by tail limits and retention. Small CPU overhead per shell action for hashing and probes.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero for success; roughly 50–300 ms for failure probes, with strict per-probe deadlines.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates another place where output could leak. Store command text and environment names, never environment values; redact tokens/keys and apply the existing audio/job retention policy to envelopes.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo implementation
A bounded read-only diagnostics implementation for post-failure probes

changes.change: Add a non-blocking preflight attestation and execution telemetry envelope to every Mac job: snapshot /observe and /ops/status immediately before dispatch; attach capability facts (inputReachability, accessibility, screenRecording, browser online), command/action ID, cwd, duration, exit code, bounded stdout/stderr digests, and post-state observation to the receipt. If a UI/browser capability is unreachable, mark the step 'not-delivered' before attempting it; retain FULL_CONTROL_MODE and do not add approval gates. Automatically classify failures as retryable (bridge/browser offline, transient timeout) versus configuration-required (permissions, missing app), and offer a one-click retry after state changes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing 'done' when nothing reached the screen, and gets an exact explanation and recovery path instead of spending repeated voice turns guessing whether the Mac or browser is at fault. Shell remains maximally capable, while every command becomes auditable and failures become recoverable.
changes.effort: Medium: shared pre/post wrapper in executor plus receipt schema and dashboard/voice formatting; no shell-policy change.
changes.risk: Preflight can become stale between snapshot and action, and bounded output may omit useful details. Label it as an attestation, capture post-state, and preserve raw local logs for explicit debugging. Never claim UI success solely from process exit.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local JSON/log storage grows roughly 2–10 KB per job after truncation.
changes.latency_impact: ~100–300 ms for local preflight/postflight; no model latency.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but command metadata may expose paths. Redact environment values and secrets; hash command text where full text is unnecessary. Does not narrow owner-authorized execution.
depends_on: /observe and /ops/status remain available to the local agent
Receipt schema supports capability evidence and a not-delivered status

changes.change: Add a cross-surface capability preflight and failure-recovery broker, without restricting FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Before dispatch, query cached liveness/permission state for Mac, browser bridge, relay, and any requested app; attach a short-lived preflight snapshot to the job. If a target is unavailable, fail fast with a typed reason (offline, permission missing, stale session, or timeout) instead of waiting ~45 seconds, and select only an explicitly safe alternate: public-page reads can fall back to relay/read_web_page, while private authenticated work is parked as a durable retry bound to the same tab/session. On reconnection, retry only failed, idempotent steps and reconcile receipts so the owner never gets duplicate actions. Surface a single spoken explanation plus a dashboard diagnostic link.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can say immediately whether something is blocked by the Mac or browser, and still get public answers when the private browser is asleep. Long waits and mysterious failures disappear, while private work resumes later instead of being lost or accidentally repeated.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight schema and 10–15 typed failure states; health-cache hooks in planner/execute; idempotency-aware retry queue; relay fallback adapter; dashboard and spoken receipt changes. No permission gate or capability reduction.
changes.risk: A stale health snapshot could misroute a job, and an overly broad fallback could expose data to the relay. Enforce source classification: authenticated content never falls back to public/relay paths; require session affinity for retries; expire snapshots quickly; preserve failed receipts and provide an explicit discard operation.
changes.cost_impact: Small background health probes and a few hundred tokens of structured metadata per job; avoids wasting expensive planner calls and 45-second failed browser attempts. Relay fallback incurs normal read/API cost only when selected.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–150 ms for cached preflight; removes tens of seconds from known-offline failures. Reconnection retries are asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves security observability without adding gates. Private tab/session identifiers remain local and are never sent to public fallback; typed provenance records where each result came from.
depends_on: A durable job/retry store (the existing browser runner backlog is still open)
A functioning browser heartbeat endpoint/extension polling loop
Implementations for the newly granted read-only Mac diagnostics tools
Shared action idempotency keys and receipt reconciliation

changes.change: Add a non-gating Shell Execution Envelope around the existing FULL_CONTROL run_shell path. Preserve arbitrary commands and unattended execution, but emit a typed per-command receipt: command ID and SHA-256 (not plaintext in cross-surface summaries), resolved cwd, start/queue times, timeout, exit code/signal, duration, stdout/stderr byte counts plus bounded tails, touched-file hints where observable, and whether the result is reversible. On failure, run a small deterministic diagnosis pass (ENOENT/cwd, permission, timeout, missing app, network/DNS, nonzero exit) and attach concrete next-step or retry parameters; stream phase events to relay/pendant and dashboard, and persist full detail locally with configurable retention. Add idempotency metadata so the planner can deliberately retry a failed command without accidentally replaying a mutation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says “do it” from the pendant, they get a useful completion or failure explanation instead of a vague timeout—especially after the Mac has gone offline, a path is wrong, or a command partially ran. They can leave the Mac unattended and later hear exactly what happened, where it ran, and whether retrying is safe, without sacrificing the maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: executor wrapper, streaming event schema, local receipt storage/retention, deterministic classifier, relay/dashboard rendering, and planner prompt/tool result integration.
changes.risk: Capturing output can expose secrets, and touched-file inference can be incomplete. Redact known credential-shaped values, keep full stdout/stderr local by default, cap tails, and mark inference as best-effort. A retry recommendation must never imply success; duplicate mutation risk is handled by explicit idempotency/retry metadata, not by blocking execution.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model/API cost for deterministic classification; modest local disk for bounded receipts. A small background model call is optional only when deterministic diagnosis is inconclusive.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful added latency on success if events are written asynchronously; failure diagnosis should be under 200 ms, with no automatic long retry.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without narrowing authority. Cross-surface payloads carry hashes, redacted summaries, and bounded tails; raw command/output remains on the Mac unless the owner explicitly requests it.
depends_on: Existing job receipts and /jobs/:jobId/receipts
Relay pipeline event delivery and dashboard job view
A shared action/result schema used by Mac planner, relay, and pendant

changes.change: Add a live capability-preflight and fallback router before Mac/browser jobs. Snapshot /ops/status plus browser heartbeat and relay reachability into a short-lived matrix (shell available, UI permissions, screen capture, browser online, pending queue). Annotate each planned step with required capability; if unavailable, automatically choose a viable alternate (shell/AppleScript for app-state work, browser queue for later, relay background job) or return one precise repair instruction. Never block trusted FULL_CONTROL shell actions; this is observability and routing only. Include the matrix and chosen fallback in the job receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Requests stop failing mysteriously when the Mac lacks Accessibility/Screen Recording or the browser extension is offline. The pendant can say exactly what happened and still complete the parts that do not need the unavailable surface, instead of making the owner repeat themselves.
changes.effort: Medium: status snapshot schema, planner annotations, fallback selection, heartbeat freshness/TTL, and receipt/dashboard rendering.
changes.risk: A stale status could choose the wrong route or queue work unexpectedly. Use short TTLs, recheck immediately before execution, mark assumptions in receipts, and preserve the existing unrestricted shell path.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small local status/heartbeat read per job. Saves planner tokens and retries.
changes.latency_impact: ~50–150 ms local preflight; avoids multi-second failed UI attempts.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no approval gate. Status contains permission and connectivity metadata only; redact paths/tokens from receipts.
depends_on: A typed representation of Mac action requirements and results
Browser heartbeat/command queue with request IDs
Durable job receipts (chg-5fc73ce3)

changes.change: Extend the existing action receipts with a shell execution envelope: normalized command digest, cwd, selected non-secret environment facts, start/end monotonic timestamps, timeout/signal, exit status, stdout/stderr byte counts, bounded tail plus content-addressed full output artifact, and a retry classification (transient, dependency/permission, deterministic failure). Stream progress events to the pendant for jobs longer than a few seconds, while keeping raw output local unless the owner asks for it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails, the owner gets an immediate, intelligible explanation and can resume from the failed command instead of wondering whether anything ran. Long jobs feel alive on the pendant, and huge logs do not flood spoken context.
changes.effort: Medium: wrap runShell result handling, local artifact retention/expiry, progress events, and receipt/dashboard fields.
changes.risk: Command output may contain secrets; default to local storage, redact common token/password patterns, cap spoken previews, and expose explicit artifact deletion. A bad retry classifier could repeat a non-idempotent command, so retries must remain advisory and never automatic for shell.
changes.cost_impact: Low local disk use with bounded retention; lower model cost by sending a short failure summary instead of full logs.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible overhead; progress streaming adds no blocking round trip.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without restricting FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Sensitive output stays on the Mac by default; only hashes and redacted summaries cross the relay.
depends_on: Implemented action receipts (chg-5fc73ce3)
A durable local job/log retention policy

changes.change: Add an append-only execution event journal beside the existing job store. Every action (including run_shell) gets a generated traceId, parentTraceId, modelTier, intent hash, start/heartbeat/end timestamps, timeout reason, exit code, stderr fingerprint, bounded stdout summary, retry lineage, and an explicit undoability verdict. Expose GET /journal/stream?since=<cursor> (SSE or long-poll) and GET /journal/:traceId, while retaining raw output locally. Add a cheap deterministic failure classifier and idempotency-aware retry metadata, but do not block or require confirmation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the pendant what a command is doing and receive a trustworthy answer even after the voice session ends. Repeated browser failures and shell failures become diagnosable; successful work can be resumed rather than repeated blindly. Existing receipts record results, but the live journal currently reports 113 unattributed jobs and no undoable actions, so it cannot explain execution history well.
changes.effort: Medium: event schema and writer in executor/jobTracker, stream endpoint, bounded local retention/rotation, and relay adapter; add integration tests for timeout, crash, reconnect, and concurrent jobs.
changes.risk: Journal growth, accidental sensitive output leakage, and event-order races. Keep raw streams local, cap summaries, redact common secret patterns, use monotonic sequence plus fsync checkpoints, and have the relay discard malformed or out-of-order events. If the stream fails, ordinary execution continues and GET /jobs remains the fallback.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; modest local disk (for example 25–100 MB rotating journal) and small CPU overhead per event. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds per event locally; SSE delivery under 300 ms when connected. No added model latency to execution.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without narrowing the owner's deliberate unrestricted shell policy. Raw command/output remains on-device; upstream receives redacted metadata and opt-in excerpts only.
depends_on: Stable local-agent authentication for the new stream
Relay resumable cursor protocol
Shared redaction and failure taxonomy across Mac and browser harnesses

changes.change: Build a trace-oriented 'What ran?' view that groups Mac and browser actions by owner request, displays a compact timeline with live/failed/retried states, and lets the owner filter by failure fingerprint or idempotency key. Selecting a failed step shows the exact redacted error, affected surface, attempt lineage, and a one-tap 'resume from here' request to the planner; never silently replays it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Instead of searching 120 jobs or hearing an incomplete voice response, the owner can see whether a long task is alive, what changed, and where it stopped. The repeated browser_list_tabs and browser_navigate failures become visible patterns rather than repeated mystery failures.
changes.effort: Medium: consume the proposed journal stream, add grouping and cursor persistence, and wire resume requests to planner with explicit owner invocation.
changes.risk: Grouping can mis-associate parallel actions or expose too much detail. Use trace parentage rather than time proximity, redact by default, and show raw output only after an explicit expand action. Resume must create a new trace linked to the old one.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; modest dashboard storage for cursors and rendered metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Live updates within one heartbeat; no effect on action execution.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental leakage by making redacted summaries the default. Authenticated Mac-agent access and per-owner dashboard authorization remain required.
depends_on: Mac execution event journal with trace IDs
Relay cursor/replay support
Planner resume API that carries idempotency and attempt lineage

changes.change: Add a resumable shell-runner beneath run_shell: create a job manifest with stable step IDs and a command hash, execute each step in its own process group, persist bounded stdout/stderr and exit metadata locally, emit heartbeat/phase events, and write a checkpoint only after successful completion. Expose status, tail, cancel, retry-failed, and resume-from-checkpoint operations; resume refuses to replay a completed step unless the planner explicitly marks it idempotent. Attach these events to the existing action receipts and relay job stream rather than replacing receipts or adding approval gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A terminal task can continue safely after the owner leaves, show real progress on the pendant, and recover from a failed step without rerunning the entire workflow or guessing what happened.
changes.effort: Medium-high: new local-agent shell job runner plus event persistence, relay forwarding, planner schema, and pendant status controls; integration tests for timeout, crash, cancellation, and non-idempotent steps.
changes.risk: A process may leave child processes or partial side effects after cancellation; use process-group teardown, explicit dirty/unknown state, and never auto-resume an uncertain step. Log truncation could hide useful context, so retain a local full artifact with bounded relay excerpts. Existing one-shot run_shell remains unchanged as a fallback.
changes.cost_impact: Small local disk usage with rotating per-job artifacts; negligible API cost for event transport, with optional cheap summarization of large logs.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement and low-latency milestone events; process startup adds roughly tens of milliseconds per step, while resume avoids repeating long work.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no reduction of FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Keep full logs local by default, redact common credentials before relay/model transmission, and record command hashes plus touched paths in the existing receipts.
depends_on: The existing action receipt/undo implementation (chg-5fc73ce3)
A relay endpoint and durable event schema for Mac job progress
Planner support for step idempotency and checkpoint manifests

changes.change: Add a live Mac readiness panel and machine-readable readiness contract: distinguish required permissions from optional capabilities, show the exact blocked operation (for example, mac-vision unavailable because Accessibility and Screen Recording are not granted), last heartbeat, browser connectivity, and the safest recovery action. Let mac-planner request a one-click/open-System-Settings route and re-probe automatically after the owner changes a permission; publish the same concise state to the pendant instead of exposing raw ops JSON.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently experiences a silent failure or an agent that says it cannot see the screen. They should immediately know what is missing, where to fix it, and when the Mac has become usable again—especially when they are wearing the pendant away from the dashboard.
changes.effort: Small-medium: normalize /ops/status into a versioned readiness schema, add dashboard cards and pendant-friendly summaries, and implement a permission-change re-probe loop.
changes.risk: Permission labels can become stale or incorrectly imply that a capability is available; timestamp every probe and keep the raw diagnostic detail available. Opening System Settings should be reversible and never claim success until a fresh probe confirms it.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API/model cost; a few local probes after a settings change.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one lightweight probe after recovery, typically sub-second; no impact on ordinary shell execution.
changes.security_impact: Only reports permission state and app names already visible to the local agent; do not transmit window contents or screen frames. No execution gates are introduced.
depends_on: A stable /ops/status readiness schema
Existing Mac dashboard and relay-to-pendant status path

changes.change: Build a local-first change ledger independent of action receipts: sample filesystem metadata and process/app activity into rotating time buckets, correlate events with agent job/action IDs when available, and label attribution as direct, likely, or unknown. Store only paths, sizes, timestamps, hashes, process identity, and event references by default; retain file contents nowhere unless explicitly captured. Add a query API that returns a signed time-window manifest and evidence pointers for the planner and relay.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: After leaving the Mac unattended, the owner can ask exactly what changed and get a useful answer even when the agent did not cause it, instead of relying on guesses or a partial list of agent receipts.
changes.effort: High: native event collection and permission-aware fallbacks, local encrypted rotation, correlation with existing jobs, query/signature format, and tests across sync, editor, installer, and agent activity.
changes.risk: Event streams may be incomplete or noisy, and process attribution can be ambiguous; report coverage and confidence rather than claiming certainty. Metadata can expose sensitive filenames, so default retention must be short and deletion must be verifiable. Collection should degrade gracefully when permissions are absent.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing CPU/disk overhead if event sampling is bounded; no routine model cost. A modest local encrypted ledger is required, with configurable retention.
changes.latency_impact: Minimal background overhead; common time-window queries should be near-instant from indexes, while correlation across large windows may take seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without granting new control authority. Keep raw ledger on the Mac, encrypt at rest, and send only redacted aggregates/evidence references through relay unless explicitly requested.
depends_on: A local encrypted metadata store and retention/deletion mechanism
Correlation hooks into existing action receipts and job IDs
A versioned relay query/result contract and confidence-aware summary UI

changes.change: Add a durable shell execution journal and resumable command runner without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: before each run, record a command fingerprint, cwd, selected environment facts, timeout, and declared outputs; stream bounded stdout/stderr chunks and exit state into the job record; on timeout, disconnect, or agent restart, classify the last checkpoint as not-started/running/finished/unknown, avoid blind reruns of unknown commands, and expose a resume/retry action that can continue from an explicit step boundary. Attach an artifact manifest (paths, sizes, hashes) and a reversible/irreversible hint to the receipt, with secret-pattern redaction applied only to logs, never to execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Long Mac tasks would stop disappearing when the laptop sleeps or the bridge drops. The owner could ask from the pendant, leave, and later receive an honest result plus the files produced, rather than a vague failure or a dangerous duplicate run. It also makes the existing maximum-access policy more trustworthy by showing exactly what happened.
changes.effort: Medium: local-agent journal schema and streaming (~2–3 days), shell wrapper/checkpoint protocol (~2 days), relay job resume endpoint and dashboard/pendant receipt integration (~2 days), failure-injection tests (~1 day).
changes.risk: A command with external side effects can still be duplicated if it dies after performing the side effect but before recording completion; unknown states must therefore remain unknown and require an explicit retry choice. Hashing large outputs costs I/O, and log redaction can hide useful text if overbroad. Recovery is to preserve raw local job state, cap hashes by size, and mark every inferred field with confidence.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for shell work; roughly 1–3 KB of D1 metadata plus bounded log chunks per run, with larger stdout/artifacts retained locally and only summarized to the relay. Engineering/storage cost is the main expense.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful added latency before launch (one journal write); streaming adds small local I/O. Receipt generation may take under a second, while hashing large artifacts is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding gates. Environment snapshots and command output can contain secrets, so default relay projection must exclude env values and redact credential-shaped output; artifact paths should be owner-visible but not broadcast to other surfaces unless requested.
depends_on: A durable job/receipt contract shared by local-agent and relay
A relay resume/status endpoint
Pendant spoken progress and completion receipt support
No change to the owner's FULL_CONTROL_MODE policy

changes.change: Implement the already-granted bounded Mac diagnostics as a real typed RPC, with one fixed query per call and a versioned response envelope: host identity, OS, hardware, battery, network, audio, displays, permissions, disk, processes, and local-agent health. Include collectedAt, source, freshness, and unavailable reasons; route it through the same relay job/receipt path so a remote planner can distinguish 'false' from 'not measured'. Do not expose arbitrary command execution through this interface; keep FULL_CONTROL shell unchanged for execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The hive could stop guessing whether the Mac is awake, reachable, permissioned, connected to Wi‑Fi, or playing audio. The pendant could say “your Mac is online but Screen Recording is off” instead of silently queuing work, and planners could choose the browser, relay, or Mac based on current facts.
changes.effort: Small to medium: implement the fixed query mapper in local-agent, add authenticated RPC/response validation, then wire the relay and dashboard status card; add tests for unavailable permissions and stale responses.
changes.risk: A process summary or network detail may reveal more than intended, and stale health can misroute work. Minimize by returning coarse process categories by default, sensitivity-tagging fields, applying a short TTL, and making freshness mandatory in every response. Recovery is to fall back to the existing bridge heartbeat and report unknown.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model cost; one small status payload per diagnostic request and modest local CPU. Dashboard storage should retain only the latest snapshot, not a history of process or network details.
changes.latency_impact: Typically sub-second locally, up to a few seconds if the Mac bridge is asleep. It should never block the pendant conversation; use cached data with an age label.
changes.security_impact: Read-only and bounded, but still sensitive. Require the existing local-agent authentication, omit usernames/paths/SSID unless explicitly requested, and make relay projections field-scoped.
depends_on: Implement one of the granted mac_readonly_diagnostics interfaces (currently schema-only)
An authenticated local-agent diagnostics route
A typed freshness/sensitivity schema shared with relay and faculty-perception

changes.change: Replace the fixed 16-kHz uplink/24-kHz downlink audio contract with a negotiated adaptive superwideband profile. The pendant should capture and Opus-encode at 24 kHz when the LTE-M link has headroom, packetize within the modem's ~2 kB TLS limit, and use Opus in-band FEC/DTX plus a small bounded jitter buffer. A relay-side congestion controller should observe RTT, queue depth, and missing sequence numbers, prioritize downlink speech during overlap, and step the uplink through 24-kHz -> 16-kHz profiles before loss becomes catastrophic; restore 24 kHz after a hysteresis window. Keep the relay transparent (no needless transcode), while the ESP32 bridge resamples the negotiated stream to its fixed 44.1-kHz SBC output.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A quiet call can actually sound like the intended 24-kHz superwideband path, but talking over the agent will no longer silently lose roughly eight seconds of the owner's speech on a saturated LTE-M link. Quality degrades briefly and intelligibly instead of failing unpredictably.
changes.effort: Medium-high: revise nRF9160 I2S/Opus framing and profile negotiation, relay scheduler and metrics, and bridge buffer tests; add an automated overlap/congestion test using recorded audio (no microphone needed).
changes.risk: Changing the full-duplex I2S clock is risky because the single peripheral currently requires byte-identical TX/RX configuration; a bad clock or jitter-buffer bound can cause underruns or silence. Recover with a feature-flagged profile, watchdog fallback to the proven 16/24 contract, and sequence-numbered traces for post-call diagnosis.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible incremental API cost; modest LTE-M traffic increase only while 24-kHz uplink is viable. Engineering/test cost dominates, especially RF contention and Bluetooth interoperability testing.
changes.latency_impact: Negotiation adds at most one short measurement window; FEC and jitter buffering add roughly 20–60 ms, trading a little latency for far fewer gaps.
changes.security_impact: No new data class or third party is required. Audio remains in the existing TLS WebSocket; telemetry should contain sequence/timing/loss metadata, never decoded speech.
depends_on: An agreed audio-profile negotiation message shared by pendant firmware and cloud-relay
A safe way to change/test the nRF9160 full-duplex I2S clock and Opus sample-rate configuration
Relay-side packet-loss/RTT instrumentation and an automated two-way congestion test

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution journal and preflight circuit breaker around every cross-surface action. Before dispatch, snapshot target health (Mac bridge, browser extension, permissions, session/tab affinity); if unhealthy, emit a typed blocked-before-start receipt immediately, enqueue a recovery plan, and resume only from a checkpoint whose prior outcome is certain. Record monotonic start/deadline/heartbeat timestamps, retry reason, and whether an outcome is unknown. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted shell exactly as-is; this is telemetry, routing, and recovery—not a gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request will stop wasting nearly a minute on a browser command that could never run, and a dropped connection will not make the agent guess whether it already clicked or submitted something. The pendant can say “browser offline; reconnecting” quickly, while the Mac and relay continue recovery in the background.
changes.effort: Medium: shared typed journal schema, preflight adapters for Mac/browser/relay, checkpoint state machine, and dashboard/pendant event projection; integration tests for offline, timeout, reconnect, and unknown-outcome cases.
changes.risk: A bad checkpoint classification could skip a needed step or duplicate a reversible one. Default unknown outcome to pause and report, use idempotency keys where supported, and preserve raw receipts for manual recovery. Journal growth is controlled by compaction with immutable summaries.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible compute/storage overhead on Mac; occasional cheap planner call during recovery. No new model call for healthy actions.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds to healthy dispatch; removes known-dead waits and enables parallel recovery heartbeats.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without reducing owner-authorized access. Store page-content-free health/error metadata by default; keep sensitive browser evidence local and reference it by receipt ID.
depends_on: A stable typed job/checkpoint contract across local agent and relay
A browser extension heartbeat/status endpoint
A Mac action for opening/focusing Safari and checking bridge polling

changes.change: Compile a live capability matrix into the planner route decision: expose per-surface health, permissions, latency, and action classes with TTLs, then select the least-dependent execution path before planning (for example, use shell/AppleScript or browser DOM actions when vision is unavailable; use relay/pendant for notification only; defer GUI actions until Accessibility/Screen Recording are actually ready). If no path is viable, return a precise reason and recovery action immediately rather than invoking a disabled loop.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an action that works with the Mac as it is, instead of a vague failure from an unavailable vision loop. It also makes the pendant’s answer honest: “I can do this through Safari, but visual control is unavailable,” rather than burning time trying the wrong body.
changes.effort: Medium: typed capability snapshots with expiry, planner routing rules, and result explanations; no change to FULL_CONTROL authorization.
changes.risk: Stale health could route to a path that has just disappeared. Require a lightweight execution-time recheck and fall back to the recovery journal; never infer that a permission is granted merely because it was previously observed.
changes.cost_impact: Saves expensive planner/vision calls and long failed retries; small local status overhead.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one cached matrix lookup and optional quick recheck; should reduce failed-task latency substantially.
changes.security_impact: No broader access. Permission state and app names are sensitive host metadata, so send only the minimum reason to relay and keep detailed diagnostics local.
depends_on: Typed health/preflight journal
A compact context projection with source timestamps and TTL
Planner adapters that advertise shell, AppleScript, browser, and vision alternatives

changes.change: Add a bounded execution evidence ledger beside action receipts. For every run_shell/run_applescript/GUI action, record a structured outcome envelope: argv or script hash (not secret-bearing raw text by default), exit code, signal, timeout, start/end monotonic timestamps, connection/agent version, stdout/stderr byte counts plus redacted snippets, and declared postcondition checks. Keep full output only as encrypted, size-capped local artifacts with TTL; link artifacts by receiptId. Add a cheap local classifier for timeout, missing executable, permission, network, and unknown-outcome failures, and expose a single per-job timeline endpoint for relay and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can see exactly why a Mac task failed and whether it changed anything, without paying a model call to reconstruct logs from scattered job fields. It also makes resume/retry decisions honest when a connection drops and lets the system choose a faster specialized remedy instead of rerunning an expensive planner.
changes.effort: Medium: shared executor wrapper, redaction/TTL store, postcondition adapters for shell and common app actions, and dashboard/relay rendering. No change to FULL_CONTROL_MODE or action authorization.
changes.risk: Output may contain secrets or personal data; default to hashes/redacted excerpts, local-only encrypted artifacts, explicit deletion TTL, and never send full output to the pendant. A classifier can mislabel failures, so it must be advisory and retain raw exit facts. Ledger corruption should never prevent the underlying action result from returning.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage (bounded per-job artifacts, e.g. 1-10 MB with TTL) and near-zero API cost; saves model tokens by making evidence directly queryable.
changes.latency_impact: Under roughly 10 ms for metadata capture; postcondition checks add only the time of the check. Artifact encryption is asynchronous where possible.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability while reducing accidental secret exfiltration through redaction and local retention. Does not narrow shell capabilities or add approval gates.
depends_on: Existing actionReceipts.js and job records
A durable job/timeline endpoint (can initially be implemented over existing /jobs and /logs)
A shared secret-redaction library

changes.change: Implement a bounded diagnostic/evidence bundle path behind the existing unrestricted shell: one request returns host identity, power/network/audio state, local-agent health, active job and correlation ID, plus redacted stdout/stderr and exit status for the selected action. Make it read-only, timestamped, and attachable to the existing action receipt; expose a stable typed interface for relay and dashboard instead of requiring repeated ad-hoc shell probes. Do not gate or reduce run_shell capability.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks whether something happened, the system can answer with a compact, trustworthy bundle—what ran, on which Mac state, and what it observed—rather than making them repeat commands or accept an unexplained 'done.' It also lets a sleeping relay distinguish a dead Mac from a failed command and tell the owner the right next step.
changes.effort: Moderate: implement the currently granted diagnostic tool, add redaction and correlation to actionReceipts, persist bounded bundles with job retention, and add dashboard rendering and tests for unavailable/stale fields.
changes.risk: Command output can contain secrets; redact environment variables, tokens, cookies, and long private payloads, and cap bytes. Diagnostics can be stale or unavailable; label timestamps and uncertainty. A bug in correlation could attach evidence to the wrong action, so use immutable job/action IDs and test concurrent jobs.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small local storage bounded per job (for example 32–128 KB). Engineering cost is primarily typed serialization, redaction, and dashboard integration.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local diagnostics; avoid collecting expensive system_profiler data unless explicitly requested or a failure requires it.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without changing the owner's maximum-access policy. Keep bundles owner-scoped, redact sensitive fields before persistence, and never expose unrestricted environment or raw authenticated browser content by default.
depends_on: Implement the granted mac_read_diagnostics/mac_readonly_diagnostics interfaces (currently schema-only/no implementation).
Stable action/job correlation IDs from actionReceipts.js.
Existing /jobs and dashboard receipt surfaces.

changes.change: Add an append-only, observability-first shell execution transcript around the existing unrestricted FULL_CONTROL runShell path (do not gate or narrow it): before launch record a command fingerprint, cwd, selected non-secret environment metadata, timeout, and parent job/plan IDs; during execution sample bounded stdout/stderr and child-process milestones; after exit record status, duration, signal, output hashes, files/artifacts explicitly reported by the command, and a normalized failure class. Emit the same receipt ID to the relay, pendant interaction, browser session, and Mac journal. Add a 'diagnose/retry' operation that can suggest a corrected command from the transcript but never silently replays it, plus automatic redaction of token-shaped values in logs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When something runs unattended while the owner is away, they can tell exactly what happened, why it failed, what it touched, and whether a retry is safe instead of hearing only 'command failed.' Cross-surface IDs let a spoken pendant request, browser tab, and Mac process be traced as one task, which is not provided by basic action receipts.
changes.effort: Medium: wrapper and journal schema in local-agent, bounded stream capture, secret redaction tests, process-group metadata, and relay/pendant receipt propagation. No executor policy change.
changes.risk: Output may contain sensitive data even after redaction; cap size, redact common credentials, and permit per-job purge. Process sampling can miss short-lived children. Hashes prove sameness, not semantic safety. Retry suggestions could be wrong, so retries remain explicit commands and retain the original transcript.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local disk roughly 2–20 KB per command after bounded capture, with configurable retention and compression. Small CPU overhead for hashing and process sampling.
changes.latency_impact: ~10–50 ms startup/finalization overhead; streaming is asynchronous and should not materially delay commands.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without restricting owner-approved maximum access. Store raw output only locally by default; send summarized/redacted receipt cross-node. Treat command text, cwd, and artifact paths as sensitive metadata.
depends_on: Existing action receipts/journal (chg-5fc73ce3)
Durable job IDs and cross-surface correlation IDs
A real implementation of the newly granted read-only diagnostics is helpful for validation but not a runtime dependency

changes.change: Add a failure-aware execution supervisor around the existing unrestricted FULL_CONTROL shell/action path (no blocking or approval): assign each action an execution fingerprint (surface, argv/command hash, cwd, environment summary, idempotency key), stream start/heartbeat/exit events to the relay, classify failures into transient connection/timeout, missing permission, stale browser target, and deterministic command error, then automatically perform only an explicitly declared recovery recipe (reconnect/refresh/retry with backoff, browser reattach, or resume from the last completed step). Persist the attempt graph beyond the current 120-job journal window and expose a compact receipt linking every retry to the original request, tier, latency, and final state. The pendant should receive one concise spoken status only when recovery is exhausted; routine successes remain silent.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks from the pendant and walks away, a failed Mac or browser action will either finish itself or explain exactly what stopped it instead of silently leaving four pending browser commands or an incomplete task. They keep maximum capability and unattended execution, but gain trustworthy 'done / recovered / needs me' outcomes and a history that survives the current rolling log.
changes.effort: Medium: typed attempt events and durable storage in local-agent, a small relay job-state consumer, recovery recipes for shell timeout/network, browser reattach, and permission diagnostics, plus pendant summary formatting and tests for duplicate/retry safety.
changes.risk: A retry can duplicate a non-idempotent shell mutation or browser submission. Recovery recipes must be opt-in per action type and default to no automatic retry for unknown commands; record the exact command hash and before/after receipts. If the Mac or relay disappears, the local attempt remains resumable and the pendant reports uncertainty rather than success.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost: deterministic classification and retry orchestration are local; only exhausted failures or a requested spoken explanation use the cheaper background model. Storage is small append-only attempt metadata (roughly 1–3 KB per attempt), with output redaction and retention controls.
changes.latency_impact: Adds near-zero latency to the first execution; transient failures incur bounded backoff (for example 1s/4s/16s). Normal successful jobs do not wait on relay acknowledgement. Spoken escalation is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: No new execution authority and no restriction of the owner's deliberate FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Store hashes and redacted environment summaries by default, never raw secrets; make command/output retention configurable and preserve the existing authenticated local-agent/relay channel.
depends_on: Durable attempt storage separate from the 120-job rolling journal
Action-type metadata declaring idempotency and safe recovery recipe
Relay event ingestion and pendant notification path
Browser session reattachment status and local permission diagnostics

changes.change: Add a typed capability-preflight and recovery coordinator between planner and executors. Before dispatch, it queries /ops/status, /browser/status, /routing, and the relevant session state, then emits a compact decision record: route, required permissions/session, freshness, retry class, fallback routes, and owner-facing reason code. On browser reconnect it reconciles pendingCommands by request/idempotency key (five are currently pending while the extension is offline), marks stale commands dead-lettered rather than replaying blindly, and links every retry/fallback to the existing job receipt and journal. It must observe and explain, not introduce blocking approval gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant stops promising actions that cannot run, recovers when the browser or relay briefly disappears, and tells the owner exactly whether work completed, is waiting, or needs a permission fix. It also prevents duplicate browser clicks after reconnect.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema, coordinator in planner/dispatcher, stale-command reconciler, receipt/journal integration, and fault-injection tests for offline browser, expired session, relay timeout, and missing Mac permissions.
changes.risk: A bad retry classification could repeat a non-idempotent browser action. Default retries to reads and explicitly idempotent steps; require an executor-provided idempotency key for mutations, and preserve before/after receipts. If coordinator fails, fall back to today's direct dispatch and report degraded observability.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost for deterministic checks; small local CPU/storage cost for decision records and dead-letter metadata. Avoids expensive planner retries and duplicate work.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms for local preflight; skip checks whose health lease is fresh. Long jobs remain asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Diagnostics stay local; relay receives only redacted typed health and reason codes. Session URLs, tab text, and permission details remain in the Mac agent. No new authority or gates are introduced.
depends_on: A concrete implementation of the already-granted mac_read_diagnostics/mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl tool, or equivalent local health provider.
A shared idempotency-key field across browser command queue and Mac job receipts.
The existing browser command queue and receipt/journal paths must expose stale-command age and terminal reason codes.

changes.change: Add a shell flight recorder and failure-aware continuation layer without reducing FULL_CONTROL_MODE. For every run_shell action, persist a bounded stdout/stderr artifact (spill larger output to a content-addressed local file), exit code/signal/timeout, start/end timestamps, cwd, selected non-secret environment facts, host fingerprint, and a normalized command label. Redact probable secrets before relay/dashboard storage while retaining the local raw artifact. Classify failures (timeout, missing binary, permission, network, nonzero application error), then let the same job resume with a model-generated corrected command or retry only when the failure class is transient; never replay completed action IDs. Expose transcript pointers and retry lineage through GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts, GET /journal/:jobId, and GET /ops/snapshot, with a cleanup endpoint/retention policy for artifacts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails after they walk away, the pendant can say exactly which command failed, what it was doing, and whether it recovered—rather than silently stopping or asking them to reproduce a terminal session. Long build/test output remains inspectable without flooding the expensive voice context, and retries continue from the failed step instead of repeating earlier side effects.
changes.effort: Medium: executor/runShell wrapper, bounded artifact store and redaction, failure classifier, resumable job state, three read routes, dashboard/relay formatting, and tests for timeout, secrets, truncation, and retry lineage.
changes.risk: Command output can contain credentials or private data; raw artifacts must remain local by default and only redacted excerpts/pointers leave the Mac. A bad transient classification could retry a non-idempotent shell command, so automatic retry must be restricted to explicit retry-safe labels or commands proven read-only; otherwise record a suggested retry and let the planner choose. Crash during recording must not change command execution semantics.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost; local disk bounded by retention (for example 100 MB), with CPU overhead only for teeing output, hashing, and redaction. A small model call is used only for failure diagnosis/correction, not normal commands.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible on normal commands; failed jobs add roughly one planner turn and any retry runtime. Large output is streamed to disk rather than held in memory.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability while preserving owner-approved unrestricted execution. Store raw stdout/stderr and environment only on-device, redact before relay, hash artifacts, and expire them automatically. No new approval gate.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo infrastructure
GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
GET /journal/:jobId
GET /ops/snapshot
durable job lifecycle with resumable step state

changes.change: Add a bridge liveness reconciler and stale-command janitor. Correlate extension heartbeat age, poll activity, pending-command count, command lease age, and the Mac agent's observed browser status instead of treating online=true as sufficient. Before dispatch, fail fast with a typed bridge_unavailable result when the last poll is stale; periodically expire/requeue orphaned commands whose 45-second lease elapsed, preserving idempotency keys so a late extension result cannot double-apply. Emit one deduplicated incident per outage and clear it on the first successful poll, with status exposed in /browser/status, /ops/status, /jobs, and the relay stream.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A browser request currently waits 45 seconds and then says the extension is offline, while status can still say online and pending commands accumulate. The owner gets a truthful, quick answer, no ghost work, and automatic continuation when Safari comes back instead of repeatedly asking the same thing.
changes.effort: Medium: heartbeat/poll timestamps, lease janitor, idempotent requeue state, typed failure, deduplicated incident event, and tests for stale/late results and restart recovery.
changes.risk: A late browser result could arrive after requeue; content-addressed action IDs and lease generations must discard duplicates. Clock skew is possible, so use monotonic local age where available. Never fail over authenticated Safari work to the relay, which lacks the owner's session.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible compute and storage; avoids wasting browser-minute budget and planner calls on known-unavailable commands.
changes.latency_impact: Unavailable browser calls fail in about one heartbeat interval (target 2–5 seconds) instead of 45 seconds; healthy calls are unchanged.
changes.security_impact: No new data access. Preserve tab/session affinity and keep private-page evidence on the Mac; outage telemetry should contain only session ID hash, not page contents or URLs.
depends_on: chg-14accc01 request IDs/tab affinity/idempotency
POST /browser/heartbeat
GET /browser/poll
GET /browser/status
GET /jobs
GET /ops/status
GET /pipeline/stream

changes.change: Create a cross-surface causality ledger that links one owner request across relay, planner routing, Mac execution, browser command, and pendant delivery using a single correlation ID and append-only event sequence. Each event should record the selected surface, decision reason, freshness proof used, action/receipt ID, result, and whether the event was observed, inferred, or merely attempted. Add a compact owner-facing 'why/where/what happened' projection that can be spoken without replaying the full prompt context, plus an exportable JSON evidence bundle for disputes or debugging.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should be able to ask, “What exactly did you do, where did it happen, and why did you believe it worked?” Today local receipts and job records exist, but they do not establish one trustworthy story across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser—especially when a stale browser status conflicts with a failed command. This would make the system accountable rather than merely plausible.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: shared correlation schema, append-only storage and retention, event propagation through relay and Mac/browser bridges, provenance projection, and recovery for partially delivered events.
changes.risk: The ledger could expose private URLs, commands, or page evidence; default spoken output must be summarized and redacted, with detailed export kept local or explicitly requested. Clock ordering must use sequence numbers and monotonic timestamps rather than wall-clock time alone. Event loss must be represented as unknown, never silently filled by inference.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable-storage and hashing cost; negligible model cost because the owner projection is deterministic for normal events. A background model is optional only for explaining unusual partial failures.
changes.latency_impact: No blocking cost on successful execution if events are buffered locally; the owner-facing summary becomes available within a few seconds. Durable flush may add minimal local I/O.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without adding execution restrictions. Bind event ingestion to the existing paired relay/Mac identity, sign event batches, encrypt detailed evidence at rest, and redact secrets before relay transmission.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo infrastructure

changes.change: Add a structured shell execution ledger without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE or adding gates: before execution record a normalized command fingerprint, cwd, timeout, initiating run/step id, and declared intent; during execution capture start/end timestamps, exit signal/code, bounded stdout/stderr previews with secret redaction, child-process summary, and resource usage; after execution attach undoability from undo.js, evidence-capsule ids, retry classification, and a machine-readable failure diagnosis. Expose it through /journal and /journal/:jobId with filters for command fingerprint, exit class, and run id, and let the planner request a retry using the receipt rather than re-planning from scratch.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When an unattended command fails or partially succeeds, the owner should hear “the build timed out after spawning X; no files changed” rather than a vague failure or an unsafe blind retry. It also makes the Mac tier faster: repeated status checks can reuse recent receipts, and the planner can distinguish a transient network failure from a permanent command error. This improves trust and recovery while preserving the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: instrument computerControl.runShell/executor and jobTracker, add bounded redaction and child/resource sampling, extend journal serialization and planner input, then test timeout, signal, huge output, and nonzero-exit cases.
changes.risk: Output could contain credentials or sensitive file contents; redact common token patterns, cap bytes, and store hashes instead of full output. Process sampling adds small overhead. If ledger persistence fails, execution must still proceed and return a minimal in-memory receipt. Never let observability become a blocking authorization gate.
changes.cost_impact: No model API cost; modest local disk growth from bounded receipts (target <16 KB per shell action) and negligible CPU for timestamps/process sampling.
changes.latency_impact: About 10–50 ms per action plus any optional child-process sampling; zero extra network round trips for the normal path.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates a sensitive local record. Encrypt or permission-protect the ledger, redact secrets before persistence, and keep raw stdout ephemeral. No change to unrestricted command/network authority.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and /journal routes
A shared run/step identifier from the cross-surface coordinator
A small planner contract for retry classification and evidence-capsule references

changes.change: Replace the single ambiguous agent.permissions.ready boolean in /ops/status with a capability matrix and stable blocker codes. Report independent readiness for shell, AppleScript/automation, accessibility UI control, screen capture, browser bridge, relay link, and audio; include observedAt, remediation URL/action, and whether each blocker affects the requested action. Preserve ready for compatibility as “all required capabilities,” but make requiredMissing/optionalMissing derive from the matrix. Have /execute attach the preflight snapshot to every failed receipt so a stale global status cannot explain a route-specific failure.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The live Mac says ready:false while requiredMissing is empty, and a browser job says only “extension offline” after 45 seconds. The owner needs to know immediately whether a task can proceed through shell, AppleScript, UI vision, or browser—and what single thing to fix—instead of treating the whole Mac as unavailable or retrying blindly.
changes.effort: Small-to-moderate: define blocker vocabulary, compute matrix from existing permission and heartbeat probes, add compatibility fields, attach snapshot IDs to receipts, and add dashboard badges. No executor policy or approval change.
changes.risk: Permission probes may be stale or disagree with reality; include timestamps and an unknown state rather than claiming ready. Do not expose raw tokens or private URLs. Existing clients that interpret ready as a hard gate must be updated to use per-action capability, while old clients retain the compatibility field.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; a few hundred bytes per status/receipt and negligible local computation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds only local probe time, preferably cached for 5–30 seconds; failed jobs return immediately with the cached blocker instead of waiting for an impossible browser poll.
changes.security_impact: Makes permission and connectivity posture more visible to relay/dashboard; send only capability codes and timestamps off-device, never detailed app or account metadata.
depends_on: GET /ops/status
GET /ops/snapshot
GET /browser/status
Existing action receipts at GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
Existing Mac permission and relay heartbeat probes

changes.change: Add a cross-surface focus lease for hands-free dictation. When the pendant starts a “put this there” utterance, the Mac agent and browser extension publish a signed snapshot containing active app/window, browser tab identity, focused-field locator, and a short expiry. The relay binds exactly one encrypted utterance envelope to that lease. Before insertion, the Mac agent verifies the same app/tab/field is still focused; if not, it pauses and asks the pendant rather than typing into a new destination. Record only a text hash and destination metadata in the receipt, with a local one-shot undo for insertion where the host supports it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It prevents the uniquely dangerous failure of hands-free input landing in the wrong window after the owner switches focus. The owner can dictate once, glance or listen to a concise target preview, and trust that a later bridge reconnect will not paste stale private words into an unrelated document or message.
changes.effort: Moderate: focus metadata adapters for macOS accessibility and the browser extension, signed lease/envelope storage in relay D1, expiry and replay checks, typed insertion plus local undo, and pendant preview/receipt phrasing.
changes.risk: Some apps expose no reliable field identity; classify those targets as unknown and require an explicit second confirmation rather than guessing. Accessibility metadata can include sensitive window titles and URLs, so keep full snapshots local and send only opaque lease IDs through relay. Recover interrupted delivery by expiring the envelope, never by silently replaying it.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; small D1/local metadata records and one short-lived encrypted text payload per use. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–300 ms for lease validation; avoids delayed incorrect insertion and expensive recovery.
changes.security_impact: Improves confidentiality by making text single-use, destination-bound, expiring, and hash-audited. It introduces a sensitive transient payload, which should be encrypted at rest and deleted after acknowledgment or expiry.
depends_on: The proposed focus-intent protocol and typed insert_text_at_focus action
Existing browser heartbeat/poll/result routes
Existing Mac action receipts and relay persistent state

changes.change: Add a low-power I2C fuel-gauge IC (for example MAX17048-class, with an interrupt line) to the pendant revision, then expose battery percentage/voltage and a low-battery event in the device heartbeat. Relay routing should use that telemetry to avoid starting long audio capture or Mac/browser work when the pendant cannot reliably receive the result; it should switch to a short text/LED status and queue the job until charging. The Mac agent should include pendant power state in job receipts so a disconnected result is distinguishable from a dead pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current pendant has no battery gauge, so the system cannot tell whether silence means a lost Mac, LTE failure, or a dying wearable. The owner gets fewer cut-off conversations and a clear “queued until charged” outcome instead of repeating a task. It also lets the system prefer compact spoken summaries when power is low without disabling the owner's unrestricted Mac access.
changes.effort: Moderate hardware revision and firmware/relay integration: route I2C (currently free), add gauge driver/calibration, heartbeat schema, relay policy, and dashboard status. Prototype on the DK with an external breakout before a PCB change.
changes.risk: I2C wiring, gauge calibration, and LTE burst noise can produce inaccurate readings; fall back to voltage-only and mark confidence low. If telemetry goes stale, treat it as unknown rather than falsely declaring low battery. Preserve the existing one-button/one-LED behavior and SD failure buffer.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$5 BOM increase at volume prototype quantities, plus <1 mA typical gauge draw (interrupt-driven). Firmware and relay storage cost is negligible; no new model call is needed for normal routing.
changes.latency_impact: Heartbeat adds a few bytes and at most tens of milliseconds; low-battery routing decisions are local/relay-side and should not add perceptible conversational latency.
changes.security_impact: Battery telemetry is low sensitivity. Do not include location or raw audio in the same heartbeat; keep device identifiers scoped and authenticated.
depends_on: A heartbeat payload/route that can carry device telemetry
Relay routing that can distinguish stale device state from live state
Pendant firmware build and a spare I2C address/interrupt GPIO in the next board revision

changes.change: Add a tiny coin vibration motor or linear resonant actuator with a dedicated driver in the next pendant revision, plus a low-power haptic event protocol. Relay job completion, browser-watch alerts, and Mac failure/reconnect events should produce distinct short patterns; the pendant firmware must queue/coalesce patterns while audio is active and fall back to the existing LED when haptics are disabled.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently has only one LED and audio output. If headphones are disconnected, audio is buffered, or the owner is in a noisy environment, completed work and urgent failures are easy to miss. A private, silent tap lets the owner know that something finished without opening a screen or starting the microphone, while the relay/Mac still provide the details when asked.
changes.effort: Hardware revision, one GPIO/PWM driver and haptic patterns in firmware, then relay event mapping and dashboard settings. Prototype with an external driver board first; reserve a GPIO and validate vibration does not couple into the microphone mechanically.
changes.risk: Motor current spikes can disturb LTE/audio rails and vibration can enter the mic. Use a transistor/current-limited driver, physical isolation, rate limits, and a firmware fallback to LED. A failed motor must not block conversations or job delivery.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$4 BOM increase in prototypes and approximately 10–80 mA only during brief pulses; negligible model/API cost. Battery impact is small if patterns are capped and coalesced.
changes.latency_impact: Event-to-tap can be sub-second after relay receipt, with no model round trip. Firmware queueing during playback adds at most a few seconds by policy.
changes.security_impact: Haptic patterns reveal only that an event exists, not its content. Provide a silent/privacy mode and avoid encoding sensitive categories in easily observable patterns.
depends_on: A relay event taxonomy for job completion, failure, and reconnect
Authenticated pendant downlink/event delivery
A revised enclosure/PCB with a safe GPIO, driver transistor, and mechanical isolation

changes.change: Build a live capability-preflight and recovery layer for every Mac/browser job. Before dispatch, consume GET /ops/status, GET /browser/status, and GET /capabilities to produce a per-action prerequisite map (browser polling, app reachability, Accessibility, Screen Recording, relay reachability).
