This directly addresses the live state: 16 failed actions, 112 actions without tier attribution, and one browser navigation repeated six times with a 100% failure rate.
changes.effort: Medium: extend jobTracker/action receipts with normalized failure fields and continuation checkpoints; add a small retry/circuit-breaker module, prerequisite probes, resume endpoint, and relay status serialization; add tests for browser-offline, permission-denied, timeout, and successful resume.
changes.risk: A bad classifier could label a recoverable failure permanent or resume from an unsafe checkpoint. Recovery: default to no automatic retry after the threshold, preserve the complete trace, allow explicit force-retry from the owner, and make each continuation idempotent. Do not transmit command contents or secrets to the relay; send only category, counts, and redacted diagnostics.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; mostly local JSON/D1 metadata. A cheaper deterministic classifier avoids spending planner tokens on routine failure diagnosis; escalate only ambiguous semantic failures.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds for local classification. Prerequisite refresh may add 1–3 seconds, but avoids repeated 120-second shell/browser attempts and avoids rerunning completed steps.
changes.security_impact: No reduction in the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy. Improve auditability by hashing/redacting argv, environment, and stderr before relay export; keep raw diagnostics local and apply retention limits.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and jobTracker persistence
Existing /jobs, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, /jobs/:jobId/cancel, and relay_job_status surfaces
Browser heartbeat/session state and Mac observability endpoints (/ops/status, /browser/status)
Routing attribution hooks in routingStats.js

changes.change: Make routing metadata an end-to-end trace context rather than an in-memory planner receipt. Generate a requestId at the pendant/relay boundary and propagate it through relay jobs, Mac /plan and /execute, browser commands, action receipts, and journal entries; record tier, model, prompt/completion token estimates, escalation reason, latency, and final outcome on every action. Add a deterministic preflight router that consults /ops/status (browser online, required permissions, relay reachability) and routes simple status/recovery queries to deterministic/background tiers, while marking impossible browser work as `waiting_for_surface` instead of repeatedly invoking the planner.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask what happened and receive one coherent answer: which device acted, what failed, how long it took, and whether model spend was justified. The system will stop wasting expensive planner calls when the browser is offline and will give a useful “reconnect Chrome” explanation instead. Today routing reports 7 requests but 112 journal actions have no tier attribution, so cost and failure explanations are incomplete.
changes.effort: Medium: introduce a trace-context object shared by relay and local-agent requests; persist compact routing receipts with jobs; update browser command envelopes and journal serializers; add preflight rules and dashboard aggregation.
changes.risk: Metadata can become noisy or accidentally include sensitive prompts. Keep command text out of cross-device receipts, store only hashes/intent labels and token counts, enforce bounded retention, and tolerate missing context without failing execution. Preflight must be advisory/status classification only, consistent with FULL_CONTROL_MODE and the owner's no-gates policy.
changes.cost_impact: Slightly more local storage and D1 writes; reduces planner spend by avoiding doomed retries and selecting deterministic/background handling for status work.
changes.latency_impact: A local preflight is sub-100 ms; propagation is negligible. It removes multi-second model calls for known-offline surfaces.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without restricting capability. Relay receives redacted IDs and outcome categories, never raw shell commands, environment, cookies, or page contents.
depends_on: Existing routingStats.js and /routing endpoint
Existing jobTracker/actionReceipts/journal persistence
Relay job identifiers and browser request IDs
Read-only /ops/status and /browser/status telemetry

changes.change: Add a non-blocking failure-aware executor recovery loop. Before dispatching a browser or Mac action, consult the live surface-health signal; after the first failure, fingerprint the error (offline, timeout, permission/dialog, invalid target), record it against the idempotency key, and choose a bounded recovery: fast-fail repeated known-offline commands instead of spending another 45 seconds, retry a timeout once with a fresh request ID only when the target is still healthy, and for public URLs offer the relay/public-browser backend. Never block or refuse an action globally: this is an execution optimization and diagnosis layer, with the original unrestricted command path retained. Emit a recovery receipt linking the failed attempt, retry, health snapshot, and final outcome.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A stuck Safari dialog or offline extension currently turns each attempt into an unexplained 45-second wait and repeated failures. The owner gets a quick, truthful diagnosis and either a recovered result or a concrete next step, while successful unrestricted Mac work remains just as capable.
changes.effort: Medium: failure classifier and per-surface health cache in the local agent, idempotent retry coordinator, receipt schema/dashboard rendering, and one relay fallback adapter. Test against offline extension, dialog-blocked Safari, timeout, and successful retry.
changes.risk: A retry could duplicate a non-idempotent action if classification is wrong. Restrict automatic retries to actions explicitly marked safe-to-retry or to attempts whose receipt proves no effect; preserve the current no-gate policy and surface ambiguity as a report, not a refusal. Recovery metadata may expose URLs and command error text, so keep it in the authenticated job store.
changes.cost_impact: Small background CPU/storage increase; fewer planner turns and fewer 45-second dead waits should reduce model/API spend. Public-browser fallback may incur provider usage only when selected.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy actions gain only a health-cache lookup; known offline failures return in milliseconds instead of ~45 seconds. A single safe retry adds at most one action timeout.
changes.security_impact: No new authority beyond existing unrestricted Mac/browser execution. Error receipts must redact environment variables, command secrets, cookies, and page bodies; retain hashes and bounded diagnostic text.
depends_on: Expose a typed surface-health snapshot from the existing browser status and Mac-agent liveness paths
Add retry-safety/idempotency metadata to action receipts
Preserve existing durable job and receipt records so recovery remains auditable

changes.change: Teach the router a deterministic execution-recovery intent that consumes job/receipt/health data directly. Phrases such as “why did that fail?”, “try it again”, and “is Safari back?” should resolve to a compact diagnostic or safe retry plan without sending the full fleet context to the planner; escalate only when the classifier finds ambiguous side effects or needs a new plan. Attach the failed job ID and recovery fingerprint so the planner does not re-interpret the same 45-second failure from scratch.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: After a Mac or browser action fails, the owner can ask a natural follow-up and get an immediate, accurate status or retry instead of paying for a full reasoning turn and waiting for the system to rediscover the same failure.
changes.effort: Small to medium: add intent patterns, receipt/health lookup, and escalation rules; add regression tests for offline, timeout, and successful retry conversations.
changes.risk: A terse follow-up like “try again” can refer to an unsafe prior mutation. Default deterministic handling only to read-only or explicitly retry-safe actions; otherwise return the existing receipt and ask the planner to interpret context, without adding a new approval gate.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces repeated planner prompts and token cost for routine recovery; negligible storage and compute.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second for receipt/status responses; safe retries retain the underlying action latency.
changes.security_impact: Queries remain authenticated and should return bounded/redacted receipt fields, never raw shell environment or browser session data.
depends_on: Failure fingerprints and recovery receipts from the integration change
A stable job-id/idempotency-key reference in follow-up utterance context

changes.change: Add a preflight-and-fallback middleware between planner and executor. For every planned action, declare required surface facts (e.g. browser_online, tab_attached, accessibility, screen_recording, vision_consent, relay_reachable). Read a short-lived capability snapshot from /ops/status and /browser/status, annotate each step as ready/deferred/fallbackable, and persist that decision in the job and receipt. Execute only ready steps; for fallbackable steps select a declared alternative (relay/public web, shell/status, or durable browser queue), then recheck the affected surface once after a failure. Emit one structured completion event containing completed, deferred, fallback, and reason codes for relay/pendant narration. This is observability and recovery, not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a fast truthful answer instead of waiting through impossible actions: e.g. 'I can read the Mac, but browser work is queued because the extension is offline; I did the public portion now.' It also stops identical browser timeouts and makes partial completion understandable.
changes.effort: Medium: capability schema, planner annotations, executor middleware, fallback registry, and relay event formatting; add integration tests for offline extension, missing permissions, stale heartbeat, and successful recovery.
changes.risk: A stale health snapshot could incorrectly defer a newly available surface or choose an inferior fallback. Use TTLs, include snapshot timestamps in receipts, and allow one bounded recheck. Never silently substitute a public source for a private authenticated page.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful model cost; local HTTP checks and JSON receipts. Small storage increase per action for capability snapshot and reason codes.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 100–300 ms to local jobs; avoids current 45-second browser timeout loops. Fallback execution can proceed in parallel where dependencies allow.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by making private/public boundary explicit and preventing accidental public fallback. Does not narrow FULL_CONTROL_MODE or add confirmations.
depends_on: A typed required-capabilities field in the existing action registry
A fallback registry that marks which alternatives are privacy-equivalent versus public-only
A relay event schema for deferred/fallback completion
The existing /ops/status and browser status endpoints being reachable from the executor

changes.change: Create a cross-surface postcondition verifier that runs after an action batch. The planner must attach a typed expected outcome to each write. After execution, the verifier retrieves the same browser tab/session or Mac foreground context, compares the observed state to the expectation, stores a provenance-bound verification record, and emits a four-state verdict: verified, unverified, unchanged, or contradicted. Aggregate verdicts across the batch and expose a redacted proof card to the relay/pendant; retain raw evidence locally. A receipt may remain successful while the user-facing result is 'completed but unverified' until this check passes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust 'done' to mean the intended world state was observed, not just that an API or keystroke returned without an error. When something is ambiguous, they get a precise next step and compact proof instead of having to inspect the Mac themselves.
changes.effort: Medium-high: typed postconditions in the planner/action registry, same-context read-after-write adapters for Mac and browser, evidence correlation, verdict persistence, and redacted voice/dashboard rendering.
changes.risk: Some applications update asynchronously or expose nondeterministic text, causing false 'contradicted' results. Support settling windows, semantic predicates, and an explicit unverified state; never retry a mutation merely because verification is inconclusive.
changes.cost_impact: One extra read per write and occasional small standard-model semantic comparison; no realtime call required for normal operation. Raw evidence increases local storage modestly.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 0.5–10 seconds depending on the surface, but replaces false immediate success with an honest bounded result. Independent postconditions can be checked in parallel.
changes.security_impact: Raw private evidence stays on the Mac/browser bridge. Relay receives only redacted fields, hashes, timestamps, and verdict unless the owner explicitly requests proof. Same-tab/session binding reduces cross-account leakage.
depends_on: Action schemas that carry typed expected outcomes
Browser same-tab read-after-write with provenance
Mac observe support for application/document postconditions
A local evidence redaction and retention policy
Relay/pendant event support for proof cards and four-state verdicts

changes.change: Add an execution-aware router that compiles a request into typed subgoals (local status, Mac shell/action, authenticated browser, public research, narration), consults live /ops/status and /browser/status before planning, and routes each subgoal independently. Cache deterministic Mac diagnostics and fail fast on an offline browser instead of spending a 45-second browser timeout; retain the full planner only for ambiguous joins. Attach the routing tier, subgoal ID, and outcome to every job receipt so the current 112 unattributed actions become attributable.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant answers faster and more reliably: a browser outage no longer stalls unrelated Mac work, repeated battery/Wi-Fi questions do not pay planner tokens, and the owner receives one coherent answer from whatever parts actually worked.
changes.effort: Medium: define subgoal schema, health capability matrix, planner handoff, and receipt propagation across relay and local agent; add replay tests for partial failure.
changes.risk: A compiler could split a task incorrectly or report a partial answer as complete. Recover by preserving the original goal, requiring a join step to mark completion, and falling back to the existing planner when confidence is low. No action is blocked; this only changes planning and observability.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces planner calls and repeated timeout retries; expected savings are material given the observed 28,971 planner-tier tokens across 3 requests and 16 failed actions. Small deterministic CPU/storage overhead.
changes.latency_impact: Health check <300 ms; independent subgoals can run concurrently. Failed browser work returns in seconds rather than ~45 seconds, while complex tasks may add a short join step.
changes.security_impact: Private tab data remains in the browser/local path; only typed status and provenance cross the relay. Existing unrestricted Mac execution policy remains unchanged.
depends_on: A shared subgoal/job schema across relay and local agent
Capability requirements and health preflight described in the recovery proposal
Receipt attribution for every action and routing tier

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution preflight and failure-aware recovery ledger for cross-surface actions. Before dispatching browser_* work, sample the existing browser status/heartbeat state and attach a health snapshot (online, lastSeenAt, pending count, tab/session affinity) to the job. If offline or stale, fail fast with a typed reason instead of waiting 45 seconds; if online but a command times out, record one bounded retry only after a fresh heartbeat, then persist a recovery hint for the relay/pendant. Drain or expire stale queued commands by idempotency key so an extension reconnect cannot replay obsolete work. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and all action permissions unchanged; this is observability, faster failure, and recovery, not a gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Browser requests would stop hanging for nearly a minute and then silently repeating. The pendant could say immediately whether the browser is disconnected, retry once when it genuinely returns, and avoid acting on stale commands after reconnection.
changes.effort: Medium: browser health snapshot in jobTracker/executor, typed failure states and bounded retry, plus queue expiry keyed by idempotencyKey; dashboard/relay rendering is a smaller follow-up.
changes.risk: A transient extension stall could be classified as offline or a retry could duplicate a non-idempotent action. Restrict automatic retry to reads and actions explicitly marked idempotent; preserve the existing receipt and expose every retry. Recovery is to rerun from the durable job record.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; saves model turns and local wait time. Small persistent metadata increase per job (health snapshot and retry record).
changes.latency_impact: Healthy browser actions add only a local status check; stale/offline actions return in under a second instead of ~45 seconds.
changes.security_impact: No new authority or data egress. Health metadata contains extension/tab state and should remain in the authenticated local journal; do not include page contents in failure telemetry.
depends_on: Existing GET /browser/status and POST /browser/heartbeat routes
Existing GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:jobId, receipts, journal, and idempotency keys
Browser extension emitting reliable lastSeenAt/command acknowledgement

changes.change: Create a single /readiness contract and dashboard/pendant renderer that fuses /ops/status, /browser/status, relay reachability, permission state, and the last 10 journal failures into four independent booleans: shell, app automation, screen/vision, and authenticated browser. Emit a stable blocker code (for example BROWSER_EXTENSION_OFFLINE, ACCESSIBILITY_MISSING, SCREEN_RECORDING_MISSING) with lastSeen, remediation URL/action, and affected queued job IDs. This is reporting only: it must never block FULL_CONTROL actions or silently retry them.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner hears one accurate answer—what the Mac can do right now and the single next fix—rather than seeing generic failures after 45-second browser timeouts. It also prevents an offline extension from being mistaken for a dead Mac or relay.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: schema, reducer, tests against contradictory states (agent ready=false but requiredMissing empty), and dashboard/pendant presentation.
changes.risk: Stale health data could mislead; include timestamps, a short TTL, and an explicit unknown state. Do not expose URLs, tab titles, or command output in the spoken summary.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible; all inputs are local status endpoints and existing receipts, reducing expensive planner retries.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local aggregation; can be polled or pushed on state transitions.
changes.security_impact: Read-only metadata only. Permission remediation must open System Settings but never grant privileges automatically. Preserve unrestricted shell policy.
depends_on: GET /ops/status and /ops/snapshot
GET /browser/status
GET /journal and job receipts
Relay health payload
Dashboard and pendant status-event plumbing

changes.change: Add an encrypted, versioned workspace-checkpoint store distinct from conversational memory. A checkpoint records only resumable handles and metadata: Mac app/window/focus identities, terminal cwd and project/branch, browser session/tab identifiers and URLs, active job IDs with receipt cursors, and the relay task/pipeline identifier. Capture atomically on explicit 'save my workspace', clean shutdown, and detected bridge loss; retain a small ring of checkpoints. Provide a deterministic restore planner that reopens/reattaches what still exists, marks conflicts instead of guessing, and emits a per-item restored/skipped/changed receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: After a restart or dropped connection, the owner can say 'continue where I left off' and recover their actual working context instead of manually hunting through apps, tabs, and unfinished jobs. This is continuity across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser—not another single-surface action.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema and encryption, Mac app/window and terminal collectors, browser reattachment, relay linkage, atomic checkpointing, restore conflict UI, and crash-recovery tests.
changes.risk: Window titles, paths, and URLs can be sensitive; encrypt locally, omit content and credentials, support exclusions, and expire old checkpoints. A vanished tab or changed file must be reported as a conflict, never silently substituted. Restore should only reopen or focus; it must not submit, send, delete, or overwrite.
changes.cost_impact: Small local storage and negligible API cost; deterministic restore avoids repeated planner calls. Optional reconciliation can use a cheap model only when identifiers conflict.
changes.latency_impact: Capture under 3 seconds; restore begins within 2 seconds and continues asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: No cookies, passwords, page bodies, microphone data, or document contents leave the Mac. Relay receives only an encrypted checkpoint reference or explicitly permitted metadata.
depends_on: A durable encrypted local checkpoint store
Mac window/focus and terminal-state collector
Browser session/tab reattachment API with stable identifiers
Relay task/pipeline checkpoint linkage
Per-item restore receipts and dashboard/pendant status presentation

changes.change: Turn the existing non-blocking observeBeforeAction signal into a capability-aware fallback hint for the planner. Before dispatch, collect a short-lived readiness snapshot (Accessibility, Screen Recording, browser-extension online/pending age, app automation grants, shell reachability) and annotate the action with viable alternate mechanisms. If a GUI/browser action is unavailable, the planner should automatically choose an equivalent permitted route (for example AppleScript or shell for a Mac setting, authenticated browser bridge versus public fetch) when semantics are equivalent; otherwise fail immediately with the exact missing permission/endpoint and a one-line owner fix. This is advisory routing only: FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unrestricted and no action is refused by policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent stops wasting 45 seconds retrying a browser or GUI action that cannot work on this Mac. It either completes through another surface or tells the owner exactly why it cannot, which is especially valuable from a pendant where a generic failure is hard to act on.
changes.effort: Moderate: normalize existing /ops/status and browser status into a cached readiness object, make executor observations available to the planner/relay, add equivalence mappings for common Mac intents, and include the chosen route plus unavailable alternatives in the receipt.
changes.risk: Fallbacks can have different semantics (AppleScript may affect the wrong app or shell may lack UI context), so mappings must be conservative and explain the substitution. Readiness can go stale between observation and dispatch; mark timestamps and treat it as a hint, never a guarantee. Do not expose permission details or URLs beyond the authenticated owner surfaces.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost: deterministic readiness and route selection avoid planner calls and repeated failed browser timeouts. Small local status probes per job, cached for seconds.
changes.latency_impact: Cuts known-unavailable browser attempts from ~45 seconds to immediate alternate execution or actionable failure; adds only a small preflight probe.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no gates. Permission state and route diagnostics remain local/owner-authenticated; relay receives only a concise reason and selected route. Fallback mappings must preserve existing unrestricted owner policy.
depends_on: Existing read-only /ops/status or /ops/snapshot and /browser/status endpoints
Existing non-blocking observeBeforeAction hook in action receipts
Existing executor route dispatch and relay job completion summaries

changes.change: Add a shell-specific execution adapter beneath FULL_CONTROL_MODE (not a policy gate): launch every run in a tracked process group with a durable job manifest containing cwd, exact command, start time, pid/process-group id, timeout, and redacted environment keys. Append stdout/stderr to a bounded per-job log with monotonically increasing byte/sequence cursors; emit started/heartbeat/output/exit/signal/timeout events to the existing journal and relay. On bridge reconnect, reconcile the process group by manifest and replay events from the last cursor instead of dispatching the command again. Extend the existing action receipt with exit code, signal, elapsed time, last output cursor, and an explicit 'cannot resume' reason for commands that died.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave a compile, export, sync, or test running and later hear the real result rather than a vague timeout or an accidental duplicate run. Failures become actionable (last output, exit signal, cwd, and whether the process is still alive), while unrestricted shell access remains intact.
changes.effort: Medium: a small local supervisor/event journal, relay replay endpoint, and adapters in executor.js plus dashboard/pendant consumers; tests for disconnect, process exit, timeout, and duplicate prevention.
changes.risk: A stale pid or reused process-group id could attach the wrong process; bind manifests to start time and verify command/cwd before reattachment. Log growth and secret leakage are risks; cap bytes, redact known secret patterns, and provide deletion. If reconciliation is uncertain, report 'unknown—no retry' rather than rerun.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model cost for lifecycle events; modest local disk and relay D1 writes per event. One background-tier summarization call only when the owner requests a human explanation of a failure.
changes.latency_impact: Launch remains near current latency. Heartbeats add negligible local work; reconnect status is available in seconds instead of waiting for an HTTP timeout.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no confirmation gate. It makes existing arbitrary commands more observable; command text and output tails are sensitive and must use the existing authenticated Mac/relay paths with retention limits.
depends_on: A durable relay event stream with replay-from-sequence semantics
A local process supervisor that survives the request handler and records manifests
Wire shell lifecycle events into existing /journal, /jobs, and receipt APIs
Pendant notification consumer for completion/failure

changes.change: Add a cross-surface incident-correlation ledger, not another executor: on every Mac, browser, relay, or pendant failure, write a compact append-only event keyed by a shared correlationId and actionId; asynchronously join events by time window and parent job, attach the existing receipt/undo verdict, record disconnect/reconnect gaps, and expose one redacted incident bundle through the dashboard. Start with local-agent hooks around executor.js and browserBridge result handling, relay ingestion from pipeline events, and a pendant event envelope carrying boot/session sequence numbers. Deduplicate retries and reconnects by idempotency key; retain raw evidence locally and only upload redacted excerpts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a failure crosses devices, the owner sees one truthful timeline—what the pendant heard, what the relay dispatched, what the Mac/browser attempted, and where it stopped—instead of several incomplete job records. It directly enables the owner's requested self-filed pendant bug reports and makes support/debugging possible without asking them to reproduce the problem.
changes.effort: Medium: shared event schema and local hooks first, relay append/query and correlation worker second, dashboard incident panel and pendant envelope third. Add deterministic tests for dropped links, duplicate results, clock skew, and redaction.
changes.risk: Incorrect time correlation could merge two simultaneous jobs or split one across reconnects. Mitigate with parent IDs, monotonic device sequence numbers, confidence labels, and never deleting source receipts. If correlation fails, preserve separate events and show the uncertainty rather than inventing a story. UART/log volume must be capped and backpressured so audio and action latency are unaffected.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost for collection/correlation; optional background summarization costs about 1–2 cents per incident. Small D1/R2 growth from bounded redacted bundles; local ring buffers avoid shipping every raw log.
changes.latency_impact: No synchronous network dependency on action execution. Hook overhead should be under 5 ms; incident joining and summarization happen asynchronously, with a draft visible in roughly 1–3 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive stdout, environment variables, bearer tokens, cookies, authenticated page content, and secret UART fields are redacted before relay persistence. Preserve hashes and source locations for integrity. Raw logs stay on-device unless the owner explicitly exports them. This adds observability, not a gate or reduced access.
depends_on: A versioned event envelope shared by local-agent, relay, browser bridge, and pendant firmware
A pendant UART ring buffer and bounded event export
A relay incident storage/query route and retention policy
A local-agent failure-event hook for shell, typed actions, browser actions, timeouts, and planner errors

changes.change: Add a low-power wear/presence sensor and a hardware privacy state to the pendant: detect skin contact or lanyard removal, latch a local microphone/audio-capture mute and emit signed wear-state transitions over the existing radio link. Relay, Mac, and browser bridges consume that state as a shared session signal: when unworn, stop starting new capture or browser reads and mark in-flight work as paused; when worn again, resume only explicitly resumable work. Include a physical LED indication and a button override for false positives, with the state retained through brief link loss.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear the pendant all day without wondering whether it is listening or whether a private Mac/browser task will continue after they set it down. Removing it would be an immediate, visible privacy boundary that works even when the relay or Mac is unreachable, while putting it back on restores continuity instead of losing the session.
changes.effort: Hardware revision for a capacitive electrode or optical/proximity sensor, firmware debounce/calibration and signed event framing, relay session-state propagation, and Mac/browser hooks that pause only resumable work. Add tests for removal during speech, radio loss, false contact, charging, and rapid wear transitions.
changes.risk: A bad fit or clothing could cause false removal and interrupt a conversation; calibration, hysteresis, LED feedback, and an explicit button override mitigate this. A sensor failure must fail closed for capture but must not erase queued work. Do not infer identity or store biometric measurements—persist only boolean state, transition time, and confidence.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $0.20–$2 for a capacitive/proximity component and PCB/layout revision, with sub-milliamp average draw. Negligible API cost; only tiny state events cross the relay.
changes.latency_impact: Local mute/latch should take under 100 ms and must not depend on the network. Cross-surface pause notification should arrive within the normal link heartbeat, with reconnect reconciliation on return.
changes.security_impact: Strengthens privacy at the device boundary: local hardware mute is authoritative and signed wear events prevent an untrusted bridge from claiming the pendant is present. It introduces no new private data beyond presence transitions and should default to unworn on ambiguous sensor state.
depends_on: A pendant firmware event type for signed wear-state transitions
A local hardware mute path that survives dropped links
Relay session-state propagation to the Mac and browser bridge
Mac/browser job semantics that distinguish resumable from non-resumable work

changes.change: Add a non-blocking capability preflight and outcome verifier to every desktop action. Before UI actions, read the existing /observe reachability facts (Accessibility trusted/eventsPost, Screen Recording, secure input, foreground app, browser session); annotate the planned action with reachable/unreachable capabilities. After execution, run a typed postcondition probe appropriate to the action (frontmost app/window, volume, file hash, browser tab URL/title, or a bounded UI-state signal). If UI input is unreachable or the postcondition is false, mark the receipt as `not_verified` rather than success and automatically choose an equivalent available route (AppleScript/system API for app settings, shell for files/status, browser bridge for tabs), retaining the original attempt and fallback as one causal action group. Persist preflight, verification, fallback reason, and evidence IDs in /jobs/:id/receipts and expose aggregate unreachable-capability counts in /observe or /ops/snapshot. This is observability and recovery only: it must never block an action or add confirmation gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today the Mac reports clicks, typing, and key presses as successful even though the live host says Accessibility is not trusted and synthesized events are rejected. The owner can believe a task completed when nothing changed. This makes spoken completion reports honest and lets the system finish the same goal through a working path automatically, while showing exactly why a UI attempt was replaced.
changes.effort: Medium: implement preflight/postcondition adapters for the existing executor action types, causal receipt grouping, and a small dashboard/relay rendering change; add integration tests with permissions false and true.
changes.risk: A weak postcondition could produce false negatives or trigger an inappropriate fallback; keep fallback selection deterministic and record all evidence. Never retry non-idempotent writes automatically; only fallback when the action declares an idempotency key and a safe equivalent. If probes fail, report unknown rather than success.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for deterministic probes; saves planner tokens and repeated retries. Small local CPU/IO overhead per action. No new cloud data beyond existing receipt metadata and redacted evidence IDs.
changes.latency_impact: Tens to a few hundred milliseconds for local probes; avoids multi-second planner retries and misleading completion turns.
changes.security_impact: No new privileges and no restriction of FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Receipts must redact shell output, URLs/query strings, and private page text; store hashes/typed facts unless the owner explicitly requests detail.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt/undo implementation
GET /observe reachability facts
GET /ops/snapshot and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts observability surfaces
existing typed action metadata/idempotency keys

changes.change: Create a cross-surface execution lineage record keyed by one owner request ID, propagated unchanged through relay, planner routing, local job, browser command, and pendant audio. Each node appends only a compact event (tier/model, prompt/context digest and token counts, action IDs, latency, status, evidence IDs, and failure classification), while full private payloads stay at their origin. Add GET /lineage/:requestId and make /routing, /journal, /jobs, and relay_job_status join on that ID. Use the lineage's completed facts and failure reasons as a bounded continuation context when a long-running job resumes, instead of resending the whole fleet context.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A single spoken request currently becomes hard to explain across the Mac and relay: many jobs are unattributed (the live journal reports 112 unattributed actions), and the owner cannot tell whether a failure was the browser, permissions, network, or model. They would get one concise, trustworthy receipt—what each body did, what it cost, and what remains—while resumed work avoids repeating expensive context.
changes.effort: Medium-high: add request-ID propagation to relay/planner/executor/browser bridge, an append-only compact lineage store with bounded retention, and join views in the existing observability routes; no new action policy.
changes.risk: Correlating old jobs without IDs can be ambiguous; mark them legacy/unattributed rather than guessing. Digests must be one-way and payloads redacted. If the lineage store is unavailable, execution continues and local job receipts remain authoritative.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/local storage and deterministic hashing overhead; reduces planner prompt tokens on retries/resumptions and avoids duplicate model calls. No extra model invocation.
changes.latency_impact: Under ~20 ms local append per event; cross-node propagation is header/field-only. Resumptions should be faster than rebuilding context.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without centralizing private page or shell contents: only typed metadata, hashes, and sensitivity labels cross nodes. Keep lineage access bearer-protected and apply the existing retention policy.
depends_on: GET /routing live routing receipts
GET /journal and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
existing browser command request IDs/idempotency keys
relay persistent agent state and durable job records

changes.change: Add a tamper-evident causal execution ledger for every Mac action, including raw action type, normalized argv/command hash, cwd, environment-key allowlist, start/end timestamps, parent planner/relay request ID, retry lineage, exit code/signal, stdout/stderr hashes plus bounded redacted excerpts, and the exact receipt/undoability verdict. Link browser commands and relay announcements to the same trace ID, and expose a read-only replay bundle endpoint that can reconstruct why a job succeeded or failed without rerunning it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac says “failed” or “done,” the owner can see what actually ran, which attempt caused it, and whether recovery is possible—especially important when shell is intentionally unrestricted and browser retries currently repeat the same failing navigate. It also makes the pendant's later “what happened?” answer trustworthy even after the 120-job store rolls over.
changes.effort: Medium: schema and append-only writer in local-agent, trace propagation through executor/browser bridge/relay, redaction and retention tests, plus dashboard timeline rendering.
changes.risk: Ledger leakage of secrets through command lines or stderr, and storage growth. Mitigate with explicit secret-pattern redaction, hashes instead of full output by default, short retention with owner export, and atomic append/recovery after crashes. This is observation-only and must never block execution.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible compute/storage cost (roughly a few KB per action, bounded and compacted); no model cost unless the dashboard asks for a natural-language explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Under 5 ms synchronous metadata write; full output hashing/redaction can finish asynchronously without delaying the action result.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability but creates a sensitive local artifact. Encrypt at rest where available, keep it Mac-local by default, and send relay only trace IDs and redacted summaries unless the owner explicitly requests detail.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and /journal need a stable trace/parent ID field.
Existing job retention needs compaction/export so causal records survive beyond the 120-job window.
Relay and browser bridge need to echo the trace ID in completion events.

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface readiness lease and wake/resume protocol. The Mac agent publishes signed capability leases (shell, accessibility, screen recording, browser extension, relay link) with freshness and reason codes; the relay expires stale leases instead of treating a last-seen browser as online, parks dependent jobs with a single causal blocker, and resumes exactly once on a verified heartbeat. The pendant receives a one-sentence blocker only when the owner asks or a configured job becomes actionable, while the dashboard shows pending work grouped by blocker rather than nine opaque browser commands.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current Mac reports browser offline, 9 pending commands, missing Accessibility/Screen Recording, and ready=false, yet callers can still spend 45 seconds retrying the same navigation. The owner gets truthful “waiting for Safari bridge” state, no duplicate work, and automatic continuation when the bridge or permission becomes available—without changing the deliberate unrestricted shell policy.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define lease schema and signatures, heartbeat/expiry handling in local agent and relay, job dependency state machine, one-shot resume deduplication, pendant and dashboard status rendering.
changes.risk: A stale or incorrect lease could delay work or resume at the wrong time. Use short TTLs, monotonic attempt IDs, explicit blocker categories, and a manual “resume now” endpoint; expiry must park rather than discard jobs.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny D1/local state and heartbeat traffic; no additional model calls. One extra relay heartbeat per surface (seconds-scale cadence, configurable for battery).
changes.latency_impact: No impact on normal actions; failed jobs become parked immediately, and resume starts within one heartbeat interval (target 5–15 seconds).
changes.security_impact: Lease contents reveal device capability state but no page data; sign leases per paired Mac/relay and never include tokens, URLs, shell commands, or authenticated content.
depends_on: GET /ops/status and GET /browser/status must expose machine-readable capability reasons and timestamps.
Existing /jobs and /journal need a parked/blocked state and dependency/attempt fields.
Browser heartbeat/poll and relay mac-bridge presence must carry a shared trace or lease ID.
A small relay-to-pendant status event path is needed for actionable resume announcements.

changes.change: Make every Mac UI action pass through a preflight/postflight reachability contract. Before ui_click, type_text, press_keys, or browser-bridge commands, capture the current /observe permission and extension state; after the action, require an observable effect (focused app/title change, DOM mutation, or typed-value readback). Store a three-state result—confirmed, unverified, or failed—in the existing receipt and journal, and emit a compact pendant event. If Accessibility is false or the browser is offline, automatically switch to a non-UI route when one exists (shell/app open/read-only) and otherwise explain the exact missing condition instead of reporting success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Right now the Mac explicitly says synthesized events are not accepted and UI actions “report success while doing nothing”; browser is offline with nine queued commands. The owner gets truthful answers and useful fallback behavior instead of silently believing a failed click or typing action happened.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight/postflight wrapper, typed receipt schema, browser result correlation, and a small dashboard/pendant formatter; no new model required.
changes.risk: Some valid actions have no immediate observable effect and would be marked unverified; recover by allowing action-specific verification strategies and retaining raw receipts. Do not block execution—this is observability and fallback only, consistent with FULL_CONTROL_MODE.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and one /observe read per UI action; no model cost for normal paths. Optional background summarization only for repeated failures.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms for local preflight and postflight; skips vision/model calls unless the action explicitly requires visual confirmation.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by keeping evidence local and emitting only status/counts to the relay; does not reduce the owner's unrestricted execution policy.
depends_on: A typed receipt extension in actionReceipts.js with confirmed/unverified/failed and verification evidence
A browser command result carrying session/tab correlation and DOM readback metadata
Existing GET /observe and GET /browser/status being callable from the executor
A pendant event schema over POST /pipeline/events

changes.change: Propagate one correlation ID and routing receipt from the pendant/relay request through planner, Mac job, browser command, and final pipeline event. Add a deterministic context ledger recording selected context sections, estimated tokens, model tier, latency, and whether the result was confirmed or merely delegated; expose per-owner-task totals in /routing and the dashboard, and let background retries reuse the original plan digest instead of resending the full fleet context.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The live routing report shows 112 of 120 retained jobs unattributed to a model tier and planner requests averaging about 8.8k tokens. The owner cannot tell whether a delayed job cost one cheap retry or repeated expensive planning. This makes asynchronous work both cheaper and explainable without changing what the agent is allowed to do.
changes.effort: Medium: correlation propagation across relay, planner, executor, browser bridge, and journal; compact digest hashing; dashboard aggregation.
changes.risk: Missing propagation in one surface could create partial records; treat absent fields as unknown rather than infer them, and preserve existing job execution. Digest reuse must invalidate on changed permissions, tab, or task state.
changes.cost_impact: Small local storage overhead; likely reduces planner-token spend substantially on retries and status questions. No additional model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible bookkeeping (single-digit milliseconds); avoids planner calls for deterministic status and retry decisions.
changes.security_impact: Store hashes and metadata rather than prompt/page contents in the cross-surface ledger; keep sensitive browser payloads local to the session.
depends_on: Existing GET /routing and routingStats.js
Durable job IDs and receipts from /jobs and /journal
Relay pipeline event correlation on POST /pipeline/events
Typed browser request IDs/session affinity from browserBridge.js and browserSessions.js

changes.change: Add a reachability-aware execution envelope around every Mac action. Before dispatch, snapshot /observe-derived facts (Accessibility/input reachability, screen recording, secure input, browser heartbeat, foreground app, session/tab identity); annotate the job with the selected route and an explicit `mayNotReach` warning, but never block in FULL_CONTROL_MODE. After dispatch, run a bounded, action-specific verification (browser command result/DOM change, app/window state, file existence/hash, volume state, or a second observation) and set receipt status to `verified`, `completed-unverified`, or `failed-to-reach` instead of treating the host API's return as success. For browser commands, automatically requeue with exponential backoff only when the extension is offline/stale, and collapse duplicate pending commands by idempotency key. Expose preflight, verification, retry history, and the exact fallback route in GET /jobs/:jobId, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, /observe, and the dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can honestly say “I changed it,” “I could not reach the screen,” or “it may have changed but I cannot verify,” rather than claiming success while Accessibility is pointed at the wrong binary or Safari is not polling. Long tasks recover after a transient browser disconnect without duplicate clicks, and the owner gets a useful explanation instead of a silent 45-second timeout.
changes.effort: Medium: central execution wrapper plus per-action verifiers, idempotency/retry state, dashboard fields, and tests against the existing browser/job/receipt paths. No model change required.
changes.risk: Verification may be inconclusive or misclassify a legitimate change; preserve raw host result and allow the job to remain completed-unverified. Retries must be limited to operations marked idempotent and use request/action keys; never replay arbitrary shell or irreversible UI actions automatically. This adds latency for verification, bounded by ~1–3 seconds for local checks and existing browser timeout for browser recovery.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small local CPU/IO. Saves expensive model turns by returning structured failure causes and avoiding repeated blind attempts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds ~0.1–1 s for local preflight and verification; browser retries are asynchronous and do not hold the voice turn open. Fast-path read-only shell can skip verification when its exit code and captured stdout are sufficient.
changes.security_impact: No new authorization or restrictions; FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted shell remain. Receipts gain sensitive metadata (paths, URLs, foreground app), so redact secrets and retain only hashes/snippets in the dashboard/log export.

changes.change: Add an execution-health preflight and fallback planner driven by the existing read-only /observe, /ops/status, /browser/status, and /routing data. Before dispatching UI or browser actions, attach a capability snapshot (accessibility/inputReachability, screen recording, browser online/lastSeen, pending-command age, relay reachability) to the job. If UI reachability is false, do not claim success: automatically route reads to shell/AppleScript where possible, route public-page reads to relay/browser-run, and return a precise unmet prerequisite for private browser work. If the bridge is offline or commands are stale, collapse/supersede duplicate pending requests by idempotency key rather than waiting 45 seconds per attempt. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and all owner-approved actions unchanged; this is observability, routing, and recovery, not a gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently can hear a receipt saying a click or typing succeeded when macOS rejected the event, and browser requests can burn nearly a minute while the extension is offline. This makes the pendant tell the truth immediately, use an alternate path when one exists, and avoid repeated dead waits.
changes.effort: Medium: health snapshot schema, planner preflight, fallback mapping for common reads, stale-command coalescing, and tests for truthful receipts.
changes.risk: A transient permission or bridge outage could cause a fallback to a less rich result or a fast prerequisite message; preserve the original requested action and make fallback provenance explicit. Never silently substitute a mutation. Recovery is retry after health changes.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; fewer wasted model turns and browser timeouts. Small local CPU/storage overhead for health snapshots.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <100 ms local preflight; avoids current 45-second browser timeout loops and unnecessary planner retries.
changes.security_impact: Read-only health metadata stays local and should redact URLs/titles from relay telemetry. No new authority or restriction is introduced.
depends_on: Existing GET /observe, GET /ops/status, GET /browser/status, GET /routing, and durable job receipts
A typed fallback registry for read-only intents

changes.change: Create a cross-surface failure-recovery ledger. When a Mac job fails, persist a normalized incident containing job/action IDs, surface, error signature, health snapshot, safe diagnostics, likely cause, retryability, and a concrete repair recipe. Let the relay/pedant query incidents by natural references ('that browser thing', 'why didn't it open') and let mac-planner resume from the failed step rather than replaying the entire plan. Automatically deduplicate repeated failures and mark incidents resolved when a later receipt verifies recovery; never auto-run a mutation merely because a repair recipe exists.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today the owner gets a failure string and must remember what happened or ask the whole task again. The pendant could explain 'the click never reached the Mac because Accessibility is assigned to another binary' or 'the browser bridge has been offline since…', then resume only the missing step after the fix.
changes.effort: Medium: normalized incident schema in the durable job store/relay D1, error fingerprinting, health-snapshot attachment, natural-reference lookup, and resume-from-step integration.
changes.risk: Error details can contain private paths, URLs, or snippets; redact secrets and keep raw diagnostics on the Mac. A bad repair classification could waste a retry, so recipes should be advisory and idempotency-aware.
changes.cost_impact: Low local/D1 storage and negligible model cost; fewer repeated planner calls and fewer duplicate actions.
changes.latency_impact: Instant status answers from stored incidents; resume adds only the remaining-step latency.
changes.security_impact: Cross-surface relay records must use existing pairing/auth and sensitivity labels. Do not send shell stdout or private page content unless explicitly requested.
depends_on: Existing durable /jobs and /journal records
Existing receipts and idempotency keys
GET /observe and /ops/status health data
Relay job-status surface and mac-planner resume support

changes.change: Ship the local agent as a single signed, stable macOS application identity whose Accessibility and Screen Recording grants are requested and consumed by the same executable that posts input events. At startup, compare the bundle ID, code-signing identity, executable path, and TCC probe result; surface a one-click repair path when they diverge. Keep the current unrestricted execution policy, but refuse to label UI work as successful when the runtime identity cannot reach the screen. Add an integration test that launches the packaged app, verifies the TCC identity, performs a zero-impact focus/read probe, and survives an app update without silently losing the grant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should not have to understand that Accessibility was granted to a different binary than the running agent. A packaging/runtime identity fix would make GUI control persist across launches and updates instead of silently doing nothing while receipts claim success.
changes.effort: Medium to high: signing and bundle packaging changes, TCC migration/repair UX, startup diagnostics, and a release test on a clean Mac and an upgraded installation.
changes.risk: Changing the signed identity can invalidate an existing grant once, requiring the owner to re-enable it; retain a clear migration prompt and preserve shell/browser capabilities while UI permission is repaired. Do not modify the TCC database programmatically.
changes.cost_impact: No per-call API cost; modest release engineering and QA cost. No meaningful runtime power draw.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible startup identity check; removes false-success retries and long GUI debugging loops.
changes.security_impact: A stable signed identity improves the meaning of the owner's explicit macOS permissions. It does not add authority or reduce FULL_CONTROL_MODE; private diagnostics remain local.
depends_on: Existing /observe inputReachability and permissions reporting
Packaged AI Pendant Agent application identity
Existing action receipts and /ops status dashboard
A clean-install and upgrade test harness

changes.change: Extend every Mac/browser action receipt into a compact execution trace: normalized action fingerprint and idempotency key, surface/session/tab, planner tier and model, queue/start/extension-response timestamps, timeout phase, effect certainty (no-effect/changed/unknown), and recovery eligibility. Persist the trace in the existing job record and expose filtered summaries through /journal and /logs; aggregate by fingerprint so repeated failures become one incident instead of dozens of opaque jobs. Redact command arguments, URLs, and typed text by default while retaining hashes and owner-visible labels.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a task fails, the owner can immediately hear or see whether Safari was offline, stuck on a dialog, timed out after execution, or never started—and whether retrying is safe. It also makes the system stop wasting time on the same failing browser navigation and makes model cost and latency attributable instead of reporting 112 unattributed jobs.
changes.effort: Medium: receipt schema migration, executor instrumentation around local-agent/browserBridge calls, journal aggregation, and a small dashboard/pendant formatter. Existing receipts and journal provide the storage and read-only surface; no action gate is required.
changes.risk: Older jobs will lack fields and must render as unknown. Incorrect effect certainty could cause an unsafe retry, so unknown must remain non-retryable. Hashing must be stable without leaking secrets; retain raw details only in the local job store under existing access. Recover by falling back to legacy receipt rendering if migration fails.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few hundred bytes per action and modest local JSON/D1 growth. Aggregation reduces future planner prompt tokens by sending one incident summary rather than repeated full errors.
changes.latency_impact: Under 5 ms local instrumentation per action; /journal aggregation may add tens of milliseconds. No extra network round trip on the execution critical path.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without narrowing the owner's deliberate FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Default redaction prevents shell command contents, authenticated URLs, and form text from entering relay/model prompts; exact data remains local for debugging.
depends_on: Existing actionReceipts/jobTracker and /journal implementation
A stable action/session fingerprint convention shared by Mac and browser bridges
Dashboard or pendant status formatter consuming the new typed fields

changes.change: Add a non-blocking action truth layer. Before dispatch, snapshot the relevant reachability state (Accessibility identity, secure-input, foreground app, browser session heartbeat). After dispatch, run an action-specific verifier: shell exit code and declared output predicate; file hash/size; app setting readback; UI accessibility-tree/text/window-state delta; browser URL/title/DOM fingerprint or command result. Store sentAt, verifiedAt, verification method, observed delta, and confidence in the existing receipt, with explicit states sent, confirmed, no-op, indeterminate, or failed. If no-op/indeterminate, automatically try one safe alternate implementation (for example AppleScript/API instead of synthetic typing) and report both attempts; never claim success solely from dispatch completion. Emit compact progress to /pipeline/events and expose aggregate no-op rates in /ops/snapshot for dashboard and relay.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops being told that a UI action succeeded when the Mac's current Accessibility identity means it did nothing. They get a fast, honest answer and useful recovery instead of silently losing work.
changes.effort: Medium: verifier registry for existing action types, one receipt schema extension, local observation adapters, and dashboard/relay rendering. Start with UI typing/clicks, shell, file writes, and browser navigation.
changes.risk: A legitimate action may have no visible delta (e.g. clicking an already-selected control), or the verifier may inspect stale UI. Mark those indeterminate rather than false, retain raw evidence locally, and allow the existing undo/job retry paths. Alternate execution must be bounded to avoid duplicate side effects.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible for local checks and hashes; occasional accessibility-tree or browser extraction work is local. Vision fallback is the only material API cost and should be rare.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–300 ms for local pre/post checks; verification can stream asynchronously so the owner hears progress immediately. Vision fallback may add several seconds.
changes.security_impact: Receipts gain potentially sensitive window titles, URLs, and snippets. Keep raw evidence local, redact relay payloads, and apply TTL deletion; no new permission gate is introduced.
depends_on: Fix Accessibility entitlement/grant so the running AI Pendant Agent identity can actually post events, or expose a truthful 'cannot verify UI' state
Extend actionReceipts.js and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts with verification fields
Wire /observe and /browser/status heartbeat snapshots into executor pre/post hooks
Define compact /pipeline/events and relay status payloads for sent-vs-confirmed
Browser reconnect/janitor should classify the existing stale pending command queue

changes.change: Build a permission-drift and dependency repair loop. On agent startup and before UI/browser work, compare the running bundle identity, Accessibility/Input Monitoring/Screen Recording state, browser-extension heartbeat, relay reachability, and configured paths. Persist a versioned diagnostic incident (for example ACCESSIBILITY_IDENTITY_MISMATCH or BROWSER_QUEUE_STALE) rather than burying it in a generic failure. Generate one Mac-native repair action/instruction with the exact System Settings pane and affected binary, let the pendant announce the short reason, and automatically re-probe after the owner fixes it. Keep the incident attached to subsequent jobs so the planner stops retrying impossible actions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one understandable explanation—'the agent is not allowed to control the screen' or 'the browser bridge has nine stale commands'—and a guided path to restore capability, instead of repeated no-op actions and 45-second timeouts.
changes.effort: Medium: normalize existing /ops/status and /observe facts into incident codes, add repair recipes and post-fix probes, and surface active incidents in dashboard, relay status, and job receipts.
changes.risk: A permission may legitimately be absent or a stale queue may contain useful work. Diagnose and label only; do not revoke, delete, or gate anything automatically. Queue cleanup remains an explicit repair action and all incidents retain evidence.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost for deterministic checks; tiny relay/database storage for incident records. No additional hardware.
changes.latency_impact: A few hundred milliseconds at startup or before a relevant action; avoids the current 45-second browser timeout and repeated retries.
changes.security_impact: System Settings instructions and bundle IDs are not sensitive; do not transmit private page contents. Incident payloads should exclude command strings and URLs unless already present in the job's local receipt.

A small local incident store and repair-recipe registry
Browser reconnect/janitor for stale pending commands

changes.change: Add an event-sourced invariant engine separate from one-shot jobs and page watches. Each invariant stores a typed desired state, evidence predicate, check cadence, expiry, quiet hours, last independently verified value, and a recovery recipe. The engine consumes Mac/browser/relay presence events, schedules checks on the cheapest available surface, records drift and recovery attempts, and requires two consecutive positive observations before declaring a repaired state. When the Mac is asleep or permissions are invalid, it records 'unverified' rather than treating absence as drift, then resumes from the relay when presence returns.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can say 'keep this true' for things such as a file backup being current, a meeting app being configured, a focus mode remaining enabled, or a private web setting retaining a value—and receive a useful drift alert instead of discovering later that a one-time action silently stopped holding.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: new durable state machine and scheduler, typed probes/recovery recipes for Mac and browser, relay wake/resume events, and dashboard controls for pause, expiry, evidence, and history.
changes.risk: A recovery recipe could repeatedly undo the owner's intentional change or create an action loop. Bound retries, require an explicit owner-selected recovery policy, detect conflicting manual changes, and expire invariants by default. Offline and permission failures must remain unverified, never falsely healthy or broken.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and background polling cost; deterministic checks are inexpensive. Background model use is limited to compiling new invariants or resolving ambiguous drift.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on ordinary actions. Checks run asynchronously; alerts are near-real-time after a presence event, while recovery can take seconds to minutes.
changes.security_impact: Invariant definitions and evidence may expose private files, app state, or logged-in pages. Store raw evidence locally, redact relay notifications, encrypt definitions, and never include page contents in routine heartbeat payloads.
depends_on: A durable invariant store and scheduler independent of existing /routines
Typed cross-surface postcondition/probe adapters
Relay presence and wake/resume event delivery
A recovery policy model with bounded retries and explicit expiry
Dashboard and pendant controls for pause, inspect evidence, and abandon

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution-readiness and postcondition verifier around every Mac/browser action. Before dispatch, snapshot typed reachability (Accessibility identity and event probe, screen recording, foreground app, browser bridge lease/queue depth, shell availability). After dispatch, require an action-specific observable postcondition: changed volume/value, opened app/window, file hash, browser URL/title or extracted text, or explicit shell exit/output. Attach readiness, verification, fallbackUsed, and failureClass to the existing receipt; mark UI actions as unverified when Accessibility is false even if the low-level API returned success. Emit a compact remediation event for the relay rather than making the executor gate or refuse anything.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing false 'done' reports. When the agent cannot control the screen, or Safari has gone offline, it can say exactly that and use a working CLI/AppleScript/browser route where available; every action still retains maximum access and no approval gate.
changes.effort: Medium: one typed verifier and action adapters in executor/actionReceipts, plus browser lease/status integration and a small remediation mapper. Add integration tests for the current Accessibility mismatch and offline queue.
changes.risk: Some actions have no observable postcondition and will become 'unverified' rather than failed; adapters could misclassify a legitimate no-op. Recover by preserving raw results and allowing the planner to select an explicit verification mode. Never replay an action solely because verification timed out.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; fewer expensive planner retries. Local storage increases receipts by roughly 1–3 KB per action and keeps sensitive evidence as hashes/typed facts unless explicitly requested.
changes.latency_impact: About 50–300 ms for local readiness checks; up to 3 seconds only when an action requests postcondition polling. Shell-only reads can skip the UI/browser checks.
changes.security_impact: Improves honesty without narrowing permissions. Raw shell output and private page content remain local; relay receives class/status/hashes by default. Existing owner policy of unrestricted execution and no confirmation remains unchanged.
depends_on: A stable typed action-to-postcondition registry for shell, AppleScript, UI, and browser actions
Fix planner-tier/request-id propagation so receipts stop accumulating unattributed actions
Durable browser command polling/retry so remediation can survive a bridge restart

changes.change: Make request identity and planner-tier attribution mandatory end to end: mint one traceId at the pendant/relay boundary, carry it through planning, delegated Mac/browser jobs, retries, and receipts, and persist planner tier, model, token estimate, latency, fallback chain, and terminal outcome. Add a compact per-request timeline to the existing journal/ops snapshot and use it to route routine status/recovery work to the cheap model automatically.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask 'what happened and why did it take so long?' and get one trustworthy answer instead of disconnected Mac jobs. It also prevents expensive realtime reasoning from being spent on routine battery checks, retries, or completion receipts.
changes.effort: Medium: request-context middleware plus fields in relay job records, local jobTracker, routingStats, and journal projection; add dashboard and spoken receipt serializers.
changes.risk: Older jobs remain unattributed and mixed-version clients may omit fields. Treat missing fields as explicitly unknown, never infer them, and preserve backward-compatible reads.
changes.cost_impact: Small local/D1 storage increase; likely lowers API spend by routing recovery, status, and scheduled work to the background tier. No extra model call is required for attribution.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible per request; a few milliseconds for context propagation and journal aggregation.
changes.security_impact: Trace IDs must be opaque and contain no URL, account, or prompt text. Keep model/token metadata separate from private action payloads; redact shell output and page text from relay-facing summaries.
depends_on: A shared trace-context schema between relay-realtime, mac-planner, browser-extension, and unified
A durable browser job runner/result stream so delegated work has one trace across restarts
Dashboard and spoken receipt support for the new timeline fields

changes.change: Add a pendant-side task-control state machine with durable intent records: short press acknowledges the current remote task, long press pauses it, double press requests cancel, and LED/haptic patterns show queued, paused, waiting-for-Mac, resumed, failed, or completed. The firmware should persist only a compact task handle, cursor version, and requested transition in its existing flash/NVS, retry delivery after reconnect, and never execute remote work itself.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely walk away from the Mac and still control a long-running browser or desktop task without reopening the app or relying on a live voice session. A glance or vibration tells them whether work is paused, waiting, or actually finished instead of leaving them guessing.
changes.effort: Medium firmware and relay integration: define signed task-transition messages, debounce button gestures, add reconnect replay and server acknowledgements, then expose the state in spoken receipts and the Mac dashboard.
changes.risk: Accidental long/double presses could pause or cancel work, and stale transition messages could target an old task. Require a matching task-handle/version, make cancel idempotent, use a distinct long-press duration, and provide a short haptic confirmation before sending the transition.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost. A few hundred bytes of persistent state and under 8 KB firmware/RAM budget; no new hardware if the existing button and LED/haptic path support the patterns.
changes.latency_impact: Local feedback under 100 ms; transition delivery depends on the relay link and is retried in the background.
changes.security_impact: The pendant sends intent only, never private page content. Authenticate transitions to the paired relay and reject stale or unpaired task handles; preserve the existing no-gate execution policy for actions themselves.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface task/checkpoint identity and lifecycle API
Relay support for idempotent pause/cancel/resume transitions
Mac/browser jobs that can honor a pause at action boundaries and report acknowledgements

changes.change: Add a browser-bridge liveness controller around the existing command queue: persist command lease/heartbeat timestamps, cap or back off retries, quarantine commands whose lease is stale or whose attempt count exceeds a threshold, and expose queue health (oldest age, claimed duration, attempts, last heartbeat, per-device online state) in /ops/status and the dashboard. When the bridge is offline or repeatedly times out, fail fast with a typed 'bridge_unhealthy' receipt instead of spending ~45 seconds per navigate and leaving nine commands pending; automatically requeue only after a fresh heartbeat, with idempotency preserved.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Safari tasks stop hanging for nearly a minute and do not silently accumulate stale work. The owner gets a truthful, immediate explanation and can recover by reopening the extension, while healthy commands still run unattended and maximum Mac access is unchanged.
changes.effort: Medium: queue schema migration, lease watchdog, retry policy, status aggregation, dashboard card, and tests for crash/reconnect/idempotent requeue.
changes.risk: A slow but valid page could be quarantined too early; use generous lease limits, explicit heartbeat extension, and manual/retry recovery. A process crash during the transition could leave a command in quarantine; provide requeue/quarantine-clear endpoints and retain receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; fewer wasted browser action round trips and fewer planner retries. Small local persistence and watchdog overhead.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy actions unchanged; unhealthy actions fail in seconds rather than ~45s, and reconnect recovery is bounded by the next heartbeat.
changes.security_impact: No new data access. Queue diagnostics should redact URLs/query strings by default and retain full details only in the existing authenticated job record.
depends_on: chg-14accc01 request IDs/idempotency/tab affinity
browser extension heartbeat/poll/result routes
existing action receipts and /ops/status observability

changes.change: Extend run_shell job receipts with bounded execution telemetry and recovery metadata: argv/command hash, resolved cwd, start/end/queue timestamps, exit code or signal, timeout classification, stdout/stderr tails with secret-pattern redaction, and a captured child-process summary on timeout. Run shell commands in a tracked process group so a timed-out command can be terminated and marked cleanly; expose a 'retry with same inputs' operation that links to the failed receipt and never duplicates a completed job.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails, the owner hears what actually happened—wrong directory, missing binary, permission error, or timeout—instead of a generic failure. The agent can recover faster from the known project-location problem and avoid leaving hidden child processes running after a timeout.
changes.effort: Medium: instrument computerControl.runShell/executor, add bounded/redacted output storage and process-group cleanup, extend receipt schema and dashboard/job API, and test exit/timeout/partial-output cases.
changes.risk: Command output can contain secrets or large logs; cap bytes, redact common tokens, and keep full raw output out of relay/pendant responses. Process-group termination can kill children intentionally spawned by a command; record the signal and make retry explicit in the job API. Existing old jobs remain readable with absent telemetry.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model cost; a small local disk increase bounded per receipt and less repeated planner work after failures.
changes.latency_impact: A few milliseconds of instrumentation; timeout failures become promptly diagnosable and cleanup is deterministic.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without reducing FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Store telemetry locally behind existing bearer auth; send only a sanitized summary to relay.
depends_on: existing action receipts at local-agent/actionReceipts.js
existing GET /jobs and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
computerControl.runShell timeout path and current unrestricted FULL_CONTROL_MODE

changes.change: Add a live capability-health handshake and dead-letter recovery loop. Before UI/browser actions, publish a typed snapshot from /ops/status + /observe (accessibility reachability, screen-recording, browser-extension heartbeat, pending-command age, relay reachability). Mark UI actions as untrusted when eventsPost=false instead of accepting success receipts; route eligible work to shell/AppleScript or relay/public-browser paths, and move stale browser commands into a retry/dead-letter state with reason, expiry, and idempotency key. Reconcile the result into /journal and /routing so every action has a tier and health snapshot.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will stop telling you that it clicked or typed when macOS ignored the event, and it will recover from a sleeping browser extension instead of silently accumulating nine commands. You get an honest spoken answer and a usable fallback without adding approval gates or reducing the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: shared health schema, preflight in executor/browser bridge, stale-command sweeper, and journal/routing fields; add integration tests for inaccessible UI and extension reconnect.
changes.risk: A fallback could choose the wrong surface or replay a non-idempotent browser action. Mitigate by only auto-retrying declared-idempotent reads, never replaying mutations, and retaining the original receipt/evidence; dead-letter rather than execute when ambiguity remains.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and one cheap deterministic status pass; avoids wasted planner calls and repeated failed browser actions.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for local health checks; avoids 120-second hangs and repeated retries.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no gates. Health snapshots must redact URLs, tab contents, and environment secrets; only capability/status metadata crosses relay.
depends_on: Existing GET /ops/status and GET /observe observability routes
Existing browser heartbeat/poll/result queue and idempotency keys
Existing durable /journal and /routing receipts
A typed fallback matrix for shell/AppleScript versus browser actions

changes.change: Introduce a single execution-trace ID propagated from relay request through planner routing, Mac executor, browser bridge, receipts, and journal. Persist a compact event chain: requested intent, selected surface/tier, health snapshot hash, exact typed action (or redacted shell fingerprint), OS-level result, external verification result, retry/fallback, and final owner-visible status. Backfill tier attribution for new jobs and expose GET /journal/:jobId/trace plus a relay-friendly redacted form.
