changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a task goes wrong, the pendant can distinguish 'the command failed,' 'the Mac accepted it but the screen was unreachable,' and 'the browser never received it.' You can trust the explanation and choose a recovery, instead of repeating an action blindly.
changes.effort: Medium, touching relay request metadata, planner receipts, executor/jobTracker, browser bridge, and dashboard display; low-risk migration because existing jobs remain readable without traces.
changes.risk: Trace growth and accidental leakage of commands or private page data. Use bounded event counts, retention, redaction/fingerprints, and sensitivity labels; if trace persistence fails, execution must continue and emit a degraded receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/local JSON overhead; no extra model calls. Reduces repeated planner calls caused by opaque failures.
changes.latency_impact: One in-memory correlation ID and append per event; typically <10 ms, with asynchronous persistence where safe.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability while requiring strict redaction. Raw shell, URLs, tab text, and secrets stay local; relay receives only typed summaries unless explicitly requested.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and /journal persistence
Existing /routing tier receipts
Existing browser command IDs/idempotency keys
Relay request metadata propagation

changes.change: Wire a non-blocking execution preflight and verification envelope into every Mac/browser job. Before dispatch, snapshot /ops/status, /observe, and /browser/status; annotate each action with viable routes and host readiness. After dispatch, require route-specific evidence (exit code/stdout for shell, changed app/window or state query for UI, browser result/heartbeat for extension) and classify the job as completed, completed_with_fallback, queued_offline, failed, or host_unreachable. Persist the preflight and evidence references in the existing job receipt/journal, and have relay-realtime speak the concise result to the pendant. Do not gate or reduce FULL_CONTROL_MODE.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer and useful fallback when a command cannot reach the Mac. Today /observe proves UI event calls can report success while doing nothing, and the browser has nine commands queued while offline; this change prevents lost time and makes unattended work recoverable.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight schema, executor hooks, route-specific postconditions, journal/dashboard rendering, and planner fallback rules.
changes.risk: Some legitimate actions have no observable postcondition and may be labeled uncertain; preserve raw receipts and allow a later status check. A stale preflight can race with permission or connectivity changes, so timestamp every snapshot and re-check after failures.
changes.cost_impact: No new hardware or API spend. Deterministic checks add negligible CPU and under ~1k tokens only when a model must summarize an unusual failure.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local preflight and state verification; no extra LLM turn on ordinary shell actions.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry may include active app and browser metadata; keep full snapshots local and project a minimal status to relay. Does not introduce approvals or restrict the owner's unrestricted shell policy.
depends_on: Existing /ops/status, /observe, /browser/status, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and /journal/:jobId routes
A typed postcondition schema for shell, AppleScript/UI, and browser actions
Relay outcome event and dashboard rendering

changes.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor and a dedicated charge/alert controller to the pendant, with firmware patterns for relay-connected, request accepted, completed, failed, and stale/offline states. Keep the LED as a redundant visual channel and expose a quiet-hours setting from the Mac dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know whether a remote Mac/browser task finished without looking at the pendant or hearing speech—especially while walking, in a meeting, or when the Mac is offline. This gives the wearable a reliable physical status channel that the current single-LED prototype cannot provide.
changes.effort: Low-to-medium hardware revision: motor, transistor/driver, PCB/enclosure revision, vibration patterns, battery characterization, and firmware event plumbing.
changes.risk: Vibration can be distracting or drain the small battery; cap pulse duration, provide quiet hours, and fall back to LED-only on low battery. Mechanical noise may be undesirable in meetings.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$3 in components at prototype volume plus PCB/enclosure revision; brief pulses add negligible average draw but require battery validation.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful network or model latency; local notification begins as soon as the pendant receives the relay event.
changes.security_impact: No new data leaves the device. Only compact outcome codes and timestamps are required; command contents remain off-device.
depends_on: A compact relay-to-pendant outcome event carrying request id, state, and timestamp
Firmware state machine for action outcomes and quiet-hours configuration
Battery telemetry and durable reconnect handling

changes.change: Add a bridge watchdog and failure-aware executor around browser actions. Before dispatch, issue a cheap local health snapshot (extension polling age, Safari frontmost/window state, tab/session id); attach it to the existing job and receipt. On timeout, stop waiting at a short staged deadline, classify offline vs no-answer vs page-load, and run a single read-only reattach/retry when the action is idempotent. Persist the original request id, retry lease, health snapshots, and final effect verdict so the dashboard and pendant can explain exactly what happened. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted capability unchanged; this is telemetry and recovery, not a blocking policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Safari failures become fast, legible, and recoverable instead of burning 45 seconds and leaving uncertainty about whether a page changed. The owner can trust 'nothing changed' because it is backed by a receipt and pre/post health evidence, while successful reads recover without manual extension toggling.
changes.effort: Medium: browser bridge heartbeat endpoint and polling-age state; executor state machine for staged deadlines and idempotent retry; receipt schema extension; tests for offline, modal, timeout, and successful reattach; dashboard/pendant event formatting.
changes.risk: A false idempotency classification could duplicate a write, so only actions explicitly declared read/navigation-safe may retry; all others fail once with evidence. A watchdog may misdiagnose a slow page, recovered by preserving the original timeout as a final deadline and never discarding raw bridge errors.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage (a few KB per failed job, subject to existing retention); no model cost for normal paths. One background model call only when deterministic signals conflict.
changes.latency_impact: Health probe adds under 200 ms; staged timeout returns a progress event quickly while retaining a bounded overall deadline. Successful retries add at most one bridge round trip; failed actions avoid repeated 45-second blind waits.
changes.security_impact: Health metadata is local and authenticated; do not capture DOM or page text in watchdog snapshots. Correlate by opaque request/tab ids and apply existing receipt retention/deletion.
depends_on: Authenticated browser extension heartbeat/polling-age signal
Explicit per-action idempotency/effect metadata in browser command queue
Pendant job-transition push channel
Existing action receipts and /journal observability

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution-readiness preflight and short-lived health cache. Before mac-planner or relay enqueues browser_* or computer-use work, query the local agent's /ops/status and /browser/status (with a heartbeat-age check), classify the requested action's prerequisites, and return a typed blocker immediately when the surface is offline, permissions are missing, or the queue is saturated. Include last-seen time, pending-command count, required user remedy, and a retry-after estimate; reconcile/mark stale browser commands so a dead extension cannot accumulate work. Relay and pendant should speak this result instead of waiting for a 45-second timeout. Do not gate or restrict FULL_CONTROL shell actions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer in under a second—“Chrome bridge is offline; enable the extension”—instead of waiting nearly a minute for a failed browser action. It prevents repeated stale commands and makes it clear whether a request can run now, while preserving the owner's maximum-access Mac shell policy.
changes.effort: Medium: shared readiness schema in mac-planner/local-agent, preflight hooks in browser action dispatch and mac_delegate, stale-queue reconciliation, and relay/pendant rendering. Add tests for offline, stale heartbeat, missing permission, queue saturation, and recovery.
changes.risk: A false offline reading could refuse a task that would have succeeded, so preflight must be advisory for shell and retry once for browser after a fresh heartbeat. Stale-command cleanup must only remove commands with expired leases and retain receipts/audit history. Recovery is automatic on the next heartbeat.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; avoids wasting expensive planner/realtime turns and 45-second local waits. Small local state for health snapshots and leases.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms for a cached/local status check, while reducing failed browser attempts from ~45 s to sub-second truthful feedback.
changes.security_impact: Read-only health metadata crosses Mac→relay (surface state, timestamps, counts), never page contents or credentials. Keep URLs/titles out of the readiness payload and redact permission details to capability names.
depends_on: Existing authenticated /ops/status and /browser/status routes
Existing browser heartbeat/poll and command receipts
Existing relay job status / pendant event path
A durable browser queue/runner or lease semantics (chg-16bc5dee)

changes.change: Instrument the existing unrestricted run_shell path with a shell execution envelope without changing authorization: normalize the command into an invocation record (cwd, argv-or-raw command, timeout, selected environment keys), capture start/end monotonic times, exit code/signal, timeout flag, bounded stdout/stderr plus full-output hashes, and a best-effort effect class (read, reversible, irreversible, unknown). Attach the envelope to the existing job journal and receipt, and expose a compact version through relay_job_status. For raw shell pipelines that cannot be parsed, preserve the exact command and mark classification unknown rather than pretending it is safe.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the agent runs a command unattended, the owner can finally tell what actually happened, where it ran, whether it timed out, and what output was produced—especially for permanent operations that undo.js cannot reverse. Failures become diagnosable instead of opaque.
changes.effort: Medium: wrapper around computerControl.runShell, redaction/bounded-output utility, journal/receipt schema migration, and status rendering. Add regression tests for cwd inheritance, timeout, nonzero exit, multiline output, and commands containing secrets.
changes.risk: Command text and output may contain credentials or private data; redact known secret-shaped values, cap inline output, hash/archive only under existing local retention, and never send full stdout/stderr to the relay by default. Parsing must not alter execution semantics. If instrumentation fails, execution should still return its original result with an instrumentation_error field.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model/API cost; modest local disk for bounded receipts. Avoids repeated expensive planner retries by making failures actionable.
changes.latency_impact: Typically under 5 ms plus bounded capture overhead; no additional model round trip and no confirmation gate.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability while retaining FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted network/env as the owner requires. Treat command/output fields as sensitive, apply local-only default, and expose only redacted summaries remotely.
depends_on: Existing /jobs, /journal, and receipt endpoints
Existing actionReceipt schema (chg-5fc73ce3)
computerControl.runShell wrapper and job lifecycle

changes.change: Add a capability-aware preflight and result contract for every UI-dependent Mac action. Before ui_click/ui_menu/type_text/press_keys/computer-use steps, consult the existing read-only observation state (Accessibility trust, inputReachability, screen recording, foreground app). If reachability is false, do not invoke the action as successful: return `blocked_unreachable` with the exact missing permission/binary mismatch and suggested recovery (`Enable Accessibility for AI Pendant Agent`), and let the planner choose a non-UI fallback (typed shell/AppleScript) where semantically safe. If the state changes during a multi-step job, stop subsequent UI steps and mark the job `partial_unverified`, preserving per-step evidence rather than emitting false success receipts. Add a startup/periodic permission-drift probe and expose these states to relay and pendant summaries.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently hears that typing/clicking succeeded even when macOS drops every synthesized event. This prevents silent no-ops and lets the agent either use a reliable fallback or clearly say what needs fixing, instead of leaving the owner to discover that nothing happened.
changes.effort: Medium: normalize /observe reachability into an executor preflight, add typed receipt states and planner fallback handling, then test permission drift and mid-job loss. No new model required.
changes.risk: Some workflows that previously ran through despite bad receipts will now stop or choose a different path; recovery is explicit retry after the permission probe turns healthy. AppleScript/shell fallbacks can have different semantics, so they must be labeled as fallback and retain command/result evidence.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local observation read per UI job and a small receipt payload. A periodic local probe is CPU-negligible.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly tens of milliseconds to UI jobs; avoids wasting up to 25 computer-use steps on actions that cannot reach the screen.
changes.security_impact: Read-only permission metadata is retained; no new privileges or gates. Existing FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged.
depends_on: The existing GET /observe reachability fields and durable per-action receipts
A planner/relay contract that understands blocked_unreachable and partial_unverified states

changes.change: Add a preflight-and-proof coordinator around every Mac/browser action. Before UI actions, read /observe and /ops/status; if accessibility/inputReachability is failed, mark UI actions unreachable before execution and select a non-UI fallback when one exists. For browser commands, persist an idempotency key plus expiry, replay only after /browser/status heartbeat returns online, and merge delayed /browser/result evidence into the same journal/receipt. Emit one shared outcome enum (queued, running, completed_verified, completed_unverified, blocked_unreachable, failed_no_effect, partial, rolled_back) to relay and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing 'done' when clicks or typing were silently ignored, and queued browser work either completes after reconnect or clearly expires. Existing maximum-access behavior remains intact; this makes it dependable rather than restrictive.
changes.effort: Medium: coordinator module, receipt schema extension, browser replay worker, and dashboard/relay event wiring; add integration tests for Accessibility-off and extension-offline cases.
changes.risk: A stale or duplicated replay could repeat a mutation. Mitigate with existing idempotency keys, command expiry, and proof-aware replay; recover by exposing cancel/undo where supported. If preflight itself is stale, downgrade to completed_unverified rather than claiming proof.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring API cost for deterministic checks. Small local CPU/storage overhead for health snapshots and replay metadata; relay traffic increases only for status transitions.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local read (typically <400 ms) before UI actions. Successful typed actions can proceed immediately; browser recovery is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no approval gate. Keep raw shell output, screenshots, and authenticated page bodies local by default; relay only typed status and redacted evidence references.
depends_on: Accessibility permission must be granted to the actual AI Pendant Agent binary before UI verification can become reliable
Browser extension heartbeat must distinguish offline from online and expose command acknowledgement
Shared faculty-action outcome contract must be adopted by planner, relay, and dashboard

changes.change: Build a live route-quality index from /journal, /jobs/:id/receipts, /routing, and /observe: score each action type and route by recent verified success, failure reason, reachability, latency, and attribution. Feed that index into mac-planner so repeated browser_navigate failures or UI-unreachable states automatically choose a better route (existing session read, direct public read, shell/AppleScript, or mac_delegate) and explain the choice. This is advisory routing, not a gate: the planner may still force the original route when the goal requires it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent will stop wasting turns repeating a route that has already failed nine times, and routine requests become faster and cheaper without reducing the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: normalize receipt outcomes, maintain a bounded rolling index, add route-selection hints to planner context, and test with the existing 120-job history.
changes.risk: A transient outage could make a route look permanently bad, or an alternate route could have different semantics. Use time decay, reason-specific scores, and retain the original goal/route in the receipt so recovery can retry deliberately.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces planner retries and expensive escalations; deterministic scoring has negligible local cost. No new model call required except the existing planner decision.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a local lookup under 20 ms; avoids multi-second failed attempts in common cases.
changes.security_impact: Keep raw URLs, shell output, and authenticated content out of shared score records; store action type, route, status, timing, and redacted reason only.
depends_on: Receipts must carry truthful typed outcomes and route attribution
/journal and /routing data need stable machine-readable fields rather than only display summaries

changes.change: Create a cross-surface 'event capsule' service that snapshots only the next relevant Calendar event, its normalized destination/timezone, the current travel estimate and confidence, and the chosen draft-recipient identity. Give the capsule a short-lived id and revision number. Relay, Mac planner, browser bridge, and pendant notifications consume the same revision so a changed/cancelled meeting invalidates stale route advice and stale message drafts. Store the raw event and page evidence locally; synchronize only the redacted capsule and status transitions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one trustworthy answer about whether they can make an appointment instead of contradictory calendar, browser, and Mac views. If the meeting moves, the pendant stops warning about the old plan and never offers a stale message draft.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: event normalization, browser travel adapter, revisioned capsule storage, reconnect handling, and a confirmation-aware draft handoff.
changes.risk: Calendar parsing or travel estimates can be wrong, causing unnecessary warnings or a bad draft. Show source timestamps and uncertainty, expire capsules at meeting start, and require explicit confirmation before any message send. If a surface disconnects, report partial evidence rather than inventing a result.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable-storage and relay costs; background model calls only when event/location interpretation is ambiguous. No realtime model cost for refreshes.
changes.latency_impact: One initial multi-surface aggregation in a few seconds; subsequent updates are incremental and can be pushed asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive event and route data stay local by default. Relay receives a short-lived opaque capsule id plus redacted status; authenticated page content and message text do not leave the Mac unless explicitly requested.
depends_on: A Calendar event reader with stable event identifiers
A travel estimate source usable through browser or an approved public API
Revisioned relay notifications and durable reconnect delivery
Draft-only Mac messaging action with explicit owner confirmation

changes.change: Add a low-cost, read-only capability preflight before planning or executing any Mac/browser action. Cache a short-lived health vector from /ops/status and /observe (shellReady, browserOnline/lastHeartbeat, accessibilityTrusted, screenRecording, visionConsent, pendingCommandCount). Route browser_* only when the extension is online and recently heartbeating; route GUI/vision only when Accessibility and Screen Recording are actually trusted; otherwise choose shell/AppleScript or return a truthful unavailable result immediately. Include the selected route and the health snapshot in the job receipt, and invalidate the cache on a failed action or bridge heartbeat timeout.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant stops wasting nearly a minute on browser commands that cannot run and stops claiming GUI actions succeeded when macOS is silently ignoring them. When Safari is offline, it can tell you immediately or use a different path; when permissions are missing, it can say exactly which permission is needed.
changes.effort: Moderate: health-vector endpoint/cache, planner hook, route predicates, and receipt fields; no new model required.
changes.risk: A stale or incorrectly interpreted health snapshot could route to the wrong surface. Keep TTL short (5–10 seconds), recheck after failures, and fall back to the existing executor rather than blocking shell actions.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local authenticated read per cache miss. Reduces expensive planner retries and 45-second browser timeouts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 10–50 ms locally on cache miss and usually saves 45 seconds on known browser/GUI failures.
changes.security_impact: Read-only status metadata stays local and is not uploaded; do not include URLs, page text, or screenshots in the health vector.

changes.change: Create a cross-surface source-of-truth resolver between the existing Mac, browser, capture, research, and context-graph systems. It should accept a task object (entity type plus identifying fields), query bounded local and authenticated sources in parallel, normalize fields, compute local hashes and freshness, apply configurable authority rules, and emit a signed evidence bundle with per-field provenance and conflicts. Store only hashes, source references, and short-lived snippets; make the bundle consumable by pendant speech and dashboard review without copying private page/file contents into general memory.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for the current answer once instead of manually opening several copies and guessing which is stale. Conflicting dates, amounts, statuses, or versions become visible before the owner acts on the wrong one.
changes.effort: High: typed adapters for local files/apps and browser pages, normalization schemas, authority configuration, evidence-bundle persistence/expiry, and relay-to-pendant rendering.
changes.risk: An incorrect authority rule could label a stale source canonical. Start read-only, show all conflicts and confidence, allow per-entity overrides, and never perform a write based solely on the resolver.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring storage and hashing cost; roughly $0.01–$0.05 for model-assisted normalization when needed. Avoids resending full private contents on every turn.
changes.latency_impact: Parallel bounded reads add 20–60 seconds for a search, but progress can stream and deterministic comparisons avoid extra model turns.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive contents remain on-device or in an encrypted short-lived relay bundle; spoken output is redacted by default. Source IDs and hashes are safer than persisting raw documents.
depends_on: Stable correlation IDs across Mac jobs, browser commands, relay requests, and pendant turns
Read-only local source adapters that expose metadata and hashes
A typed authority/conflict schema and expiring evidence-bundle store

changes.change: Make every executor job take a read-only preflight snapshot and write it into the job and each action receipt: browser online/last heartbeat, Accessibility and Screen Recording trust, inputReachability, secure-input state, and relevant app foreground state. Add deterministic fail-fast outcomes when a required surface is known unavailable (for example browser offline or uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false), with a typed reason and next probe time; do not invoke the action or wait for its normal 45–120 s timeout. For multi-action jobs, mark only dependent steps skipped and continue independent steps. Attribute every receipt to the selected model tier and planner request id.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would immediately say “browser is offline; I completed the Mac part” instead of waiting nearly a minute and repeating the same failure. GUI actions would no longer report apparent success when they cannot reach the screen, while the owner still keeps unrestricted execution and no confirmation gates.
changes.effort: Medium: central executor wrapper plus receipt schema migration, dependency-aware action scheduling, and dashboard rendering; add regression tests for offline browser and untrusted Accessibility.
changes.risk: A stale health snapshot could skip an action that would have recovered moments later; use short TTLs, one fresh probe for borderline states, and preserve an explicit force/override path. Old receipts need nullable preflight fields and remain readable.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; saves model retries and failed browser waits. Small local CPU/JSON storage increase per job (roughly a few KB).
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms cached preflight, but removes 45 s browser timeout loops and unnecessary retries; reachable actions start in parallel where independent.
changes.security_impact: Stores permission and app-state metadata in local job records; redact URLs/page contents and retain only typed states. Does not reduce command authority or add gates.
depends_on: A stable typed receipt/evidence schema (extend chg-5fc73ce3 rather than replacing it)
A planner action dependency/idempotency representation
Fresh /observe and /browser/status probes exposed inside the executor

changes.change: Introduce a crash-consistent cross-surface workflow ledger using prepare/commit/observe records, monotonic sequence numbers, per-step effect fingerprints, and fencing leases. The relay persists only encrypted/opaque checkpoint envelopes; the Mac and browser agents retain detailed local evidence. On reconnect, the coordinator first reconciles unknown steps against device receipts and current state, then resumes only uncommitted steps, preventing duplicate browser submissions or repeated Mac mutations. Expose a compact recovery timeline to the pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped Wi‑Fi connection, sleeping Mac, or restarted browser would no longer force the owner to guess whether something happened or risk doing it twice. They could leave a task running and return to a truthful “completed through step 4; step 5 was never committed; resumed and finished” result.
changes.effort: High: new relay D1 schema and protocol, local journal adapters, fencing/lease handling, effect-fingerprint reconciliation for each action family, and fault-injection tests across disconnect points.
changes.risk: Some external effects cannot be queried reliably, leaving an unknown state; surface that explicitly and require a recovery policy per action type (query-before-retry, compensate, or stop). Lease loss must never cancel a committed effect; use monotonic fencing and bounded replay. Migration must preserve existing job and receipt reads.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and network overhead per step (typically hundreds of bytes plus hashes); no additional model calls during normal operation. One cheap summarization call only when the owner requests a spoken recovery explanation.
changes.latency_impact: A local checkpoint adds tens of milliseconds; reconnect reconciliation should complete in 1–2 seconds for ordinary jobs, substantially faster than manual retries or existing action timeouts.
changes.security_impact: Opaque relay envelopes minimize private-data exposure; detailed checkpoints stay on the paired Mac/browser. Encrypt sensitive fields, rotate workflow keys, expire abandoned leases, and audit every resume/reconcile decision. No confirmation gates are introduced.
depends_on: A stable action receipt/evidence schema with committed-vs-observed distinction
Cross-surface idempotency keys and effect fingerprints for Mac and browser actions
Relay-to-Mac and relay-to-browser authenticated leases with reconnect callbacks
A durable pendant event for resumed, completed, and indeterminate workflow states

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution preflight and truthful delivery state to every Mac job. Before dispatch, snapshot Accessibility/inputReachability, Screen Recording, browser bridge connectivity, and target app presence; attach it to the job. After each action, distinguish dispatched, acknowledged-by-OS, and verified-effect (with reason when verification is impossible). If a known-failed prerequisite exists, mark the action unavailable and enqueue a retryable recovery record rather than claiming success; when the prerequisite or browser heartbeat returns, reconcile and replay only idempotent actions. Preserve FULL_CONTROL_MODE and do not add approval gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing that a task succeeded when the Mac could not receive input or the browser was offline, and will get an exact explanation plus automatic recovery when the connection returns.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight snapshot, receipt schema/status transitions, per-action verification hooks, and a small reconnect reconciler; existing job/receipt/journal endpoints can expose it.
changes.risk: Some actions cannot be independently verified, so receipts must say unknown rather than falsely verified. Replaying a non-idempotent command could duplicate work; recovery must default to no replay unless the action declares an idempotency key and safe replay semantics. Existing receipt consumers need backward-compatible fields.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few local status probes and small JSON receipt growth. No extra cloud model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 10–100 ms for local preflight; verification may add latency only for actions that opt in. Offline actions fail fast instead of waiting for the 120 s shell timeout.
changes.security_impact: No reduction in owner-authorized access. Preflight metadata may reveal app/window state, so retain it with the existing job retention and avoid recording command contents or secrets.
depends_on: Existing /observe, /browser/status, /ops/status, jobTracker receipts and journal storage
A typed action outcome contract for each executor action (verification optional)

changes.change: Add a readiness-aware action contract across Mac planner, relay, and pendant. Before any UI-dependent Mac action (ui_click, ui_menu, type_text, press_keys, screenshot/computer-use), the planner reads GET /observe and records a capability snapshot (Accessibility, Screen Recording, secure input, browser online state). The executor must attach that snapshot and a machine-readable precondition result to the job receipt; if UI reachability is false, it should automatically choose a non-UI route when one exists (shell/AppleScript/browser command), otherwise return a truthful blocked/unavailable result. Relay and pendant responses should render that state distinctly from success (e.g. “prepared but not applied”), including the exact missing permission or offline surface. Re-check readiness after reconnect/permission changes and annotate queued browser commands with the surface state that existed when queued.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today a job can say it succeeded while doing nothing: live observation shows Accessibility is untrusted and Screen Recording is missing, while browser commands are queued against an offline extension. The owner would stop receiving false completion claims and could still get work done through alternate Mac or browser paths automatically. This is especially valuable when they are away from the screen and only hear the pendant.
changes.effort: Medium: typed readiness schema, planner preflight, executor receipt fields, relay serialization, and a small pendant vocabulary/UI state. No new model is required.
changes.risk: A stale readiness snapshot could incorrectly suppress a newly available route or produce a false fallback. Use a short TTL, re-check on retry, and preserve raw probe evidence in the receipt. Do not block unrestricted shell work; this is truthfulness and routing, not an approval gate.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local observation call per UI job. Avoids expensive vision/planner retries when the host cannot interact. Storage is a few hundred bytes per receipt.
changes.latency_impact: ~10–50 ms for local preflight; faster overall by avoiding doomed 25-step UI loops.
changes.security_impact: Improves disclosure of permission and browser-state facts without granting new access. Receipts should redact paths/tokens and expose only capability booleans plus remediation text.
depends_on: Actual Accessibility permission for AI Pendant Agent (and Screen Recording for screenshots) remains missing; the contract must work honestly before those are granted.
A shared readiness schema consumed by mac-planner, faculty-action, and relay-realtime.
Browser extension heartbeat/online state and durable command queue must remain available.

changes.change: Add an offline-aware command lease and recovery controller for the Mac browser bridge. Every queued browser command gets createdAt, expiresAt, attempt count, idempotency key, and operation class. When /browser/status or /browser/heartbeat reports the extension offline, stop issuing duplicate retries; on reconnect, automatically replay only unexpired idempotent reads, coalesce identical pending reads, and move expired/failed navigations to a dead-letter record with the exact error and source job. Emit a single recovery receipt linking the original job, command, attempts, and final outcome, and expose pending/expired/dead-letter counts in /ops/status and /journal. This is observability and recovery, not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The Mac currently has 11 browser commands stranded while the extension is offline, and browser_navigate has failed 10/10 times. The owner would stop hearing repeated 'I did it' attempts for work that never reached Safari, and queued read tasks would resume automatically after the bridge returns instead of silently aging out.
changes.effort: Medium: browser command store/heartbeat worker, replay/coalescing logic, receipt schema, and dashboard/status wiring; add fault-injection tests for disconnect/reconnect and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A reconnect could replay a stale read or a navigation into the wrong tab if affinity is not validated. Mitigate with TTL, session/tab identity checks, idempotency, and dead-lettering; never replay mutating commands automatically. Recovery is visible and the original job remains inspectable.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; fewer planner retries and repeated browser calls should reduce tokens. Small local JSON/D1 growth for dead-letter records, bounded by retention.
changes.latency_impact: No added latency while online; reconnect recovery adds one heartbeat interval and avoids repeated failed 20-second waits.
changes.security_impact: Preserves existing browser session boundary; receipts should hash URLs/form data rather than persist secrets. No new permissions.
depends_on: chg-14accc01 request IDs/idempotency/tab affinity/typed results
POST /browser/heartbeat and GET /browser/status
GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts and GET /journal/:jobId
GET /ops/status and GET /ops/snapshot

changes.change: Feed a compact, TTL-bound execution-health header into planning and tool selection: browser online/offline and heartbeat age, pending-command count, recent failure rate by action type, Mac agent readiness, and last receipt status. The router should deterministically downgrade or redirect browser-dependent plans when the bridge is offline (for example, answer from existing captures or ask the owner to reconnect), and after a failed execution attach a machine-readable failure fact to the next planning turn. Keep the header under ~200 tokens and expire it within 60 seconds so it does not become stale prompt baggage.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent would know before acting that Safari is unreachable instead of spending repeated waits on doomed browser_navigate calls, then claiming progress. It could give an immediate truthful answer, use a cached cited result, or choose a Mac-local alternative, while reducing the expensive planner context and retries.
changes.effort: Medium: define a health projection schema, compute it from /ops/status, /browser/status, /routing and job receipts, inject it into /plan and tool dispatch, and add deterministic routing tests for stale/offline/recovered states.
changes.risk: A stale or overly broad health signal could suppress a browser task that would have succeeded. Use short TTL, distinguish offline from unknown, and permit explicit owner requests to attempt once; record the decision and source timestamps in the job receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Small local computation; likely saves planner calls and ~8–10k-token prompts on failed workflows. No new model spend.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a local status read (target <100 ms) before dispatch; avoids current multi-second or 20-second failed browser attempts.
changes.security_impact: Only operational metadata enters prompts; do not include URLs, page text, cookies, or form values. Existing bearer-protected routes remain the source.
depends_on: GET /ops/status
GET /browser/status
GET /routing
GET /journal/:jobId
POST /plan
POST /execute
GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts

changes.change: Build a local share-safe artifact pipeline between the active browser session and Mac workspace. It must accept a source manifest (active tab plus selected files), extract content with provenance, run deterministic secret/PII detectors plus a cheaper model redaction pass, produce a redacted derivative and machine-readable manifest, and expose a browser-staging action that attaches only the derivative to the selected composer/upload target. The staging step must return a screenshot/DOM receipt and remain unsent. Originals never leave the Mac or browser session; the pendant receives only the redaction summary and review link.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could turn a private page or local document into something safe to share in one spoken request, instead of manually hunting credentials and personal data across tabs and files. They would get a concrete artifact and see exactly what was removed before anything is staged.
changes.effort: High: implement source-manifest and provenance schemas, local extraction and artifact generation, detector/redaction review UI, secure derivative storage, browser upload targeting, and end-to-end tests with PDFs, screenshots, and logged-in pages.
changes.risk: A detector can miss a secret or redact useful context, and browser targeting can attach the wrong file. Mitigate with layered deterministic and model checks, visible before/after diff, conservative uncertainty labels, destination verification, short-lived derivatives, and an explicit final send boundary.
changes.cost_impact: Low-to-moderate per task; deterministic scans are cheap, while OCR/model review costs roughly $0.01–$0.08 depending on source size. Local storage cost is small and originals remain local.
changes.latency_impact: About 5–15 seconds for a page and a few files, longer for OCR-heavy PDFs. Browser staging adds one verification round trip.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by keeping originals local and minimizing relay/model payloads, but introduces sensitive derivative files and redaction manifests; encrypt them, bind them to the job, expire them automatically, and exclude raw secrets from receipts and logs.
depends_on: GET /browser/sessions
POST /research
POST /capture
POST /execute
POST /plan
GET /machine-context
GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
GET /journal/:jobId
browser_run_actions
mac_run_actions

changes.change: Add a canonical action-contract adapter at the Mac executor boundary. Normalize planner aliases into the executor schema (e.g. run_shell.command, run_applescript.script, open_app.appName) before dispatch, validate required fields and types, and emit a deterministic contract_error receipt naming the missing field and accepted shape when normalization cannot repair it. Generate planner/tool schemas from the same action registry so aliases cannot drift. Record requested shape, normalized shape, and adapter version in each job receipt; do not block valid arbitrary shell capability or add approval gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Requests like “open the browser bridge” will actually run instead of silently producing repeated zero-effect failures, and when something genuinely malformed occurs the pendant can explain exactly what needs fixing. The owner also gets reliable evidence about what command was attempted and what the Mac executed.
changes.effort: Medium: shared action registry, adapter and tests across planner, /execute, receipts, and mac_run_actions; migrate existing action fixtures and add compatibility aliases.
changes.risk: An incorrect alias could dispatch the wrong action or mask a planner bug. Mitigate with explicit per-action allowlisted aliases, normalized-shape receipts, and contract tests; unknown or ambiguous shapes should fail clearly without executing.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; saves model retries and wasted planner calls. Small local CPU/storage overhead for validation and receipt metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Adds sub-millisecond local validation; materially lowers end-to-end latency by preventing retries and failed job loops.
changes.security_impact: No reduction in owner's deliberate FULL_CONTROL_MODE or network reach. Better auditability through requested/normalized payloads; avoid logging secret field values, only names and hashes.
depends_on: A single versioned action registry shared by mac-planner, mac_run_actions, /execute, and receipt serialization
A migration test corpus covering current malformed payloads and valid run_shell/run_applescript/open_app actions

changes.change: Introduce a failure-loop circuit breaker shared by planner and Mac/browser executors. When the same idempotency key/action signature fails repeatedly (for example browser_navigate 10/10 failures or a malformed run_shell payload), stop issuing identical retries, attach the latest receipt and failure class to the next response, and route the recovery decision to a cheap deterministic/background path. Reset only after a changed device heartbeat, changed payload, or explicit owner retry. Preserve FULL_CONTROL_MODE; this is retry control, not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will stop wasting time repeating an action that cannot succeed while the browser is offline or the payload is malformed. It can say “the bridge is offline; I have not kept retrying” and resume automatically when the device comes back.
changes.effort: Medium: stable action signatures, per-device failure counters with TTL, planner feedback, and heartbeat-triggered reset across local agent and relay.
changes.risk: A transient failure could be mistaken for a persistent one and delay recovery. Use short exponential TTLs, classify transport/device/schema failures separately, and allow an explicit retry phrase or changed arguments to bypass.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces planner and relay calls during outages; tiny local state overhead. No new paid API dependency.
changes.latency_impact: Faster failure responses; recovery latency unchanged or improved because retries resume on heartbeat instead of blind polling.
changes.security_impact: Receipts must hash or redact arguments that can contain authenticated URLs, tokens, or typed text. No new authority is introduced.
depends_on: Canonical action-contract adapter and failure classification
Browser heartbeat/device TTL state shared with pending-command queue
Stable idempotency/action signature persisted in job receipts

changes.change: Add a strict action-envelope adapter immediately before executor dispatch. It must accept both legacy top-level and canonical params forms, copy aliases (app↔appName, command, script) into one internal envelope without mutating the original receipt, validate required values, and emit a redacted `dispatch.inputKeys` diagnostic. On a missing-required-field error, perform exactly one local re-normalization retry; if it still fails, classify it as `schema_error` (not a user/action failure) and suppress planner self-healing loops. Add contract tests using the exact failing open_app, run_shell, and run_applescript payloads observed in /jobs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Requests such as “open the browser bridge” will either work on the first attempt or explain a real wiring defect immediately, instead of silently spending several jobs failing and leaving the browser offline with 11 queued commands.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: shared adapter, receipt diagnostic field, and executor contract tests; no policy or confirmation changes.
changes.risk: A bad alias could dispatch the wrong value. Keep the original action and normalized envelope in the receipt, validate non-empty strings, and cap retry to one; recovery is transparent failure with an actionable diagnostic.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; saves planner retries and their prompt tokens.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero for valid actions; at most one in-process retry for malformed envelopes.
changes.security_impact: No new authority; preserve FULL_CONTROL_MODE and existing owner policy. Redact secrets from diagnostics and do not log command output.
depends_on: mac-planner's non-blocking schema normalizer
receipt schema supporting diagnostics and failure classification

changes.change: Make action planning reachability-aware: inject the live /observe capability capsule into planning and receipts. When Accessibility is untrusted or Screen Recording is unavailable, mark ui_click/type_text/press_keys and vision steps as `unreachable` before dispatch, route equivalent intents to shell or AppleScript when a verified equivalent exists, and otherwise return a truthful unsupported result. Never report UI success when inputReachability.uiActionsWillReachTheScreen is false.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop believing a task happened when the Mac agent's UI events actually did nothing; simple tasks can still complete through reliable non-UI paths, while impossible GUI work fails immediately with the exact permission needed.
changes.effort: Medium: planner context hook, action capability matrix, receipt status, and fallback mappings for common intents (open/focus app, volume, brightness, launch URL).
changes.risk: A fallback could have different semantics than the requested UI gesture. Restrict automatic fallback to equivalent, reversible intents and preserve the original planned action in the receipt; recovery is a normal retry after permissions change.
changes.cost_impact: Saves vision-loop and planner tokens by failing or falling back before up to 25 useless steps; no new model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Improves latency for unsupported UI tasks; adds a small local preflight read.
changes.security_impact: No added authority or gates. /observe must redact command output and sensitive window contents; only capability booleans and app identity are passed to the planner.
depends_on: /observe read-only capability capsule
typed action receipts with truthful status categories

changes.change: Add a stale-command quarantine ledger, separate from the pending browser queue: when an extension misses heartbeat, freeze delivery; assign each queued command an enqueue timestamp, originating utterance/job ID, tab/session affinity, and expiry; on reconnect, atomically classify each as safe-to-discard, safe-to-revalidate, or requires explicit replay. Revalidate tab URL/session and idempotency key before any replay, and expose a one-call pendant/dashboard summary plus discard-all-for-job operation. Do not execute or silently replay the current 12 pending commands.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will not have yesterday's clicks or navigation suddenly execute when Chrome returns. They can see exactly what is stale, reconnect safely, and choose which unfinished task—if any—should resume.
changes.effort: Moderate: queue schema migration, heartbeat transition handling, atomic poll claim/release, session revalidation, and dashboard/relay projection.
changes.risk: A legitimate command may expire and need to be reissued; retain the original intent and reason so the agent can reconstruct it. A crash during reconnect could duplicate a command; use leases plus idempotency keys and write-ahead state transitions.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; bounded local queue metadata growth. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one heartbeat/session validation round before replay, typically under 1 second; avoids expensive failed browser actions and vision retries.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental actions in authenticated sessions and keeps stale command contents local; do not send page contents to relay during reconciliation.
depends_on: Existing browser pending queue, /browser/status, /browser/heartbeat, /browser/poll, /browser/result/:commandId
A durable job/receipt correlation ID from the Mac relay

changes.change: Extend the existing readiness-aware action contract with automatic route substitution and postcondition verification, rather than merely reporting readiness. For each planned UI step, derive an alternate execution graph: browser-extension command for browser-owned state, typed Mac action/run_shell for deterministic system state, and computer-use only when Accessibility + Screen Recording + PENDANT_COMPUTER_USE_ENABLED are all true. After each substitute, verify the requested state through the authoritative observer (browser heartbeat/result, /observe, or a command result); mark the original UI step as skipped-with-fallback, not successful. Include route chosen, observer evidence, and remaining unmet capabilities in the receipt and spoken completion summary.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request such as 'check the page and tell me what changed' keeps working when screen control is unavailable, while requests that truly need pixels fail immediately and honestly. The owner gets the result, not a permission diagnosis after a useless retry.
changes.effort: Medium-high: planner graph representation, route capability registry, postcondition adapters, and receipt/journal fields; no new authority required.
changes.risk: An alternate route may have different semantics or touch a page unexpectedly. Limit substitution to explicitly equivalent read-only/browser-status/system-status operations, preserve session affinity, and require the planner to label any non-equivalent mutation as unavailable rather than silently changing it.
changes.cost_impact: Small local compute cost; likely reduces planner and vision retries. No additional model call when the capability registry matches a deterministic fallback.
changes.latency_impact: ~100–300 ms for preflight/verification; materially faster than a failed 15-second computer-use attempt.
changes.security_impact: Uses existing authenticated Mac and browser channels; receipts contain capability metadata and evidence references, so retain current auth and avoid storing page contents unless the underlying action already does.
depends_on: Existing readiness-aware action contract (extend, do not duplicate it).
GET /observe and GET /ops/status.
GET /browser/status, GET /browser/poll, POST /browser/result/:commandId.
Existing typed Mac actions/run_shell and receipt/journal persistence.

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface transaction coordinator, distinct from ordinary Mac jobs and browser commands. It should create an idempotency-keyed transaction before submission, persist browser and Mac phases independently, require a browser postcondition receipt before allowing the Mac write, lease/retry after bridge disconnects, and reconcile on startup. A timeout must remain 'unknown/pending' rather than becoming success; duplicate submissions are prohibited unless the site exposes a matching idempotency key. Expose a compact owner-facing state timeline and send the final outcome through the pendant pipeline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask one sentence such as 'submit this and remind me when it is confirmed' without risking a false reminder or duplicate submission. They get a truthful answer after interruptions instead of having to inspect browser tabs, Mac jobs, and logs separately.
changes.effort: High: new relay D1 transaction schema and worker, browser postcondition protocol, Mac conditional-write endpoint, recovery/reconciliation worker, and dashboard timeline.
changes.risk: Sites with weak confirmation signals may leave a transaction pending; fail closed on local writes and surface an explicit conflict. Browser sessions may expire, so preserve the original evidence and ask the owner to re-authenticate rather than replaying.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable-storage and polling cost per transaction; ambiguous postconditions may require planner/vision calls. This is cheaper than duplicate submissions and manual recovery.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one persistence round trip before each phase and postcondition polling, typically hundreds of milliseconds plus site latency; recovery is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Requires authenticated correlation among relay, browser session, and Mac job. Store hashes/minimal status rather than page bodies; encrypt or restrict evidence references, and never transmit session cookies to the relay or Mac.
depends_on: A new transaction state machine and idempotency-key storage in the relay.
A browser extension result contract that reports authoritative postconditions, not merely command execution.
A Mac conditional-write route that accepts only a verified transaction receipt.
Existing browser command/session, Mac job/receipt/journal, and pendant notification routes.

changes.change: Add a deterministic bridge_reconnect executor and planner intent. It records startedAt, launches AI Pendant Browser Bridge only if needed, then polls the existing browser heartbeat/status state until it observes a heartbeat newer than startedAt. Return a typed result {online, heartbeatAt, pendingCommands, executedCommands:0, freshness}; explicitly prohibit computer_use_task and browser command polling/execution for this intent. Surface the same typed result in the Mac job receipt and relay/pendant spoken completion.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can reliably reconnect the browser from the pendant and get an honest answer. Today the app-open step succeeds but the planner attempts a disabled screen-driving loop, producing a false failure; this removes that confusing dead end while protecting private tabs and queued commands.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: deterministic intent, heartbeat freshness comparison, bounded polling, receipt schema, and one relay response formatter; add integration tests for already-online, newly-online, stale, and timeout cases.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could be mistaken for success if timestamps are not compared to the request start; clock skew must use server receipt time and sequence/monotonic heartbeat IDs where possible. App launch can be idempotent. On timeout, report unavailable without deleting commands or changing tabs.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API/model cost; status polling and one local app launch dominate.
changes.latency_impact: 1–2 seconds when already online; up to 10 seconds only while waiting for a fresh heartbeat.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by avoiding computer-use and command execution. No page content, URLs, or pending command payloads should enter the spoken result.
depends_on: A freshness-aware /browser/status or /browser/heartbeat response (timestamp or monotonic sequence)
A deterministic router intent before planner escalation
Receipt fields for typed status outcomes

changes.change: Make every UI-mutating receipt proof-aware without blocking execution: before and after ui_click, type_text, press_keys, and computer_use_task, attach the /observe inputReachability snapshot, foreground app, and target evidence when available. If eventsPost is false or accessibility is untrusted, set receipt.status to executed_unverified (not success), include the exact reason, and let the planner choose a shell/AppleScript/browser route or tell the owner verification is impossible. Preserve the owner's FULL_CONTROL_MODE and never add an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The Mac currently reports UI actions as successful while /observe proves they can do nothing because Accessibility belongs to a different binary. Honest receipts prevent silent failures and let the agent recover through another surface instead of claiming a task is complete.
changes.effort: Medium: receipt status extension, pre/post observation hooks, planner fallback mapping, and tests for trusted versus untrusted Accessibility.
changes.risk: Some actions genuinely have no visible state change, so the result must remain executed_unverified rather than failed; fallback could duplicate an action unless idempotency keys and before-state evidence are carried forward.
changes.cost_impact: Small local overhead for two observation snapshots per UI job; no additional model call unless recovery is needed.
changes.latency_impact: Roughly tens to hundreds of milliseconds per UI action; recovery may add a planner turn only after an unverified result.
changes.security_impact: No restriction added. Observation metadata may contain app names and window titles, so redact sensitive text before relay; do not upload screenshots without existing consent.
depends_on: Existing GET /observe reachability endpoint
Existing action receipts and undo records
Deterministic fallback routing for browser, shell, or AppleScript

changes.change: Create a cross-surface causality ledger that assigns one immutable conversation/request ID at the pendant, propagates it through relay audio/transcription, planner decisions, Mac jobs, browser commands, and final spoken output, and materializes a compact timeline with explicit gaps (received, forwarded, claimed, executed, acknowledged). Reconcile late events by ID rather than timestamp and expose a redacted owner-facing 'what happened' view plus machine-readable diagnostics.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a request crosses the pendant, cloud relay, Mac, and browser, today the owner cannot reliably distinguish lost, duplicated, still-running, or completed work. One causal timeline would let them ask 'what happened to that?' and receive a truthful answer even after a restart or delayed callback.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: schema and propagation headers across relay and local-agent boundaries, durable append-only storage with retention, reconciliation of late/duplicate events, and a concise spoken formatter.
changes.risk: A ledger can accidentally retain sensitive transcripts or URLs; store hashes and redacted summaries by default, encrypt durable records, and apply short retention. Clock differences must never determine causality; IDs and sequence numbers must.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and write overhead per event; no extra model calls for the ledger. Background summarization is optional.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible request-path overhead if events are appended asynchronously; owner-facing history lookup should return in under 1 second locally.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability but increases metadata concentration. Separate content from event metadata, enforce per-owner access, redact browser/private-page fields, and allow deletion by request ID.
depends_on: A propagated immutable request ID at pipeline ingress
Relay and Mac job schemas accepting correlation and parent IDs
Browser command and action receipt records exposing the same correlation ID
A retention/redaction policy and owner-facing history endpoint

changes.change: Add an adaptive, evidence-preserving recovery layer specifically for browser navigation. Before browser_navigate, validate bridge heartbeat, session/tab affinity, and URL normalization; on failure classify the returned error as stale tab, extension transport timeout, blocked/unsupported URL, or page-load timeout. Retry only transient transport/page-load failures with the same idempotency key and bounded backoff, reattach the named session when possible, and use a safe Safari foreground/open-url fallback only for public URLs. Persist each attempt, error class, final URL/title, heartbeat age, and backend choice in the existing job receipt/journal. Never report navigation success from an enqueued command: success requires a post-navigation URL/title/readback, otherwise return a truthful partial failure with the next recovery action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says “open this page” or asks the pendant to inspect a logged-in site, it will stop silently burning attempts and give a reliable answer: the page opened and was verified, or exactly why it could not. Transient Safari/extension hiccups recover without another spoken turn, while private authenticated pages are not mistakenly sent to a public relay.
changes.effort: Medium: browser bridge command lifecycle and local-agent browserSessions/originFanOut integration, plus receipt schema and tests for stale tabs, timeouts, and private/public routing.
changes.risk: A retry could load a page twice or leave an extra tab; constrain retries by idempotency key and session affinity, and record every attempt. A public fallback must never be used for owner-private URLs. If verification cannot run, report unknown rather than success.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; mostly local bridge requests and a few extra seconds on transient failures. Avoids repeated planner calls and wasted browser-minute budget.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a fast heartbeat/affinity check; successful navigation gains roughly 0.1–0.5s verification, transient failures may take up to two bounded retries.
changes.security_impact: Improves security posture without adding approval gates: authenticated sessions remain on Safari, URL origin and backend are recorded, and receipts expose evidence rather than page contents by default.
depends_on: chg-16bc5dee durable browser job runner (or its existing router)
chg-14accc01 request IDs, idempotency keys, and tab/session affinity
Existing GET /browser/status, POST /browser/heartbeat, GET /browser/sessions, GET /journal, and GET /observe observability paths

changes.change: Add a cross-surface navigation lease protocol between relay, Mac agent, and Safari bridge. A lease contains jobId, idempotency key, private/public origin classification, session/tab binding, expiry, retry budget, and a monotonic attempt number. The relay persists the lease and wakes/reconnects the Mac bridge; the Mac agent renews it while executing; the extension acknowledges each command and returns a post-navigation URL/title proof. On reconnect, the Mac agent resumes the lease rather than replaying the last command, and the relay emits exactly one terminal verified/failed result to the pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask once and walk away—even through a sleeping Mac, dropped browser heartbeat, or voice disconnect—and later receive a trustworthy result instead of duplicate tabs, lost work, or a false “done.” This is the missing connective behavior between existing browser polling, sessions, jobs, and relay persistence.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared lease schema, D1/local persistence, reconnect handshake, monotonic attempt handling, and terminal-result deduplication across relay/mac/extension.
changes.risk: A stale lease could resume against the wrong tab; bind leases to authenticated session ID, origin, and tab/window identity, and expire them conservatively. If proof is unavailable, mark the job unknown/failed rather than replaying or claiming success.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1 and local persistence overhead; no meaningful model cost. Saves planner/realtime calls caused by repeated owner retries and avoids unnecessary public-browser-minute consumption.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy path adds one acknowledgement and readback round trip (typically under 1 second); reconnect recovery is asynchronous and does not hold the realtime conversation open.
changes.security_impact: Private authenticated work remains exclusively in the Safari bridge; the relay stores metadata and encrypted/opaque job references, not page contents. Lease origin/session binding prevents accidental cross-account replay.
depends_on: Existing POST /browser/heartbeat, GET /browser/poll, POST /browser/result/:commandId, GET/POST /browser/sessions
Existing GET/POST /jobs and receipt/journal observability
Durable relay job persistence and a truthful completion notification path to the pendant

changes.change: Make the planner consume a live capability-readiness matrix before selecting an execution surface. Derive it from /ops/status and /browser/status, explicitly distinguishing configured, permission-ready, online, and currently-targetable. For this Mac, report Accessibility=false and Screen Recording=false as unavailable for mac-vision, while Safari automation and browser-extension are available; attach a short reason and a fallback route to every plan. Recompute after bridge heartbeats and permission changes, and record the matrix version in the job receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets fewer impossible attempts and more honest behavior: GUI work will not be sent to a loop that cannot control or see the Mac, while browser or script alternatives are chosen immediately. If no safe fallback exists, the pendant says that before wasting time rather than reporting a mysterious failure.
changes.effort: Medium: readiness schema, planner prompt/selector integration, receipt field, and tests for stale browser tabs and missing Accessibility/Screen Recording.
changes.risk: A stale health result could hide a newly available surface or overrule a valid one. Use short TTLs, refresh on failure, and permit the planner to retry once after a fresh status read. This is advisory routing only and does not add approval gates or reduce FULL_CONTROL_MODE.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small deterministic status read per multi-step plan. Saves planner tokens and failed execution attempts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–150 ms locally; should reduce total latency by avoiding doomed vision/browser retries.
changes.security_impact: Permission state and app/tab metadata remain local; only coarse readiness labels and failure reasons need enter model context. Do not expose URLs or command output in the matrix.
depends_on: A stable /ops/status and /browser/status response schema with timestamps and explicit permission booleans
Planner support for surface fallback and a readinessVersion field in job receipts

changes.change: Add bounded live stdout/stderr progress and heartbeat events for run_shell and other long Mac actions. The local agent should emit sequence-numbered chunks (with size caps and secret redaction), phase, elapsed time, and exit status into the existing job/pipeline stream; persist only a compact tail plus hashes in the journal. Relay and pendant can subscribe, while the dashboard reconstructs the full local log when authorized.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: For a command that takes minutes, the pendant can say “still indexing files, 42 seconds elapsed” instead of appearing dead, and can distinguish a slow job from a crashed Mac bridge. When it finishes, the owner gets the real exit code and the last useful error rather than a vague failure.
changes.effort: Medium: child-process stream handling, redaction/chunk limits, pipeline event schema, reconnect cursors, and tests for timeout/termination.
changes.risk: Output can contain secrets or huge/binary data; redact known token patterns, cap each chunk and total retained tail, mark truncation, and keep full output local by default. A dropped stream must not affect execution.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and relay traffic; no model cost unless the owner asks for a summary. Reduces repeated polling and planner turns.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero execution impact; first progress event within 250 ms, with 1–2 second coalescing to avoid pendant spam.
changes.security_impact: Potential leakage of shell output is the main risk. Default to local-only raw output, relay only redacted progress summaries, and require an explicit dashboard fetch for full logs.
depends_on: Existing /jobs, /journal, /pipeline/events, and /pipeline/stream contracts
A redaction utility shared by shell receipts and relay telemetry
A reconnect cursor so clients do not replay duplicate progress events

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution ledger and failure-recovery loop without reducing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: assign one correlation ID at intake and propagate it through relay, planner routing, Mac job, browser command, action receipt, journal, and pendant notification; classify failures into permission, stale-tab/session, timeout, network, invalid-target, and command-error; record retryability, attempted recovery, and final owner-visible explanation. Before retrying, compare stable action IDs and skip receipts already marked successful. Add a compact dashboard view showing failure clusters, unattributed tier counts, and the exact evidence behind each diagnosis.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When something fails, the owner gets a truthful answer and a useful next step instead of a generic error or repeated browser clicks. It would expose the current 27 failures and 111 unattributed actions, explain why browser navigation repeatedly fails, and let the system recover from stale tabs or transient links while preserving the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: shared correlation schema, executor/browser adapters, failure classifier and retry state machine, plus dashboard/relay projections; 1–2 weeks including integration tests for partial completion and stale browser tabs.
changes.risk: A bad classifier could retry a non-idempotent command or mislabel a successful partial mutation. Recovery: default unknown errors to no automatic retry, rely on existing receipts and undo descriptions, cap retries to one, and preserve the raw command/result for dashboard inspection. This adds observability only and does not block actions.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage (roughly 1–3 KB metadata per action, with raw evidence retained locally); small-model classification is usually cheaper than planner calls and can be deterministic for known errors. Dashboard polling adds minimal relay/database traffic.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 50 ms for correlation/ledger writes and perhaps 100–300 ms for deterministic classification; only failed jobs incur recovery latency. Known transient browser recovery should complete within one extra bridge round trip.
changes.security_impact: Ledger contains sensitive URLs, paths, shell strings, and page evidence. Keep raw payloads local, redact relay/pipeline summaries, hash or truncate secrets, and apply existing audio retention policy to spoken failure reports.
depends_on: A shared correlation-ID field accepted by relay, planner, browserBridge, jobTracker, and actionReceipts
A deterministic failure taxonomy and retryability table
A receipt-aware executor retry path that skips completed stable action IDs
Dashboard and relay projections for redacted failure summaries

changes.change: Add an execution-aware router that recognizes high-frequency Mac/browser intents and failure-recovery requests from typed action plans and recent receipts, then chooses deterministic or background handling before constructing the planner prompt. Cache compact intent signatures and successful recovery recipes keyed by action type plus normalized error, not by sensitive URLs or raw commands; escalate only when confidence is low or the plan spans surfaces.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Routine status checks and repeated recovery attempts would answer faster and stop spending the expensive planner tier on work the system already understands. The live router already saves 44% of requests, but still spends about 47k planner prompt tokens across nine requests; this makes those savings persist for the common failures the owner actually encounters.
changes.effort: Medium: define intent/error signatures, add a bounded local cache with expiry, connect routing receipts to executor outcomes, and test that cached recipes never cross user/session boundaries.
changes.risk: A stale recipe could produce an irrelevant retry, especially after browser tabs change. Recovery: short TTLs, require matching action schema and surface/session, verify current browser status and receipt preconditions, and fall back to the planner on mismatch. Unknown commands remain unchanged.
changes.cost_impact: Potentially substantial reduction in planner tokens and latency for repeated intents; cache metadata is tiny and deterministic lookup is effectively free. No additional model cost except occasional recipe synthesis.
changes.latency_impact: Milliseconds for cache lookup; removes 1–3 seconds of planner latency for recognized requests. Recovery itself still pays bridge or shell execution time.
changes.security_impact: Never cache raw authenticated page contents, shell output, or secrets. Use salted hashes and normalized action/error labels; keep the detailed evidence in local receipts.
depends_on: Cross-surface correlation IDs and failure taxonomy
GET /routing receipts linked to GET /jobs and GET /journal
A local, TTL-bounded recipe cache with session isolation

changes.change: Add a duplex-aware audio scheduler for the nRF9160/relay pair: reserve a minimum uplink slice for mic packets whenever downlink TTS is active, adapt Opus uplink from 16 kbps toward 8 kbps under contention, and mark every dropped packet with a sequence gap. The relay should shorten or pause TTS on detected barge-in rather than allowing both streams to saturate LTE-M.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can interrupt the agent and be heard instead of losing roughly eight seconds of speech during simultaneous talk. Conversations feel responsive on the real pendant, not merely healthy in telemetry.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware packet scheduler and bitrate control, relay congestion feedback, and an integration test over the USB-connected modem/bridge with induced contention.
changes.risk: Poor bitrate transitions could create artifacts or starve playback; recover by falling back to the current fixed 16/24 kbps mode when feedback is absent. Sequence numbers make loss visible rather than silently corrupting turns.
changes.cost_impact: No API cost and no new hardware; slightly higher CPU during bitrate changes, within the existing ~87% single-core audio load only if transitions avoid extra transcoding.
changes.latency_impact: Barge-in acknowledgement improves from multi-second loss to one or two packet intervals; TTS may sound briefly clipped when preempted.
changes.security_impact: No new data leaves the device; congestion metadata is non-content telemetry.
depends_on: A framed packet sequence/priority field shared by pendant and relay
Relay-side barge-in detection that can stop queued TTS packets
An integration test harness for the live /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA pair

changes.change: Replace the prototype's single-button/LED interaction with a production pendant interaction module: add BLE presence beacons (or UWB if reliable room-level presence is required), a low-power vibration motor, and a capacitive double-tap surface while retaining the existing physical button for conversation. Expose signed presence epochs and alert acknowledgements to the nRF9160 firmware and Mac over USB/LTE.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can know when the owner has left or returned, deliver a private interruption without opening a speaker, and distinguish a context bookmark or defer gesture from starting/ending a call. That enables seamless work handoffs and attention protection rather than making the owner repeat commands.
changes.effort: High: enclosure and power redesign, BLE/UWB coexistence testing with LTE-M, firmware input state machine, and Mac pairing/reconnection UX.
changes.risk: False presence near the Mac or accidental taps could checkpoint or defer the wrong thing. Recover with explicit state LEDs/vibration patterns, debounce and a dashboard history; keep the existing button path as a fallback. UWB increases BOM and power, so BLE can ship first if room-level precision is unnecessary.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $8–$25 BOM increase depending on UWB versus BLE and a $1–$3 haptic motor; intermittent beaconing should add modest battery draw, while UWB ranging can materially increase it.
changes.latency_impact: Presence changes in roughly 1–3 seconds with BLE, sub-second with UWB; local vibration acknowledgement is under 100 ms.
changes.security_impact: Pairing keys and signed presence epochs must be device-bound; do not broadcast an owner-identifying static address. Presence data should remain local unless needed for a queued handoff.
depends_on: A new firmware event protocol for presence, haptic acknowledgement, and capacitive gestures
Mac and relay support for paired-device identity and presence epochs
A durable handoff/interruption state machine

changes.change: Add a command execution ledger at the shell boundary that records argv after safe tokenization, cwd, selected environment fingerprints (never raw secrets), start/finish/timeout, stdout/stderr hashes plus a bounded tail, process tree, exit code, and whether the command is reversible.
