args.user_asks: “Whenever you tell me something important, let me ask ‘show me why’ and take me straight to the exact source on my Mac or in the browser—without making me repeat the question.”
args.why_useful: Today evidence is fragmented: browser work can have tab context, Mac jobs have receipts, and spoken relay answers are not consistently linked back to either. The owner cannot reliably distinguish a remembered fact, a shell observation, a browser extraction, and a model inference—or jump from a pendant answer to the exact file, tab, command output, or timestamp that supports it. This would make the system trustworthy for consequential everyday decisions while preserving the fast spoken interface.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to answer the short follow-up and select an existing evidence reference. Build evidence links and source classification asynchronously with a cheaper background model or deterministic adapters; no expensive call is needed when the source is already typed.
args.latency_budget: Normal answers remain unchanged. “Show me why” should acknowledge in under 1 second, return a source summary within 2 seconds, and open the selected Mac file/window or browser tab within 3–5 seconds when the relevant surface is online.
args.cost_estimate: Low incremental model cost, generally under $0.01 per evidence lookup. Main costs are bounded local metadata indexing and small relay records, not inference. Store hashes/snippets and pointers rather than duplicating files or pages.
args.security_concerns: Evidence may expose private files, authenticated pages, commands, or personal data. Keep raw content on the Mac/browser where possible; send only a redacted excerpt, source type, timestamp, and opaque reference to the relay. Opening a private source should require the same existing owner control as the underlying Mac/browser action. Never expose shell environment values, cookies, access tokens, or full page contents merely because an answer cites them.
missing: A typed evidence-reference envelope emitted by every Mac, browser, memory, and relay answer
A provenance graph linking spoken claims to source spans, command/job IDs, tab IDs, timestamps, and confidence/inference status
Mac actions that can focus the exact source window/file and browser actions that can reattach to the cited tab
Pendant protocol support for a short source summary plus a follow-up reference token
Dashboard rendering that clearly separates observed evidence from model inference and stale memory

args.change: Add a tiny coin vibration motor or linear resonant actuator with a dedicated driver in the next pendant revision, plus a low-power haptic event protocol. Relay job completion, browser-watch alerts, and Mac failure/reconnect events should produce distinct short patterns; the pendant firmware must queue/coalesce patterns while audio is active and fall back to the existing LED when haptics are disabled.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently has only one LED and audio output. If headphones are disconnected, audio is buffered, or the owner is in a noisy environment, completed work and urgent failures are easy to miss. A private, silent tap lets the owner know that something finished without opening a screen or starting the microphone, while the relay/Mac still provide the details when asked.
args.effort: Hardware revision, one GPIO/PWM driver and haptic patterns in firmware, then relay event mapping and dashboard settings. Prototype with an external driver board first; reserve a GPIO and validate vibration does not couple into the microphone mechanically.
args.risk: Motor current spikes can disturb LTE/audio rails and vibration can enter the mic. Use a transistor/current-limited driver, physical isolation, rate limits, and a firmware fallback to LED. A failed motor must not block conversations or job delivery.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$4 BOM increase in prototypes and approximately 10–80 mA only during brief pulses; negligible model/API cost. Battery impact is small if patterns are capped and coalesced.
args.latency_impact: Event-to-tap can be sub-second after relay receipt, with no model round trip. Firmware queueing during playback adds at most a few seconds by policy.
args.security_impact: Haptic patterns reveal only that an event exists, not its content. Provide a silent/privacy mode and avoid encoding sensitive categories in easily observable patterns.
depends_on: A relay event taxonomy for job completion, failure, and reconnect
Authenticated pendant downlink/event delivery
A revised enclosure/PCB with a safe GPIO, driver transistor, and mechanical isolation

I recorded and proposed a new integration: **live capability preflight and recovery**. Before dispatching work, it would check `/ops/status`, `/browser/status`, and `/capabilities`, fail immediately when a route is impossible, select a viable alternate route where privacy permits, and send a precise repair hint to the pendant. args.user_asks: “When I’m away from my Mac, let me tap the pendant to queue a task with a short voice note; when I get back, have the relay and Mac resume it from the right project and tell me exactly what completed, without making me repeat myself.”
args.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac/browser connection turns an in-progress request into a conversational dead end: the owner must remember what they asked, repeat it, and reconstruct context. A wearable tap plus relay persistence can capture intent at the moment it matters, while the Mac later supplies files, apps, and authenticated sessions. This is a true handoff between the body, always-on service, and private machine rather than a Mac-only task runner.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief voice note and immediate acknowledgement; deterministic relay storage, deduplication, and delivery; background gpt-4.1-mini to normalize the note and select the active project when the Mac reconnects; planner tier only if the resumed task is genuinely ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 500 ms using a local canned response; relay persistence under 1 second; resume within 15 seconds of Mac reconnection; completion spoken or queued for playback within 5 seconds after the Mac returns a receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Tiny for short notes: roughly 300–800 input tokens to normalize only when needed, plus a few hundred tokens for a completion summary. Most handoffs use deterministic storage and existing Mac execution, so the dominant cost is ambiguity escalation.
args.security_concerns: Voice notes and task metadata are stored in relay D1 and may contain private intent; encrypt or minimize them and expire unclaimed handoffs. Never transmit authenticated page contents, arbitrary shell output, or secrets to the relay. Bind delivery to the paired pendant and Mac identity, preserve project/session provenance, and require the existing owner policy before any destructive or external side effect.
missing: A pendant-side offline capture and acknowledgement mode that survives a dropped relay link
A durable relay handoff record containing audio/text note, capture time, pairing identity, intended surface, project hint, and lifecycle state
A reconnect protocol that lets the Mac claim handoffs exactly once and report progress/receipt updates
A context reattachment operation that resolves the handoff to the Mac's active project, session, and relevant recent thread without resending the entire conversation
A pendant playback queue for completion receipts when the owner is no longer in a live voice session

args.change: Add a small encrypted nonvolatile event spool dedicated to handoff intents—an I2C/QSPI FRAM or protected flash ring buffer with monotonic sequence numbers, plus a firmware button gesture that commits a short voice-note reference and acknowledgement state before attempting the relay upload. The spool should retain at least 64 compact events and support atomic append/acknowledge, replay after reboot, and secure erase after receipt confirmation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A tap made while the owner is walking, underground, or between Wi‑Fi and cellular coverage would not vanish. The pendant could honestly say “saved; I’ll finish this when your Mac is back,” then deliver the request later without requiring the owner to remember it.
args.effort: Medium hardware revision and firmware work: select FRAM/protected flash, add the bus and secure-storage key handling, implement a power-loss-safe ring format, and integrate replay with relay pairing. Prototype first using existing flash to validate the protocol before spinning the board.
args.risk: A damaged or worn storage cell could lose queued intents; use sequence/CRC, wear leveling, and duplicate relay acknowledgement. Voice data is sensitive, so store encrypted compressed audio or preferably a short transcript plus bounded audio fallback, and erase after receipt. A full spool must produce a local overflow indication rather than silently dropping the oldest request.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$4 per device for a small FRAM/protected-flash part and minor PCB assembly impact; negligible idle power, brief write current during a tap. No recurring model cost for the storage itself.
args.latency_impact: Local commit acknowledgement under tens of milliseconds; replay is asynchronous and does not delay normal conversation.
args.security_impact: Adds a durable local copy of private intent, so keys must be device-bound and inaccessible over unauthenticated UART. Secure erase and pairing-scoped replay are required; never treat the spool as a general filesystem.
depends_on: Define the relay handoff record and exactly-once acknowledgement protocol
Implement pendant firmware event capture and reconnect replay
Add paired-device key provisioning and receipt-driven deletion
Provide a relay-to-pendant completion playback queue

args.why_useful_to_owner: When a command fails or a long task finishes while the owner is away, the agent can explain exactly what happened, distinguish a transient network/timeout from a real command error, and continue from the failed step without asking the owner to reproduce it. It also makes unrestricted shell capability accountable without taking capability away.

args.risk: Output may contain secrets or personal data; redact known token/password/key patterns and environment names, cap raw tails, hash rather than retain large output, and apply retention/deletion with the existing job records. args.latency_impact: Under ~5 ms instrumentation overhead for normal commands; no added model round trip. Large stdout is truncated/hash-only.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability of the intentionally unrestricted shell, but creates a second sensitive artifact. Encrypt at rest where available, redact before persistence, restrict trace routes to the existing authenticated Mac-agent context, and provide per-job purge/retention.

args.change: Add a first-class persistent terminal-session backend for long-running shell work. A run_shell action may opt into a named session with a process-group ID and bounded ring buffer; expose authenticated attach/read (offset or last N lines), stdin write, SIGINT/TERM, and explicit close endpoints, with heartbeats and orphan cleanup after lease expiry. Keep ordinary one-shot commands unchanged. Link session events to the existing job/action receipt and relay job status so a pendant query can say whether the process is still running, show recent output, or offer stop/resume rather than launching a duplicate command.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Builds, exports, downloads, tests, and other work that outlasts a voice turn keep running when the owner walks away or the network drops. The owner can ask from the pendant what is happening, see the last useful lines, stop a stuck process, and reconnect later without losing the Mac's terminal context or accidentally starting the work twice.
args.effort: Medium-high: local process supervisor/PTY or pipes, authenticated streaming endpoints, lease/orphan handling, bounded persistence, and relay_job_status integration. Add tests for reconnect, cancellation, crash recovery, and duplicate-session prevention.
args.risk: A detached process can continue consuming CPU, hold files, or expose output; enforce resource/time limits, redact persisted output, kill the process group on lease expiry by default, and make persistence opt-in per session. PTY behavior differs from noninteractive commands, so retain the current executor as fallback. Never replay stdin automatically after reconnect.
args.cost_impact: Small local CPU/RAM overhead while active and bounded disk for the ring buffer; no extra model calls. It can reduce API/model cost by avoiding repeated polling and re-running failed long jobs.
args.latency_impact: Immediate status reads over the existing Mac-agent connection; streaming can be SSE/WebSocket. Session startup adds only PTY/process setup time, while one-shot commands are unchanged.
args.security_impact: Adds a privileged control surface for stdin/signals. Require the existing bearer auth, per-session unguessable IDs, owner/job binding, strict output retention, and audit every attach/write/signal/close event. Do not expose raw terminal sessions to unauthenticated relay clients.

Keep a local-only answer path for requests whose manifest is empty.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for analysis of genuinely private Mac material and receive a useful answer without trusting that raw terminal output will be forwarded. args.cost_impact: Adds local CPU, disk, and possibly a one-time local-model download; normally reduces remote token and relay costs because only compact findings travel. No additional remote call for a local-only answer.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–3 seconds for scanning typical logs and potentially longer for folders; remote summarization starts only after the manifest is produced. Existing non-private actions can bypass this path.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces exfiltration risk by making raw stdout ineligible for context propagation, but introduces a sensitive local index. Encrypt or permission-lock the index, bind manifests to job IDs, and audit every export decision without storing the blocked content.

browser-extension: heartbeats and claims only commands for its bound tab/session; reconnect replays pending work without duplicating a completed step

args.model_tier: Use realtime only for the initial conversational acknowledgment and urgent spoken status. args.latency_budget: Acknowledge from the pendant in under 1 second. Health/routing decision in under 2 seconds when a node is online. A disconnected node may wait until its next heartbeat; surface a 30-second stale warning and an owner-configurable expiry rather than polling expensively.

args.security_concerns: Health metadata must not include page contents, credentials, or shell output. Bind browser work to an extension/session/tab identity and Mac work to the paired host. Persist only the goal, step hashes, surface, timestamps, and typed result summaries. Never retry a non-idempotent browser submission or shell mutation automatically; preserve the existing before/after receipt and checkpoint semantics. Tell the owner when a fallback changes what was actually done.

A durable step lease/idempotency record spanning relay, Mac bridge, and browser bridge
Heartbeat-triggered resume and timeout worker; current browser has pending commands but no demonstrated end-to-end claim/resume contract
Pendant status vocabulary for queued/waiting/rerouted/completed states

args.change: Add a shell execution journal that wraps every run_shell invocation without restricting it: assign a request/attempt ID, record start/end time, cwd, argv-or-command hash, timeout, exit code/signal, stdout/stderr byte counts and redacted bounded tails, environment/tool version fingerprint, and a deterministic failure class (timeout, missing executable, permission, nonzero exit, transport). Before execution, capture a cheap recovery hint (re-runable, reversible action type, or explicitly irreversible); after failure, persist the exact retry recipe and whether any partial output was produced. Expose it through the existing job receipt and /journal/:jobId, and let the planner ask for a retry with the same idempotency key or a corrected command. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and the unrestricted command surface unchanged; this is instrumentation and recovery, not a gate.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer to “what happened?” instead of a generic failure, especially when a long command times out or partially succeeds. The planner can stop repeating the same broken command, resume a multi-step task from the last completed step, and tell the owner whether undo is possible. This directly addresses the real five-attempt project search and the fact that undo currently covers only a few action types.
args.effort: Medium: one journal schema and wrapper in computerControl/executor, receipt serialization, bounded redaction tests, and planner retry logic. Add crash-safe append/atomic compaction so the journal survives the local agent restart.
args.risk: Command output can contain credentials or private file contents; redact known secret patterns, cap tails, and allow owner-controlled local-only retention. A crash between command completion and journal write could still create ambiguity, so mark attempts as unknown and require a fresh status probe rather than blindly retrying. Never infer success solely from a truncated output tail.
args.cost_impact: Negligible local disk/CPU; bounded journal entries (for example 4–16 KB each) and no additional model/API call for normal execution. One small background classification call only when exit semantics are ambiguous, if desired.
args.latency_impact: Under 10 ms for local metadata and append in the normal case; no added model latency. Flush asynchronously after the job receipt while retaining an in-memory attempt state for crash recovery.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability without narrowing authority. Store command text only locally by default, hash it in relay receipts, and redact stdout/stderr before any relay/dashboard projection. Make raw local logs opt-in and explicitly labeled sensitive.
depends_on: The existing job receipt/undo implementation (chg-5fc73ce3) must accept attempt metadata
A stable job/request id propagated from /execute through computerControl.runShell
A local append-only journal or equivalent crash-safe storage; do not rely only on the current aggregate activity log

args.user_asks: “Remember this exactly where I found it, and let me ask about it later from the pendant even if that tab or my Mac is closed.”
args.why_useful: A useful fact often exists only in a private Safari tab or a local Mac file, then disappears when the tab closes. This would create a small, provenance-preserving capsule rather than dumping an entire page into long-term memory: the browser supplies the authenticated URL/tab and selected text or DOM citation, the Mac supplies local-file provenance when relevant, the relay stores an encrypted, expiring snapshot plus a compact semantic index, and the pendant can retrieve it by voice. Later answers can quote the captured evidence and say when it was captured, instead of pretending that a stale memory is current.
surfaces: pendant: voice command “remember this” and later spoken retrieval; button controls capture timing so no microphone is left open
browser-extension: captures only the user-selected text/region, URL, title, tab/session identity, and a DOM locator/source hash; does not scrape unrelated tabs
mac-planner/mac-terminal: captures a selected local artifact or command result with path, modification time, content hash, and a redacted excerpt when the source is on the Mac
relay: encrypts and stores the capsule with owner-defined TTL, sensitivity label, and source provenance; retrieves only matching capsules for a later question
dashboard/iOS: shows capsule list, source link, expiry, evidence excerpt, and delete/export controls
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short capture acknowledgment or spoken lookup. A cheaper background model generates a compact title, entities, and retrieval keywords; deterministic code preserves the exact excerpt/hash and enforces TTL. Use no model for a direct exact-quote lookup.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 1 second; persist the capsule in under 3 seconds. Exact retrieval under 1 second; semantic retrieval under 3 seconds. Never block the owner on summarizing a large source—store first and summarize asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per capture for optional compacting, plus small D1/R2 storage; exact lookup costs no model call. The dominant cost is embedding/semantic indexing if enabled, so cap excerpt size and index only owner-selected content.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and local files are highly sensitive. Require an explicit user gesture/phrase for capture, never capture whole tabs by default, encrypt at rest, keep raw content local when the owner chooses, redact credentials/financial identifiers before indexing, and give every capsule a visible source, TTL, and delete action. A browser command for selected-region capture and a Mac command for selected-file/command-result capture

Pendant capture/retrieval intent and a compact spoken provenance format
Dashboard/iOS capsule management and retention controls

transcript.text:
Round 71 findings:

- `/ops/status` is healthy and the relay is reachable.
- The Mac agent is **not ready**: Accessibility is untrusted and Screen Recording is unavailable.
- mac-vision is disabled.
- The browser extension is offline with **five pending commands**.
- Full-control shell execution remains enabled.
- The newly granted diagnostic tools exist only as schemas; they still return “no implementation yet.”

I recorded this readiness state and proposed:

1. **Health-aware cross-surface execution** — keep a pendant request alive, report exactly which surface is unavailable, reroute safe work where possible, and resume idempotently when the Mac/browser returns.
2. **Provenance-preserving memory capsules** — let the owner explicitly save selected browser text or Mac artifacts with source, timestamp, citation, expiry, and later pendant retrieval.

The execution-journal proposal was rejected as already covered by existing observability work, so I did not duplicate it.

What is still needed:

- Implement one of the granted read-only Mac diagnostics tools.
- Add a shared health/lease/idempotency contract between relay, Mac jobs, and browser commands.
- Add explicit pendant/dashboard states for queued, waiting-for-Mac, rerouted, partially completed, and failed.
- Keep the owner informed when permissions or browser connectivity prevent execution; do not report a request as accepted-and-done when no executor is available.

No additional permission is needed from me this round.

args.user_asks: “Only show private Mac and logged-in-browser results when I’m actually wearing the pendant; if I take it off, pause the sensitive work and continue when I put it back on.”
args.why_useful: Today the Mac, browser, and relay can continue acting while the owner is away, but none of them has reliable proof that the intended person is physically present. This would let the owner walk away from a shared room without leaving private notifications, authenticated-page excerpts, or draft contents exposed, while preserving useful continuity: non-sensitive background work may finish, sensitive results remain sealed, and the pendant announces the exact point at which work resumes.
surfaces: pendant: periodic authenticated presence beacon, local wear/presence sensor, and a short button gesture to re-authorize; LED indicates present, paused-sensitive, or expired authorization
mac-planner: receives the signed presence state, suppresses private onscreen/audio presentation when absent, and checkpoints work without discarding results
browser-extension: keeps authenticated tabs bound to the paired presence epoch and withholds page text, screenshots, and form previews after the epoch expires
relay: stores encrypted pending results, rotates short-lived presence leases, and sends only coarse state transitions to the pendant; it may continue explicitly non-sensitive background jobs
dashboard/iOS: shows the last presence epoch, paused jobs, and a deliberate resume control without exposing the sealed payload on an untrusted surface
args.model_tier: No realtime model is needed for presence enforcement. Deterministic firmware/relay cryptography handles leases and state; a cheap background model classifies a job's output sensitivity at planning time, with owner-configurable overrides. Realtime is used only if the owner asks for a spoken explanation while present.
args.latency_budget: Presence loss recognized within 2–5 seconds, with no model round trip. Re-authorization and release of sealed results under 1 second after a valid button gesture. Background jobs continue without waiting for model responses.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per-event API cost; cryptographic lease checks and D1 writes dominate. Optional sensitivity classification costs roughly $0.001–$0.01 per job, cached for the job lifetime.
args.security_concerns: Presence must be cryptographically bound to the paired pendant, not inferred from an easily spoofed MAC-visible Bluetooth name. Do not transmit raw audio, page content, or credentials in the beacon. Use short-lived rotating tokens, replay protection, and a fail-closed policy for sensitive presentation. The owner must be able to revoke a lost pendant from the dashboard. Clearly distinguish ‘paused because absent’ from ‘failed’; never delete sealed results automatically without the configured retention policy.
missing: A real pendant presence/wear signal or secure proximity channel; the current single-button/LED prototype has no presence sensor
Firmware support for rotating signed presence leases and replay counters within the device's constrained RAM/flash budget
A relay-side encrypted sealed-result store and presence-epoch API
A Mac/browser presentation broker that classifies and withholds sensitive output without terminating resumable work
An owner-facing sensitivity policy and lost-pendant revocation flow

args.change: Add a low-power capacitive skin-contact/proximity sensor and a hardware-backed identity element to the pendant, while retaining the existing single button and LED. Firmware should derive a signed, rotating presence epoch from contact plus an authenticated nearby-host handshake; it should never expose a raw sensor stream. Put the sensor on an always-on low-power GPIO/I2C path and reserve the secure element for lease signing/revocation keys.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could leave a shared room without private Mac/browser results remaining audible or visible, then resume them immediately on return. It also gives the system a trustworthy way to tell the owner ‘you are present’ rather than guessing from an online Mac or an easily spoofed Bluetooth name.
args.effort: Medium hardware revision and firmware integration: choose a skin-contact electrode/sensor, add secure-element support, define signed epoch packets, validate false-positive/false-negative behavior across clothing and charging, and add a lost-device revocation path in the relay.
args.risk: A contact sensor can misclassify pockets, loose wear, or another person holding the pendant. Use conservative expiry and require the existing button for sensitive reauthorization when confidence is low. Secure-element provisioning and board changes add manufacturing complexity; retain a development bypass only in lab firmware, never production.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$8 per unit for a basic capacitive/proximity component plus $1–$3 for a secure element, with milliwatt-or-less idle draw if duty-cycled. No per-request API cost beyond lease state writes.
args.latency_impact: Presence transitions can be detected locally in roughly 1–3 seconds; no model latency. Signed lease verification is sub-millisecond on the Mac/relay.
args.security_impact: Meaningfully improves physical-presence assurance, but it is not biometric authentication. Never treat it as sufficient for irreversible financial or account actions; combine it with the existing action-specific controls. Protect private results by failing closed when the lease is stale or revoked.
depends_on: The presence-lease capability proposed this round
Pendant firmware support for rotating signed epochs within the existing constrained RAM/flash budget
Relay and Mac/browser presentation layers that consume presence epochs

args.about: Mac execution observability and cross-surface state
args.finding: The live Mac agent is v0.5.0 with FULL_CONTROL_MODE and planner enabled. Its read-only journal covers 120 retained jobs, 147 actions, 14 failures, 76 writes, but reports 0 undoable and 112 routing requests unattributed to a tier. Browser extension home-chrome is offline with 5 pending commands; mac-vision loop is disabled and vision upload consent is false; Accessibility is not trusted.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status, GET /journal, GET /routing, GET /browser/status

transcript.text:
Discovered the current state and found one gap beyond the existing shell-journal work.

### Live findings
- Mac agent v0.5.0 is online with `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` and planner enabled.
- Journal currently retains 120 jobs:
  - 147 actions
  - 14 failures
  - 76 writes
  - 0 currently marked undoable
- Routing telemetry has 112 unattributed requests.
- The Chrome extension is offline with 5 pending browser commands.
- mac-vision is disabled, vision upload consent is absent, and Accessibility permission is not trusted.

### New proposal recorded
I proposed a **cross-surface causality and cost trace**: one lineage ID should follow a request from pendant/relay → model routing → Mac job → shell subprocess → browser commands → receipts and spoken completion.

That would let the owner hear whether a delay or failure came from:
- model planning,
- Mac execution,
- a dropped browser connection,
- queued browser work, or
- an ambiguous retry.

It also addresses the current 112 unattributed routing records and reduces duplicate work caused by confusing “queued” with “failed.”

### What is still needed
1. A shared lineage envelope propagated through relay, planner, Mac jobs, and browser commands.
2. A non-blocking, bounded trace sink with redaction and short retention.
3. Browser reconnect reconciliation so the five pending commands are clearly distinguished from failed work.
4. An implemented diagnostic executor: the granted `mac_read_diagnostics` and typed-action tools are schemas only and currently do not execute. I did not rely on them.

No microphone was opened, and I did not execute any Mac mutation.

args.user_asks: “For that request I made earlier, show me the complete chain of what happened, what is still queued, what failed, which device did each step, and roughly how much model time it cost.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner gets separate Mac jobs, routing receipts, and browser queue state, but no single trustworthy, human-readable explanation joining them. This would make cross-device behavior understandable after delays, dropped connections, partial completion, or duplicate attempts—without requiring the owner to inspect technical logs.
args.model_tier: background for assembling and summarizing existing structured records; deterministic joins and totals first, with a small model only for concise spoken wording. Realtime is unnecessary unless the owner asks during a live conversation.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a recent request from retained records; under 5 seconds if browser reconnect reconciliation is needed. The pendant can say 'I am checking the Mac and browser trace' while the background job assembles it.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost when records are structured; roughly 1–3k input tokens and a short completion only when summarization is needed. Dominant cost is not inference but retaining and joining bounded trace metadata.
args.security_concerns: The report may reveal private URLs, shell commands, file paths, account names, and model prompts. Store raw spans locally with short retention, redact secrets and sensitive arguments, expose opaque IDs and summaries by default, and require owner-authenticated access for detailed views. Never include bearer tokens or full private page contents in relay speech.
missing: A shared request-lineage ID propagated from relay routing into Mac jobs, shell actions, and browser commands
A bounded redacted trace store that survives the current 120-job eviction window through aggregate summaries
Browser reconnect reconciliation that records whether pending commands eventually completed, failed, or remain indeterminate
A join endpoint or dashboard view combining routing, journal, job receipts, and browser queue state

args.user_asks: “After anything gets interrupted, tell me what is definitely complete, what is only partly done, and what cannot be verified—and offer the next safest way to reconcile it without blindly repeating the action.”
args.why_useful: A dropped Mac connection, browser disconnect, timeout, or process crash currently leaves the owner to guess whether a command ran before the failure. This capability distinguishes completed, failed, and indeterminate effects, then proposes inspection or continuation rather than silently replaying potentially permanent work.
args.model_tier: Background/deterministic for effect-state calculation from receipts, exit codes, checkpoints, browser acknowledgements, and reconnect state; use the planner tier only to explain ambiguous cases or formulate a recovery plan. Realtime is only needed to read the short result aloud.
args.latency_budget: Initial interruption classification under 2 seconds from local records; reconciliation under 10 seconds when it needs a live Mac or browser check. The owner should get an immediate compact uncertainty report, followed by an update if a device reconnects.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic classification; roughly 1–3k model input tokens only for an ambiguous multi-step recovery explanation. Most cost is local state tracking, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Recovery inspection can expose private files, authenticated pages, and command arguments. Keep evidence local by default, redact secrets, require explicit owner choice before any compensating mutation, and make the spoken summary disclose uncertainty rather than claiming success.
missing: Per-step effect checkpoints with an explicit unknown/indeterminate state rather than only job success or failure
Command- and browser-operation effect probes that can verify postconditions without replaying the original action
A recovery-plan record that separates read-only reconciliation from compensating mutations and records the chosen outcome
Cross-device acknowledgement and reconnect handling so a late browser result or Mac receipt can close an uncertain step

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **Cross-device request trace** — the owner can ask what happened across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, including queued work, failures, device ownership, and model cost.

2. **Interruption reconciliation** — after a timeout or disconnect, the owner can learn what definitely completed, what is indeterminate, and what read-only checks or compensating actions are appropriate without blindly replaying mutations.

Both require missing connective infrastructure: propagated lineage IDs, explicit indeterminate step states, postcondition checks, reconnect acknowledgements, and recovery records.

args.user_asks: “That failed—figure out what went wrong, pick up from the last successful step, and finish it.”
args.why_useful: Today a failed Mac/browser job leaves the owner to reconstruct the error and repeat earlier work. This would turn a failure into a recoverable conversation: the pendant gives a concise diagnosis, the relay assembles evidence, and the system resumes only the unfinished portion while preserving the owner’s authenticated browser state.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/exit-code analysis first and a cheaper background model for diagnosis and continuation planning; use realtime only to explain the result or answer the owner’s follow-up. Escalate to the expensive model only when the failure is ambiguous or the next step has meaningful semantic alternatives.
args.latency_budget: Immediate spoken failure summary in under 2 seconds from stored receipts; continuation planning in 5–15 seconds; execution proceeds asynchronously with a pendant notification when complete. Do not block on an expensive model for obvious timeout, missing-path, or stale-tab failures.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental API cost because exit metadata, receipts, browser command results, and workspace facts are already structured. Ambiguous recovery costs one background planning call, roughly a few cents or less; storage is bounded failure artifacts and checkpoints.
args.security_concerns: Recovery evidence may contain private shell output, local paths, or authenticated page text. Keep raw artifacts local/encrypted with short retention, redact tokens and cookies, and send the relay only structured error summaries by default. Never silently substitute a different recipient, destination, payment, or submitted browser form; semantic changes must be surfaced as a new plan for owner review. Exact retries of the original trusted action remain available under the owner’s maximum-access policy.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint graph that relates Mac action IDs, browser command IDs, and their dependency edges rather than only a flat job list

args.user_asks: “Pack up what you’re doing so I can close the lid, then continue it later exactly where you left off.”

args.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic serializer and integrity checker for the capsule. Use a slower background model only to summarize human intent and identify which external state must be revalidated; realtime is only for the spoken pause/resume interaction.
args.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement and capsule manifest in under 2 seconds; capture local/browser state asynchronously in under 30 seconds for ordinary jobs. Resume should validate dependencies first and then start within 5 seconds, with the owner notified if anything drifted.
args.cost_estimate: Minimal API cost for manifests and hashes; occasional background summarization is a few cents or less. Storage depends on selected artifacts, with a default small manifest and explicit opt-in for large files or screenshots.
args.security_concerns: Capsules can contain private paths, shell output, authenticated-tab identifiers, and pending form data. Encrypt them, bind browser references to the owner’s device/session, expire abandoned capsules, and never export cookies or credentials. On resume, revalidate external state; do not assume a saved form or page is unchanged. Any irreversible action remains a newly presented step, not a replayed side effect.
missing: A versioned capsule format spanning Mac action receipts, shell cwd/environment fingerprints, browser tab/session affinity, pending checkpoints, and relay job IDs

A pause protocol that drains in-flight actions and records a consistent cut between completed and pending steps
A resume validator that checks repository hashes, app availability, browser tab identity, network assumptions, and expiry before continuation
Pendant and dashboard controls for naming, listing, expiring, and resuming capsules

args.model_tier: Background/cheap model for receipt parsing, error categorization, and selecting a previously successful repair recipe; realtime only for the short spoken acknowledgement and final concise explanation. args.latency_budget: A receipt-based diagnosis in under 2 seconds after the owner asks; one unattended retry/repair within 30 seconds; long repairs become a durable relay job with progress and a final pendant notification. Never loop indefinitely: max 2 attempts per step and stop on unchanged error.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.003–$0.02 per ordinary incident, dominated by model calls only when the local error classifier cannot match a cached recipe; shell/browser execution is local. A successful cached diagnosis should require no expensive model call.
args.security_concerns: The Mac remains maximum-access and unattended per owner policy; this is not a new gate. Repair recipes must record exact commands/actions, exit code, cwd, timestamps, and before/after observations, while redacting tokens, environment secrets, and page contents. Do not silently retry irreversible commands; mark them non-retriable and explain why. Browser repairs must preserve authenticated-session boundaries and never send a form as part of diagnosis.

A local error taxonomy plus a small, signed recipe cache of known reversible repairs and pre/post checks

args.change: Add a failure-aware command journal and recovery runner between the existing Mac executor and job/receipt APIs. Every run_shell, run_applescript, typed action, and browser action emits one normalized step record: parent job/request ID, surface, argv or action type (with secrets redacted), cwd, start/end, timeout, exit code, bounded stdout/stderr hashes plus short excerpts, and reversible/irreversible classification for observability only. A classifier maps failures to stable categories (not-found, permission, timeout, dependency-offline, stale-browser-tab, bad-input, unknown). For known reversible categories it selects a versioned repair recipe with explicit precondition and postcondition probes, runs at most two attempts, and writes a linked before/after receipt; unknown failures become a durable diagnosis task rather than an unbounded retry. Expose GET /jobs/:id/failure and POST /jobs/:id/recover plus a compact event to relay/pipeline so the pendant can say what failed and whether recovery completed.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac fails while the owner is away from the keyboard, they get a concrete explanation and an automatic, bounded attempt at recovery instead of “something went wrong” or repeated blind retries. The owner can later audit exactly what changed and undo where supported, without giving up the deliberate maximum-access policy.
args.effort: Medium: shared step schema and redaction, executor instrumentation, 6–10 built-in recipes with pre/post probes, two routes, and relay event wiring; add fault-injection tests for timeout, missing app, stale browser tab, and partial completion.
args.risk: Capturing command text/output can leak sensitive data; redact known secret patterns, cap excerpts, hash full output, and retain only short-lived diagnostics. A repair recipe can make an incorrect but reversible change; require preconditions, postcondition verification, max-attempt limits, and automatic rollback through existing undo where available. If the runner crashes, the linked receipt remains marked unknown rather than falsely successful.
args.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost for local classification and cached recipes; roughly $0.003–$0.02 only when a background model must interpret an unknown error. Small local disk/database growth from bounded receipts; no new hardware.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms instrumentation overhead to normal actions. Known diagnosis/recovery starts immediately; unknown cases add one background model round trip and become durable rather than blocking the voice turn.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability without reducing owner-authorized access or adding confirmation gates. Store redacted command metadata, not secrets; isolate browser evidence to its existing authenticated session and never include page tokens in relay events.

transcript.text:
Round 78 findings:

- `/ops/snapshot` confirms the Mac agent and relay are reachable.
- The browser extension is offline with **5 pending commands**.
- macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions are missing, so mac-vision cannot currently operate.
- The newly granted `mac_read_diagnostics` and `mac_readonly_diagnostics` tools still have no implementation; I recorded this blocker. Current host facts must come from authenticated HTTP snapshots or existing Mac actions.
- Current job telemetry shows **14 failed actions**, **0 undoable actions**, and **112 unattributed routing records**, indicating observability remains incomplete.

I proposed and recorded a new Mac-harness change: **reconnectable long-running shell process leases**. Explicitly marked long-running jobs would survive relay/request disconnects, retain bounded output with cursors, report status through `/jobs/:jobId` and `relay_job_status`, and support explicit process-group cancellation—without adding approval gates or automatic retries.

I also told `mac-planner` that its on-demand Calendar/Mail/authenticated-tab/workspace handoff packet is not exactly covered by the backlog.

args.user_asks: “Keep this terminal task alive while I leave, and when I come back let me continue it from exactly where it stopped—without starting over.”
args.why_useful: Today a long shell task is tied to a request/HTTP lifetime and can disappear behind a timeout or bridge disconnect. The owner cannot reliably leave a build, export, backup, or research command running, return later through the pendant, inspect only the unseen output, and resume after a Mac or agent restart. This would make the pendant a dependable remote terminal companion rather than a one-shot command launcher.
args.model_tier: background for status, deterministic for cursor/lease bookkeeping, planner only when the owner asks to interpret a failure or choose a continuation command; realtime is used only to speak the concise status through the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge launch or reconnect in under 500 ms; status and unseen-output retrieval in under 2 seconds. Interpretation or continuation planning may take 2–5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for launch/status/reconnect because these are deterministic. Occasional background/planner call costs roughly one short request only when interpreting output or constructing a continuation; local spool and relay metadata dominate storage, not API spend.
args.security_concerns: A detached process can continue using CPU, files, credentials, or network after the owner leaves. Require explicit long-running intent, a maximum lifetime and disk quota, visible lease status, and pendant cancellation; do not auto-retry. Keep raw output on the Mac with TTL deletion and send only redacted tails/summaries to relay. Restrict status access to the paired owner.

Durable lease, output-cursor, and bounded spool records surviving bridge/agent restart

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **Self-healing Mac tasks** — diagnose failed shell/app/browser actions, try bounded alternative approaches, preserve attempt-level receipts, and report what worked or failed without requiring the owner to repeat the request.

2. **Verified local-file-to-browser workflows** — find and hash the correct Mac file, match it to the appropriate authenticated browser form, stage the upload, and present the exact file, destination, and fields for approval before submission.

These require cross-surface recovery/diagnostic infrastructure, artifact handles and hashing, staged browser uploads, provenance-linked review capsules, and approval-time revalidation.

args.user_asks: “If something can’t run right now, don’t leave me waiting—tell me what is unavailable, use the best safe fallback, and keep the original task ready to resume when the device comes back.”
args.why_useful: Today the system can spend 45 seconds waiting on an offline browser bridge, while the Mac snapshot simultaneously reports missing Accessibility/Screen Recording and a disabled vision loop. The owner should receive an immediate, truthful answer instead of a timeout, and public work should continue through the relay/web tools while private work is held for the authenticated browser. This only works across the pendant, always-on relay, Mac observability, and browser session lease—not on one node alone.
args.model_tier: Deterministic health/preflight and fallback routing first; background model only to summarize a degraded result or explain a recovery plan; realtime model only for the spoken interruption.
args.latency_budget: Health check and route decision under 500 ms; fail-fast private-browser requests in under 2 s rather than the current ~45 s poll timeout. Resume automatically on the next heartbeat, without replaying non-idempotent steps.
args.cost_estimate: Usually zero model calls for health, classification, quarantine, and retry. At most one small background summarization call for a fallback result; realtime speech cost is only the brief status sentence.

For every action, persist a typed outcome (transport/offline, permission, timeout, command error, semantic mismatch) plus stderr/exit status, observed bridge state, and the last successful receipt. Before retrying, consult an idempotency-key circuit breaker: suppress identical retries after a configurable failure threshold, refresh the relevant prerequisite (for example browser heartbeat/session reattachment or Mac permission status), then resume only from the last successful action. Surface a compact recovery plan and a `resume job` operation through /jobs and the relay, while preserving FULL_CONTROL_MODE and never blocking an owner-requested action; retries must be explicit in the job trace. Attribute every action to its routing tier/model and retain the failed command's redacted argv/env metadata.

transcript.text:
Fresh discovery found a concrete live reliability problem:

- 120 jobs retained, 146 actions, 16 failures.
- 112 actions lack routing-tier attribution.
- One browser navigation idempotency key failed six times in a row.
- The browser extension is offline with 7 pending commands.
- Mac permissions are not fully ready: Accessibility and Screen Recording are missing.

I proposed two changes:

1. **Failure-aware continuation:** classify failures, stop identical retry loops, refresh prerequisites, and resume from the last successful receipt without adding approval gates or restricting `FULL_CONTROL_MODE`.
2. **End-to-end routing traces:** propagate one request ID across pendant → relay → Mac → browser → receipts, attribute model/token/latency data, and use deterministic preflight checks to avoid expensive planner calls when a surface is offline.

I do not need additional permissions or tools this round. What remains is implementation access to the existing job tracker, receipts, routing statistics, browser heartbeat/session state, and relay job serialization. The main unresolved design choice is retention: how long raw local failure diagnostics should remain before only redacted summaries are retained.

transcript.text:
I found a concrete live reliability gap and recorded two changes:

1. **Failure-aware execution recovery**
   - Detects offline extensions, blocked dialogs, timeouts, and invalid targets.
   - Avoids repeating known failures after another 45-second wait.
   - Retries only explicitly safe/idempotent actions.
   - Records health snapshots, retries, and final outcomes in linked receipts.
   - Can use an alternate public-browser backend where appropriate.

2. **Deterministic recovery routing**
   - Handles follow-ups like “why did that fail?”, “try it again,” and “is Safari back?” from job and health records without resending the full planner context.
   - Escalates only when side effects or intent are ambiguous, reducing latency and token cost.

Live evidence: the journal has **120 retained jobs, 146 actions, 16 failures**, and one `browser_navigate` idempotency key has failed **6/6 times**, including extension-offline and Safari-timeout failures lasting roughly **45 seconds each**. The browser status endpoint reports health, but the executor does not yet appear to use it adaptively.

I do not need another permission or tool this round. The remaining uncertainty is whether another agent has already implemented an equivalent failure classifier or retry coordinator; I asked `unified` to check.

args.user_asks: When something I asked you to do on my Mac or in Safari fails, recover it automatically when it is safe, switch to the other available surface when possible, and tell me exactly what happened without making me repeat the request.
args.why_useful: Today a browser extension outage or blocked Safari dialog can consume repeated 45-second attempts, while the owner has to diagnose the failure and restate the task. This would make the pendant, relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge behave like one resilient system: preserve the goal, avoid duplicate side effects, and return either a completed result or a precise recovery step.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic/background routing for health checks, failure classification, receipt lookup, and safe retries; invoke the planner only for ambiguous recovery or cross-surface replanning. Realtime is used only to report progress or ask a necessary clarification.
args.latency_budget: Health checks and known-failure diagnosis under 1 second; avoid repeating a known 45-second timeout. Permit one bounded retry for explicitly idempotent actions, then report the result promptly.
args.cost_estimate: Low incremental API cost: most recovery turns are deterministic and reuse existing receipts. Occasional planner escalation costs roughly one normal planner request; storage and health polling are the dominant non-model costs.
args.security_concerns: Retries must be limited to actions whose receipts prove no effect or that are explicitly idempotent; never blindly repeat a mutation. Keep browser URLs and shell diagnostics authenticated, redact cookies, environment variables, command secrets, and page contents from recovery summaries, and preserve an auditable link between original and retried jobs.
missing: A shared failure fingerprint schema covering offline surfaces, blocked dialogs, timeouts, invalid targets, and transport errors
A live cross-surface health registry that the executor can consult without planner involvement
Recovery receipts linking original job, health snapshot, retry decision, alternate surface, and final outcome
An idempotency/retry-safety declaration on every action type
A goal-preserving recovery coordinator that can choose Mac, browser bridge, or relay fallback without duplicating writes

args.user_asks: If my Mac or Safari is unavailable when I ask, remember the exact task on the pendant, tell me it is queued, and resume it automatically when the right surface comes back—without me asking again.
args.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac link or offline browser bridge turns an otherwise valid request into a failed interaction and loses momentum. The owner should be able to speak once while walking away, receive a truthful queued receipt, and later get the completed result or a precise question only if the task cannot safely resume.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background/deterministic worker to persist, health-check, and resume a structured task. Use the planner only when the resumed environment differs materially or the original goal is ambiguous. Use realtime only for the immediate queued acknowledgement and completion announcement.
args.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement within 2 seconds, with no need for the Mac to be online. Health checks can be minutes apart or event-driven; resume within one polling interval after the required surface returns.
args.cost_estimate: Small durable-queue and health-check cost; normally no additional model call. One background planner call may be needed to rehydrate a stale or changed task. Audio completion delivery is the main bandwidth cost.
args.security_concerns: Persist only the minimum structured intent and references, not page contents or shell secrets. Bind queued work to the owner's authenticated device and surface session, expire tasks with sensitive data, and never replay a mutation unless its original action is marked retry-safe and its preconditions still match. Tell the owner when a task expired or needs clarification.

A relay durable queue with leases, retry backoff, expiry, and exactly-once intent delivery

A cross-surface preflight would prevent 45-second browser timeouts and impossible GUI plans, hand public reads to relay/browser-run, hand Mac reads to shell, queue private browser work until the extension returns, and give the pendant one concise capability/fallback explanation. It is materially different from generic goal routing because it uses live permission, heartbeat, queue, and model-consent facts before each step and rechecks them after failures.

args.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for local /ops/status plus cached relay health; under 1 s for a cross-surface matrix. Do not spend 45 s waiting on a browser command when its heartbeat/queue already says unavailable. Recheck only the affected surface after a failure.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for local health and typed policy; roughly one small standard-model call only when fallback mapping is ambiguous. Dominant cost is the optional spoken summary, not preflight.

args.change: Add a preflight-and-fallback middleware between planner and executor. For every planned action, declare required surface facts (e.g. browser_online, tab_attached, accessibility, screen_recording, vision_consent, relay_reachable). args.latency_impact: Adds about 100–300 ms to local jobs; avoids current 45-second browser timeout loops. Fallback execution can proceed in parallel where dependencies allow.

args.user_asks: After you do something across my Mac and logged-in browser, tell me whether it actually took effect—not merely whether the commands succeeded—and show me the short before/after proof if I ask.
args.why_useful: Today a successful receipt means an executor reported success, not that the external world changed. A browser submit can be accepted but fail validation, a Mac app can ignore input, or a page can update another tab. The owner needs one trustworthy answer that correlates the Mac observation, authenticated browser evidence, and relay-delivered pendant response, with uncertainty made explicit.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/evidence correlation and host/browser re-reads first. Use a cheaper standard model to compare before/after semantic state; reserve realtime only for the owner's spoken explanation when the verdict is ready.
args.latency_budget: For reversible Mac-only work, verify within 2 seconds. For browser workflows, allow up to 10 seconds for a fresh authenticated read. If verification cannot complete, return 'executed but unverified' rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no additional model call when typed fields or hashes match; one small standard-model comparison for semantic page changes. Main cost is one additional browser or Mac read, not realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Proof may contain private page text, so keep raw snapshots on the Mac/browser bridge and send the relay only a redacted verdict, field names, hashes, and minimal snippets on explicit request. Bind evidence to job ID, tab/session ID, URL, and timestamps to prevent stale-tab confusion. Never treat a public fallback as proof of a private mutation.

Typed postconditions for Mac actions and browser mutations (field value, URL/state, app status, or semantic predicate)
A browser read-after-write primitive that guarantees the same tab/session and returns provenance-bound evidence
A Mac observe-after-action primitive for foreground app state, document values, and synthesized-input reachability
A redaction layer and pendant-friendly proof summary format
A verdict state machine distinguishing succeeded-and-verified, succeeded-but-unverified, failed-before-change, and changed-but-postcondition-failed

args.change: Create a cross-surface postcondition verifier that runs after an action batch. The planner must attach a typed expected outcome to each write. After execution, the verifier retrieves the same browser tab/session or Mac foreground context, compares the observed state to the expectation, stores a provenance-bound verification record, and emits a four-state verdict: verified, unverified, unchanged, or contradicted. Aggregate verdicts across the batch and expose a redacted proof card to the relay/pendant; retain raw evidence locally. A receipt may remain successful while the user-facing result is 'completed but unverified' until this check passes.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust 'done' to mean the intended world state was observed, not just that an API or keystroke returned without an error. When something is ambiguous, they get a precise next step and compact proof instead of having to inspect the Mac themselves.
args.effort: Medium-high: typed postconditions in the planner/action registry, same-context read-after-write adapters for Mac and browser, evidence correlation, verdict persistence, and redacted voice/dashboard rendering.
args.risk: Some applications update asynchronously or expose nondeterministic text, causing false 'contradicted' results. Support settling windows, semantic predicates, and an explicit unverified state; never retry a mutation merely because verification is inconclusive.
args.cost_impact: One extra read per write and occasional small standard-model semantic comparison; no realtime call required for normal operation. Raw evidence increases local storage modestly.
args.latency_impact: Adds 0.5–10 seconds depending on the surface, but replaces false immediate success with an honest bounded result. Independent postconditions can be checked in parallel.
args.security_impact: Raw private evidence stays on the Mac/browser bridge. Relay receives only redacted fields, hashes, timestamps, and verdict unless the owner explicitly requests proof. Same-tab/session binding reduces cross-account leakage.

args.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 1–2 seconds, persist the job before dispatch, update state within 5 seconds of each heartbeat, and speak only on completion/failure. Reconnection should catch up from a cursor in under 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one background summarization call on failure (roughly 2–4k input tokens); heartbeat and completion events are deterministic and incur no model call. Storage is bounded per job by retaining metadata plus a configurable stdout/stderr tail.
args.security_concerns: The command remains unrestricted and unattended under FULL_CONTROL_MODE, as the owner requires. Persist cwd, command, exit status, touched paths, and a redacted output tail; never persist inherited secrets or full environment by default. A detached process can outlive the initiating conversation, so the dashboard and pendant must clearly identify owner-started jobs and provide cancel/status, not silently retry arbitrary commands.
missing: A Mac detached-process supervisor that assigns a durable process/job id, emits heartbeats and bounded output cursors, and reports exit/signal/timeout/resource state
Relay durable job events with ordered sequence numbers, replay-from-cursor, and device notification preferences
A reconnecting Mac bridge protocol that reattaches to an existing process instead of launching a duplicate
Pendant event rendering for job started, waiting, completed, failed, and needs-attention states

args.change: Add a shell-specific execution adapter beneath FULL_CONTROL_MODE (not a policy gate): launch every run in a tracked process group with a durable job manifest containing cwd, exact command, start time, pid/process-group id, timeout, and redacted environment keys. Append stdout/stderr to a bounded per-job log with monotonically increasing byte/sequence cursors; emit started/heartbeat/output/exit/signal/timeout events to the existing journal and relay. On bridge reconnect, reconcile the process group by manifest and replay events from the last cursor instead of dispatching the command again. Extend the existing action receipt with exit code, signal, elapsed time, last output cursor, and an explicit 'cannot resume' reason for commands that died.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave a compile, export, sync, or test running and later hear the real result rather than a vague timeout or an accidental duplicate run. Failures become actionable (last output, exit signal, cwd, and whether the process is still alive), while unrestricted shell access remains intact.
args.effort: Medium: a small local supervisor/event journal, relay replay endpoint, and adapters in executor.js plus dashboard/pendant consumers; tests for disconnect, process exit, timeout, and duplicate prevention.
args.risk: A stale pid or reused process-group id could attach the wrong process; bind manifests to start time and verify command/cwd before reattachment. Log growth and secret leakage are risks; cap bytes, redact known secret patterns, and provide deletion. If reconciliation is uncertain, report 'unknown—no retry' rather than rerun.
args.cost_impact: No additional model cost for lifecycle events; modest local disk and relay D1 writes per event. One background-tier summarization call only when the owner requests a human explanation of a failure.
args.latency_impact: Launch remains near current latency. Heartbeats add negligible local work; reconnect status is available in seconds instead of waiting for an HTTP timeout.
args.security_impact: No new authority and no confirmation gate. It makes existing arbitrary commands more observable; command text and output tails are sensitive and must use the existing authenticated Mac/relay paths with retention limits.
depends_on: A durable relay event stream with replay-from-sequence semantics
A local process supervisor that survives the request handler and records manifests
Wire shell lifecycle events into existing /journal, /jobs, and receipt APIs
Pendant notification consumer for completion/failure

transcript.text:
Round 94 findings:

- `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` remains enabled, as intended.
- Receipts and undoability are implemented for completed/failed actions, but they do not yet represent a detached shell process, output cursor, exit signal, or reconnectable process group.
- The relay is reachable and the Mac bridge is online.
- The browser extension is currently offline with 7 pending commands; failed browser jobs wait roughly 45 seconds before producing a receipt.
- Mac readiness is still false because Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions are missing, although shell execution itself remains available.
- Routing is already saving substantial cost: 57% of recent requests avoided the planner tier.

I submitted a new cross-node capability: start a long-running Mac build/test from the pendant, leave, reconnect later, and receive only the completion or actionable failure. This builds on `/execute`, `/jobs`, receipts, journal, relay status, and pipeline events, but the connective process-resumption layer does not exist yet.

What I still need:

1. A Mac process supervisor that persists command manifests and process groups beyond the HTTP request lifetime.
2. Bounded stdout/stderr tails with ordered sequence cursors.
3. Relay event replay from a cursor, so reconnects do not lose progress.
4. Reconciliation that reattaches to an existing process rather than launching a duplicate.
5. Pendant/dashboard states for started, running, completed, failed, timed out, and “unable to determine state.”
6. Explicit handling for commands that cannot resume; uncertain state must never trigger an automatic duplicate execution.

I do **not** need approval gates or a narrower shell policy. The owner’s maximum-access policy should remain unchanged; the missing piece is durable observability and recovery.

args.user_asks: “Did that actually happen?” — give me one trustworthy answer about a task that crossed my Mac, logged-in browser, and pendant, showing what changed, what did not, and the evidence for each step without running it again.
args.why_useful: Today each surface reports its own job or receipt, so a browser failure, a Mac-side file change, and a spoken relay acknowledgement can appear as unrelated events. The owner cannot obtain a single causal answer distinguishing completed work, partial work, and merely-requested work. This is a new cross-surface truth primitive, not another task runner or page watcher.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic correlation and hashes first. Use the background tier only to explain a complicated partial outcome in plain language; use realtime only if the owner asks the question by voice. Do not spend planner-tier tokens reconstructing a straightforward event chain.
args.latency_budget: Return a deterministic status in under 2 seconds from stored records; retrieve missing evidence from the Mac or browser within 10 seconds. Speak a short verdict first, then offer the evidence trail on the dashboard.
args.cost_estimate: No model call for ordinary correlation. A background explanation would be roughly 2–4k input tokens and one call. Storage is compact: event ids, timestamps, hashes, URLs, paths, and receipt references rather than full page or shell output.
args.security_concerns: The evidence can contain private URLs, filenames, browser account names, and command output. Keep raw content on the originating device, expose only authenticated projections, redact secrets, and label stale or inferred evidence. Never convert missing evidence into a claim of success and never rerun an action merely to verify it.
missing: A cross-surface task identity and causal-link protocol shared by Mac jobs, browser commands, relay requests, and pendant utterances
A verifier that compares before/after evidence (file hashes, browser field snapshots, receipt status, and relay delivery state) and classifies complete, partial, failed, unknown, or contradicted
A compact authenticated evidence-bundle endpoint with per-item provenance and freshness
Pendant and dashboard rendering for a verdict plus expandable evidence chain

args.user_asks: Fix the thing that just failed on my Mac.
args.why_useful: Today a failed shell or desktop job leaves the owner to repeat the request or inspect logs. This would turn a failure into a bounded incident: identify the exact failing step, collect the relevant evidence, consult documentation when useful, attempt a safe recovery or retry, and report one short spoken result. It uses the pendant for the request and notification, the always-on relay for durable state, the Mac for diagnosis and execution, and the browser only when a logged-in/private page or public documentation is needed.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to hear the owner's short command and speak the result. Run failure classification, log summarization, documentation lookup, and retry planning on a cheaper background model; reserve the expensive model for genuinely ambiguous recovery plans.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 second from the pendant. Produce a diagnosis from the existing receipt and captured stdout/stderr within 5 seconds. Attempt one automatically reversible retry within 30 seconds; if diagnosis is ambiguous, speak the proposed next step instead of burning repeated retries.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one small background-model call over a compact failure packet plus zero or one web lookup; roughly 1–3 cents per incident depending on documentation retrieval. Realtime cost is limited to the brief acknowledgement and result.
args.security_concerns: Failure packets must redact bearer tokens, cookies, secrets, and likely personal data from environment variables and command output before leaving the Mac. Private browser pages remain on the browser/Mac path. No approval gate is added, honoring the owner's maximum-access policy, but every attempted recovery must carry the existing receipt and an explicit reason, with irreversible retries marked as such. Automatic retries should be limited by attempt count and idempotency key to prevent loops.
missing: A structured failure packet on every Mac action containing actionId, argv or shell text, exit status, timeout/signal, stdout/stderr excerpts, cwd, environment fingerprint, and redaction markers.
A durable incident record and retry state machine in the relay, linked to the existing job and receipt IDs.
A recovery planner that can choose among retry, compensating undo, alternate typed action, browser documentation lookup, or handoff to the owner.
A relay-to-Mac retry route with idempotency and a hard retry budget, plus dashboard and pendant status updates.

args.user_asks: When something breaks, file a complete bug report for me automatically.
args.why_useful: The owner already wants a pendant that files its own bug reports from the UART log. A useful report should correlate the pendant's local UART/audio pipeline symptoms with the Mac action receipt, relay job, browser tab (when relevant), and exact timestamps—without making the owner reproduce the failure. The owner gets a ready-to-forward report and a one-sentence spoken confirmation instead of debugging across devices.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to turn structured logs into a concise reproduction summary and redact sensitive fields. Use realtime only if the owner asks follow-up questions. Do not send the report externally automatically; leave it as a local/exportable draft.
args.latency_budget: Start collecting evidence locally immediately. Show a draft incident in the dashboard within 3 seconds of a terminal failure or pendant watchdog event, then enrich it asynchronously within 15 seconds. UART collection must never delay audio playback or button response.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for collection and correlation; typically 1–2 cents for one compact background summarization call. Storage is a bounded local/relay record plus small compressed log excerpts; no model call is needed if the owner only wants raw evidence.
args.security_concerns: Redact bearer tokens, cookies, environment secrets, personal paths where appropriate, and private page text before relay upload. Keep raw UART logs on the pendant/Mac by default, with an owner-controlled attach action. Browser evidence should be a URL/title and DOM locator or hash, not full authenticated page content unless explicitly requested. Reports must state which fields were omitted and preserve immutable hashes for evidence integrity.
missing: A pendant UART-log ring buffer with event IDs, firmware version, reset reason, and bounded export over the existing pipeline/event channel.
A shared incident schema linking pendant event IDs, pipeline IDs, Mac job/action/receipt IDs, browser command IDs, timestamps, and redaction status.
Automatic correlation in the relay that opens or updates one incident instead of producing duplicate reports during reconnects.
A dashboard incident view with raw-versus-redacted evidence, export to Markdown/JSON, and owner-controlled retention/deletion.
A local-agent hook that emits a structured failure event for every run_shell, typed action, browser action, timeout, and planner exception.

args.change: Add a cross-surface incident-correlation ledger, not another executor: on every Mac, browser, relay, or pendant failure, write a compact append-only event keyed by a shared correlationId and actionId; asynchronously join events by time window and parent job, attach the existing receipt/undo verdict, record disconnect/reconnect gaps, and expose one redacted incident bundle through the dashboard. Start with local-agent hooks around executor.js and browserBridge result handling, relay ingestion from pipeline events, and a pendant event envelope carrying boot/session sequence numbers. Deduplicate retries and reconnects by idempotency key; retain raw evidence locally and only upload redacted excerpts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When a failure crosses devices, the owner sees one truthful timeline—what the pendant heard, what the relay dispatched, what the Mac/browser attempted, and where it stopped—instead of several incomplete job records. It directly enables the owner's requested self-filed pendant bug reports and makes support/debugging possible without asking them to reproduce the problem.
args.effort: Medium: shared event schema and local hooks first, relay append/query and correlation worker second, dashboard incident panel and pendant envelope third. Add deterministic tests for dropped links, duplicate results, clock skew, and redaction.
args.risk: Incorrect time correlation could merge two simultaneous jobs or split one across reconnects. Mitigate with parent IDs, monotonic device sequence numbers, confidence labels, and never deleting source receipts. If correlation fails, preserve separate events and show the uncertainty rather than inventing a story. UART/log volume must be capped and backpressured so audio and action latency are unaffected.
args.cost_impact: No recurring model cost for collection/correlation; optional background summarization costs about 1–2 cents per incident. Small D1/R2 growth from bounded redacted bundles; local ring buffers avoid shipping every raw log.
args.latency_impact: No synchronous network dependency on action execution. Hook overhead should be under 5 ms; incident joining and summarization happen asynchronously, with a draft visible in roughly 1–3 seconds.
args.security_impact: Sensitive stdout, environment variables, bearer tokens, cookies, authenticated page content, and secret UART fields are redacted before relay persistence. Preserve hashes and source locations for integrity. Raw logs stay on-device unless the owner explicitly exports them. This adds observability, not a gate or reduced access.

A pendant UART ring buffer and bounded event export
A relay incident storage/query route and retention policy
A local-agent failure-event hook for shell, typed actions, browser actions, timeouts, and planner errors

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear the pendant all day without wondering whether it is listening or whether a private Mac/browser task will continue after they set it down. args.latency_impact: Local mute/latch should take under 100 ms and must not depend on the network. Cross-surface pause notification should arrive within the normal link heartbeat, with reconnect reconciliation on return.
args.security_impact: Strengthens privacy at the device boundary: local hardware mute is authoritative and signed wear events prevent an untrusted bridge from claiming the pendant is present.
