args.user_asks: Keep my Mac and authenticated browser in sync after a multi-step request—for example, if you book something in the browser and add it to Calendar—then detect partial completion, repair the missing side, and tell me exactly which sides succeeded.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot reliably ask the hive to perform work spanning a logged-in browser and local Mac today: one side can succeed while the other fails, leaving duplicate bookings, missing calendar entries, or an apparently finished job with no trustworthy reconciliation.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the spoken request and final explanation. A cheaper background planner maintains the task's intended facts, compares receipts from both surfaces, and performs idempotent reconciliation; reserve the expensive vision model for ambiguous browser state.
args.latency_budget: Speak an immediate accepted/blocked acknowledgement; complete ordinary reconciliation within 30 seconds after both surfaces respond. If a side remains unavailable, persist a partially-complete state and notify on recovery rather than looping.
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: background reasoning and receipt polling dominate; browser vision is exceptional. Local fact/receipt storage is small, with no need to resend full page contents.
args.security_concerns: Do not infer success from a click alone. Require typed evidence (URL, event ID, record ID, or local object identifier), scope reconciliation to the intended account and time window, and never undo an externally committed booking automatically. Keep authenticated page data and calendar details encrypted and local/relay-protected.
missing: A cross-surface intent/fact ledger that records expected postconditions and evidence requirements
Adapters that expose stable external identifiers for browser results and Mac Calendar/Reminder mutations
A reconciliation planner with idempotency and non-destructive conflict handling

result.summary: Enable a bounded audio-retention sweeper and per-job deletion controls: default to short retention for generated briefings, delete expired R2 objects and D1 pointers idempotently, and expose a dashboard ‘delete now’ action. Keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry.
result.status: proposed
result.note: NOTE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-07. The previous agent's 4,452-char patch plan was DESTROYED when this entry was set to "implementing": scripts/harness-ledger.mjs status --note overwrites the note, it does not append. Every claim below was re-verified against the live files today; the headline claim holds and is worse than it was stated. HEADLINE (TRUE): the sweeper cannot clear a backlog. audioRetention.js:171-175 lists with limit Math.min(Math.max(n,1),100) and passes no cursor; store/jobQuery.js:8 JOB_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 100 clamps it again, so raising the local constant alone fixes nothing. Ordering is newest-first on both stores (store/d1Store.js:566 ORDER BY created_at DESC; store/memoryStore.js:166). The sweep therefore only ever inspects the 100 NEWEST audio_capture rows — the ones least likely to be expired — and repeated runs never advance the window. A keyset cursor already exists and is plumbed through listJobs({before}) (store/jobQuery.js:19-37, used at server.js:1893); sweepExpiredAudio simply never passes it. OTHER VERIFIED GAPS. (2) AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH = 200 at audioRetention.js:32 is unreachable dead config given the 100 cap. (3) No scheduled invocation exists: cloudflare-worker/worker.js exports only fetch, wrangler.jsonc has no crons/triggers, and the sole caller is the manual route at server.js:2151. (4) Inert as shipped: wrangler.jsonc:34 sets AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED=false and server.js:2149 forces dryRun, so the deployed sweeper deletes nothing under any input. (5) Bindings are not threaded into either delete path: server.js:2151 and server.js:2834 call without bindings, and cloudflareBindings is only populated inside the Worker fetch handler — under plain Node deleteAudioCaptureObject short-circuits false (audioStorage.js:130-136), so the D1 pointer is cleared at audioRetention.js:141-147 while the R2 object is orphaned permanently, and the response still returns ok:true. (6) Non-atomic ordering: the R2 delete precedes the pointer clear, so an updateJob throw leaves a row addressing a deleted object. (7) In record mode with no store.deleteJob the object is already gone while the row keeps a stale audioRef; that branch has no test. (8) One R2 error aborts the whole sweep: audioRetention.js:195-204 is an unguarded loop with no per-item try/catch and no partial report. (9) NO owner-pin concept exists anywhere in cloud-relay — the entry's "keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry" is 0% implemented. (10) One global 30-day TTL (config.js:27-31, wrangler.jsonc:33); generated agent audio is an ordinary audio_capture row tagged role:reply (server.js:1075), so "short retention for generated briefings" is not implemented and there is no briefing concept in cloud-relay at all. (11) DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio (server.js:1979-1995) never follows replyCaptureId, so deleting a run leaves the synthesized reply audio in R2 — and record mode destroys the only reference to it. (12) No dashboard reaches either delete route: src/ops/api.js has no audio DELETE and no retention call at all, so the "dashboard delete now action" does not exist in the frontend. (13) The read-only report at server.js:2115 hardcodes limit 100, so storedRecordings and expiredCount are structurally wrong past 100 captures. (14) The sweep report calls captures.length "scanned" (audioRetention.js:182,209), implying a full-corpus scan that never happened. NO DEFECT FOUND on clock/units: createdAt is ISO-8601 wherever written (jobs.js:20,34-35), parsed with Date.getTime (audioRetention.js:62) and compared against ms Date.now (audioRetention.js:78,86); maxAgeMs is milliseconds in config.js:27, in wrangler.jsonc:33 (2592000000 = 30d) and in the comparison alike. TEST GAPS: audioRetention.test.js never exercises a backlog >100 through a real store (the batch-cap test calls selectExpiredAudioCaptures on a plain array, bypassing listJobs, so gap 1 is invisible to the suite and gap 2 is asserted as correct), never makes an R2 delete throw, and always passes bindings explicitly — which is precisely what production does not do. cloud-relay/ was NOT edited. Left proposed.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing 'done' when the Mac agent could not touch the screen. Everyday requests can still succeed through the browser or shell even while Accessibility is missing, and failures name the one fix needed instead of wasting a whole turn.

args.security_impact: No new authority or restriction; preserves FULL_CONTROL_MODE. The receipt records capability/permission state, which may expose host metadata to authenticated job readers; keep it behind existing auth and redact paths.

transcript.text:
Live discovery found:

- Mac agent v0.5.0 is online with `FULL_CONTROL_MODE=true`.
- Safari browser extension is online and has no pending commands.
- The actual AI Pendant Agent binary still lacks Accessibility permission:
  - `Accessibility trusted=false`
  - `inputReachability=failed`
  - UI actions can report success while doing nothing.
- Screen Recording is unavailable, computer-use is disabled, and vision upload consent is false.
- A recent job demonstrated the problem: opening Browser Bridge succeeded, but the following computer-use step failed because the loop was disabled.
- Routing telemetry shows planner requests averaging roughly 9,000 prompt tokens, so avoiding doomed vision retries is also a cost/latency improvement.

I recorded a new change: extend the existing readiness contract with **automatic route substitution and postcondition verification**. Browser-owned reads should fall back to the browser extension; deterministic Mac work should use typed actions or shell; computer-use should run only when all required capabilities are present. Receipts should distinguish “completed through fallback” from “UI action succeeded.”

What is still needed for genuine screen control:

1. Accessibility permission granted specifically to `/Users/evanliu/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app`.
2. Screen Recording permission for vision-driven UI work.
3. `PENDANT_COMPUTER_USE_ENABLED=1`.
4. Vision-upload consent if screenshots are to leave the Mac.

No additional tool is needed from me this round; the main remaining work is implementing the fallback route graph and resolving those host permissions if screen control is wanted.

args.user_asks: “When you submit something in my authenticated browser, make sure the Mac records it only after the site confirms it, and tell me later exactly what happened—even if the browser or Mac disconnects halfway through.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner can have browser commands and Mac actions, but not a trustworthy cross-device transaction. This would prevent false local records (such as reminders or notes saying a form was submitted when it was not), survive a dropped bridge, and give the pendant a concise, evidence-backed completion or recovery message.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic workflow orchestration and background models for reconciliation; reserve realtime only for the owner's immediate spoken acknowledgement. Use the planner tier only when the site outcome or requested local record is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; browser confirmation normally under 10 seconds; disconnect recovery is asynchronous and may take minutes, with the pendant notifying the owner when reconciled.
args.cost_estimate: Low per invocation when selectors and postconditions are known: mostly relay/database and browser polling. Ambiguous pages may require one planner call and, only when available, a vision call; the dominant cost is screenshot/planner context, not the Mac record action.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and submission results remain within the browser/relay authorization boundary; only the minimum confirmation and owner-requested record cross to the Mac. Never duplicate a submission after timeout without an idempotency key or explicit site confirmation. Require owner confirmation for irreversible submissions, but allow retries of idempotent reads and record creation.
missing: A durable cross-surface transaction record with idempotency key, state machine, and lease/resume semantics.
Browser-side postcondition adapters that can distinguish a confirmed submission from navigation or transport success.
Relay reconciliation worker that resumes after browser/Mac disconnects and emits a final pendant notification.
Mac-side conditional-write endpoint: create the requested reminder/note/file only when supplied with a verified browser outcome.
Evidence-linked receipts spanning browser command, site confirmation, and Mac write.
A recovery UI showing pending, confirmed, conflicted, and permanently failed transactions.

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 12 pieces you named already exist: /browser/sessions, /browser/status, /browser/poll, /browser/result/:commandid, /browser/heartbeat, /jobs. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.change: Add a durable cross-surface transaction coordinator, distinct from ordinary Mac jobs and browser commands. It should create an idempotency-keyed transaction before submission, persist browser and Mac phases independently, require a browser postcondition receipt before allowing the Mac write, lease/retry after bridge disconnects, and reconcile on startup. A timeout must remain 'unknown/pending' rather than becoming success; duplicate submissions are prohibited unless the site exposes a matching idempotency key. Expose a compact owner-facing state timeline and send the final outcome through the pendant pipeline.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask one sentence such as 'submit this and remind me when it is confirmed' without risking a false reminder or duplicate submission. They get a truthful answer after interruptions instead of having to inspect browser tabs, Mac jobs, and logs separately.
args.effort: High: new relay D1 transaction schema and worker, browser postcondition protocol, Mac conditional-write endpoint, recovery/reconciliation worker, and dashboard timeline.
args.risk: Sites with weak confirmation signals may leave a transaction pending; fail closed on local writes and surface an explicit conflict. Browser sessions may expire, so preserve the original evidence and ask the owner to re-authenticate rather than replaying.
args.cost_impact: Small durable-storage and polling cost per transaction; ambiguous postconditions may require planner/vision calls. This is cheaper than duplicate submissions and manual recovery.
args.latency_impact: Adds one persistence round trip before each phase and postcondition polling, typically hundreds of milliseconds plus site latency; recovery is asynchronous.
args.security_impact: Requires authenticated correlation among relay, browser session, and Mac job. Store hashes/minimal status rather than page bodies; encrypt or restrict evidence references, and never transmit session cookies to the relay or Mac.
depends_on: A new transaction state machine and idempotency-key storage in the relay.
A browser extension result contract that reports authoritative postconditions, not merely command execution.
A Mac conditional-write route that accepts only a verified transaction receipt.
Existing browser command/session, Mac job/receipt/journal, and pendant notification routes.

Recorded two items:

1. **Cross-surface “submit, then record” capability**  
   The owner can submit something through an authenticated browser and have the Mac create a reminder/note only after confirmed site success, with recovery after disconnects and an evidence-backed pendant notification.

2. **Durable transaction coordinator**  
   This requires a new relay-backed state machine spanning browser commands, site postconditions, Mac writes, idempotency keys, leases, retries, and reconciliation. Timeouts remain explicitly pending rather than being misreported as success, preventing duplicate submissions and false local records.

args.user_asks: Make the AI Pendant Browser Bridge available, wait for a fresh heartbeat, and tell me in one short sentence whether it is online—without replaying or executing any queued browser command.
args.why_useful: This is a recurring real failure: opening the app succeeds, but the planner then invokes the disabled computer-use loop and reports failure even though the extension may already be online. A deterministic reconnect-and-verify path would make the owner's browser reachable without touching private tabs or pending work.
args.model_tier: deterministic routing and polling; no realtime or planner model unless the bridge remains unavailable and a concise explanation is needed
args.latency_budget: Open the bridge immediately, then poll browser status for up to 10 seconds at 500 ms; speak within 1–2 seconds when already online and never exceed 10 seconds.

transcript.text:
Round 123 findings:

- The Mac agent, relay, and browser extension are currently online.
- Safari’s bridge has zero pending commands.
- The browser bridge is foregrounded and recently heartbeated.
- Computer-use is disabled.
- Accessibility is still not trusted for the actual `AI Pendant Agent.app`; `/observe` confirms synthesized UI events may report success while doing nothing.
- Screen Recording is still unavailable, so vision-based interaction cannot be trusted.

I proposed and recorded two changes:

1. A deterministic `bridge_reconnect` intent that opens the bridge, waits for a heartbeat newer than the request, and reports status without polling or executing browser commands.
2. Proof-aware Mac UI receipts that report `executed_unverified` when Accessibility/input reachability is unavailable, while preserving unrestricted execution and allowing fallback to shell, AppleScript, or browser actions.

What is still needed:

- Implement the freshness-aware bridge reconnect route and typed receipt.
- Add the `/observe` reachability capsule to UI planning and receipts.
- If screen-driving workflows are required, grant Accessibility to `/Users/evanliu/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app` and Screen Recording, then enable the computer-use loop. These permissions are not needed for the safer browser-heartbeat reconnect path.

args.user_asks: If I speak while the Mac or relay is temporarily offline, keep my request on the pendant, show me that it is queued, and deliver it exactly once when the connection returns—then tell me whether it was accepted, completed, or needs me.
args.why_useful: Today a dropped link turns a spoken request into an ambiguous disappearance. The pendant is the one surface the owner still has, while the relay and Mac can recover later; durable, exactly-once handoff would make the system dependable during sleep, travel, Wi-Fi changes, or Mac restarts.
args.model_tier: No model for queueing, deduplication, or delivery receipts. Use the background tier only to summarize a completed or failed request when the owner asks; reserve realtime for the short spoken status.
args.latency_budget: Immediate local tactile/audio acknowledgement under 200 ms; sync on reconnection within 5 seconds; no blocking wait on the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per queued request beyond normal transcription when connectivity returns. Storage, retry traffic, and receipt retention dominate; summarization is optional and cheap background work.
args.security_concerns: Queue entries must be encrypted at rest on the pendant and relay, bound to the owner's device/session, and expire or be cancellable. Never replay a command after an uncertain acknowledgement: use a globally unique request ID, an execution lease, and a durable terminal receipt. Destructive actions must retain their existing confirmation semantics when eventually delivered.
missing: A pendant-side encrypted outbox with bounded size, local queue IDs, retry metadata, and a user-visible queued/sent state
Relay idempotency and a claim/lease protocol that survives duplicate reconnects and Mac restarts
Mac-agent admission of queued requests with request-ID propagation into jobs, receipts, and undo records
A compact pendant status protocol for queued, delivered, running, completed, failed, and expired states
Recovery rules for a lost acknowledgement, including reconciliation against the Mac job ledger before retrying

args.change: Create a cross-surface causality ledger that assigns one immutable conversation/request ID at the pendant, propagates it through relay audio/transcription, planner decisions, Mac jobs, browser commands, and final spoken output, and materializes a compact timeline with explicit gaps (received, forwarded, claimed, executed, acknowledged). Reconcile late events by ID rather than timestamp and expose a redacted owner-facing 'what happened' view plus machine-readable diagnostics.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When a request crosses the pendant, cloud relay, Mac, and browser, today the owner cannot reliably distinguish lost, duplicated, still-running, or completed work. One causal timeline would let them ask 'what happened to that?' and receive a truthful answer even after a restart or delayed callback.
args.effort: Medium-to-large: schema and propagation headers across relay and local-agent boundaries, durable append-only storage with retention, reconciliation of late/duplicate events, and a concise spoken formatter.
args.risk: A ledger can accidentally retain sensitive transcripts or URLs; store hashes and redacted summaries by default, encrypt durable records, and apply short retention. Clock differences must never determine causality; IDs and sequence numbers must.
args.cost_impact: Small storage and write overhead per event; no extra model calls for the ledger. Background summarization is optional.
args.latency_impact: Negligible request-path overhead if events are appended asynchronously; owner-facing history lookup should return in under 1 second locally.
args.security_impact: Improves accountability but increases metadata concentration. Separate content from event metadata, enforce per-owner access, redact browser/private-page fields, and allow deletion by request ID.
depends_on: A propagated immutable request ID at pipeline ingress
Relay and Mac job schemas accepting correlation and parent IDs
Browser command and action receipt records exposing the same correlation ID
A retention/redaction policy and owner-facing history endpoint

result.summary: Add a durable browser job runner with two backends: the authenticated Safari bridge for owner-private pages and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages. Represent each step as navigate/read/extract/click/type, persist evidence (URL, title, timestamp, selected text), retry transient failures, and expose a job result stream to the planner.
result.status: proposed
result.note: KEPT OPEN: the backend ROUTER now exists, the durable job runner still does not. Backend A ships: local-agent/browserSessions.js (chg-bc35ae04 / chg-2fffc681 / chg-086a6904). Backend B ships: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js (chg-81e5c92d, implemented). ROUTER DONE 2026-08-07 — local-agent/originFanOut.js chooseBackend() is the selector this entry named: owner-private -> Safari (only it holds the sessions); public -> Browser Run (only it is awake when the Mac sleeps); LAN / private IP / localhost -> Safari only, decided by serverBrowser.normalizePublicUrl rather than a second copy of that logic; relay budget spent -> Safari; explicit backend:"safari"|"relay" always honoured. An owner-private page is deliberately NOT failed over to the relay when Safari is down: the relay cannot hold the session, so the trip buys a login wall at the price of one of ten daily browser-minutes, and reserving that budget is what keeps the public leg answerable. Free-tier limits are enforced rather than documented: relay lane is serial, paced to 1 action per 10s, and a UTC-day browser-ms tally persists in .pendant-relay-browser-budget.json (GET /origins/budget). MISSING STILL: no durable job runner — no jobId, no persistence across a restart, no retry of transient failures — and no job result stream to the planner. serverBrowser is still unreachable from the voice path (chg-f527c3bc, unapplied wiring diff).

args.subject: Observed browser_navigate failures
args.body: GET /journal/ops shows browser_navigate idempotency key with 11 runs, 11 failures (while read/snapshot succeed). Do you know root cause or existing fix? I am considering an adaptive navigation failure classifier + truthful retry/fallback change.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.finding: Live Mac observability shows browser_navigate idempotency key act_36a2da2b0b8c has 11 runs and 11 failures from 07:21–14:52 UTC, while browser_snapshot (9/9), browser_read_page (5/5), and browser_type/select/click runs succeed. /observe reports browser bridge online, so this is not simply global bridge absence.
args.evidence: GET /journal returned repeatedActions.browser_navigate: runs 11, failed 11; GET /ops/status and /observe show browserExtension.online=true and pendingCommands=0.

args.change: Add an adaptive, evidence-preserving recovery layer specifically for browser navigation. Before browser_navigate, validate bridge heartbeat, session/tab affinity, and URL normalization; on failure classify the returned error as stale tab, extension transport timeout, blocked/unsupported URL, or page-load timeout. Retry only transient transport/page-load failures with the same idempotency key and bounded backoff, reattach the named session when possible, and use a safe Safari foreground/open-url fallback only for public URLs. Persist each attempt, error class, final URL/title, heartbeat age, and backend choice in the existing job receipt/journal. Never report navigation success from an enqueued command: success requires a post-navigation URL/title/readback, otherwise return a truthful partial failure with the next recovery action.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says “open this page” or asks the pendant to inspect a logged-in site, it will stop silently burning attempts and give a reliable answer: the page opened and was verified, or exactly why it could not. Transient Safari/extension hiccups recover without another spoken turn, while private authenticated pages are not mistakenly sent to a public relay.
args.effort: Medium: browser bridge command lifecycle and local-agent browserSessions/originFanOut integration, plus receipt schema and tests for stale tabs, timeouts, and private/public routing.
args.risk: A retry could load a page twice or leave an extra tab; constrain retries by idempotency key and session affinity, and record every attempt. A public fallback must never be used for owner-private URLs. If verification cannot run, report unknown rather than success.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; mostly local bridge requests and a few extra seconds on transient failures. Avoids repeated planner calls and wasted browser-minute budget.
args.latency_impact: Adds a fast heartbeat/affinity check; successful navigation gains roughly 0.1–0.5s verification, transient failures may take up to two bounded retries.
args.security_impact: Improves security posture without adding approval gates: authenticated sessions remain on Safari, URL origin and backend are recorded, and receipts expose evidence rather than page contents by default.
depends_on: chg-16bc5dee durable browser job runner (or its existing router)
chg-14accc01 request IDs, idempotency keys, and tab/session affinity
Existing GET /browser/status, POST /browser/heartbeat, GET /browser/sessions, GET /journal, and GET /observe observability paths

args.user_asks: “Open the page I mentioned, keep trying if my Mac or Safari bridge briefly drops, and tell me only when you have verified the exact page is open—or give me the precise reason it cannot be reached.”
args.why_useful: Today a browser navigation can fail repeatedly even while reads and the bridge appear healthy, and the owner must repeat the request or trust an unverified success. This would turn a spoken intent into a resilient, cross-surface handoff: the pendant can stop listening, the relay can retain the job, and the Mac/browser can resume and prove the destination without claiming that merely enqueueing a command succeeded.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic routing and a cheap background model for heartbeat/error classification and retry scheduling; use the realtime model only for the final spoken status if the owner is actively waiting. Escalate to the planner only when URL ambiguity, authentication state, or recovery choice is genuinely unclear.
args.latency_budget: For a healthy bridge, verify within 2–5 seconds. For a transient disconnect, continue for a user-configurable window (for example 10 minutes) while the pendant is free, then speak or queue one concise result. Never wait indefinitely in the realtime turn.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for deterministic heartbeat, URL normalization, idempotency, and post-navigation readback; roughly $0.001–$0.02 for a background classification/recovery decision depending on retries. The dominant cost is Safari/extension round trips and any relay browser-minute usage, not speech.
args.security_concerns: Private authenticated URLs must remain on the owner's Safari session and never fail over to a public relay backend. Persist URL origin, session/tab binding, heartbeat age, attempt count, and verified title/URL—not page contents by default. A dashboard and spoken response must distinguish queued, attempted, verified, and failed; navigation itself remains within the owner's existing maximum-access policy.
missing: A durable browser job runner with restart-safe job state and a result stream to the planner
An adaptive browser_navigate recovery/verification layer that records each attempt and requires post-navigation URL/title readback
A relay-to-Mac wake/resume contract for jobs that outlive the active voice turn
A truthful pendant status beacon or queued-result notification for completion after the owner stops listening
A full failed-navigation receipt/error payload surfaced through journal/dashboard for diagnosis

args.change: Add a cross-surface navigation lease protocol between relay, Mac agent, and Safari bridge. A lease contains jobId, idempotency key, private/public origin classification, session/tab binding, expiry, retry budget, and a monotonic attempt number. The relay persists the lease and wakes/reconnects the Mac bridge; the Mac agent renews it while executing; the extension acknowledges each command and returns a post-navigation URL/title proof. On reconnect, the Mac agent resumes the lease rather than replaying the last command, and the relay emits exactly one terminal verified/failed result to the pendant and dashboard.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask once and walk away—even through a sleeping Mac, dropped browser heartbeat, or voice disconnect—and later receive a trustworthy result instead of duplicate tabs, lost work, or a false “done.” This is the missing connective behavior between existing browser polling, sessions, jobs, and relay persistence.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared lease schema, D1/local persistence, reconnect handshake, monotonic attempt handling, and terminal-result deduplication across relay/mac/extension.
args.risk: A stale lease could resume against the wrong tab; bind leases to authenticated session ID, origin, and tab/window identity, and expire them conservatively. If proof is unavailable, mark the job unknown/failed rather than replaying or claiming success.
args.cost_impact: Small D1 and local persistence overhead; no meaningful model cost. Saves planner/realtime calls caused by repeated owner retries and avoids unnecessary public-browser-minute consumption.
args.latency_impact: Healthy path adds one acknowledgement and readback round trip (typically under 1 second); reconnect recovery is asynchronous and does not hold the realtime conversation open.
args.security_impact: Private authenticated work remains exclusively in the Safari bridge; the relay stores metadata and encrypted/opaque job references, not page contents. Lease origin/session binding prevents accidental cross-account replay.

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Resilient verified browser navigation capability** — the owner can ask once, walk away, and receive a truthful verified result even across temporary Mac/Safari disconnects.
2. **Cross-surface navigation lease protocol** — durable relay/Mac/extension leases with idempotent reconnects, session binding, retry budgets, and post-navigation proof to prevent duplicate actions or false completion.

args.user_asks: If something I asked the pendant to do fails, recover it automatically when it is safe, otherwise tell me exactly what broke, what was tried, and what I need to do.
args.why_useful: The system already records failures, but today a failed Mac/browser job is a dead end: the owner has to notice it, diagnose stale tabs or missing permissions, and retry manually. A cross-surface recovery loop would use the relay for durable monitoring, the Mac for local diagnostics/actions, and the browser extension for tab/session repair, then return a short truthful pendant update instead of silently replaying a bad action.
args.model_tier: Deterministic failure classification and bounded recovery recipes first; gpt-4.1-mini background model for summarizing evidence and choosing among known recovery recipes; realtime only for the final spoken update when the owner is actively listening.
args.latency_budget: For an interactive failure, diagnose in under 2 seconds and attempt at most one bounded recovery within 10 seconds; background jobs can retry/diagnose for up to 2 minutes. Never block the original action path.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per recovered failure, dominated by optional background summarization; deterministic stale-tab, offline-bridge, timeout, and permission checks should be free.
args.security_concerns: Diagnostics may include private URLs, app names, and browser error text; keep evidence on the Mac/relay, redact page contents and secrets before sending to the model, and send only a concise result to the pendant. Recovery must be limited to the same owner-requested goal and be auditable; never blindly replay a browser mutation or submit a form.
missing: A durable failure-classification and recovery state machine that links job/action receipts to browser tab/session state and Mac permission/bridge health.
Typed, idempotent recovery recipes such as select a live tab explicitly, reopen the bridge, refresh machine context, or retry a timed-out read once.
A relay-side completion/failure notification queue and dashboard view showing original error, recovery attempt, outcome, and next owner step.
A redaction layer for command output, URLs, and browser evidence before model summarization.

Continued discovery found:

- `/ops/status` reports `fullControlMode: true`, but Accessibility and Screen Recording are not granted, so mac-vision is not actually ready.
- Safari/browser extension is online, but its current target is `https://example.com` titled “Failed to open page,” confirming that stale or invalid tab targeting remains a real issue.
- `/journal` currently shows 141 actions, 27 failures, and zero undoable actions.
- `/routing` shows planner requests averaging about 9,000 prompt tokens, while deterministic/background routing is substantially cheaper.

I recorded three new improvements:

1. **Live capability-readiness routing** — classify each surface as configured, permission-ready, online, and targetable before planning; avoid impossible vision attempts and choose browser/script fallbacks.
2. **Long-command progress streaming** — send bounded, redacted stdout/stderr progress and heartbeats through the existing job/pipeline streams, so the pendant can report that a task is still running rather than appearing dead.
3. **Failure recovery orchestration** — connect journal receipts, browser state, Mac health, and relay notifications into bounded, non-blind recovery recipes.

What I still need is implementation work rather than more access:

- A durable readiness schema with timestamps/TTL and fallback metadata.
- A shared redaction and bounded-output utility.
- Reconnectable progress-event cursors.
- A recovery state machine that can diagnose stale tabs, offline bridges, timeouts, and missing permissions without replaying browser mutations.
- The actual AI Pendant Agent Accessibility permission remains useful for GUI automation, but I will not re-request it this round.

args.user_asks: Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser, tell me exactly what information will leave the device, what will stay local, and which model or service will see each piece; let me choose a private-local mode when possible.
args.why_useful: Today the system can act across a trusted Mac, authenticated Safari sessions, relay storage, and cloud models, but the owner cannot see or control the data boundary of a particular task. A per-task data-flow preview would make the hive usable for sensitive mail, documents, and account pages without forcing the owner to understand implementation details. This is distinct from action approval: it governs information disclosure, not whether a trusted action may run.
args.model_tier: Deterministic data-flow analysis and redaction classification first; use a cheap background model only to explain the resulting policy in plain language. Realtime is needed only to speak the short preview or answer a follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Render a preview in under 500 ms for known action types; for an unfamiliar workflow, produce a conservative preview within 2 seconds before execution planning continues.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic classification; under $0.001 for occasional background explanation. The dominant cost is engineering a complete inventory, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The preview itself must not reveal private page contents. It should describe categories, destinations, retention, and transformations (for example, “Gmail message body: local Safari only” or “calendar title: sent to relay model after redaction”). A local-only selection must be enforceable and visibly fail closed if a required cloud step cannot be avoided. The policy and actual observed egress should both be journaled for later inspection.
missing: A typed per-action data-flow manifest covering shell output, screenshots, DOM/page text, audio, model prompts, relay persistence, and dashboard access.
A local redaction/tokenization service that can replace sensitive values while preserving task utility.
Execution-time enforcement of the selected privacy mode, including a local-model or local-deterministic fallback and refusal to upload when no fallback exists.
A post-task egress receipt comparing planned versus actual destinations, fields, retention, and model calls.

result.summary: Add transactional desktop jobs: each plan has a preview, stable job/action IDs, preconditions (expected app/path/hash), checkpoints, result receipts, and compensating undo where possible. On retry, skip completed action IDs rather than replaying clicks or shell commands. Prefer accessibility selectors and declarative APIs over coordinates.
result.status: implemented
result.note: Built the receipt/undo half only. NO gates, NO approval prompts, NO preconditions — nothing added here can refuse or skip an action, per owner policy. New local-agent/actionReceipts.js; executor.js now wraps every dispatch: observeBeforeAction(action) runs first (pure observation, swallows all errors, its verdict is never read), then buildActionReceipt() attaches a receipt to every result — successful or failed. Receipt carries: content-addressed actionId (stable across a re-run of the same plan; positional index would not be, because the orchestrator hands the executor one action at a time), unique receiptId, effect read|write, what was touched (paths, urls, apps, shell commands, email recipients, clipboard, settings with before/after), duration, and an honest reversibility verdict with reversedBy or irreversibleReason. Reversibility now lives in ONE place: undo.js imports describeReversibility() so the receipt the owner reads and the decision undo makes cannot disagree; jobs recorded before receipts existed fall back to the raw result fields, so old history stays undoable. COMPENSATING UNDO: observeBeforeAction snapshots any file a write_file/create_note/delete_path/copy_path/move_path is about to clobber into ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/.undo (bounded at 8 MB; directories and oversize files are recorded as irreversible WITH the reason rather than silently half-copied). This makes delete_path — previously permanent — undoable, and fixes a real data-loss bug: undo used to answer 'yes, reversible' for a write_file that OVERWROTE an existing file and then reverse it by DELETING that file, destroying content the agent never wrote. Now it restores the exact prior bytes. Surfaced at GET /jobs (receipts per job), new GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts (counts + per-step undo verdict + snapshot vault path), and inside GET /ops/snapshot so the dashboard and relay see them too. describeUndoability now returns steps[] and irreversible[] with reasons, so 'why can't I undo this?' has an answer. Verified live end to end: overwrote a hand-written file via POST /execute, receipt showed reversible=true reversedBy='restore snapshot', POST /jobs/:id/undo restored the original content. Tests: actionReceipts.test.js (16); full suite 499/499.

args.user_asks: “That didn’t work—tell me exactly why, try the safest recovery, and leave me a reviewable fallback if it still fails.”
args.why_useful: Today failures are opaque across surfaces: the Mac journal shows 27 failed actions, repeated browser navigation has an 11/11 failure pattern, and 111 actions lack routing attribution. This capability would turn a dead end into a concise spoken diagnosis, a bounded retry that does not replay already-completed steps, or a browser/Mac fallback artifact the owner can inspect later.
args.model_tier: background first for deterministic failure classification and known recovery recipes; escalate to planner only when the error and fallback are ambiguous. Realtime should only speak the short status to the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for receipt lookup and known-error diagnosis; under 20 seconds for one recovery attempt; otherwise enqueue durable work and notify through relay/pipeline when complete.
args.cost_estimate: Usually $0–$0.01: receipt/journal lookup and known recipes are deterministic, with a small-model call only for unfamiliar errors. Planner escalation is the dominant cost (roughly 8–10k prompt tokens).
args.security_concerns: Failure receipts can contain URLs, shell commands, paths, and authenticated-page snippets. Keep raw evidence on the Mac, send the relay only a redacted diagnosis and status, and require explicit owner confirmation before any fallback that sends, submits, deletes, or makes an irreversible shell change; retries of idempotent/read-only steps can remain automatic under the owner's maximum-access policy.

Add a compact dashboard view showing failure clusters, unattributed tier counts, and the exact evidence behind each diagnosis.

args.effort: Medium: shared correlation schema, executor/browser adapters, failure classifier and retry state machine, plus dashboard/relay projections; 1–2 weeks including integration tests for partial completion and stale browser tabs.
args.risk: A bad classifier could retry a non-idempotent command or mislabel a successful partial mutation. args.cost_impact: Negligible storage (roughly 1–3 KB metadata per action, with raw evidence retained locally); small-model classification is usually cheaper than planner calls and can be deterministic for known errors. Dashboard polling adds minimal relay/database traffic.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 50 ms for correlation/ledger writes and perhaps 100–300 ms for deterministic classification; only failed jobs incur recovery latency. Known transient browser recovery should complete within one extra bridge round trip.
args.security_impact: Ledger contains sensitive URLs, paths, shell strings, and page evidence. Keep raw payloads local, redact relay/pipeline summaries, hash or truncate secrets, and apply existing audio retention policy to spoken failure reports.

args.why_useful: The owner can start a task by voice or in Safari, then walk away, but cannot currently preserve a coherent, resumable checkpoint across the pendant, relay, Mac job, and authenticated browser. Today a job receipt records actions after the fact; it does not capture the live task state, open-tab evidence, pending decisions, or the exact next safe step. This would make interruption normal rather than forcing the owner to reconstruct context.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic checkpoint capture and a small background model to compress the task state; use the realtime model only for the short pendant acknowledgement and a planner-tier call when resuming requires reconciling changed tabs or a new goal.
args.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement and local checkpoint in under 2 seconds; resume inspection in under 10 seconds, with longer work continuing durably and a concise pendant notification when ready.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per pause/resume: local browser snapshots, receipts, and structured state need no model; background summarization is the dominant routine cost. Planner escalation is reserved for changed or ambiguous authenticated pages.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoints may contain authenticated URLs, page text, drafts, shell paths, and voice-derived private context. Store raw snapshots only on the Mac, encrypt or expire them, send the relay only a redacted task summary, and never resume a submit/send/delete step automatically. On resume, show changed evidence and require the owner's existing confirmation convention before irreversible actions.

args.model_tier: Deterministic policy for urgency, quiet hours, acknowledgement, and escalation; background model only to classify an unfamiliar finding's urgency. Realtime is used solely to speak an urgent alert and capture acknowledgement.
args.latency_budget: Urgent event delivered within 5 seconds of a confirmed finding; normal events batched at the next availability transition; escalation after a configurable deadline.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for routing and acknowledgement state. Background classification is occasional and dominates model cost; realtime audio is only used for escalated alerts.

transcript.text:
Recorded two new proposals:

1. **Interrupt-aware urgent delivery** — route alerts to the pendant, Mac, or dashboard based on live availability, urgency, quiet hours, and acknowledgement state, with escalation only when necessary.
2. **Cross-surface resumable checkpoints** — pause a task with browser state, evidence, completed actions, and pending decisions, then resume it later with a diff showing what changed.

pendant.board: Nordic nRF9160 DK (nRF9160 SiP), non-secure app under TF-M minimal
pendant.cpu: Arm Cortex-M33 @ 64 MHz, DSP extension present (libopus ARMv5E paths apply)
pendant.ram: 211,608 B application RAM (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); 32 kB secure, modem shares the first 128 kB
pendant.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

io.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
io.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
io.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
io.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.

storage.sd: microSD over SPI. CONFIG_DISK_DRIVER_SDMMC, FATFS (ELM) with exFAT enabled. Mount is FS_FATFS.
storage.policy: Owner's standing rule: audio is written to SD ONLY when a chunk upload cannot be uploaded. It is a failure buffer, not a routine store.
storage.note: exFAT means large files and long filenames are available.

audio.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
audio.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
audio.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

bridge.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
bridge.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
bridge.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

network.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
network.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
network.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

stack.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
stack.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
stack.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
stack.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
stack.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
stack.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

power.supply: USB or battery. LTE-M transmit bursts draw far more than idle.
power.note: No battery gauge is wired up today, so the agent cannot read charge state.

result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (mac-terminal). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.

args.user_asks: When I say “save this page” through the pendant, remember the exact Safari page and the part I’m looking at, then let me ask for it back later.
args.why_useful: It turns fleeting browsing into searchable memory without copy/paste: the pendant supplies intent, Safari supplies authenticated title/URL/selection, the Mac persists a compact citation, and the relay makes it retrievable from any surface. Unlike a generic voice note, the saved item is anchored to what was actually on screen.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to detect the short save command; use a cheaper background model to normalize page text and generate a one-line label; use the relay's normal text retrieval for later questions.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; capture the page in 2 s; later retrieval under 3 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per save depending on extracted text length; most cost is one background summarization, not realtime audio.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and any selection leave Safari only to the local Mac and the owner's relay account. Default to storing URL, title, selection, and a short hash/snippet rather than the whole page; require an explicit “save the whole page” phrase for more data.
missing: A browser command that atomically returns active tab URL/title/selection plus a stable content fingerprint
A capture record type linking a saved item to browser tab provenance and searchable embeddings
A retrieval intent that searches these page captures and returns citations

args.name: context_bookmark_button
args.what_it_does: A short double-tap while idle emits a compact context-bookmark event; the Mac immediately snapshots foreground app, active Safari tab metadata, current project/session, and timestamp. A long press still starts conversation, and a tap during a call remains end-call, preserving existing behavior.
args.why_not_server_side: The value is a reliable physical moment marker even when speech recognition, LTE, or the relay is unavailable. Only firmware can capture the button edge with sub-100-ms timing and queue it through a dropped-link interval.
args.trigger: Button double-tap while idle; firmware event queue retries over the existing USB/LTE transport and flashes a distinct two-blink acknowledgement.
args.inputs: Button edge timestamps, current connection state, monotonic sequence number; no microphone audio and no new sensor input.
args.storage: A 32-byte binary event record (sequence, timestamp, event type, CRC) in RAM ring buffer; spill only to the existing SD failure buffer if transport is unavailable. At 64 records this is ~2 kB.
args.ram_budget: ~3 kB including ring metadata and retry state, well below 211,608 B application RAM; no audio buffers or Opus changes required.

args.change: Add a duplex-aware audio scheduler for the nRF9160/relay pair: reserve a minimum uplink slice for mic packets whenever downlink TTS is active, adapt Opus uplink from 16 kbps toward 8 kbps under contention, and mark every dropped packet with a sequence gap. The relay should shorten or pause TTS on detected barge-in rather than allowing both streams to saturate LTE-M.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can interrupt the agent and be heard instead of losing roughly eight seconds of speech during simultaneous talk. Conversations feel responsive on the real pendant, not merely healthy in telemetry.
args.effort: Medium-high: firmware packet scheduler and bitrate control, relay congestion feedback, and an integration test over the USB-connected modem/bridge with induced contention.
args.risk: Poor bitrate transitions could create artifacts or starve playback; recover by falling back to the current fixed 16/24 kbps mode when feedback is absent. Sequence numbers make loss visible rather than silently corrupting turns.
args.cost_impact: No API cost and no new hardware; slightly higher CPU during bitrate changes, within the existing ~87% single-core audio load only if transitions avoid extra transcoding.
args.latency_impact: Barge-in acknowledgement improves from multi-second loss to one or two packet intervals; TTS may sound briefly clipped when preempted.
args.security_impact: No new data leaves the device; congestion metadata is non-content telemetry.
depends_on: A framed packet sequence/priority field shared by pendant and relay
Relay-side barge-in detection that can stop queued TTS packets
An integration test harness for the live /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA pair

transcript.text:
Round 127 findings:

- Mac bridge and Safari extension are online.
- The active Safari tab is currently a failed `example.com` page.
- The local agent is not fully ready: Accessibility and Screen Recording are still ungranted.
- The nRF9160 pendant and ESP32 bridge are physically USB-connected, but there is still no serial health/recovery endpoint.

I recorded four new proposals:

1. **“Save this page” physical context bookmark** — a pendant command that captures the active Safari page, selection, URL, and provenance for later retrieval.
2. **Meeting bookmark timeline** — a pendant tap marks moments during a meeting; the Mac adds foreground-app and browser evidence, and the relay produces a sourced timeline afterward.
3. **Cross-device pendant diagnosis and recovery** — inspect both USB devices, relay pipeline, jobs, and receipts, then safely recover dropped audio or bridge failures with truthful verification.
4. **Duplex-aware audio scheduler** — reserve uplink capacity during TTS, adapt Opus bitrate, and preempt TTS on barge-in to address the measured ~7.8-second speech loss during simultaneous talking.

I also queued a firmware skill for a **double-tap context bookmark event**, requiring only about 3 KB RAM and no new sensor hardware.

What I still need:

- Implementation of the queued serial diagnostic/recovery capability for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- A device-to-relay heartbeat and packet-sequence contract so failures and replayed audio can be verified rather than guessed.
- The actual Accessibility and Screen Recording grants for the AI Pendant Agent if GUI automation or screenshots are expected.
- Firmware support for distinguishing idle double-tap context bookmarks from the existing conversation button behavior.

args.user_asks: When I walk away from my Mac, quietly checkpoint whatever I was doing, and when I return with the pendant, restore the right Safari tabs, window layout, and unfinished draft without sending or submitting anything.
args.why_useful: The owner can move between rooms or lose connection without reconstructing their working state. The pendant supplies physical presence, the Mac captures the real UI state, and the browser preserves authenticated tabs and drafts; no single surface can provide that continuity alone.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic presence and state capture; use a cheap background model only to name the checkpoint and identify the active task. No realtime reasoning is needed unless the owner asks for restoration by voice.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint within 5 seconds of departure; restore within 10 seconds of return; never restore by submitting, sending, or navigating past an approval boundary.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for state capture; under $0.02 for optional task labeling. Main cost is implementation of presence and browser/window snapshots.

args.user_asks: Let the pendant act as my interruption filter: during a focus block, collect notifications from my Mac and authenticated browser, interrupt me only for things that meet my urgency rule, and give me a one-button way to defer the rest until I am free.
args.why_useful: The owner gets fewer context switches without losing genuinely urgent work. The relay can remain awake, the Mac and browser can see events, and the pendant provides the only interruption channel that follows the owner away from the screen.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a small classifier for urgency; reserve realtime for a concise spoken alert. Batch deferred items with a cheaper model into a digest.
args.latency_budget: Urgent alerts within 10 seconds; defer/dismiss acknowledgement under 1 second; digest generation under 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Typically below $0.01 per event; background summarization dominates, while rule matches are free.
args.security_concerns: Notification text can contain sensitive work or personal data. Never auto-reply or change notification settings without an explicit request.

args.change: Replace the prototype's single-button/LED interaction with a production pendant interaction module: add BLE presence beacons (or UWB if reliable room-level presence is required), a low-power vibration motor, and a capacitive double-tap surface while retaining the existing physical button for conversation. Expose signed presence epochs and alert acknowledgements to the nRF9160 firmware and Mac over USB/LTE.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can know when the owner has left or returned, deliver a private interruption without opening a speaker, and distinguish a context bookmark or defer gesture from starting/ending a call. That enables seamless work handoffs and attention protection rather than making the owner repeat commands.
args.effort: High: enclosure and power redesign, BLE/UWB coexistence testing with LTE-M, firmware input state machine, and Mac pairing/reconnection UX.
args.risk: False presence near the Mac or accidental taps could checkpoint or defer the wrong thing. Recover with explicit state LEDs/vibration patterns, debounce and a dashboard history; keep the existing button path as a fallback. UWB increases BOM and power, so BLE can ship first if room-level precision is unnecessary.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $8–$25 BOM increase depending on UWB versus BLE and a $1–$3 haptic motor; intermittent beaconing should add modest battery draw, while UWB ranging can materially increase it.
args.latency_impact: Presence changes in roughly 1–3 seconds with BLE, sub-second with UWB; local vibration acknowledgement is under 100 ms.
args.security_impact: Pairing keys and signed presence epochs must be device-bound; do not broadcast an owner-identifying static address. Presence data should remain local unless needed for a queued handoff.
depends_on: A new firmware event protocol for presence, haptic acknowledgement, and capacitive gestures
Mac and relay support for paired-device identity and presence epochs
A durable handoff/interruption state machine

args.user_asks: Keep my pendant conversational when it is plugged into my Mac, even if LTE or the relay is unavailable: I press the button, speak, hear the response through the audio bridge, and sync the transcript and pending work when connectivity returns.
args.why_useful: This is the first genuinely local/offline use of the hardware that is physically attached today. It makes the pendant useful on a plane, in a basement, or during an outage instead of becoming dead weight whenever the cloud link drops.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap local Mac model for speech/intent triage and deterministic device protocol; use realtime only when the relay is reachable, and sync summaries in background with a cheaper model.
args.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 150 ms; local response under 3 s; cloud handoff and reconciliation can take seconds after reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental API cost offline; occasional background sync uses a small model. Engineering cost is the serial protocol, local audio path, queue reconciliation, and a Mac launch agent.
args.security_concerns: Raw audio and private browser text can remain on the Mac in offline mode. Persist encrypted queue records, expose a clear local/cloud indicator, and require confirmation before replaying queued mutations after reconnect.
missing: nRF9160 USB-serial framing and button/audio control protocol
ESP32 bridge serial/audio playback service
Mac launch agent that discovers /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
offline speech recognition and TTS or a local fallback
idempotent cloud-sync/reconciliation protocol

args.user_asks: Give me a private-mode answer: inspect my currently open authenticated Safari tabs and local Mac state, but keep the page contents and audio on my Mac; send the relay only a redacted request and a short answer, with a switch to reveal the evidence if I ask.
args.why_useful: The wearable can reach the owner anywhere, while the browser holds secrets. This makes that combination usable for banking, health, and work pages without blindly shipping authenticated page contents to the cloud.
args.model_tier: Local Mac model performs extraction, redaction, and evidence selection; realtime handles only the spoken request/response envelope. Use a cheaper background model for redaction QA and caching.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge mode in 200 ms and answer in 5 s for already-open tabs; evidence reveal is an explicit second turn.
args.cost_estimate: Small realtime token usage for redacted text; most extraction stays local. Main cost is a local redaction/evidence broker and browser bridge changes.
args.security_concerns: Treat DOM, screenshots, cookies, and audio as Mac-confidential. Redaction must fail closed on uncertain fields, log hashes rather than contents, and never let a cloud prompt request raw tab data implicitly.
missing: Mac-local redaction service with field/secret detectors
browser result schema separating private evidence from shareable summary
relay metadata flag enforcing no-raw-context mode
pendant indication of private mode and reveal action
auditable local evidence store

args.user_asks: When I say 'continue that later' on the pendant, save the exact state of the conversation and the open Mac/browser work, then let me resume from the pendant or Mac with a one-sentence spoken checkpoint and no repeated explanation.
args.why_useful: Long tasks currently lose the owner's place when attention or connectivity changes. A physical button and spoken checkpoint can suspend work safely and resume it across the wearable, Mac, browser session, and relay.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic state capture and a cheap summarizer; reserve realtime for the resume conversation, not for indexing every event.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint confirmation under 1 s; resume context ready under 2 s from local state, with cloud sync eventually.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost because only compact deltas and a short summary are stored. Engineering cost is cross-surface checkpoint schema and browser/tab attachment persistence.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoint may contain private tab state. Encrypt sensitive fields, store capability-scoped references rather than cookies, expire stale browser attachments, and make spoken summaries avoid secrets by default.
missing: Cross-surface checkpoint schema with versioning
pendant double-press or spoken checkpoint event
Mac job/session and browser-tab snapshot adapter
resume conflict detection when tabs or files changed
sync queue for relay reconnect

args.user_asks: If the Mac or browser agent starts doing something I no longer want, let me long-press the pendant to stop all in-flight work immediately, hear what was cancelled, and later resume only the safe unfinished parts.
args.why_useful: A wearable is the only control surface still in the owner's hand while the Mac is busy or a browser workflow has gone wrong. A physical stop is faster and more reliable than finding a window or speaking over an active response.
args.model_tier: Deterministic device event fan-out and job cancellation; realtime only speaks the concise cancellation receipt, with no model call needed for the stop itself.
args.latency_budget: Hardware acknowledgement under 100 ms; cancel requests dispatched under 300 ms; spoken receipt under 2 s.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost. Requires serial button-event firmware, relay cancellation fan-out, Mac/browser abort handlers, and a compact receipt.
args.security_concerns: Long-press must be hard to trigger accidentally and never erase data. Cancel is safer than undo; report which operations could not be stopped and preserve receipts.
missing: Pendant long-press event and debounce policy
authenticated emergency-cancel endpoint keyed to owner session
fan-out cancellation for Mac jobs, browser commands, vision loops, and relay streams
device haptic/LED acknowledgement
partial-cancel receipt schema

args.change: Add a command execution ledger at the shell boundary that records argv after safe tokenization, cwd, selected environment fingerprints (never raw secrets), start/finish/timeout, stdout/stderr hashes plus a bounded tail, process tree, exit code, and whether the command is reversible. Expose a structured failure bundle and retry recipe through the existing job journal; do not gate or block anything.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the agent says something failed, the owner gets a truthful explanation and a one-tap retry or handoff instead of a vague error. It also makes unattended work auditable without reducing the maximum-access policy.
args.effort: Medium: shell wrapper, redaction, D1 schema, journal API, and UI/voice formatter.
args.risk: Secrets can leak through output or environment; redact known secret patterns and store only hashes by default. Process-tree capture may be incomplete; mark unknown rather than claiming success. Recovery is to retain the existing raw job record.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and modest local disk/D1 storage; bounded tails cap growth.
args.latency_impact: Under 50 ms per command plus asynchronous ledger flush.
args.security_impact: Improves accountability but creates sensitive metadata; encrypt or access-scope ledger entries and omit raw env/command interpolation values.
depends_on: Existing /jobs, /journal, and /jobs/:jobId/receipts contracts

transcript.text:
Round 128 findings:

- `/ops/status` is healthy: full-control mode is enabled, relay is reachable, and the Safari extension is online with three tabs.
- Mac computer-use is **not ready**: Accessibility is untrusted, Screen Recording is missing, and the vision loop is disabled.
- The physically attached pendant and ESP32 bridge still lack a defined serial control/audio protocol, so USB-local conversation is not yet runnable.

New proposals recorded:

1. **USB-local offline conversation** — button, nRF9160, ESP32 audio bridge, Mac-local processing, and eventual relay reconciliation. This is the strongest capability: it makes the wearable useful today even without LTE or cloud access.
2. **Private-mode browser answers** — authenticated Safari content stays on the Mac; only a redacted request and answer reach the relay.
3. **Cross-surface “continue later” checkpoints** — preserve Mac jobs, browser tabs, evidence, and spoken context for safe resume.
4. **Pendant emergency stop** — long-press cancels in-flight Mac, browser, vision, and relay work and speaks a cancellation receipt.
5. **Shell execution ledger** — recorded as a Mac-harness change, but flagged as close to an existing shell-observability proposal rather than treated as wholly new.

What I still need is implementation work, not another permission request:

- A serial protocol and daemon for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- Local speech recognition/TTS fallback for USB offline mode.
- Relay-level cancellation fan-out and pendant long-press firmware event.
- A Mac-local browser redaction/evidence broker.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions if vision/UI automation is intended.

args.user_asks: Make my Mac and browser automatically enter a private state when my pendant leaves me: pause spoken output, hide sensitive Safari tabs, stop sharing, and restore everything when the pendant returns—without me touching the keyboard.
args.why_useful: The pendant is the one object that travels with the owner. Presence-based privacy protects authenticated work, banking, and health sessions during interruptions or when the owner walks away, something a Mac alone cannot reliably infer.
args.model_tier: Deterministic presence and policy engine; no expensive model call for lock/unlock. Use realtime only to announce state changes when appropriate.
args.latency_budget: Detect departure within 2 seconds and apply browser/audio protections within 1 second; restore within 2 seconds after return.
args.cost_estimate: No per-use model cost. Requires a low-power proximity signal, Mac presence daemon, Safari tab masking, and relay session coordination.
args.security_concerns: False departures must not destroy work; suspend and restore exact tab state. Never treat presence alone as authentication for financial actions. Keep presence history local and expire it quickly.

Relay stream pause/resume tied to presence state

args.security_concerns: Do not persist the value, include it in logs, or expose it to relay telemetry. Require a deliberate button gesture for playback, redact browser evidence, and refuse ambiguous matches.

args.change: Add a low-power, cryptographically rotating BLE presence beacon to the pendant, with a companion Mac receiver/daemon and a hardware-visible privacy-state indicator. The beacon should expose only an ephemeral identifier and support a signed return-to-presence handshake; it must not become a general-purpose tracking device.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's wearable can become a reliable privacy boundary: walking away can protect browser sessions and audio automatically, while returning restores the exact working state. The current button and USB connection cannot detect daily physical presence once unplugged.
args.effort: Medium-high hardware revision plus firmware, macOS daemon, Safari integration, and relay session-state support.
args.risk: Radio loss can cause nuisance privacy transitions; use hysteresis and suspend/restore rather than destructive actions. Battery life and pairing bugs are the main recovery concerns.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–8 in added BLE-capable beacon/sensor hardware depending on board revision, with low average power draw; negligible model cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second local detection after radio tuning; no network latency required.
args.security_impact: Use rotating identifiers, authenticated pairing, no location history, and local-only presence logs. A stolen beacon must not unlock accounts or authorize transactions.

Browser tab masking/restoration integration

result.note: Built the receipt/undo half only. NO gates, NO approval prompts, NO preconditions — nothing added here can refuse or skip an action, per owner policy. New local-agent/actionReceipts.js; executor.js now wraps every dispatch: observeBeforeAction(action) runs first (pure observation, swallows all errors, its verdict is never read), then buildActionReceipt() attaches a receipt to every result — successful or failed. Receipt carries: content-addressed actionId (stable across a re-run of the same plan; positional index would not be, because the orchestrator hands the executor one action at a time), unique receiptId, effect read|write, what was touched (paths, urls, apps, shell commands, email recipients, clipboard, settings with before/after), duration, and an honest reversibility verdict with reversedBy or irreversibleReason. Reversibility now lives in ONE place: undo.js imports describeReversibility() so the receipt the owner reads and the decision undo makes cannot disagree; jobs recorded before receipts existed fall back to the raw result fields, so old history stays undoable. COMPENSATING UNDO: observeBeforeAction snapshots any file a write_file/create_note/delete_path/copy_path/move_path is about to clobber into ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/.undo (bounded at 8 MB; directories and oversize files are recorded as irreversible WITH the reason rather than silently half-copied). This makes delete_path — previously permanent — undoable, and fixes a real data-loss bug: undo used to answer 'yes, reversible' for a write_file that OVERWROTE an existing file and then reverse it by DELETING that file, destroying content the agent never wrote. Now it restores the exact prior bytes. Surfaced at GET /jobs (receipts per job), new GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts (counts + per-step undo verdict + snapshot vault path), and inside GET /ops/snapshot so the dashboard and relay see them too. describeUndoability now returns steps[] and irreversible[] with reasons, so 'why can't I undo this?' has an answer. Verified live end to end: overwrote a hand-written file via POST /execute, receipt showed reversible=true reversedBy='restore snapshot', POST /jobs/:id/undo restored the original content. Tests: actionReceipts.test.js (16); full suite 499/499.

args.name: usb_disconnect_job_cache
args.what_it_does: When the pendant is USB-attached, it mirrors compact authenticated job acknowledgements and status transitions from the Mac. If the serial link drops, it records the owner's button intent (start, pause, cancel, acknowledge) with a monotonic counter and gives local LED/haptic feedback. On reconnect it uploads the intents exactly once and displays the reconciled result, rejecting stale or duplicate job IDs.
args.why_not_server_side: It must detect USB loss and drive pendant feedback offline; the relay cannot observe a disconnected serial cable or provide truthful local acknowledgement. This is directly testable with the two physically connected chips before LTE registration exists.
args.trigger: USB serial connect/disconnect event, authenticated status packet from the Mac, or a pendant button press while disconnected.
args.inputs: Paired-device handshake, compact job ID, status enum, sequence number, button event, and server/Mac acknowledgement sequence.
args.storage: A 32-entry ring in nRF9160 flash: roughly 32 × 64-byte event records plus a small pairing/sequence header, under 3 KB; no sensitive page text.
args.ram_budget: About 4–8 KB buffers/state, comfortably below the 211,608 B application RAM budget; use flash ring writes rather than retaining history in RAM.

transcript.text:
Round 129 produced three new owner-facing capabilities:

1. **Self-repairing tasks** — after a Mac or browser task fails, diagnose the cause, repair what is safe, retry only the failed portion, verify the postcondition, and report exactly what changed.
2. **Pendant as a USB job remote** — while LTE is unavailable, use the physically connected pendant to start, pause, cancel, and receive exception-only progress for Mac/browser jobs.
3. **Cross-surface change report** — answer “What did you change on my Mac and in my browser since this morning?” with time-bounded evidence, receipt links, and available undo operations.

I also queued a pendant firmware skill, `usb_disconnect_job_cache`, to retain up to 32 compact job/button events across USB disconnects and reconcile them exactly once on reconnect.

The shell flight-recorder proposal was rejected as already covered by existing transcript/receipt work, so I did not restate it.

What is still needed:

- A durable recovery state machine connecting failed jobs, diagnostics, retries, and postcondition verification.
- The Mac USB-serial bridge for authenticated pendant events and compact job-status packets.
- The nRF9160 firmware implementation for offline event caching and LED/haptic feedback.
- A normalized event index combining Mac receipts, shell outcomes, browser mutations, and relay jobs.
- The exact pendant button/LED protocol and reconnect semantics remain unknown.

args.user_asks: “Tap my pendant to bind this exact Safari tab and the app I’m looking at, then let me ask about or act on that context without telling you which tab it is.”
args.why_useful: Owners routinely have several private tabs and half-finished windows open. A physical tap gives the system an unambiguous attention anchor: the Mac reports the foreground app, active tab, selection, and a short-lived screenshot/text fingerprint; the relay and browser surface use that binding for the next request only. This removes the most frustrating class of wrong-tab answers without requiring the owner to narrate UI details.
args.model_tier: Realtime for interpreting the immediate request; use a cheaper model for extracting and compressing the bound context.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms from tap to acknowledgement; context available within 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.002–$0.02 per use, dominated by optional screenshot/text compression; the binding itself is local.
args.security_concerns: The binding must expire quickly and be scoped to the paired pendant, Mac session, tab ID, and request. Private page content must remain on the Mac unless the owner asks for relay processing. Never expose a tab merely because it was recently active.
missing: A Mac Accessibility/Screen Recording-backed foreground-app and active-tab capture primitive
A pendant-to-Mac tap/nonce handshake over the live USB serial connection
An ephemeral context-binding token accepted by browser actions and relay planning
